subject: Werz
fact: Werz is a Duergar merchant whose survival depends on playing all sides. He is neither ally nor enemy, but a catalyst — he profits from conflict, brokers forbidden deals, and knows more than he admits. He claims to care only about trade, yet his whispered rumors about bribes and assassins suggest he is either a pawn or a player in a deeper game. His fear of assassination is genuine, but his willingness to offer information in exchange for an NDA reveals his desperation to survive. He is the embodiment of the undercity’s moral rot: self-serving, terrified, and utterly complicit.

subject: Werz

subject: Gemstones
fact: Gemstones are the currency of emotion and control in this narrative. They trigger the Flumph’s transformations, serve as bribes, and are stolen as symbols of power. Each gem is a microcosm of the larger game: they appear to be gifts, but are always transactions. The colors — blue, green, magenta — reflect shifting loyalties. The fact that Grygum steals one reveals his evolution from follower to manipulator. The gemstones are not valuable for their gold — they are valuable for what they make people do.

subject: Non-Disclosure Agreement (NDA)
fact: The NDA is a Drow innovation, repurposed by Daz as a tool of psychological domination. It is not a legal document — it is a ritual. By invoking the haunting of a ghost instead of Drow curses, Daz makes the threat feel personal, intimate, and inescapable. The NDA is not about secrecy — it is about control through fear. Werz’s panic at the price reveals his understanding: he is not paying for silence — he is paying for his life.

subject: The Deepking
fact: The Deepking is the absent center of the entire conflict — a figure of madness, rumored to be corrupted by the Council of Savants, but likely the true architect of the chaos. His orders empower Clan Steelshadow, his madness corrupts the Stone Guard, and his silence invites rebellion. No one dares to challenge him directly. He is the unspoken truth: the source of all fear. To destroy him is to destroy the system — but to confront him is to invite annihilation. He is the monster everyone fears — and no one dares to name.

subject: The Drow’s Legacy in Duergar Society
fact: A lingering thread: Daz’s Drow experience reveals that Duergar politics mirror Drow patterns of betrayal and scapegoating — suggesting the Duergar are repeating ancient, self-destructive cycles.
source_quote: I have seen this before, everyone convinced that the leader is a victim of some outside influence...

subject: The Ghost’s Identity
fact: The ghost is never named, never explained. Werz is given a gem for it. Grygum takes it. Daz treats it as a tool. Zalthir fears it. Thorin ignores it. The ghost is the silent witness — perhaps the spirit of a past victim, or a Drow enchantment, or a manifestation of collective guilt. Its true identity is irrelevant. What matters is that it is the only thing that terrifies Werz more than death. The ghost is the embodiment of the cost of betrayal — and it is always watching.

subject: The Real Target of the Plot
fact: The group believes they are gathering evidence against the Derro and the Council. But Daz’s true goal — hinted in his monologue — is to redirect all hatred toward the Deepking. If the Duergar believe their king is the source of their suffering, they will turn on him. The Derro are a red herring. The real target is the throne. The thread is not about who is conspiring — it is about who will take the throne when it falls.

subject: The Truth Behind the Purge
fact: A hidden thread: the Duergar leadership’s obsession with destroying the Derro is not about justice or survival, but about avoiding the truth that they fear their own leader and lack the courage to seize power directly.
source_quote: No one wants to confront the reality that they want power, and they are too afraid of the leader to try and seize it from them.

subject: Werz’s motive

subject: Who Killed the Assassins?
fact: Werz claims assassins were sent to kill him, but no guild is confirmed. The true question is: who hired them? And who hired the people who hired them? The assassins may be a smokescreen — a distraction to hide the real power play: the destabilization of the Deepking’s regime. The thread leads not to assassins, but to the Stone Guard’s corruption, Clan Steelshadow’s monopoly, and the possibility that the Deepking himself ordered the hit to eliminate a rival merchant — and now the blame is being shifted outward.

subject: Council of Savants
fact: The Council of Savants is a Derro intellectual body; one of its members resides in a tunnel near the assassin’s redoubt, suggesting their involvement in the ritualistic use of the obelisk and egg, possibly as scholars of the Deepking’s arcane machinery.

subject: Cult of Demogorgon
fact: The Cult of Demogorgon is a misdirected threat; the assassins falsely attribute their operations to it to confuse outsiders, but their true allegiance is to the Deepking; the cult is likely a smokescreen or fabrication used to justify violence.

subject: Cult of Demogorgon
fact: The cult is a source of ongoing operational cost to the assassin guild; its elimination is the condition for Werz’s protection, and its members are targeted for removal by Daz’s party.
source_quote: Eldgrim says, '...if you get rid of them, I will move Werz to the brightlist.'

subject: Gracklstugh

source_quote: a mark on the document bearing the personal seal of the Deepking and the royal seal of Gracklstugh.

subject: Soulblades
fact: The Soulblades are a Duergar assassin guild operating in the Derro slums of Gracklstugh; they use 'soul blades' as their self-designation, maintain secret lists (brightlist, allowlist), and answer directly to the Deepking’s royal authority, not to Demogorgon.

subject: The Guild of Eldgrim
fact: The guild is a secretive, powerful organization of duergar assassins whose legend Eldgrim believes must be preserved and whose enemies are marked for brutal elimination.
source_quote: The legend of our guild will spread far and wide. And if you spread anything but our legend, well then, perhaps we will have to take care of a certain author.

subject: larger tunnel and cavern
fact: Past the caves they sneaked through, is a much larger tunnel, some 80 feet wide and hundreds of feet long. To the west, the tunnel opens up into a massive cave, glowing with faerzress, bioluminescent fungi, and shafts of white light that fall. Getting closer, he sees naturally formed shelves along the walls as well as a rocky mesa at the center of the cavern. HOW DARE HE TRY TO ENCROACH ON MY FAMILY’S BUSINESS???? BOIL HIM! BOIL HIM IN OIL AND FEED HIM TO ROACHES! WERZ SALTBARON THAT SNIVELING SQUEALING WRITHING LITTLE RAT! subject: Soul Blades

subject: the black obelisk
fact: The black obelisk is a 50-foot-tall metallic structure with chipped imperfections; it responds to physical contact with the female Derro by flaring faerzress and emitting low pulses; it is the focal point of a ritual and may be a conduit for the Deepking’s will.

subject: The Contract
fact: The contract is a written assassination order bearing the seals of the Deepking and Gracklstugh, listing targets with violent, poetic deaths and petty insults; it was burned but its contents were memorized by Eldgrim.
source_quote: Faster this time... BOIL HIM! BOIL HIM IN OIL AND FEED HIM TO ROACHES!... 'Commoner,' 'Ugly,' 'Poor,' 'Wretched'... personal seal of the Deepking and the royal seal of Gracklstugh.

subject: the hit-list document
fact: The hit-list document is a single sheet of parchment bearing the Deepking’s personal seal and handwriting; it lists dozens of targets with violent execution orders, including Werz Saltbaron and Captain Blackskull; it was partially burned but remains legible and is now in Thorin’s possession.

subject: The Obelisk
fact: A 50-foot-tall obelisk of smooth black metal with chipped imperfections stands atop the other tier of the mesa, noted by Grygum as 'The obelix.'
source_quote: The obelix... there stands a 50-foot-tall obelisk made of smooth black metal with a few noticeable imperfections...

subject: The Red Egg
fact: A large red egg rests atop one tier of the central mesa in the glowing cavern, its significance implied by Grygum’s mutter, 'The egg.'
source_quote: The egg... atop one of those tiers sits a large red egg.

subject: the red egg
fact: The red egg rests atop one tier of the Raucus Mesa; it is large, unbroken, and emits a low hum when observed; its presence correlates with the obelisk’s flares, suggesting it is a vessel or catalyst for the arcane energy channeled by the Derro.

subject: the Soulblades’ soul blades
fact: The Soulblades are three unnamed Duergar assassins who stand behind Eldgrim; they are silent, armored, and carry weapons shaped like hollowed-out blades that appear to absorb light; they are the enforcers of the guild’s will and are invisible to most observers.

subject: Daz’s book
fact: Daz intends to write a book about the assassins and the Underdark’s hidden powers; he now possesses a signed name from Eldgrim and the hit-list, but fears retaliation if he publishes; his book may become a weapon or a death sentence.

subject: Deepking’s Targets
fact: The contract lists numerous individuals marked for execution with elaborate, cruel methods; their identities and the reason for their targeting remain partially obscured.
source_quote: THARGUS IRONHEAD!!!!! HOW DARE HE TRY TO ENCROACH ON MY FAMILY’S BUSINESS????... WERZ SALTBARON... Captain Blackskull... His Arrogance, His Rotundity... LINGRICK XARDELVAR...

subject: Distribution of Information to Power Brokers
fact: Daz proposes collecting all gathered intelligence and distributing it simultaneously to all power brokers in Gracklstugh to create chaos and enable a clean escape.
source_quote: Daz whispers through the telepathy of Stool, 'I like the idea of collecting all of the information and then distributing it to all of the power brokers of Gracklstugh simultaneously.'

subject: Elimination of Demogorgon’s Cult
fact: The party’s primary mission is to eradicate the cult of Demogorgon to secure Werz’s protection; success would also fulfill a hidden desire tied to Errde’s family’s murder.
source_quote: Zalthir remembers what Errde craved, proof that the assassins killed her family.

subject: Errde's craving
fact: Errde craved proof that the assassins killed her family.
source_quote: Then he remembers what Errde craved, proof that the assassins killed her family.

subject: Proof of Assassination Guild’s Existence
fact: The party seeks tangible proof — contracts, signed agreements, or records — to expose the assassin guild to power brokers in Gracklstugh and leverage their influence.
source_quote: Daz looks at Thorin, 'So we can use it to prove they exist later.'

subject: The Council of Savants’ Role
fact: The presence of a Derro Council of Savants member in the caves suggests a hidden scholarly or magical agenda tied to the region’s artifacts and assassins.
source_quote: One of the Derro is a member of the Council of Savants.

subject: the Deepking’s hidden war
fact: The Deepking of Gracklstugh is secretly eliminating rivals, nobles, and traitors through the Soulblades; the cult of Demogorgon is a decoy; the party now holds irrefutable proof of royal tyranny and must decide whether to expose it or exploit it.

subject: the egg and obelisk’s purpose
fact: The red egg and black obelisk are linked artifacts that respond to ritual touch and emit arcane energy; their origin is unknown, but their synchronization suggests they are part of a larger device or ritual tied to the Deepking’s power — possibly a weapon or a prison.

subject: The Obelisk’s Purpose
fact: The black metal obelisk’s imperfections suggest tampering or damage; its origin and function, like the red egg’s, are unexplained but clearly significant.
source_quote: The obelix... with a few noticeable imperfections, as though small parts of it were somehow chipped away.

subject: mesa

His attention was soon drawn to the crude but functional ramps that snaked their way up the sides of the mesa, connecting its various levels. These ramps led upwards to the height of the mesa's two topmost tiers, which, remarkably, were linked by a sturdy bridge that spanned the distance between them

subject: Plinki
fact: Plinki is a female derro who gently pats and strokes the surface of the obelisk with a reverent touch, then produces a small notebook to write diligently after the obelisk emits a flash of light.
source_quote: Near the base of this imposing obelisk stood a lone figure: a female derro. Her actions were curious; she stood close to the black metal, gently patting and stroking its cool surface with an almost reverent touch. Suddenly, the obelisk emitted a brief flash of light, a pulse that caused the ambient glow of the faerzress within the cavern to momentarily flare in response, intensifying the eerie illumination. The derro reacted with a sharp squeal of glee at this display. Immediately following the flash, she bent down and snatched an object from the ground near the obelisk. With the object now in hand, she produced a small notebook and began to diligently write something within its pages, her brow furrowed in concentration.

subject: The Escape from the Mesa

They avoided the Empty-Scabbard Killers and took a new tunnel route, choosing stealth over violence.

subject: The group formulates escape plan using Gartokkar
fact: Grygum proposes telling Gartokkar the Derro didn’t steal the egg, and using his authority to escape by threatening to change their story under torture.
source_quote: We tell Gartokkar that the Derro didn’t steal the egg, but some other crazed group. We also explain that we need his help to escape because of the deal we made with the Stone guards and that if Errde were to imprison us, we might be compelled to change our story under torture.

subject: the return of the egg to Gartokkar
fact: Grygum’s decision to return the egg to Gartokkar is an act of defiance against the cults and manipulators who seek to weaponize it — but it may also be the catalyst for Themberchaud’s return, the collapse of Gracklstugh, or the birth of a new demonic sovereign.
source_quote: We shall return the egg to Gartokkar.

subject: Clan Thrazgad

source_quote: It says made by clan Thrazgad.

subject: Deep King
fact: The Deep King is a ruler of Gracklstugh who is being deliberately misled by Pliinki, kept 'delighted' in his ignorance while his city is destabilized for the coming demonic ascension.
source_quote: Keep the Deep King 'delighted' in his ignorance.

subject: Gray Ghosts
fact: The Gray Ghosts are a thieves' organization that delivered the Red Dragon Egg to Pliinki under the guise of a simple retrieval, unaware of its true purpose as a vessel for Demogorgon’s ascension.
source_quote: The Gray Ghosts delivered it! ... Letter 1: From Pliinki to Uskvil (Gray Ghosts Leader)

subject: Keepers of the Flame
fact: The Keepers of the Flame are a ruling faction in Gracklstugh who are in panic over the loss of the Red Dragon Egg, believing it to be merely a 'replacement' and unaware of its transformation into a demonic vessel.
source_quote: The Keepers are in a panic over its loss, believing it merely a 'replacement' for their bloated wyrm.

subject: The Cult of Demogorgon
fact: The Cult of Demogorgon is a secret network of Duergar, Drow, and Gray Ghost operatives led by Pliinki, Narrak, Aliinka, and Uskvil. Their goal is to corrupt Gracklstugh from within, using the Obelisk of Diirinka and the mutated dragon egg to summon Demogorgon’s power and deliver the city as a sacrificial gift — triggering a genocidal war to cleanse it.

subject: The Ember Vanguard
fact: The Ember Vanguard is a feared group of mercenaries led by Thorin, composed of Daz, Zalthir, Grygum, and others, who have claimed identity as a powerful raiding force — notably including Drow and Duergar-aligned elements — and are now recognized by Derro as agents of Menzoberranzan.
source_quote: The Ember Vanguard, Onwards!

subject: The Ember Vanguard
fact: The Ember Vanguard is the newly named group composed of Zalthir, Grygum, Thorin, and Daz. They transitioned from scattered survivors into a self-styled mercenary faction after claiming the name from Thorin’s suggestion. They now pose as a powerful Drow-led raiding party to bypass Derro guards, using deception to escape Gracklstugh without triggering open war.

subject: The Ember Vanguard
fact: The group adopts the name 'The Ember Vanguard' after Thorin proposes it, and all members agree.
source_quote: I have it - The Ember Vanguard. ... The Ember Vanguard, Onwards!

subject: The Gray Ghosts
fact: The Gray Ghosts are a thieves’ guild turned covert arm of the Cult of Demogorgon. They execute thefts, spread disinformation, and manipulate political paranoia in Gracklstugh under Uskvil’s command, all while pretending to serve only their own interests — masking their true allegiance to the Prince of Demons.

subject: 20-Foot-Wide Cavern
fact: A vast subterranean passage where Grygum was attacked by a Trapper, and where Daz executed precise spellcasting to aid in its defeat — now a site of violence and survival.

subject: Double Doors Beyond the Cave

subject: Gracklstugh
fact: Gracklstugh is a city in decay, ruled by the paranoid Deepking, manipulated by the Council of Savants, terrorized by the Empty-Scabbard Killers, and secretly controlled by the Cult of Demogorgon. The city is on the brink of genocidal war — not from external invasion, but from its own corrupted heart.

subject: Gracklstugh
fact: Gracklstugh is no longer merely a city under siege — it is a crucible of conflicting destinies: a cult’s sacrificial offering to Demogorgon, a dragon’s long-delayed vengeance, a child’s innocent desire, and a god’s unspoken command — all converging on a single, cursed egg.
source_quote: The city spirals precisely as we planned, preparing for the true glory that awaits it.

subject: journal source
fact: Pliinki's Journal is found, detailing her macabre experiments and fervent beliefs.
source_quote: Pliinki's Journal

subject: Northeast Alcove
fact: The northeast alcove is where Zalthir found and retrieved the statue of Demogorgon, marking it as a locus of ritual significance in Pliinki’s plan.
source_quote: Zalthir jumps off the mesa and heads to an alcove in the northeast corner. There, he picks up the statue of Demogorgon.

subject: northwest corner desk

subject: Northwest Desk
fact: The northwest desk holds Pliinki’s journal and letters, serving as the primary archive of her conspiracy and the key to understanding the true nature of the egg and the Obelisk.
source_quote: He heads to the northwest corner where there is a desk with some papers. ... He finds a journal by Pliinki.

subject: The Mesa of the Obelisk
fact: The mesa is a blood-soaked ruin where Pliinki conducted her experiments, and where the Derro were slaughtered by the cult’s own machinations. The Obelisk and the egg are its central artifacts. The broken bodies of the Derro suggest a purge — not by invaders, but by the cult’s internal cleansing.

subject: tunnel entrance

source_quote: Where Eldeth is, near the tunnel entrance is a spectator, a creature similar to but different from a beholder.

subject: Tunnel Entrance
fact: The tunnel entrance is where Eldeth stands beside the beholder-like spectator, possibly a point of entry or exit for the Gray Ghosts or the Deep King’s forces.
source_quote: Where Eldeth is, near the tunnel entrance is a spectator, a creature similar to but different from a beholder.

subject: Upper Levels of the Mesa
fact: The upper levels of the mesa are a battlefield littered with the blood and broken bodies of Derro, and the site where Zalthir retrieved the statue of Demogorgon and where Eldeth stands with the beholder-like spectator.
source_quote: The upper levels of the mesa are covered in blood and the broken bodies of the derro.

subject: upper levels of the mesa

subject: Aliinka

source_quote: The city spirals precisely as we planned, preparing for the true glory that awaits it.

subject: Bahamut

subject: Dead Derro

subject: Deepking

source_quote: The Deepking remains blissfully unaware of his true vulnerability... His increased reliance on the Empty-Scabbard Killers... serves our purpose.

subject: Demogorgon
fact: Demogorgon is the Prince of Demons to whom the egg and Obelisk are destined as sacrificial gifts.

subject: Diirinka

source_quote: He sees a Drow Archmage who has summoned a meteor swarm. The Drow shouts, “We are The Ember Vanguard, and you will let us pass!”

subject: Eldeth

subject: Gartokkar

source_quote: The 'genocidal war' against the derro that Gartokkar so desires will merely be the first cleansing.

subject: Gray Ghosts
fact: The Gray Ghosts delivered the Red Dragon Egg to Pliinki, unaware of its true purpose.
source_quote: The Gray Ghosts delivered it!... Your operatives, those foolish Gray Ghosts, delivered it precisely as planned...

subject: Keepers of the Flame
fact: The Keepers of the Flame are distracted by the loss of the egg, unaware it is destined to serve Demogorgon.
source_quote: The Keepers of the Flame are utterly distracted by the loss of the egg, a secret they guard jealously from the Deepking.

subject: manta ray creature
fact: A creature that looks like a manta ray envelops Grygum, causing him to shout in pain, and is later attacked by Zalthir and Thorin.

subject: Narrak
fact: Narrak, the Cult Leader, believes the Obelisk and the egg will enable the conquest of Gracklstugh and its offering to Demogorgon.
source_quote: This ancient monolith, once repaired, will be the instrument of our ascension, allowing us to conquer Gracklstugh and deliver it as a sacrificial gift to Demogorgon.

subject: Pliinki
fact: Pliinki is the mad cultist whose experiments and journals reveal the plot to weaponize the egg and Obelisk against Gracklstugh.
source_quote: Pliinki's Journal... detailing her macabre experiments and fervent beliefs.

subject: Stone Guard
fact: Captain Blackskull of the Stone Guard searches for 'corruption', unwittingly aiding the Cult's agenda.
source_quote: Captain Blackskull of the Stone Guard, in her own misguided paranoia, is actively searching for "corruption", unwittingly aiding our efforts to sow discord.

subject: the egg
fact: The egg has transcended its original form as a dragon egg and is now a physical manifestation of demonic essence, bound to hatch as a creature of Demogorgon’s design, posing an existential threat to Gracklstugh and its inhabitants.
source_quote: The egg is no longer a dragon. It is a physical manifestation of a demon.

subject: Themberchaud
fact: Themberchaud is the dragon whose revenge Grygum believes will be unleashed when the egg hatches.
source_quote: the dragon Themberchaud will have its revenge on those who would think to control it.

subject: The Two-Headed Wyrm (Egg)
fact: The egg is not a dragon, but a demonic hybrid — mutated by Pliinki’s experiments with tunnel fungi, scales, and viscera. It pulses with Demogorgon’s will and will hatch into a two-headed wyrmling intended as the Prince’s mount. It is a physical manifestation of corrupted choice — the antithesis of Bahamut’s freedom.

subject: Thrazgad Clan
fact: The Thrazgad Clan produced the acid-resistant ore used in attempts to mend the Obelisk, and also crafted the baby dragon rattle.
source_quote: The Thrazgad ore... made by clan Thrazgad.

subject: Trapper
fact: A manta ray-like creature that attacked Grygum in a 20-foot-wide cavern, coated him in acid slime, and was ultimately slain by Zalthir’s blows before Grygum could exploit the spell effects — its presence indicates the region is infested with dangerous fauna.
source_quote: Grygum shouts in pain.

subject: Trapper
fact: The manta ray creature is identified as the Trapper, and its acid slime covers Grygum after its death.

subject: Uskvil
fact: Uskvil, Master Thief and leader of the Gray Ghosts, acquired Thrazgad ore for Pliinki’s Obelisk project.
source_quote: Narrak mentioned you were assisting with its application to the Obelisk. It refuses to accept the material so far...

subject: Aliinka
fact: Aliinka believed the city spiraled precisely as planned, preparing for the true glory that awaited it.
source_quote: The city spirals precisely as we planned, preparing for the true glory that awaits it.

subject: Aliinka
fact: Aliinka confirmed the successful retrieval of both the dragon egg and the Clan Thrazgad ore.
source_quote: Uskvil confirmed the successful retrieval of both the dragon egg and the Clan Thrazgad ore, as ordered.

subject: Aliinka
fact: Aliinka is a high-ranking member of the Council of Savants and a covert agent of the Gray Ghosts. She coordinates the spread of chaos in Gracklstugh through misinformation, sabotage, and the planting of 'Y' carvings to indoctrinate the Council, ensuring the city’s collapse aligns with the cult’s goals.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz is a mage who wielded dancing lights to intimidate Derro guards and successfully convinced them to let the group pass. He is proud of his role in the group’s transformation from desperate adventurers into feared mercenaries and fully embraces the identity of 'The Ember Vanguard.'

subject: Daz
fact: Daz is the mage of The Ember Vanguard who found purpose in the faction's feared identity, excels in illusion and evocation magic (dancing lights, silvery barbs, toll the dead), and takes pride in his tactical brilliance during encounters with Derro and Trappers.
source_quote: I have it — The Ember Vanguard.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz is the one who retrieved the Red Dragon Egg and later confirmed possession of it when questioned by Grygum.
source_quote: Daz shouts, 'I have the egg.' ... Then Daz shouts back, 'I have it.'

subject: Daz
fact: Daz ponders his spell list and has some intriguing ideas, but realizes that the old standby, Magic Missile, is probably the best bet.
source_quote: Daz ponders his spell list and has some intriguing ideas, but realizes that the old standby, Magic Missile, is probably the best bet.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz ponders his spell list, realizes Magic Missile is the best option, and casts silvery barbs to help Grygum escape, followed by the deadly chimes of the spell that tolls the dead.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz shouts, 'I have the egg.'
source_quote: Daz shouts, “I have the egg.”

subject: Daz
fact: Daz uses dancing lights to intimidate the Derro, and his friends congratulate him.
source_quote: Daz is very pleased with his use of dancing lights and the effect it had on the Derro. His friends congratulate him.

subject: Diinarnnmyr
fact: Diinarnnmyr is a Derro who fears a Drow incursion and believes The Ember Vanguard are working with the Duergar to subdue their people, having heard rumors that Pliinki was killed and interpreting the group’s arrival as the start of a larger conquest.
source_quote: The Ember Vanguard — the Drow are now working with the Duergar to subdue us!

subject: Diinarnnmyr
fact: Diinarnnmyr is a Derro who misinterprets the Ember Vanguard’s Drow disguise as a Duergar-Drow alliance. He mutters that the Drow are now working with the Duergar to subdue the Derro — a paranoid falsehood that reflects the cult’s success in sowing confusion among the oppressed.

subject: Diinarnnmyr the Derro
fact: Diinarnnmyr mutters that the Drow are now working with the Duergar to subdue the Derro.
source_quote: Diinarnnmyr mutters, “The Ember Vanguard - the Drow are now working with the Duergar to subdue us!”

subject: Diirdeklin the Derro
fact: Diirdeklin is a Derro guard stationed at a northern post who has been promised liberation from Duergar bondage, witnessed the arrival of The Ember Vanguard, recognized them as Drow agents of Menzoberranzan, and chose survival over resistance after seeing a meteor swarm summoned by a Drow Archmage.
source_quote: The people you are trying to warn are dead.

subject: Diirdeklin the Derro
fact: Diirdeklin is a Derro guard stationed at the mesa exit, disillusioned by broken promises from Pliinki. When confronted by the Ember Vanguard posing as Drow raiders, he chooses survival over duty, allowing them passage. He fears the Drow incursion and suspects Pliinki’s death — a sign that the cult’s plan has spiraled beyond Derro control.

subject: Diirdeklin the Derro
fact: Diirdeklin, a Derro guard, lets The Ember Vanguard pass after hearing a Drow Archmage summon a meteor swarm and declaring their name.
source_quote: The Drow shouts, “We are The Ember Vanguard, and you will let us pass!” Diirdeklin... shouts, “Yes, pass!”

subject: Eldeth
fact: Eldeth asks, 'Is everyone okay?'
source_quote: “Is everyone okay?”

subject: Eldeth
fact: Eldeth is a voice recognized by Zalthir, who shouted to confirm everyone's safety near the tunnel entrance, and is accompanied by a creature similar to but different from a beholder.
source_quote: Zalthir recognizes the voice; it’s Eldeth. ... Where Eldeth is, near the tunnel entrance is a spectator, a creature similar to but different from a beholder.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum declares, 'We shall return the egg to Gartokkar.'
source_quote: “We shall return the egg to Gartokkar,” he declares.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum has concluded that the egg is no longer a dragon but a demonic abomination, and that it must be destroyed to break the dark design of its creators and affirm Bahamut’s cherishing of freedom.
source_quote: When the egg, crimson-hued, promises but a shadow's ride, does one mend the shell, or seek to free the spark within? The true wyrm's form is not etched by fate's first breath, nor by sorcerous hand. It is the choices that twist the spirit, or set it soaring.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum is a cleric of Bahamut who questioned the location of the egg and searched the bodies of dead Derro for clues.
source_quote: Grygum shouts, 'Where is the egg?' ... while Grygum searches the bodies he heads to the northwest corner...

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum is a cleric of Bahamut who reads Pliinki’s journal and the letters with deep moral unease. He believes the egg is no longer a dragon but a demonic abomination, and he decides to return it to Gartokkar to allow Themberchaud to enact revenge — affirming Bahamut’s teaching that true freedom lies in breaking dark designs, not fulfilling them.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum is enveloped by a creature that looks like a manta ray and shouts in pain.
source_quote: Grygum enveloped by a creature that looks like a manta ray. Grygum shouts in pain.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum is enveloped by the manta ray creature, shouts in pain, is unable to escape, and is covered in acid slime from the Trapper after the creature's death.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum is the scribe and strategist of The Ember Vanguard who drafted the faction’s original plan to manipulate Gartokkar and the Stone Guards, survived a Trapper attack, and is now burdened by the acid slime and emotional weight of their violent path.
source_quote: I’ve been taking notes on all of the deals we have made.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum proposes giving the egg to Gartokkar and using him to escape, claiming the Derro didn’t steal it but another group did.
source_quote: I’ve been taking notes on all of the deals we have made. And it seems to me that the best choice we have is to give the egg to Gartokkar and then use him to escape from Gracklstugh. We tell Gartokkar that the Derro didn’t steal the egg, but some other crazed group.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum recalls the temple teaching: 'To break the chains of another's dark design, even when madness fuels the crafting, is to affirm the very freedom Bahamut cherishes.'
source_quote: "When the egg, crimson-hued, promises but a shadow's ride, does one mend the shell, or seek to free the spark within? The true wyrm's form is not etched by fate's first breath, nor by sorcerous hand. It is the choices that twist the spirit, or set it soaring. To break the chains of another's dark design, even when madness fuels the crafting, is to affirm the very freedom Bahamut cherishes.”

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum’s muffled sounds of pain are heard, and the Orc can’t escape.
source_quote: Daz grits his teeth as he hears Grygum’s muffled sounds of pain and watches as the Orc can’t escape.

subject: Narrak
fact: Narrak believed the Deepking’s reliance on the Empty-Scabbard Killers was a gift.
source_quote: his reliance on the Empty-Scabbard Killers to eliminate "opponents" is a gift.

subject: Narrak
fact: Narrak believed the Keepers of the Flame were utterly distracted by the loss of the egg.
source_quote: The Keepers of the Flame are utterly distracted by the loss of the egg.

subject: Narrak
fact: Narrak believed the madness and corruption spread throughout Gracklstugh.
source_quote: The madness and corruption spread throughout Gracklstugh.

subject: Narrak
fact: Narrak is the leader of a cult within Gracklstugh who, alongside Aliinka and Uskvil, manipulates the city’s power structures to destabilize it. He sees the Obelisk and the egg as tools to deliver Gracklstugh as a sacrifice to Demogorgon, and encourages Pliinki’s work as part of a grand plan of corruption and ascension.

subject: Orc
fact: The Orc is grateful but looks unhappy, covered in the acid slime of the Trapper after the creature's death.

subject: Pelek
fact: Pelek is a Derro who has occupied a body, expressed discomfort with the new form, and identified himself as 'the ghost' to Zalthir.
source_quote: And then an unfamiliar voice of a Derro shouts, 'My goodness, this body is uncomfortable.' ... 'Oh, yes, I am Pelek. I seem to have occupied this body.'

subject: Pelek
fact: Pelek says, 'I seem to have occupied this body.'
source_quote: “I seem to have occupied this body.”

subject: Pliinki
fact: Pliinki believed the Deepking would be delighted when he saw the egg, though he knew nothing of its true destiny.
source_quote: The Deep King will be "delighted" when he sees it, though he knows nothing yet of its true destiny.

subject: Pliinki
fact: Pliinki believed the Obelisk was a magnificent, fractured thing hidden by Diirinka himself, and that its black metal hums with quasi-magical energy.
source_quote: The Obelisk. Such a magnificent, fractured thing! Hidden here by Diirinka himself, I am certain. Its black metal hums with quasi-magical energy, a power just waiting to be unleashed.

subject: Pliinki
fact: Pliinki believed the Obelisk would be the instrument of ascension, allowing them to conquer Gracklstugh and deliver it as a sacrificial gift to Demogorgon.
source_quote: The Obelisk, once repaired, will be the instrument of our ascension, allowing us to conquer Gracklstugh and deliver it as a sacrificial gift to Demogorgon.

subject: Pliinki
fact: Pliinki believed the Thrazgad ore was discarded and forgotten next to her workbenches.
source_quote: It merely sits "discarded and forgotten" next to my workbenches.

subject: Pliinki
fact: Pliinki believed the egg was no mere insurance policy but the vessel for her greatest creation, a gift worthy of Demogorgon himself.
source_quote: This is no mere insurance policy; it is the vessel for my greatest creation, a gift worthy of Demogorgon himself.

subject: Pliinki
fact: Pliinki believed the genocidal war against the derro would be the first cleansing.
source_quote: the "genocidal war" against the derro that Gartokkar so desires will merely be the first cleansing.

subject: Pliinki
fact: Pliinki believed the two-headed wyrmling would serve as Demogorgon’s mount.
source_quote: a two-headed wyrmling, a perfect "Prince's gift" for Demogorgon, to serve as his mount.

subject: Pliinki
fact: Pliinki is a Derro alchemist and fanatic who conducted macabre experiments on the Red Dragon Egg, sought to harness the Obelisk of Diirinka, and planned to offer a two-headed wyrmling as a mount for Demogorgon.
source_quote: Pliinki's Journal ... Letter 1: From Pliinki to Uskvil (Gray Ghosts Leader)

subject: Pliinki
fact: Pliinki is a deranged Duergar alchemist and cultist who orchestrated the theft of the Red Dragon Egg and the acquisition of the Obelisk of Diirinka. She believes the egg will hatch into a two-headed wyrm to serve Demogorgon and that the Obelisk will be the instrument of Gracklstugh’s conquest and sacrificial offering to the Prince of Demons.

subject: The Ember Vanguard
fact: The group adopted the name 'The Ember Vanguard' as their faction name.
source_quote: I have it - The Ember Vanguard.

subject: The Orc
fact: The Orc is grateful, but he looks unhappy as he is covered in the acid slime of the Trapper.
source_quote: But the Orc is grateful, but he looks unhappy as he is covered in the acid slime of the Trapper.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin is a well-meaning but tactless companion who found a giant dragon baby rattle made by Clan Thrazgad. He inadvertently offends Zalthir by expressing desire for a 'pure dragon,' but later proposes the name 'The Ember Vanguard' for their group, which unites them despite its awkwardness.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin is the charismatic and determined leader of The Ember Vanguard who imposed the faction's name against hesitation, believes in the power of mythic identity, and leads the group with conviction despite mockery.
source_quote: We need a name! Like the First Faction was the legendary heroes that saved the North!

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin is the feared mage of the Ember Vanguard!
source_quote: He is the feared mage of the Ember Vanguard!

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin leads the group west instead of south, where the Empty Scabbard Killers live, after passing through the doors.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin leads them west, instead of south, where the Empty Scabbard Killers live.
source_quote: Once past the doors, Thorin leads them west, instead of south, where the Empty Scabbard Killers live.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin shouts, 'Yes, we’re all fine.'
source_quote: Thorin shouts, “Yes, we’re all fine.”

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin, unaware of the weight of his words, remains fixated on the idea of owning a dragon, revealing a childlike innocence that contrasts sharply with the dark machinations surrounding the egg and the city’s fate.
source_quote: We should get a baby dragon. I would like to have a dragon. It would be so cool if we had a dragon.

subject: Uskvil
fact: Uskvil is the leader of the Gray Ghosts, a thieves’ guild turned covert operative for the cult. He procured the Thrazgad ore for the Obelisk and oversaw the retrieval of the dragon egg, all while keeping the Deepking and Keepers of the Flame in ignorance of the true purpose behind their actions.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir and Thorin attack the creature, trying to get it to release Grygum.
source_quote: He watches as Zalthir and Thorin attack the creature, trying to get it to release Grygum.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir attacks the manta ray creature alongside Thorin, strikes it a few more times with his fist, and witnesses its death.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir is a dragonborn who discovered the journal of Pliinki, the letters between cult leaders, and the Obelisk's connection to the dragon egg and Demogorgon. He initially considered condemning the Derro and Duergar to genocidal war but now seeks to minimize chaos and escape Gracklstugh discreetly.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir is a member of The Ember Vanguard who initially advocated for discretion, later accepted the faction’s identity, and now operates under its banner — though he remains wary of the dangers they face, including the Empty Scabbard Killers.
source_quote: The Empty Scabbard Killers might want to kill us.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir is a monk who dispelled magical darkness, sensed supernatural presence, and retrieved the statue of Demogorgon from an alcove in the northeast corner of the mesa.
source_quote: Zalthir tenses. 'The ghost,' he thinks. ... Zalthir jumps off the mesa and heads to an alcove in the northeast corner. There, he picks up the statue of Demogorgon.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir knew he had enough to condemn the Derro and Duergar to a genocidal war that would result in the utter destruction of the city of Gracklstugh.
source_quote: Zalthir knows he has enough to condemn the Derro and Duergar to a genocidal war that will result in the utter destruction of the city of Gracklstugh.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir mutters, 'I vote we get out of here as discreetly as possible, creating the least amount of chaos as possible.'
source_quote: Zalthir mutters, “I vote we get out of here as discreetly as possible, creating the least amount of chaos as possible.”

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir recognizes the voice of Eldeth and sighs as he dispels the darkness.
source_quote: Zalthir recognizes the voice; it’s Eldeth. Zalthir sighs and dispels the darkness.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir strikes the creature a few more times with his fist, and the beast dies before Grygum can take advantage of the spell.
source_quote: Zalthir strikes the creature a few more times with his fist, and the beast dies before Grygum can take advantage of the spell.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir thought, 'Leemooggoogoon, Demogorgon, two-headed baby dragons - …'
source_quote: “Leemooggoogoon, Demogorgon, two-headed baby dragons - …” he thinks to himself.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir, a dragonborn, is deeply unsettled by Thorin’s innocent words and Grygum’s condemnation of the egg, as his own identity is implicitly called into question by the moral and metaphysical framing of purity and abomination.
source_quote: Zalthir stares at him, confused, 'What?'

subject: baby dragon rattle
fact: A giant baby rattle made by Clan Thrazgad is found, inscribed with 'made by clan Thrazgad'.
source_quote: It says made by clan Thrazgad.

subject: baby dragon rattle
fact: A giant rattle, marked 'made by clan Thrazgad,' was found by Thorin and is physically identical to the ore used in the Obelisk's failed repair, suggesting a deeper, possibly magical connection between the Thrazgad Clan, the egg, and draconic manipulation.
source_quote: It says made by clan Thrazgad.

subject: baby dragon rattle
fact: Thorin finds a giant baby rattle made by Clan Thrazgad.
source_quote: It says made by clan Thrazgad.

subject: dancing lights effect
fact: Daz's use of dancing lights intimidated the derro guard, enabling passage.
source_quote: Daz is very pleased with his use of dancing lights and the effect it had on the Derro.

subject: deadly chimes of the spell that tolls the dead
fact: Daz follows up with the deadly chimes of the spell that tolls the dead, which contributes to the Trapper's death.

subject: deadly chimes of the spell toll the dead
fact: Daz follows up with the deadly chimes of the spell toll the dead.
source_quote: So he casts silvery barbs to help Grygum escape, and then Daz follows up with the deadly chimes of the spell toll the dead.

subject: dragon egg value
fact: The dragon egg is a vessel for Demogorgon's greatest creation, a two-headed wyrmling destined to serve as his mount.
source_quote: The Red Dragon Egg! What a marvel! ... This is no mere insurance policy; it is the vessel for my greatest creation, a gift worthy of Demogorgon himself.

subject: journal by Pliinki
fact: Zalthir finds a journal by Pliinki detailing her macabre experiments and fervent beliefs.
source_quote: He finds a journal by Pliinki.

subject: Journal of Pliinki
fact: The Journal of Pliinki details her experiments on the Red Dragon Egg, her attempts to empower the Obelisk of Diirinka, and her fanatical devotion to Demogorgon’s ascension.
source_quote: Pliinki's Journal ... Here are some journal entries from the perspective of Pliinki, detailing her macabre experiments and fervent beliefs.

subject: Letter 1: From Pliinki to Uskvil
fact: Pliinki informs Uskvil that the Gray Ghosts delivered the egg as planned, and the Thrazgad ore remains 'discarded and forgotten' next to her workbenches.
source_quote: The Obelisk... It refuses to accept the material so far, stubbornly sitting "discarded and forgotten" next to my workbenches.

subject: Letter 2: From Aliinka to Pliinki
fact: Aliinka confirms the successful retrieval of the dragon egg and Thrazgad ore, and notes that the city spirals precisely as planned.
source_quote: Uskvil confirmed the successful retrieval of both the dragon egg and the Clan Thrazgad ore, as ordered. The city spirals precisely as we planned...

subject: Letter 3: From Pliinki to Uskvil
fact: Pliinki expresses frustration that the Thrazgad ore has proven useless in mending the Obelisk’s fractures.
source_quote: That acid-resistant ore from the Thrazgad Clan... has proven useless in mending its cracks. It still sits "discarded and forgotten" next to my workbenches.

subject: Letter 4: From Narrak to Pliinki
fact: Narrak writes that the Obelisk, once repaired, will be the instrument of ascension to conquer Gracklstugh and deliver it as a sacrificial gift to Demogorgon.
source_quote: This ancient monolith, once repaired, will be the instrument of our ascension, allowing us to conquer Gracklstugh and deliver it as a sacrificial gift to Demogorgon.

subject: Letter from Pliinki to Uskvil
fact: The letter from Pliinki to Uskvil, leader of the Gray Ghosts, confirms the successful delivery of the egg, the failure of Thrazgad ore to mend the Obelisk, and the ongoing destabilization of Gracklstugh for Demogorgon’s coming reign.
source_quote: Letter 1: From Pliinki to Uskvil (Gray Ghosts Leader)

subject: letter source
fact: Four letters from Pliinki, Aliinka, and Narrak to Uskvil and others detail the conspiracy to destabilize Gracklstugh.
source_quote: He also finds some letters

subject: obelisk energy
fact: The Obelisk's black metal hums with quasi-magical energy, a power just waiting to be unleashed.
source_quote: Its black metal hums with quasi-magical energy, a power just waiting to be unleashed.

subject: Obelisk of Diirinka
fact: The Obelisk of Diirinka is a black-metal artifact humming with quasi-magical energy, hidden in the mesa and sought by Pliinki to be used as an instrument of conquest and sacrifice to Demogorgon.
source_quote: The Obelisk. Such a magnificent, fractured thing! ... Its black metal hums with quasi-magical energy ... It will be the instrument of our ascension.

subject: Pliinki's Journal
fact: Pliinki’s journal details her macabre experiments with the Obelisk and the dragon egg, her belief in Demogorgon’s coming, and her plan to use Gracklstugh’s destruction as a sacrifice. It reveals her conviction that true freedom lies in serving the Prince of Demons — a direct counterpoint to Bahamut’s teachings.

subject: Pliinki's Journal, Day 17 – The Stone of Diirinka
fact: Pliinki writes that the Obelisk's black metal hums with quasi-magical energy, and Thrazgad ore sits 'discarded and forgotten' next to her workbenches.
source_quote: Its black metal hums with quasi-magical energy... It merely sits "discarded and forgotten" next to my workbenches.

subject: Pliinki's Journal, Day 25 – The Prince's Gift Arrives
fact: Pliinki writes that the Red Dragon Egg is no mere replacement, but the vessel for her greatest creation, a gift worthy of Demogorgon.
source_quote: The Red Dragon Egg! What a marvel!... This is no mere insurance policy; it is the vessel for my greatest creation, a gift worthy of Demogorgon himself.

subject: Pliinki's Journal, Day 38 – Mutagenic Progress!
fact: Pliinki notes that the egg pulses with new life, and she surrounds it with hair, scales, fungi, and precious viscera to create a two-headed wyrmling for Demogorgon.
source_quote: The egg pulses with new life... hair, scales, fungi from the tunnels, and... other, more precious viscera. My goal is clear, a two-headed wyrmling, a perfect "Prince's gift" for Demogorgon, to serve as his mount.

subject: Pliinki's Journal, Day 47 – The Obelisk Responds
fact: Pliinki writes that the Obelisk hungers for more power and will be the instrument of ascension to conquer Gracklstugh and deliver it as a sacrificial gift to Demogorgon.
source_quote: It hungers for more power, more chaos! This monolith will be the instrument of our ascension, allowing us to conquer Gracklstugh and deliver it as a sacrificial gift to Demogorgon.

subject: Pliinki's Journal, Day 54 – Anticipation and Destiny
fact: Pliinki writes that the egg’s dual-headed presence is forming, and the Obelisk will herald the Prince’s arrival and the 'genocidal war' to cleanse the city.
source_quote: The egg is nearing its time!... The Obelisk, too, senses the coming shift. Its purpose... is to herald the Prince's arrival and the "genocidal war" that will cleanse this city.

subject: Red Dragon Egg
fact: The Red Dragon Egg is a magical artifact that has been mutated by Pliinki's experiments to become a two-headed wyrmling intended as a mount for Demogorgon, disguised by the Keepers as a mere 'replacement'.
source_quote: The Red Dragon Egg! What a marvel! ... The egg pulses with new life ... a two-headed wyrmling, a perfect 'Prince's gift' for Demogorgon.

subject: Scrap of Paper
fact: A piece of paper used by Grygum to record all faction deals and strategies, later referenced to justify the plan to manipulate Gartokkar and the Stone Guards — a physical artifact of the group’s cunning.
source_quote: Grygum pulls out a scrap of paper, 'I’ve been taking notes…'

subject: silver candlestick value
fact: The silver candlesticks flanking the Lolth altar are worth 25 gp each.
source_quote: So he casts silvery barbs to help Grygum escape, and then Daz follows up with the deadly chimes of the spell toll the dead.

subject: silvery barbs
fact: Daz casts silvery barbs as a spell to help Grygum escape from the Trapper.

subject: silvery barbs
fact: Daz casts silvery barbs to help Grygum escape.
source_quote: So he casts silvery barbs to help Grygum escape, and then Daz follows up with the deadly chimes of the spell toll the dead.

subject: Statue of Demogorgon
fact: The statue of Demogorgon is a physical representation of the Prince of Demons, retrieved by Zalthir from an alcove in the northeast corner of the mesa, signaling the culmination of Pliinki’s ritual design.
source_quote: Zalthir jumps off the mesa and heads to an alcove in the northeast corner. There, he picks up the statue of Demogorgon.

subject: statue of Demogorgon
fact: Zalthir picks up the statue of Demogorgon.
source_quote: there, he picks up the statue of Demogorgon.

subject: The Dragon Baby Rattle
fact: The dragon baby rattle, made by Clan Thrazgad, was found by Thorin. Its presence in the mesa suggests the Derro were aware of the egg’s significance and possibly involved in its protection or manipulation. The rattle’s design and location imply a ritualistic or symbolic connection to the egg’s transformation.

subject: The Obelisk of Diirinka
fact: The Obelisk of Diirinka is an ancient black metal monolith hidden in the mesa, humming with quasi-magical energy. Pliinki and the cult believe it can be repaired to channel chaos and conquer Gracklstugh, but the Thrazgad ore meant to mend it remains discarded and ineffective. It is the key to their ritual to summon Demogorgon’s power.

subject: The Red Dragon Egg
fact: The Red Dragon Egg, stolen by the Gray Ghosts, has been corrupted by Pliinki’s mutagenic experiments. It now pulses with demonic energy and is destined to hatch into a two-headed wyrm serving Demogorgon. Grygum believes it must be returned to Gartokkar so that Themberchaud may claim vengeance — not destroyed, but unleashed.

subject: thrazgad ore
fact: The Thrazgad ore has been discarded and forgotten next to the workbenches, resisting all attempts to mend the Obelisk’s fractures.
source_quote: It merely sits "discarded and forgotten" next to my workbenches.

subject: Bahamut’s silence
fact: Grygum recalls that Bahamut’s clerics never gave him a straight answer — suggesting that divine will in this matter is not to be commanded, but discerned through action, and that the true test lies not in destroying evil, but in choosing freedom over control.
source_quote: Bahamut’s clerics never gave him a straight answer.

subject: Drow-Duergar Alliance Rumor
fact: A growing belief among Derro that The Ember Vanguard represents a secret alliance between Drow of Menzoberranzan and Duergar forces — a threat that could destabilize the entire Underdark hierarchy.
source_quote: The Ember Vanguard — the Drow are now working with the Duergar to subdue us!

subject: Grygum's location
fact: Grygum is trapped in the cavern, but the exact location of his entrapment is not specified in this session.
source_quote: Grygum enveloped by a creature that looks like a manta ray.

subject: Identity of the Ghost
fact: Pelek’s occupation of a body and declaration as 'the ghost' introduces supernatural ambiguity — whether this is possession, a spirit, or a magical phenomenon tied to the Obelisk’s energy.
source_quote: 'Oh, yes, I am Pelek. I seem to have occupied this body.' ... 'The ghost,' he thinks.

subject: Missing Egg
fact: The Red Dragon Egg was reported missing by Grygum, though Daz later claimed possession — creating uncertainty about its true location and whether it has already hatched or been concealed.
source_quote: Grygum shouts, 'Where is the egg?' ... Then Daz shouts back, 'I have it.'

subject: Pliinki’s Fate
fact: The disappearance or death of Pliinki, a Derro who promised Diirdeklin liberation from Duergar bondage, now interpreted as evidence of a larger Drow operation — a mystery that fuels Derro paranoia.
source_quote: And if they killed Pliinki, that means that they have bigger plans.

subject: the fate of the egg
fact: Grygum has declared the egg must be returned to Gartokkar to trigger Themberchaud’s vengeance upon its captors — a move that may fulfill prophecy, unleash destruction, or break the cycle of control — but its outcome remains unknown and dangerously volatile.
source_quote: When this abomination hatches, the dragon Themberchaud will have its revenge on those who would think to control it.

subject: The Fate of the Egg
fact: The egg’s true nature — no longer a dragon but a demonic vessel — creates a moral thread unresolved. Grygum believes returning it to Gartokkar allows divine retribution; Zalthir fears unleashing it will doom the city; Daz and Thorin are indifferent. The group has chosen action over consensus, but the egg’s hatching may yet determine Gracklstugh’s fate.

subject: The Identity of the Ember Vanguard
fact: The name 'The Ember Vanguard' was chosen by Thorin as a symbol of rebirth from ashes. But its adoption by a group that now impersonates Drow assassins creates a thread of irony: are they becoming the monsters they sought to stop? The name may haunt them as much as the egg.

subject: elapsed time
fact: An hour passes between two events in the session.
source_quote: An hour later

subject: session date
fact: The events described occur during a single, continuous journey through the subterranean tunnels of Gracklstugh, beginning with the aftermath of a battle and ending at a cavern of ritual madness.
source_quote: And so we continue on our journey through the caves...

subject: session date
fact: The session occurs on the 5th day of the 2nd Tenday of Taraskh 1493 DR.
source_quote: On the 5th day of the 2nd Tenday of Taraskh 1493

subject: session date
fact: This event occurs during the session following the party’s descent into the lower tunnels of Gracklstugh, after the defeat of previous threats and before confronting larger factions. The timeline is marked by escalating tension and the revelation of hidden loyalties.
source_quote: Now let’s take a look at her more closely...

subject: session date
fact: This sequence occurs during the party’s continued journey through the Underdark, following the collapse of the Ashwood Council and the flight from surface civilization.
source_quote: And so we continue on our journey through the caves...

subject: the day the Ember Vanguard entered the ritual cavern
fact: On this day, the Ember Vanguard entered a cavern filled with Trillimac books, ritual circles, and Derro conducting experiments for Demogorgon, and killed Skiit, intimidated Ulnara, and narrowly avoided a patrol.
source_quote: I walk in quietly. We don’t need light, because we can all see in the dark... I finally spot the inhabitants, some Derro and Death dogs... Narrak... shouts - 'We are conducting experiments!'

subject: Daz
fact: Daz casts Maximillian’s Earthen Grasp to crush the Derro Skiit, who is beginning to wake up.
source_quote: I cast Maximillian’s Earthen Grasp and start to crush the poor unfortunate creature.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz casts Toll the Dead, and the Derro Skiit’s heart stops and he dies.
source_quote: So I cast Toll the Dead, and the deadly chimes echo throughout the caves, but only it’s intended target hears them, and his heart stops, and he dies.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz enters a cavern with a hellish red glow, spiral patterns on the walls, and a glowing ritual circle on a platform.
source_quote: The cavern floor rises to form a natural 5-foot-high platform. A glowing ritual circle dominates the top of the platform.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz finds books titled “The Spiraling Descent: A Treatise on Duality and Madness,” “The Prince's Gift: On the Creation of Favored Spawn,” and “Rituals of the Two-Headed Beast,” confirming Demogorgon’s influence.
source_quote: I look carefully and notice a few of the titles - “The Spiraling Descent: A Treatise on Duality and Madness,” and “The Prince's Gift: On the Creation of Favored Spawn”, and “Rituals of the Two-Headed Beast.”

subject: Daz
fact: Daz notes that the Derro are conducting experiments and chanting in unison under Narrak’s direction.
source_quote: They chant back at him - “For what purpose!”

subject: Daz
fact: Daz notices a Derro standing over a pit with an unbelievable smell emanating from it.
source_quote: I see a single Derro standing over a pit, with an unbelievable smell emanating from it.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz notices the Derro is wearing an amulet of Demogorgon.
source_quote: Wait, that’s interesting, he’s got an amulet of Demogorgon.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz observes that the Derro are terrified of Drow and react with subservience when confronted by their presence.
source_quote: Ulnara looks at me, and she realizes that I am Drow. And that the Drow do not mess around.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz observes the Derro muttering to himself and recalls that such muttering is a common trait among the irrevocably insane of the Derro.
source_quote: Now that’s interesting, he seems to be muttering to himself. Bah, it’s a common trait among the irrevocably insane of the Derro.

subject: Daz kills Skiit with Toll the Dead
fact: Daz casts Toll the Dead, whose chimes are heard only by the target, causing Skiit’s heart to stop and killing him instantly, despite prior escape attempts.
source_quote: So I cast Toll the Dead, and the deadly chimes echo throughout the caves, but only it’s intended target hears them, and his heart stops, and he dies.

subject: Derro Attack After Bahamut Invocation
fact: Grygum’s declaration of faith in Bahamut triggered an immediate, violent attack from the Derro, who perceive it as blasphemy against their two-headed deity. The party was forced into combat despite attempts at diplomacy.
source_quote: The moment that Grygum mentioned 'Bahamut,' I knew we were in for it. These Derro... don't take kindly to anything outside their two-headed deity. And sure enough, they immediately attack.

subject: derro madness observation
fact: Zalthir observes the Derro’s madness and acts without speaking, knowing their nature.
source_quote: I observe everything and say nothing. My mind is clear. I act without speaking. I do because I know.

subject: derro patrol encounter
fact: A Derro patrol stumbles upon the Ember Vanguard and immediately attacks upon hearing the name 'Bahamut.'
source_quote: The moment that Grygum mentioned 'Bahamut,' I knew we were in for it. And sure enough, they immediately attack.

subject: Derro Patrol Encounter
fact: The party was ambushed by a Derro patrol after successfully bypassing their lair. Daz’s confidence in their stealth was proven correct as the Derro reacted with fear and derangement rather than aggression.
source_quote: And so we continue on our journey through the caves, when a Derro patrol stumbles on us. Daz insists we march as if we own this place. And it works. The creatures are fearful and somewhat deranged.

subject: Discovery of Demogorgon Ritual Evidence
fact: Daz uncovered a ritual chamber filled with texts and papers implicating Demogorgon in the Derro’s corruption. The evidence is sufficient to convince Errde Blackstaff, though Daz considers withholding it to prevent manipulation.
source_quote: Errde Blackstaff wants evidence of Demogorgon’s influence, and here it is. And amongst the books are various papers.

subject: Divine Scrutiny
fact: A term Grygum invents to avoid answering direct questions about his allegiance. It is a theatrical facade masking his uncertainty and hypocrisy, used to confuse and delay adversaries with pseudo-theological verbosity.
source_quote: ‘It is, in fact, a Divine Scrutiny, a profound act of investigation into the very threads of our intertwined fates...’

subject: divine scrutiny
fact: Grygum invokes a Divine Scrutiny, a profound act of investigation into the threads of intertwined fates in Gracklstugh.
source_quote: a Divine Scrutiny, a profound act of investigation into the very threads of our intertwined fates, here in this churning city of Gracklstugh

subject: emerald vanguard naming
fact: Grygum declares the group the 'Ember Guard,' later corrected to 'Ember Vanguard.'
source_quote: We are the Ember Guard," shouts Grygum. I smile. I like that name.

subject: experimental ritual
fact: An experimental ritual is being conducted by Narrak and his apprentices in service of Demogorgon’s will.
source_quote: We are conducting experiments!

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum claims the question of allegiance is a Divine Scrutiny requiring consideration of Aspects of the Truth and Divine Ledgers.
source_quote: That is a question that requires more than a simple answer. It is, in fact, a Divine Scrutiny, a profound act of investigation into the very threads of our intertwined fates, here in this churning city of Gracklstugh.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum pretends to be a preacher and responds to Ulnara with his preacher’s voice to maintain control.
source_quote: “We shall, certainly,” says Grygum in his preacher’s voice.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum pushes the Derro over the cliff while Daz unleashes a light show.
source_quote: I push him over the cliff. At the same time, Daz unleashes a light show.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum shouts, 'May the power of the platinum dragon cure us all!' as a theatrical act of divine magic.
source_quote: “May the power of the platinum dragon cure us all!” I shout.

subject: Grygum pushes Skiit into the pit
fact: Grygum pushes Skiit over the cliff at the same time Daz unleashes a light show, triggering a chain of events that leads to Skiit's resurrection and eventual death by Toll the Dead.
source_quote: I push him over the cliff. At the same time, Daz unleashes a light show.

subject: Narrak
fact: Narrak shouts, 'We are conducting experiments! For the elevation of the Derro, the Triumph of Demogorgon, and the destruction of the Duergar!'
source_quote: He shouts - “We are conducting experiments!” They chant back at him - “For what purpose!” He screams - “The only purpose that matters! The elevation of the Derro, the Triumph of Demogorgon, and the destruction of the Duergar!”

subject: Narrak conducts ritual experiments
fact: Narrak leads Derro apprentices in ritual experiments under the red glow of the cavern, chanting to elevate the Derro, triumph Demogorgon, and destroy the Duergar, surrounded by forbidden texts.
source_quote: We are conducting experiments! For what purpose! The only purpose that matters! The elevation of the Derro, the Triumph of Demogorgon, and the destruction of the Duergar!

subject: narrak's experiment
fact: Narrak, a Derro with warped intellect, leads experiments for the elevation of the Derro and the triumph of Demogorgon.
source_quote: We are conducting experiments! ... The elevation of the Derro, the Triumph of Demogorgon, and the destruction of the Duergar!

subject: pit trap discovery
fact: A poorly disguised pit trap is discovered upon entering the hellish cavern.
source_quote: I look down at what he is pointing at, and it’s a poorly disguised pit trap.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin declares 'East' when asked whether to go left or right, ending the discussion.
source_quote: I say - “East.”

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin dismisses two mad Derro as having no value and chooses not to fight them.
source_quote: I squint at the tents and the room and say, “No. There is nothing of value here.”

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin kills a Derro with his longsword and declares, 'This is how the Bahamut walks!'
source_quote: I brought my longsword down hard on the Derro, attacking Grygum. The sword cut through his flimsy armor and into his chest, and it dropped like a sack of rocks. Dead. "This is how the Bahamut walks!" I declared, standing over his fallen form, ready to take on the next fool who dared challenge us.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin observes that the Derro are Dwarves corrupted by mindflayers, barely Dwarves anymore, and not creatures to reason with.
source_quote: The Derro themselves were predictably clumsy. One swung at me, but my armor held. The other landed a hit on Grygum, but our allies were quick to retaliate, dealing a good chunk of damage to him. Zalthir, bless his arcane heart, summoned his darkness, enveloping a couple of them. Then, in a burst of brilliant speed, he critically struck one of the Darrow. Impressive. Daz, always quick with a spell, launched his magic missiles. A flurry of arcane energy streaked across the tunnel, and the Derro had struck, already reeling, and fell. One down. Good. The remaining Derro, true to their limited intellect, continued their mindless attacks. One swung wildly at Zalthir, missing entirely. Another charged Grygum, screaming some incoherent babble about their master. My armor held, and I parried his pathetic attack. "One head is better than two!" I roared, pushing him back. My chance came again, and I didn't hesitate. I brought my longsword down hard on the Derro, attacking Grygum. The sword cut through his flimsy armor and into his chest, and it dropped like a sack of rocks. Dead. "This is how the Bahamut walks!" I declared, standing over his fallen form, ready to take on the next fool who dared challenge us. But they were all dead.

subject: Thorin declares 'East' at the fork
fact: Thorin, exhausted by debate, arbitrarily declares 'East' as the path forward, leading the group toward a chamber filled with cages, Derro muttering about the prince’s hunger and dark lake scales.
source_quote: Left or right?' I ask. The discussion begins, and I am too tired for this, so I say - 'East.'

subject: toll the dead casting
fact: Daz casts Toll the Dead, its chimes echoing only for the intended target, killing the Derro instantly.
source_quote: I cast Toll the Dead, and the deadly chimes echo throughout the caves, but only it’s intended target hears them, and his heart stops, and he dies.

subject: travel to Sloobludop
fact: Sloobludop is approximately eight days away via the Darklake.
source_quote: the town of Sloopdopblop is just eight days away

subject: zombie creation
fact: Ulnara promises to turn Skiit into a zombie to serve the cult of Demogorgon forever.
source_quote: after he’s dead I will turn him into a zombie and he will serve the cult of Demogorgon forever!

subject: Cult of Demogorgon
fact: A dangerous and chaotic cult that has infiltrated derro society, promising power and restoration to the broken. Skiit and Ulnara are true believers, interpreting Demogorgon’s influence as divine mandate. Their devotion warps their perception of reality and loyalty.
source_quote: I am a follower of Demogorgon! Pliinki has said that anybody who follows Demogorgon is making the Derro proud and powerful.

subject: Cult of Demogorgon
fact: A pervasive, decentralized cult among the Derro that worships the Two-Headed Demon Lord as the source of their twisted power and supposed redemption. It is used to justify atrocities, control lower Derro, and oppose the Duergar. Its influence is evident in rituals, tomes, and the delusions of its followers.
source_quote: ‘The only purpose that matters! The elevation of the Derro, the Triumph of Demogorgon, and the destruction of the Duergar!’

subject: Derro
fact: The Derro are a collective faction devoted to the elevation of their kind and the triumph of Demogorgon, with a genocidal intent toward the Duergar.
source_quote: The elevation of the Derro, the Triumph of Demogorgon, and the destruction of the Duergar!

subject: Derro
fact: The Derro are a race of mad, twisted dwarves once enslaved and mentally corrupted by mind flayers. They are obsessed with Demogorgon, prone to delusions of grandeur, and incapable of rational diplomacy. Their society is fragmented, chaotic, and dominated by cultish fervor.
source_quote: They are Dwarves that were slaves of the mindflayers, who corrupted their fundamental nature until they are barely Dwarves. They are mad.

subject: Derro
fact: The Derro are a subterranean race of twisted, insane dwarves once enslaved by mind flayers. Their minds were shattered, leaving them paranoid, superstitious, and obsessed with false gods like Demogorgon. They serve as necromancers and laborers in the pits of Gracklstugh, perpetuating their broken culture.
source_quote: I recall the stories of the Derro, creatures that served the mind flayers and had their minds destroyed.

subject: Derro
fact: The Derro are former slaves of the mind flayers, whose minds were destroyed and replaced with fanatical devotion to Demogorgon, making them mad, paranoid, and incapable of rational discourse with outsiders.
source_quote: The Derro are Dwarves that were slaves of the mindflayers, who corrupted their fundamental nature until they are barely Dwarves. They are mad. These are not creatures to reason with.

subject: Duergar
fact: The Duergar are a subterranean dwarven race hostile to the Derro, often seen as oppressors or rivals. The Derro cultists blame them for their suffering and vow destruction, though the Duergar themselves are not present in this scene.
source_quote: ‘I don’t believe you guys work for us. I think you work for the Duergar or the Mindflayers!’

subject: Duergar
fact: The Duergar are a targeted faction of the Derro, subject to their genocidal campaign in service of Demogorgon’s triumph.
source_quote: The elevation of the Derro, the Triumph of Demogorgon, and the destruction of the Duergar!

subject: Ember Vanguard
fact: The Ember Vanguard is a disciplined group of explorers and spellcasters who operate with stealth and tactical precision. They enter dangerous caverns without light, isolate themselves from non-combatants, and prioritize evidence collection over direct confrontation.
source_quote: The Ember Vanguard will march in, but we tell our companions to wait outside.

subject: Ember Vanguard
fact: The Ember Vanguard is a group that claims authority over the caverns, uses intimidating titles, and manipulates Derro through fear and psychological dominance, though their true allegiance is ambiguous.
source_quote: We are the Ember Guard," shouts Grygum. I smile. I like that name.

subject: Ember Vanguard
fact: The Ember Vanguard is a name invented by Grygum to intimidate and unify the party’s identity. It is not a real organization but a performative label used to project authority over derro and cultists. Ulnara adopts it to appease the Drow, believing it to be a powerful faction.
source_quote: We are the Ember Guard," shouts Grygum. I smile. I like that name.

subject: Ember Vanguard
fact: The Ember Vanguard is a self-proclaimed group that Grygum and Daz adopt as a cover identity to intimidate derro and other cave-dwellers. It is a fabricated title with no formal structure, used strategically to project authority and exploit fear of the unknown.
source_quote: ‘We are the Ember Guard,’ shouts Grygum. I smile. I like that name.

subject: cage chamber
fact: Cages assembled from scrap iron line both sides of a chamber, with a spiral path marked by stone pylons.
source_quote: cages assembled from scrap iron on both sides of the chamber. A spiral path circles into the center of the room, marked off by small stone pylons.

subject: cave entrance with brimstone stench
fact: A cave entrance emits a stench of brimstone and chemicals, distinct from the usual Derro decay.
source_quote: the unspeakable stench that seems to follow the Derro emanates here. This time it is the smell of brimstone and chemicals.

subject: cave entrance with fungi and offal
fact: A cavern entrance features mounds of fungi and offal flanking a narrow tunnel.
source_quote: a crack in the southeast wall of the pit leads to a narrow tunnel, flanked by mounds of fungi and offal.

subject: Derro Chamber with Scrap-Iron Cages
fact: This cavern is filled with scrap-iron cages, spiral stone pylons, and bubbling cauldrons emitting a foul odor. It is the lair of deranged Derro who worship a two-headed deity and perform forbidden rituals. The air is thick with the stench of decay and magical corruption.
source_quote: The smell is coming from cages assembled from scrap iron on both sides of the chamber. A spiral path circles into the center of the room, marked off by small stone pylons.

subject: Gracklstugh
fact: A churning, subterranean city of madness and decay, where derro, duergar, and mind flayers clash in secret wars. The pit of Ulnara is one of many necromantic operations hidden in its tunnels, sustained by fear, faith, and the lingering influence of ancient enslavement.
source_quote: Here in this churning city of Gracklstugh.

subject: gracklstugh
fact: Gracklstugh is the churning city where Divine Scrutiny and tangled fates occur.
source_quote: here in this churning city of Gracklstugh

subject: pit of Ulnara
fact: The pit of Ulnara contains body parts and zombies, fed by the Derro for the great project.
source_quote: tossing body parts over the ledge into the pit

subject: ritual cavern
fact: The ritual cavern is lit by hellish red glow, with spiral patterns on walls, silent dripping water, and rampantly growing fungi; it contains books titled 'The Spiraling Descent: A Treatise on Duality and Madness,' 'The Prince's Gift: On the Creation of Favored Spawn,' and 'Rituals of the Two-Headed Beast.'
source_quote: The cavern floor rises to form a natural 5-foot-high platform. A glowing ritual circle dominates the top of the platform. Around the platform are books made from Trillimac... 'The Spiraling Descent: A Treatise on Duality and Madness,' and 'The Prince's Gift: On the Creation of Favored Spawn', and 'Rituals of the Two-Headed Beast.'

subject: Ritual Cavern of the Two-Headed Beast
fact: A vast subterranean cavern lit by hellish red glow, with spiraling wall patterns, silent dripping water, and rampant fungal growth. At its center lies a glowing ritual circle, surrounded by forbidden tomes on duality, madness, and spawn creation, indicating deep Demogorgon influence.
source_quote: The cavern floor rises to form a natural 5-foot-high platform. A glowing ritual circle dominates the top of the platform. Around the platform are books made from Trillimac.

subject: ritual platform
fact: A glowing ritual circle dominates a 5-foot-high natural platform in the cavern.
source_quote: The cavern floor rises to form a natural 5-foot-high platform. A glowing ritual circle dominates the top of the platform.

subject: the chamber of experiments
fact: The chamber is a deeply unsettling space where Narrak and his apprentices conduct experiments under the influence of Demogorgon.
source_quote: His presence in this space is deeply unsettling, a chilling testament to the insidious influence of the demon lord he serves.

subject: The Pit of Ulnara
fact: A vast, stinking chasm in the southeast wall of the tunnel, filled with decomposing flesh, offal, fungi, and shambling zombies. It is the heart of the Derro necromantic project, fed by body parts tossed over the edge. The faerzress glows around it like fog, concealing the true horror within.
source_quote: The glow of faerzress is everywhere, seeming to flow like fog around dark shapes shambling across the pit.

subject: tunnel turn
fact: The tunnel turn leads to the pit where the Derro stands over body parts.
source_quote: I follow Grygum and Thorin around the turn of the tunnel and see a single Derro standing over a pit

subject: Velkynvelve elevation
fact: Velkynvelve sits 100 feet above the cavern floor.
source_quote: Drow outpost was 100' in the sky

subject: chasme count
fact: Four chasme demons are present in the cavern above the prisoners' tower.
source_quote: four chasme and two vrock

subject: Death Dogs
fact: Canine undead creatures that patrol the cavern with Narrak’s ritual circle. They are likely bred or raised by the Derro cultists as guardians and are attuned to the foul energies of the space.
source_quote: The cavern floor rises... and I finally spot the inhabitants, some Derro and Death dogs.

subject: Death dogs
fact: Death dogs are predatory, supernatural canines that accompany Derro in their subterranean lairs. They are silent, stealthy, and blend into the hellish red glow of the caverns, remaining unnoticed until provoked.
source_quote: I finally spot the inhabitants, some Derro and Death dogs. They don’t notice us, so we continue.

subject: Death dogs
fact: Death dogs are present in the ritual cavern alongside Derro, silently observing the rituals without initiating conflict until provoked.
source_quote: And I finally spot the inhabitants, some Derro and Death dogs. They don’t notice us, so we continue.

subject: Demogorgon
fact: Demogorgon is a demon lord being served by Narrak and the Derro, whose influence drives their chaotic evil and genocidal agenda.
source_quote: The Triumph of Demogorgon

subject: derro count
fact: A single Derro stands over a pit with an unbelievable smell emanating from it.
source_quote: a single Derro standing over a pit, with an unbelievable smell emanating from it

subject: derro cultists
fact: Two Derro speak incoherently near a tent, one obsessed with the prince’s hunger, the other with the dark lake and obsidian scales.
source_quote: More of this, always more, the mastery demands... Water it chips, not like the dark lake. There, I pulled something from the dark ones, A scale smooth, this polished obsidian, but it shimmered like madness.

subject: derro named skiit
fact: Skiit, a Derro, is tossed into the pit by Grygum, later awakens, and seeks permission to kill Spiderbait.
source_quote: Skiit looks at me and then points at Spiderbait, 'Can I kill that one over there?'

subject: Derro patrol
fact: A Derro patrol stumbles upon the Ember Vanguard, immediately attacking upon hearing the name Bahamut, revealing their fanatical devotion to Demogorgon and hatred of outsider deities.
source_quote: The moment that Grygum mentioned 'Bahamut,' I knew we were in for it. These Derro... don't take kindly to anything outside their two-headed deity. And sure enough, they immediately attack.

subject: derro patrol members
fact: Multiple Derro, corrupted former dwarves of the mind flayers, attack the Ember Vanguard after hearing Bahamut’s name.
