source_quote: The Derro themselves were predictably clumsy... They are mad. These are not creatures to reason with.

subject: narrak
fact: Narrak, a Derro with frenetic, terrifying intellect, leads ritual experiments for Demogorgon’s triumph.
source_quote: Narrak. His pale, derro features are perpetually contorted, twisting into a grotesque mask of terrifying, spiraling madness.

subject: Ogre Zombie
fact: An Ogre Zombie emerges from a crack in the southeast wall of the pit, demanding to know who intrudes, and is confronted by the Ember Vanguard.
source_quote: From there, a voice and an Ogre Zombie emerge. 'What is the meaning of this? Who are you? Who do you think you are?'

subject: ogre zombie
fact: An Ogre Zombie emerges from a crack in the southeast wall of the pit.
source_quote: a voice and an Ogre Zombie emerge.

subject: Ogre Zombie
fact: An Ogre Zombie emerges from the pit, demanding answers from the party. It is part of Ulnara’s undead workforce, shambling among offal and fungi, and is likely a failed experiment or reanimated guard from the derro project.
source_quote: What is the meaning of this? Who are you? Who do you think you are?

subject: Ogre Zombie
fact: An undead brute that emerges from the pit, demanding answers. It is part of Ulnara’s undead army and exhibits the mindless aggression typical of reanimated giants, though its speech suggests lingering sentience or necromantic corruption.
source_quote: ‘What is the meaning of this? Who are you? Who do you think you are?’

subject: Zombies
fact: Numerous zombies fill the pit below Ulnara’s operation, constructed from body parts tossed over the ledge. They are the living result of the Derro’s necromantic project, animated and controlled by Ulnara for the cult of Demogorgon.
source_quote: I see a lot of zombies.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz is a Drow wizard and lethal pragmatist who uses precision magic to eliminate threats. He kills Skiit with Toll the Dead, crushes undead with Maximillian’s Earthen Grasp, and breaks Ulnara’s arrogance by revealing his race. He prefers direct action over rhetoric and is unimpressed by cultist posturing.
source_quote: I snap my fingers, trying to kill him, but the derro escapes. So I cast Toll the Dead...

subject: Daz
fact: Daz is a quick-witted spellcaster who specializes in magic missiles and tactical leadership. He commands the Ember Vanguard, insists on caution, and is the first to recognize ritualistic evidence of Demogorgon’s influence in the caves.
source_quote: Daz, always quick with a spell, launched his magic missiles. A flurry of arcane energy streaked across the tunnel, and the Derro had struck, already reeling, and fell.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz is a ruthless, calculating Drow spellcaster who operates with cold efficiency. He uses fear, lethal magic, and precise strikes to dominate derro and necromancers. He is pragmatic, distrustful of evidence, and sees through the delusions of others.
source_quote: ‘I snap my fingers... but the derro escapes.’ ‘Toll the Dead... his heart stops, and he dies.’

subject: Derro
fact: Derro are corrupted former dwarven slaves of mindflayers, now mad and devoted to a two-headed deity. They are physically weak, intellectually limited, and violently hostile to outsiders—especially those who invoke Bahamut. They inhabit caverns lined with scrap-iron cages and ritual cauldrons.
source_quote: The Derro themselves were predictably clumsy... They are mad. These are not creatures to reason with.

subject: Derro
fact: The Derro are described as slaves of the mindflayers, whose fundamental nature was corrupted until they are barely Dwarves and are mad.
source_quote: The Derro themselves were predictably clumsy. One swung at me, but my armor held. The other landed a hit on Grygum, but our allies were quick to retaliate, dealing a good chunk of damage to him. Zalthir, bless his arcane heart, summoned his darkness, enveloping a couple of them. Then, in a burst of brilliant speed, he critically struck one of the Darrow. Impressive. Daz, always quick with a spell, launched his magic missiles. A flurry of arcane energy streaked across the tunnel, and the Derro had struck, already reeling, and fell. One down. Good. The remaining Derro, true to their limited intellect, continued their mindless attacks. One swung wildly at Zalthir, missing entirely. Another charged Grygum, screaming some incoherent babble about their master. My armor held, and I parried his pathetic attack. "One head is better than two!" I roared, pushing him back. My chance came again, and I didn't hesitate. I brought my longsword down hard on the Derro, attacking Grygum. The sword cut through his flimsy armor and into his chest, and it dropped like a sack of rocks. Dead. "This is how the Bahamut walks!" I declared, standing over his fallen form, ready to take on the next fool who dared challenge us. But they were all dead.

subject: Derro
fact: The Derro believes he is a true believer of Demogorgon and that following Demogorgon makes the Derro proud and powerful.
source_quote: I am a follower of Demogorgon! Pliinki has said that anybody who follows Demogorgon is making the Derro proud and powerful. And we’re going to be great again!

subject: Derro
fact: The Derro has blue-gray skin, pale eyes lacking irises and pupils, and thin, stringy hair that is dull white and constantly greasy.
source_quote: He has blue, gray skin and pale eyes that lack both irises and pupils. He has thin, stringy hair, dull white, constantly looking greasy and unkempt.

subject: Derro
fact: The Derro revere a two-headed deity and are hostile to any outside religious claims, especially Bahamut.
source_quote: These Derro, bless their simple, deranged minds, don't take kindly to anything outside their two-headed deity.

subject: Derro
fact: Two Derro in the chamber speak incoherently, one about the prince’s hunger and the other about pulling a scale from the dark lake that shimmered like madness.
source_quote: More of this, always mor,e the mastery demands. Many contributions, the prince is hungry, always hungry,” says one. The other intones as it stares intently into the murky bubbling cauldron, tracing an invisible pattern with a dirty finger, “Water it chips, not like the dark lake. There, I pulled something from the dark ones, A scale smooth, this polished obsidian, but it shimmered like madness. In the dim light came from the deep, the deepest part with voices seeing.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum believes Bahamut is boring and Stroud was exciting.
source_quote: Bahamut is boring. Stroud was exciting. Bahamut, not so much.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum is a charismatic, preacher-like cleric who claims to worship Bahamut but uses theatricality and psychological manipulation to control derro. He is emotionally inconsistent, alternating between gentleness and cruelty, and often misjudges derro reactions due to his temple-bred naivete.
source_quote: ‘I worship Bahamut!’ ‘That is a question that requires more than a simple answer. It is, in fact, a Divine Scrutiny...’

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum is a cleric of Bahamut who uses theatrical divine rhetoric to mask his own uncertainty. He pushed Skiit into the pit, interrogated Ulnara about the project’s progress, and coined the name 'Ember Guard' to intimidate. His gentleness fails to control derro, but his bluster and actions create openings for Daz.
source_quote: That is a question that requires more than a simple answer. It is, in fact, a Divine Scrutiny...

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum is a cleric of Bahamut who uses theatricality and performative piety to manipulate others.
source_quote: “I worship Bahamut!”

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum is a preacher who proclaims, 'I worship Bahamut!' and is met with immediate hostility from Derro who revere Demogorgon as their sole deity.
source_quote: I worship Bahamut!

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum is a preacher who worships Bahamut and is prone to shouting philosophical declarations in dangerous situations. He is currently leading the party through Derro-infested caves and has provoked an attack by invoking Bahamut's name.
source_quote: I worship Bahamut!

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum mutters that the two Derro are mad.
source_quote: Grygum mutters, “They are mad.”

subject: Narrak
fact: Narrak is a Derro ritualist with perpetually contorted features, frenetic eyes, and a warped intellect, leading experiments to elevate the Derro, triumph Demogorgon, and destroy the Duergar.
source_quote: We are conducting experiments! For what purpose! The only purpose that matters! The elevation of the Derro, the Triumph of Demogorgon, and the destruction of the Duergar!

subject: Narrak
fact: Narrak is a Derro with perpetually contorted features, unnervingly bright eyes, and a warped intellect consumed by chaotic evil, serving Demogorgon.
source_quote: His pale, derro features are perpetually contorted, twisting into a grotesque mask of terrifying, spiraling madness. His eyes, perhaps unnervingly bright in the dim light, dart about with a frenetic, almost desperate energy. He gestures wildly at a few apprentices. There’s an undeniable, warped intellect simmering beneath his frantic movements, but it is utterly consumed by the chaotic evil that seems to radiate from his very being.

subject: Narrak
fact: Narrak is a derro orchestrator whose pale, contorted features radiate spiraling madness, serving the demon lord Demogorgon and consumed by chaotic evil.
source_quote: His eyes dart about with a frenetic, almost desperate energy.

subject: Narrak
fact: Narrak is a derro ritualist and mad scholar who leads experiments in a cavern filled with Demogorgon-themed tomes. He is a terrifying blend of warped intellect and chaotic evil, obsessed with elevating the Derro, destroying the Duergar, and serving Demogorgon.
source_quote: ‘We are conducting experiments!... The elevation of the Derro, the Triumph of Demogorgon, and the destruction of the Duergar!’

subject: Skiit
fact: Skiit is a Derro who mutters to himself, wears tattered leather stained with grime, and carries an amulet of Demogorgon, believing that following the demon lord makes the Derro proud and powerful.
source_quote: I am a follower of Demogorgon! Pliinki has said that anybody who follows Demogorgon is making the Derro proud and powerful. And we're going to be great again!

subject: Skiit
fact: Skiit is a derro cultist of Demogorgon who believes following the demon lord will restore Derro pride and power. He is mentally unstable, mutters to himself, and obsesses over Pliinki’s promises. He was thrown into a pit by Grygum and later killed by Daz’s Toll the Dead.
source_quote: ‘Pliinki promised Skiit a better job.’ ‘I am a follower of Demogorgon! We’re going to be great again!’

subject: Skiit
fact: Skiit is a derro cultist of Demogorgon, mentally fractured and obsessed with promises of better jobs from Pliinki. He mutters to himself, wears tattered stained leather and cloth, and tends to a pit of body parts. He was pushed into the pit by Grygum, revived, and then killed by Daz with Toll the Dead.
source_quote: But Pliinki promised Skiit a better job.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin is a battle-hardened dwarf warrior who relies on brute force, armor, and blunt pragmatism. He dismisses madness as irrelevant, avoids unnecessary conflict, and has zero patience for philosophical talk. He is the group’s most effective combatant against derro.
source_quote: ‘One head is better than two!’ ‘No. There is nothing of value here.’ ‘East.’

subject: Ulnara
fact: Ulnara is a Derro necromancer and cultist of Demogorgon who transforms from arrogance to subservience upon realizing Daz is a Drow, and promises to turn corpses into zombies for the cult.
source_quote: Your lordship! Or was it the Ember Vanguard? What a wonderful name for such a powerful group. Do not worry, after he’s dead I will turn him into a zombie and he will serve the cult of Demogorgon forever!

subject: Ulnara
fact: Ulnara is a derro necromancer and cultist of Demogorgon who oversees the ‘great project of Ulnara of the Council of Savants.’ She initially appears arrogant but collapses into subservience upon realizing Daz is a Drow. She seeks to turn corpses into zombies for Demogorgon’s cult.
source_quote: ‘Your lordship! Or was it the Ember Vanguard?... I will turn him into a zombie and he will serve the cult of Demogorgon forever!’

subject: Ulnara
fact: Ulnara is a derro necromancer and high cultist of Demogorgon, in charge of the great project of Ulnara of the Council of Savants. She oversees the pit of zombies and body parts, initially arrogant but broken by Daz’s display of power after realizing he is a Drow. She offers service to the Ember Vanguard to save herself.
source_quote: The great project of Ulnara of the Council of Savants!

subject: Ulnara
fact: Ulnara is a necromancer, a cultist of Demogorgon, and a derro who shifts from arrogance to subservience upon realizing Daz is a Drow.
source_quote: Ulnara looks at me, and she has that look of someone who thought they had all the cards, and understood what was going on, and realizes she doesn’t anymore. Her arrogance disappears, and her sniveling, subservient persona emerges.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir is a silent, disciplined monk whose actions are precise and purposeful. He communicates only through deeds — summoning darkness, landing critical strikes, and observing without judgment. He is the group’s most reliable and composed member.
source_quote: I observe everything and say nothing. My mind is clear. I act without speaking. I do because I know.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir is an arcane spellcaster who uses darkness and critical strikes to devastating effect. He is exhausted but effective in combat, having critically struck a Derro with a precise spell and summoned darkness to envelop multiple enemies.
source_quote: Zalthir, bless his arcane heart, summoned his darkness, enveloping a couple of them. Then, in a burst of brilliant speed, he critically struck one of the Darrow.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir observes everything and acts without speaking, driven by clear, unspoken knowledge.
source_quote: I observe everything and say nothing. My mind is clear. I act without speaking. I do because I know.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir observes everything and says nothing, acting without speaking because he knows.
source_quote: I observe everything and say nothing. My mind is clear. I act without speaking. I do because I know.

subject: Amulet of Demogorgon
fact: A dark artifact worn by Skiit, symbolizing his allegiance to the Two-Headed Demon Lord. It is the key to his delusional belief in Derro supremacy and the source of his defiance against the party.
source_quote: Wait, that’s interesting, he’s got an amulet of Demogorgon.

subject: Amulet of Demogorgon
fact: A dark, twisted artifact worn by Skiit, radiating chaotic power and reinforcing his delusions of divine favor. It is the physical symbol of his allegiance to Demogorgon and the catalyst for his defiance against the party.
source_quote: Wait, that’s interesting, he’s got an amulet of Demogorgon.

subject: amulet of Demogorgon
fact: An amulet of Demogorgon is worn by Skiit, a Derro who believes it grants him divine favor and power, and is the sole symbol of his devotion in a world of fractured faith.
source_quote: Wait, that’s interesting, he’s got an amulet of Demogorgon.

subject: amulet of Demogorgon
fact: The Derro wears an amulet of Demogorgon.
source_quote: he’s got an amulet of Demogorgon

subject: death dogs
fact: Death dogs are present in the hellish red-glowing cavern with Derro.
source_quote: some Derro and Death dogs.

subject: demogorgon cultist derro
fact: The Derro named Skiit claims to be a follower of Demogorgon, believing it makes the Derro proud and powerful.
source_quote: I am a follower of Demogorgon! Pliinki has said that anybody who follows Demogorgon is making the Derro proud and powerful.

subject: derro hair and skin
fact: The Derro has blue-gray skin, pale eyes lacking irises and pupils, and dull white, greasy, unkempt hair.
source_quote: He has blue, gray skin and pale eyes that lack both irises and pupils. He has thin, stringy hair, dull white, constantly looking greasy and unkempt.

subject: derro papers
fact: Papers found among the Trillimac books contain evidence of Demogorgon’s influence.
source_quote: amongst the books are various papers. Knowing these creatures, there is probably enough evidence to convince Errde of whatever she wants.

subject: maximillian’s earthen grasp
fact: Daz uses Maximillian’s Earthen Grasp to crush the wounded Derro, but it escapes.
source_quote: I cast Maximillian’s Earthen Grasp and start to crush the poor unfortunate creature.

subject: Polished Obsidian Scale
fact: A smooth, shimmering scale of polished obsidian, taken from the 'dark ones' by a Derro. It glows faintly in dim light and is described as shimmering 'like madness,' indicating magical corruption from the Deep Dark or Demogorgon's influence.
source_quote: A scale smooth, this polished obsidian, but it shimmered like madness.

subject: silver candlestick value
fact: The silver candlesticks flanking the Lolth altar are worth 25 gp each.
source_quote: a pair of heavy silver candlesticks worth 25 gp each

subject: Trillimac books
fact: Books titled 'The Spiraling Descent,' 'The Prince's Gift,' and 'Rituals of the Two-Headed Beast' are found in the ritual chamber.
source_quote: books made from Trillimac... 'The Spiraling Descent: A Treatise on Duality and Madness,' 'The Prince's Gift: On the Creation of Favored Spawn', 'Rituals of the Two-Headed Beast.'

subject: Trillimac Books
fact: These forbidden books, bound in Trillimac, contain esoteric rituals and theological treatises on the Two-Headed Beast, duality, and the creation of favored spawn. Titles include 'The Spiraling Descent,' 'The Prince's Gift,' and 'Rituals of the Two-Headed Beast.' They are key evidence of Demogorgon's corruption.
source_quote: Titles — 'The Spiraling Descent: A Treatise on Duality and Madness,' and 'The Prince's Gift: On the Creation of Favored Spawn', and 'Rituals of the Two-Headed Beast.'

subject: Trillimac books
fact: Trillimac books are found in the ritual cavern, inscribed with forbidden texts on duality, madness, and the creation of favored spawn for Demogorgon.
source_quote: Around the platform are books made from Trillimac... 'The Spiraling Descent: A Treatise on Duality and Madness,' and 'The Prince's Gift: On the Creation of Favored Spawn', and 'Rituals of the Two-Headed Beast.'

subject: Trillimac Tomes
fact: Books bound in Trillimac leather containing forbidden knowledge on Demogorgon’s influence, Derro ascension, and ritual madness. They are evidence of the cult’s scholarly corruption and serve as potential leverage against Errde Blackstaff.
source_quote: ‘The Spiraling Descent: A Treatise on Duality and Madness,’ ‘The Prince's Gift: On the Creation of Favored Spawn,’ ‘Rituals of the Two-Headed Beast.’

subject: Daz's allegiance
fact: Daz is unsure who he and the Ember Vanguard work for, having struck numerous deals with various parties.
source_quote: However, we have struck numerous deals with various other parties, and I'm no longer sure what to say.

subject: Derro Ritual Texts and Their Origin
fact: The origin of the Trillimac books and the true identity of 'the Prince' referenced in the texts remain unknown. Whether 'the Prince' is Demogorgon, a mindflayer overlord, or something older is unconfirmed.
source_quote: The Prince's Gift: On the Creation of Favored Spawn

subject: Divine Scrutiny
fact: Grygum frames questions of allegiance as 'Divine Scrutiny,' a profound act of investigation into the threads of intertwined fates, turning simple queries into meandering theological debates.
source_quote: That is a question that requires more than a simple answer. It is, in fact, a Divine Scrutiny, a profound act of investigation into the very threads of our intertwined fates, here in this churning city of Gracklstugh.

subject: Divine Scrutiny
fact: Grygum’s obsession with framing every question as a 'Divine Scrutiny' is a narrative thread that masks his own lack of certainty. It is a performative ritual he uses to avoid direct answers, but it inadvertently creates space for Daz’s lethal clarity to dominate.
source_quote: It is, in fact, a Divine Scrutiny, a profound act of investigation into the very threads of our intertwined fates...

subject: Grygum’s Faith and Its Consequences
fact: Grygum’s unyielding devotion to Bahamut repeatedly provokes deadly reactions from cultists. Whether this is divine courage or reckless folly remains in question, and future encounters may escalate beyond combat.
source_quote: Grygum shouts, 'I thought we could have a deep Phylosophical conversation!'

subject: Grygum's worship of Bahamut
fact: Grygum claims to worship Bahamut, but the Derro react violently to this, suggesting his faith is either performative or dangerously out of step with the local reality.
source_quote: “I worship Bahamut!”

subject: purpose of experiments
fact: The ultimate purpose of the experiments remains unresolved, tied to the Derro’s quest for elevation and Demogorgon’s triumph.
source_quote: For what purpose!

subject: The Fate of the Books
fact: Daz possesses the evidence but is undecided whether to deliver it to Errde Blackstaff. The moral and political consequences of revealing—or concealing—this knowledge are unresolved.
source_quote: I might not want to give it to her. But I know her type; if she doesn’t get evidence, she’ll invent it.

subject: The Great Project of Ulnara
fact: A mysterious, ongoing Derro necromantic operation overseen by Ulnara, involving body parts, zombies, and ritual sacrifice. Its true purpose is unknown, but it is tied to Demogorgon’s influence and the Derro’s desire for rebirth.
source_quote: ‘The great project of Ulnara of the Council of Savants!’

subject: 2nd day of the 2nd tenday of Myrtul
fact: The date marks the second day of the party’s operation against the cult. It is when Pelek remains tied, the ritual resumes, and the Ember Vanguard launches their attack. It is the temporal anchor for the battle’s events.

subject: 2nd day of the 2nd tenday of Myrtul
fact: The second day of the second tenday of Myrtul is when the group awakens to find Pelek still tied up. Grygum collects his winnings from JimJar’s bet. Pelek reflects on sleep and death. The group then departs from Buppido’s lair to re-infiltrate the cultist cavern, where they observe a distracted Derro and a new two-headed stone giant statue.

subject: session date
fact: The session occurs on the 2nd day of the 2nd tenday of Myrtul.
source_quote: 2nd day of the 2nd tenday of Myrtul

subject: session date
fact: This sequence occurs during an active dungeon session, with events unfolding in real-time as the party engages in combat, ritual disruption, and tactical magic use.
source_quote: I raise an eyebrow.", "I nod.", "Finally, Narrak emerges...

subject: acid vomit from Grygum
fact: Grygum vomits a wave of acid after an incantation, a side effect of his magic that is not a spell he wishes to cast.
source_quote: I look at him as he straightens and vomits forth a wave of acid. This is not a spell I wish to cast.

subject: Acid Vomiting Ritual
fact: Grygum undergoes a violent physical transformation after being struck, vomiting a wave of acid—a non-spell, ritualistic manifestation of inner corruption or divine perversity tied to the cult’s influence.
source_quote: Grygum moaning in pain, then in incantation. There is a violent heaving. I look at him as he straightens and vomits forth a wave of acid.

subject: acid vomit spell
fact: Grygum vomits forth a wave of acid after a violent heaving.
source_quote: vomits forth a wave of acid

subject: attack on the cult
fact: The Ember Vanguard launches a coordinated assault using Zalthir’s darkness, Daz’s Scorching Rays, Grygum’s acid vomiting and guiding bolt, Thorin’s melee strikes, and Maximilian’s Earthen Grasp. The Ettin survives, Narrak is trapped, and the ritual is halted mid-incantation.

subject: curse spreading claim
fact: Narrak claims, 'You cannot stop the inevitable... the curse spreads!'
source_quote: You cannot stop the inevitable... the curse spreads!

subject: Darkness Ambush
fact: Zalthir casts a magical darkness over the Derro and Ettin, obscuring vision and enabling surprise attacks; the environment becomes chaotic, with combatants striking blindly and magical effects interfering with perception.
source_quote: Zalthir and I had discussed what we should do. He plans to use his darkness...", "From inside it, Narrak shouts...

subject: Daz
fact: Daz cast Maximillian’s Earthen Grasp on where he thought Narrak was.
source_quote: I could keep them there with a spell. And so I cast Maximillian’s Earthen Grasp on where I think he is.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz cast scorching rays — three spears of flame — toward the Ettin, feeling invigorated and empowered.
source_quote: Three spears of flame, raging hues of orange and red, appear above me. My skin prickles and sweats under their intense heat—but I am not frightened. I feel invigorated. Empowered. These are the vessels of my inner fury.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz explained that there is no danger from Pelek/Derro and that tying him up would make them safer, referencing the past death of a group member at Buppido's hands.
source_quote: Daz, however, explains that there is no such danger. And that they would all be safer with the ghost tied up. The last time they trusted someone, Buppido killed one of their group.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz realized the Derro avoided noticing them because they were trying to avoid being seen by Narrak, like how Priestesses of Lolth made others invisible out of fear.
source_quote: I finally understand why that Derro, who should have seen us, has not noticed us. He’s trying to avoid being seen by Narrak. I’ve seen that before, when the various Priestesses of Lolth would get angry, and everyone tried hard to be invisible.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz whispered to the Ember Vanguard that the Derro are performing a summoning ritual to make the Stone Giants sprout a second head, which probably explains what happened to the Stone Giant that fought them in the Dark Lake District.
source_quote: I turn and whisper to the Ember Vanguard, "They are performing some kind of summoning ritual to make the Stone Giants sprout a second head. This probably explains what happened to the Stone Giant that fought us in the Dark Lake District."

subject: Daz’s recognition of Lolth’s Priestesses
fact: Daz recognizes the Derro’s behavior of hiding from Narrak as identical to how subordinates hide from Priestesses of Lolth.
source_quote: I’ve seen that before, when the various Priestesses of Lolth would get angry, and everyone tried hard to be invisible. A high-level cleric can kill you very easily.

subject: Daz’s scorching rays
fact: Daz casts three spears of scorching flame, describing them as roaring beasts and vessels of his inner fury.
source_quote: Three spears of flame, raging hues of orange and red, appear above me. My skin prickles and sweats under their intense heat—but I am not frightened. I feel invigorated. Empowered. These are the vessels of my inner fury. They roar like fierce beasts as I hurl them toward the Ettin.

subject: Daz’s scorching rays as expression of inner fury
fact: Daz describes his scorching rays as vessels of his inner fury, roaring like beasts, indicating emotional investment in his magic.
source_quote: These are the vessels of my inner fury. They roar like fierce beasts as I hurl them toward the Ettin.

subject: Daz’s scorching rays strike
fact: Daz hurls three spears of scorching flame at the Ettin, feeling empowered and invigorated as the flames roar like beasts.
source_quote: Three spears of flame, raging hues of orange and red, appear above me. My skin prickles and sweats under their intense heat—but I am not frightened. I feel invigorated. Empowered. These are the vessels of my inner fury. They roar like fierce beasts as I hurl them toward the Ettin.

subject: Daz’s targeting
fact: Daz selects the Ettin as his primary target during the ambush.
source_quote: He plans to use his darkness, and wants to know who I will target. I say the Ettin.

subject: Daz’s targeting of Ettin
fact: Daz selects the Ettin as his primary target during the ambush, indicating strategic priority.
source_quote: He plans to use his darkness, and wants to know who I will target. I say the Ettin.

subject: death as sleep debate
fact: Pelek/Derro muses on whether death is a form of sleep.
source_quote: There is this whole question about whether death is a form of sleep.

subject: derro avoidance behavior
fact: A Derro avoids being seen by Narrak, as high-level clerics can kill easily.
source_quote: He’s trying to avoid being seen by Narrak... A high-level cleric can kill you very easily.

subject: Derro’s chant variation
fact: The Derro perform a second chant during the ritual, with altered lines about the Deepking falling and Narrak’s vision, after being corrected by Narrak.
source_quote: Two heads! Two heads! A glorious sight! The Deepking falls into endless night! Narrak's vision, sharp and keen! The Prince of Chaos, always unseen!

subject: Derro’s failed coordination
fact: The Derro repeatedly fail to coordinate their chant and attacks, leading to missed strikes and ritual failure.
source_quote: But the Derro only do so half heartedly... ... Another Derro rushes out of Zalthir’s darkness and attacks Grygum, missing.

subject: Derro’s failed ritual
fact: The Derro’s ritual fails due to lack of vigor, mispronunciation, and interruption by the Ember Vanguard, despite Narrak’s repeated commands for more passion.
source_quote: But the Derro only do so half heartedly, at which point the one I assume is Narrak, like every choir director ever shouts, “Silence, you blithering half-wits! More vigor! This city's doom, a ritual! Dig it!"

subject: Derro’s failed ritual
fact: The Derro’s ritual fails due to lack of vigor, poor coordination, and interruption by the Ember Vanguard.
source_quote: But the Derro only do so half heartedly... ... You cannot stop the inevitable... the curse spreads!

subject: Derro’s missed attacks
fact: Two Derro attack Grygum and Zalthir in the darkness but miss their targets, indicating poor combat coordination.
source_quote: One of the Derro rushes out of Zalthir’s darkness, notices Grygum, and strikes him while chanting, “You shall die! You shall die!” ... Another creature attacks Zalthir in the darkness. It took shrieks something intelligible. I don’t hear the sound of weapons making contact with flesh...

subject: Derro’s preoccupation with death dog
fact: One Derro is distracted by a death dog, allowing the Ember Vanguard to infiltrate undetected.
source_quote: There is a derro who, by all rights, should see us, but he seems to be preoccupied with a death dog, desperately trying hard not to be noticed.

subject: Derro’s preoccupation with death dog
fact: One Derro is so preoccupied with avoiding a death dog that he fails to notice the Ember Vanguard’s infiltration.
source_quote: There is a derro who, by all rights, should see us, but he seems to be preoccupied with a death dog, desperately trying hard not to be noticed.

subject: Ettin’s resilience
fact: The Ettin survives multiple attacks and smiles after being hit, suggesting it is corrupted or unnaturally resilient.
source_quote: A guiding bolt from Grygum strikes the Ettin, and it groans and then smiles.

subject: Ritual of Demogorgon
fact: The cult performs a ritual invoking Demogorgon using a chant that demands the grafting of additional heads onto Stone Giants. The ritual’s effects are believed to have altered a Stone Giant in the Dark Lake District. The chant is sourced from a book, and its success is implied by the presence of the statue and the Derro’s chanting. The group observes the ritual but delays intervention, trusting Hgraam to reverse its effects.

subject: Ritual of the Two-Headed
fact: A cult ritual is being performed to transform giants into two-headed monsters, involving synchronized chanting, positional alignment, and the accumulation of severed heads; failure to perform with vigor risks collapse of the ritual’s power.
source_quote: We have successfully converted another of Hgraam’s giants to a two-headed monster.", "Now we shall convert one more, and by golly, they will lay waste to Gracklstugh!

subject: ritual performance
fact: The cult performs a ritual to graft a second head onto a Stone Giant, using a chanted incantation, Derro acolytes, and a stone statue as a focus. The ritual is disrupted by the Ember Vanguard’s attack, causing confusion and failure in performance. Narrak blames the Derro’s lack of vigor.

source_quote: we have this process that allows us to convert our dead enemies into zombies.

subject: Cult of Demogorgon
fact: The Cult of Demogorgon, led by Narrak, performs rituals to graft second heads onto Stone Giants using Derro acolytes. Their goal is to empower Demogorgon by creating monstrous avatars to destroy Gracklstugh. They rely on chanted incantations, fear magic, and ritual precision, and are deeply hierarchical with Narrak as an authoritarian choir director.

subject: Derro
fact: The Derro are a subterranean cult faction devoted to Demogorgon, performing ritualistic transformations and chants to empower their city’s doom; they are obedient to Narrak but lack discipline, requiring constant correction.
source_quote: He motions to all of the Derro to surround him...", "The Derro groan and gather around him.", "The Derro only do so half heartedly...

subject: Ember Vanguard
fact: The Ember Vanguard is a cohesive adventuring group focused on infiltrating and destroying the Demogorgon-worshipping cult. They use stealth, magic, and coordinated attacks. Members include Daz, Zalthir, Grygum, Thorin, and JimJar. They are distrustful of past betrayals and rely on divine intervention (Hgraam) and tactical patience.

subject: Ember Vanguard
fact: The Ember Vanguard is a group of warriors bound by magical fear and ritual alignment with Narrak’s cult; they are susceptible to psychological manipulation and serve as both targets and unwitting enforcers of the ritual’s power.
source_quote: the three members of the Ember Vanguard look terrified.", "They are bunched up; it’s time to attack.

subject: Myconid Circle
fact: A group of sentient fungi led by the Myconid who communicate via spores. They convert dead enemies into zombie-like entities and view themselves as nonviolent. They are emotionally invested in Rump-a-dump and seek reconciliation, but are misunderstood and feared by the Ember Vanguard.

subject: Buppido’s Lair
fact: Buppido’s Lair is a grim, bone-strewn site where the Ember Vanguard has previously faced betrayal. It serves as their base of operations and is referenced as the origin of past trauma, particularly the death of a party member by Buppido.

subject: Buppido’s lair
fact: Buppido’s lair is the group’s former base, now abandoned and grim, filled with dead bones and an altar to a demonic power. It is referenced as the site of a past betrayal where Buppido killed one of their group. The group departs from here to return to the cultist cavern.

subject: Buppido’s lair
fact: Buppido’s lair is the previous stronghold of the cult, from which the Ember Vanguard departs before returning to the cultist cavern.
source_quote: And so we head out from Buppido’s lair and find ourselves once again outside of the cultist cavern.

subject: Cultist Cavern
fact: The Cultist Cavern is a hidden chamber beneath Buppido’s lair where the Demogorgon cult performs its rituals. It contains a platform with a stone giant statue, a group of chanting Derro, an Ettin guard, and a head cultist named Narrak. The cavern is poorly lit and filled with the stench of brimstone.

subject: Cultist Cavern
fact: The cultist cavern is the site of repeated ritual activity targeting Demogorgon and the grafting of heads onto Stone Giants. It contains a central platform with a two-headed stone giant statue, five chanting Derro, an Ettin, a death dog, and a chief cultist holding the ritual book. The party has infiltrated it stealthily multiple times, with Derro often distracted or preoccupied. It is the focal point of the current mission to end the cult.

subject: cultist cavern
fact: The cultist cavern is the site of the ritual, where Derro chant around a platform with a two-headed stone giant statue, and where the Ember Vanguard sneaks in undetected.
source_quote: And so we head out from Buppido’s lair and find ourselves once again outside of the cultist cavern. And once again, we have managed to sneak into the room.

subject: cultist cavern location
fact: The cultist cavern is located outside of Buppido’s lair.
source_quote: outside of the cultist cavern

source_quote: all the derro are covered in his magical darkness

source_quote: preoccupied with a death dog, desperately trying hard not to be noticed

fact: The final resting place is Buppido’s lair, a grim place full of dead bones and an altar to some demonic power.
source_quote: We are once again at the final resting place of Buppido. It’s a grim place, full of dead bones, and an altar to some demonic power or some mad idea.

subject: Gracklstugh
fact: Gracklstugh is the cult city targeted for destruction by the ritual; it is the ultimate goal of the two-headed transformation and the locus of the cult’s apocalyptic ambitions.
source_quote: they will lay waste to Gracklstugh!

subject: Monastery
fact: The monastery is referenced by Zalthir as a place where children were taught silence. He uses it as a metaphor to express his frustration with the Myconid’s incessant chatter and his desire for peace.

subject: platform
fact: The platform holds a statue of a stone giant with a second head emerging from it, and is surrounded by Derro during the ritual.
source_quote: There is a statue of another two-headed stone giant. ... They all move to their positions. ... A statue of a stone giant with a second head emerging from it.

subject: stone giant statue height
fact: The statue of a stone giant with a second head emerging from it is only 2 feet tall.
source_quote: it is only 2 feet tall

subject: Whorlstone's Depths
fact: Whorlstone's Depths is the mythic source of Demogorgon’s power, where spiraling rituals originate and madness flows upward into the cult’s city; it is referenced in chant as the origin of corruption.
source_quote: From Whorlstone's depths, the spirals turn!

subject: death dog
fact: A death dog is present in the cultist cavern, and one Derro is preoccupied with trying not to be noticed by it.
source_quote: There is a derro who, by all rights, should see us, but he seems to be preoccupied with a death dog, desperately trying hard not to be noticed.

subject: Death Dog
fact: A death dog is present in the cultist cavern, distracting a Derro who is desperately trying not to be noticed. The party successfully sneaks past because the Derro is occupied with the creature, allowing them to enter undetected.

subject: Demogorgon’s Influence
fact: Demogorgon’s presence manifests as madness, spiraling rituals, and physical corruption; its influence warps perception, causes acid vomiting, and empowers the cult’s rituals with terrifying, reality-bending effects.
source_quote: His madness flows, our city drools!", "Demogorgon’s madness flows through me!", "the curse spreads!

subject: Derro
fact: Derro are the chanting cultists who perform the ritual, are concealed by Zalthir’s darkness, attack Grygum and Zalthir, and are berated by Narrak for lack of vigor.
source_quote: Five Derro are chanting. ... One of the Derro raises a hand, and asks where, and the head cultist shouts, “OVER THERE!!!” ... Another Derro rushes out of Zalthir’s darkness and attacks Grygum, missing.

subject: derro count
fact: Five Derro are chanting.
source_quote: five Derro are chanting

subject: Ettin
fact: An Ettin is present near the cult’s central platform, positioned next to the obvious boss. It is observed by Daz and mentioned as part of the ritual’s defensive or symbolic arrangement. It is not directly engaged but is noted as a significant threat in the chamber.

subject: Ettin
fact: The Ettin is a two-headed creature targeted by Daz, struck by Thorin and Grygum, and attacks the frightened Thorin with its morning star.
source_quote: I say the Ettin. ... The Ettin raises his battle axe and strikes the frightened Thorin, and misses, but the morning star hits. ... A guiding bolt from Grygum strikes the Ettin, and it groans and then smiles.

subject: ettin count
fact: An Ettin is present next to the obvious boss.
source_quote: an Ettin .

subject: Stone Giant (two-headed statue)
fact: A statue of a two-headed stone giant, two feet tall, stands at the center of the ritual platform. It is the focal point of the cult’s summoning ritual, which seeks to graft additional heads onto Stone Giants. Daz and Grygum link it to a prior encounter with a Stone Giant in the Dark Lake District. It is not alive but represents the ritual’s intended effect.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz is a cleric of the Ember Vanguard who understands cult tactics from Lolth's priesthood and targets the Ettin during the ritual assault. He casts Scorching Rays and Maximilian’s Earthen Grasp, and recognizes the Derro's fear of Narrak as analogous to Lolth's priestess dynamics.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz is leading the group through another ritual targeting a demon, having witnessed the successful use of the ritual by the Drow. He observes the acrid stench of brimstone, eerie campfire atmosphere, and five Derro chanting in harmony. He identifies the central statue as a two-headed stone giant and correctly links it to a prior encounter with a Stone Giant in the Dark Lake District. He cautions Thorin against rushing in and notes the ritual’s source: a book in the chief cultist’s hands. He later hears the chant invoking Demogorgon and recognizes the ritual’s intent: grafting additional heads. He is aware that Grygum’s spells are nearly ready and that Hgraam may reverse the effects on Stone Giants. He is amused when Zalthir misunderstands the size of the statue, realizing it is only two feet tall.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz is the one who targets the Ettin during the ambush, and recognizes the behavior of Derro avoiding Narrak as similar to Priestesses of Lolth silencing their subordinates.
source_quote: I finally understand why that Derro, who should have seen us, has not noticed us. He’s trying to avoid being seen by Narrak. I’ve seen that before, when the various Priestesses of Lolth would get angry, and everyone tried hard to be invisible.

subject: Demogorgon
fact: Demogorgon is the demon invoked in the ritual chant, described as the Prince of Chaos whose madness flows through the cultists.
source_quote: For Demogorgon, the city will burn! ... Demogorgon’s madness flows through me!

subject: Derro
fact: A Derro is present in the cultist cavern, preoccupied with a death dog and failing to notice the party’s infiltration. He is possessed by Pelek, a ghost who fears losing control of him. The Derro’s body is used as a vessel, and his actions are under the influence of Pelek’s consciousness. He is restrained with knots that hold, as confirmed the next day.

subject: Derro
fact: A group of Derro chant the ritual incantation for Demogorgon, fail to perform with vigor, and are controlled by Narrak. They are blinded by Zalthir’s darkness, attack Grygum and Zalthir, miss their strikes, and are overwhelmed by the Ember Vanguard’s assault. One Derro is preoccupied avoiding Narrak’s notice.

subject: Ettin
fact: The Ettin is a two-headed monstrosity guarding the ritual platform, targeted by Daz during the attack. It wields a battle axe and morning star, is struck by Grygum’s guiding bolt and Thorin’s attack, and survives the initial assault with a smile after being damaged.

subject: Gracklstugh
fact: Gracklstugh is the city targeted by the cult’s ritual, which they intend to lay waste to after converting more Stone Giants.
source_quote: Now we shall convert one more, and by golly, they will lay waste to Gracklstugh!

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum is a cleric of the Ember Vanguard who prepares spells to counter the cult’s effects, ties up Pelek/Derro, and later vomits acid in a violent reaction to ritual magic. He casts a guiding bolt at the Ettin, is affected by Narrak’s fear spell, and is the target of multiple Derro attacks. He collects a bet win from JimJar over knot durability.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum is a cleric or divine caster who channels acid through violent ritual vomiting after being attacked; he survives lethal trauma and responds with potent, unorthodox magic, suggesting deep ties to chaotic or necrotic forces.
source_quote: Grygum moaning in pain, then in incantation. There is a violent heaving. I look at him as he straightens and vomits forth a wave of acid.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum is struck by a Derro, vomits acid after incantation, casts a guiding bolt at the Ettin, and is affected by Narrak’s fear spell before being freed by Zalthir’s darkness.
source_quote: One of the Derro rushes out of Zalthir’s darkness, notices Grygum, and strikes him while chanting, “You shall die! You shall die!” ... I look at him as he straightens and vomits forth a wave of acid. A guiding bolt from Grygum strikes the Ettin, and it groans and then smiles.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum is the one who notices the need to stop the ritual, but his spells are almost finished, and he later receives divine insight that Hgraam can reverse the ill effects on the Stone Giants.
source_quote: Grygum turns to me, “I know we want to stop this ritual, but my spells are almost finished.” ... We are told that Hgraam should be able to reverse whatever ill effects on the Stone Giants.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum is uncertain about the safety of Pelek/Derro and questions whether the ghost is a threat.
source_quote: At first, I am confused and uncertain. More to the point, are we safe with this ghost?

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum prepares to pray when Pelek, now possessing a Derro body, asks to be tied up out of fear he might lose control and the Derro might kill them. Grygum is uncertain of their safety with the ghost. Daz reassures him, citing past betrayal by Buppido that resulted in a group member’s death. As they tie Pelek up, JimJar makes a bet that the knots won’t hold. The next day, Pelek remains tied, and Grygum collects his winnings. Upon untying him, Pelek reflects on the ambiguity of death and sleep, sparking a philosophical impulse in Grygum that is cut short by the need to prepare for battle. Grygum later reassures Thorin that Hgraam can handle the new two-headed stone giant statue, and their mission remains to end the cult.

subject: Hgraam
fact: Hgraam is a divine agent of the Ember Vanguard believed capable of reversing the ill effects of the cult’s ritual on Stone Giants. Grygum and the party rely on Hgraam’s potential to undo the grafting magic, though Hgraam does not appear directly.

subject: Hgraam
fact: Hgraam is a member of the group with the ability to reverse the ill effects inflicted upon Stone Giants by the cult’s ritual. Daz and Grygum both recognize this ability, and it is cited as the reason they can delay immediate action against the statue. It is implied Hgraam’s magic will mitigate the ritual’s grafting of additional heads.

subject: Hgraam
fact: Hgraam is referenced as a divine entity who can reverse the ill effects on the Stone Giants, invoked by Grygum’s divine insight.
source_quote: We are told that Hgraam should be able to reverse whatever ill effects on the Stone Giants.

subject: JimJar
fact: JimJar bets Grygum that his knots on Pelek will not hold, and later loses the bet when Pelek remains tied up the next day.
source_quote: JimJar again offers one of his silly bets. He bets me that my knots won’t hold. ... And when we wake up, Pelek/Derro is still tied up. And I collect my winnings.

subject: JimJar
fact: JimJar is a member of the Ember Vanguard who places bets on mundane outcomes, including whether Grygum’s knots will hold. He is the source of comic relief and distraction during tense moments.

subject: JimJar
fact: JimJar is a recurring member of the group who makes frivolous bets. He bets Grygum that the knots restraining Pelek/Derro will not hold. His behavior is described as silly, and he is present during the tying of Pelek. Grygum wins the bet the next day.

subject: Myconid
fact: A Myconid communicates telepathically with Zalthir about Rump-a-dump, a dissatisfied member of her circle. She insists on nonviolence, equates her kind with zombies, and claims the group can convert enemies into undead. Zalthir grows frustrated with her persistence and eventually silences her by invoking parental advice.

subject: Myconid
fact: The Myconid is a persistent, emotionally driven creature who communicates through spores. She insists on resolving the matter of Rump-a-dump, a dissatisfied member of her circle whom she believes is being mistreated. She claims no one should be killed because the targets are like her, and reveals her kind’s ability to convert dead enemies into zombies. She becomes upset when Zalthir expresses fear of becoming one, accusing him of not helping her friends. She eventually falls asleep after Zalthir invokes parental wisdom, leaving him to reflect on her behavior.

subject: Myconid
fact: The Myconid speaks to Zalthir about Rump-a-dump, insists on non-violence toward her kind, and claims they convert enemies into zombies, before falling asleep after Zalthir’s frustration.
source_quote: The childlike voice of the Myconid. ... “Rump-a-dump would never let them do that! You don’t want to help my friends, and so why should I help you?” ... And the creature falls asleep.

subject: Narrak
fact: Narrak is the choir-like head cultist who directs the Derro’s ritual, uses fear magic, and is ultimately trapped by Daz’s spell.
source_quote: Silence, you blithering half-wits! More vigor! This city's doom, a ritual! Dig it! ... I will use fear! ... You cannot stop the inevitable... the curse spreads!

subject: Narrak
fact: Narrak is the head cultist leading a ritual to transform giants into two-headed monsters, demanding fervor and precision in chant and movement; he is the emotional and magical core of the Derro cult, and his madness drives their actions.
source_quote: Hear me, you two-headed fools! His madness flows, our city drools! From Whorlstone's depths, the spirals turn! For Demogorgon, the city will burn! More heads for grafting! More for the pile!

subject: Narrak
fact: Narrak is the head cultist leading the ritual to graft second heads onto Stone Giants for Demogorgon. He is obsessed with ritual precision, shouts motivational commands, and is the source of a fear spell that affects the Ember Vanguard. He emerges from Zalthir’s darkness and screams about the inevitable spread of the curse after being trapped by Maximilian’s Earthen Grasp.

subject: Narrak
fact: Narrak is the head cultist who leads the ritual chant, berates the Derro for lack of vigor, casts fear using a white feather, and is trapped in Zalthir’s darkness after being targeted by Maximillian’s Earthen Grasp.
source_quote: Silence, you blithering half-wits! More vigor! This city's doom, a ritual! Dig it! ... I will use fear! He takes a white feather and points at Thorin, Grygum, and Zalthir, says the magic words, and the three members of the Ember Vanguard look terrified. ... You cannot stop the inevitable... the curse spreads!

subject: Pelek
fact: Pelek is a Derro possessed by a ghost who is tied up after concern he might lose control, and later speaks about death as a form of sleep while being untied.
source_quote: I haven’t had a good night's sleep in ages. Although it’s unclear if I am sleeping … There is this whole question about whether death is a form of sleep. I suppose I will find out.

subject: Pelek
fact: Pelek is a ghost possessing the body of a Derro. He fears losing control of the Derro host and requests to be restrained. He acknowledges uncertainty about whether he is truly sleeping or dead. After being tied up, he expresses relief at having had a restful night — unusual for him — and muses on the philosophical question of whether death is a form of sleep.

subject: Pelek/Derro
fact: Pelek is a ghost possessing the body of a Derro, feared for losing control and potentially killing the party. He is tied up by the group after Daz reassures them that restraint is safer than trust, referencing past betrayal by Buppido. He mutters on the nature of death as sleep upon being untied.

subject: The Ettin
fact: The Ettin is a two-headed monstrosity serving as a frontline combatant for the Derro cult; it is resistant to magical damage, capable of wielding dual weapons, and is the primary target of the party’s assault.
source_quote: The Ettin points at the three of us outside of the darkness...", "The Ettin raises his battle axe and strikes the frightened Thorin...", "A guiding bolt from Grygum strikes the Ettin, and it groans and then smiles.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin is a member of the Ember Vanguard rendered terrified by Narrak’s fear spell; he is struck by the Ettin’s morning star while incapacitated, indicating vulnerability to psychological magic.
source_quote: the three members of the Ember Vanguard look terrified.", "The Ettin raises his battle axe and strikes the frightened Thorin, and misses, but the morning star hits. Thorin looks battered.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin is a warrior of the Ember Vanguard who is cautious about rushing into battle, listens to Zalthir’s warnings, and is targeted by Narrak’s fear spell. He is struck by the Ettin’s morning star, survives the encounter, and expresses concern for the Stone Giants’ fate.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin is eager to rush into the cultist chamber upon seeing the two-headed stone giant statue and later the Ettin. He is repeatedly cautioned by Daz and Zalthir, and he listens. He expresses concern for the safety of the giants, believing they need protection. He is displeased when told the effects on the Stone Giants might be reversed, but ultimately understands the need for patience. He points out the statue to Grygum, who reassures him Hgraam can handle it.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin is targeted by Narrak’s fear spell, is struck by the Ettin’s morning star while frightened, and attempts to strike the Ettin with success after the fear is broken.
source_quote: The Ettin raises his battle axe and strikes the frightened Thorin, and misses, but the morning star hits. Thorin looks battered. ... But Thorin has a better chance to strike the creature, and he does.

subject: Whorlstone
fact: Whorlstone is the location from whose depths the spirals turn, referenced in the ritual chant as the origin of the magic.
source_quote: From Whorlstone's depths, the spirals turn!

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir casts darkness to conceal the Derro, breathes fire into it, warns of a madness-inducing effect from the ritual circle, and later moves the darkness over Narrak to break the fear spell.
source_quote: There’s some kind of effect that the circle has on those who enter it. Some kind of madness gripped my mind, but my monk training allowed me to stop it. Be careful! I move the darkness over Narrak. As the source of the Ember Vanguard’s fear is no longer visible, they are no longer affected by it.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir is a member of the Ember Vanguard who uses darkness magic to obscure the battlefield, coordinates attacks with the party, and employs tactical repositioning to counter magical effects; he is observant and decisive in combat.
source_quote: I want to watch!", "Let’s attack now.", "They are bunched up; it’s time to attack.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir is a monk of the Ember Vanguard who uses magical darkness to conceal the party during the ritual attack. He breathes fire, detects madness effects within the ritual circle, and misjudges the size of the stone giant statue as 2 feet tall. He is impatient with the Myconid’s persistent chatter and struggles to distinguish friend from foe among the undead myconids.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir is impatient with the Myconid's persistent demands and has worn thin on his patience.
source_quote: My patience has worn thin. And at this time, in the monastery, the young children would have learned to be silent, I wonder if this creature can learn to be quiet.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir is meditating when interrupted by a Myconid who insists on talking to Rump-a-dump, a dissatisfied member of her circle. The Myconid claims Rump-a-dump is connected to a prior group of ape-like creatures and insists no one should be killed because they are like her. Zalthir feigns ignorance, attempts to postpone the matter, and grows frustrated as the Myconid persists, claiming he never listens. The Myconid reveals their ability to convert dead enemies into zombies, alarming Zalthir. He warns he does not wish to become one. The Myconid becomes emotional, accusing him of not helping her friends. Zalthir, seeking quiet, invokes parental wisdom to calm the situation, and the Myconid falls asleep. He reflects on parental complaints while observing her slumber.

subject: acid vomit
fact: A violent, non-magical reaction experienced by Grygum after exposure to ritual magic. He vomits a wave of acid, which is not a spell he chose to cast but a consequence of the cult’s influence.

subject: Book in chief cultist’s hands
fact: A book held by the chief cultist is the source of the ritual chant used to summon Demogorgon and graft additional heads onto Stone Giants. Daz identifies it as the origin of the incantation, and Grygum later confirms its role in the cult’s magic.

subject: book in chief cultist's hands
fact: The book in the chief cultist's hands contains the ritual chant used by the Derro, and is referenced as the source of the incantation.
source_quote: Ah, the book in the chief cultist's hands.

subject: Maximilian’s Earthen Grasp
fact: A spell cast by Daz to trap Narrak in earthy tendrils. It successfully immobilizes the cult leader mid-ritual, causing him to scream about the inevitable spread of the curse.

subject: Maximillian’s Earthen Grasp
fact: Maximillian’s Earthen Grasp is cast by Daz to trap Narrak in the darkness, causing him to scream in rage.
source_quote: And so I cast Maximillian’s Earthen Grasp on where I think he is. ... Narrak screams in rage - “You cannot stop the inevitable... the curse spreads!”

subject: scorching rays
fact: A spell cast by Daz that summons three spears of flame to attack the Ettin. The spell is described as roaring like beasts and is fueled by Daz’s inner fury.

subject: scorching rays
fact: Daz casts three spears of flame as scorching rays, roaring with orange and red hues, aimed at the Ettin.
source_quote: Three spears of flame, raging hues of orange and red, appear above me. My skin prickles and sweats under their intense heat—but I am not frightened. I feel invigorated. Empowered. These are the vessels of my inner fury. They roar like fierce beasts as I hurl them toward the Ettin.

subject: statue of stone giant
fact: The statue is a two-headed stone giant, two feet tall, located on the platform, and is mistaken by Zalthir as being massive until he realizes its true size.
source_quote: I look at him confused, and I show him the statue on the platform. He sighs as he realizes it is only 2 feet tall.

subject: stone giant statue
fact: A two-headed stone statue of a Stone Giant, 2 feet tall, serves as the ritual focus for the cult’s grafting magic. Zalthir initially believes it to be massive, but realizes its true size, causing him to sigh in disbelief.

subject: white feather
fact: A white feather used by Narrak to cast a fear spell on the Ember Vanguard. It is the focus of the spell that induces terror in Thorin, Grygum, and Zalthir until Narrak is obscured by darkness.

subject: White Feather
fact: The white feather is a ritual focus used by Narrak to cast fear magic; it is a symbolic tool of control, linking the caster’s will to the emotional state of the Ember Vanguard.
source_quote: He takes a white feather and points at Thorin, Grygum, and Zalthir...

subject: white feather
fact: The white feather is used by Narrak to cast a fear spell on Thorin, Grygum, and Zalthir.
source_quote: He takes a white feather and points at Thorin, Grygum, and Zalthir, says the magic words, and the three members of the Ember Vanguard look terrified.

subject: Hgraam
fact: It is told that Hgraam should be able to reverse whatever ill effects on the Stone Giants, but the nature or source of this ability is not explained.
source_quote: We are told that Hgraam should be able to reverse whatever ill effects on the Stone Giants.

subject: Hgraam’s reversal capability
fact: The party’s belief that Hgraam can reverse the grafting magic on Stone Giants is an unconfirmed thread. No one has seen Hgraam, and the ritual’s damage remains unaddressed, leaving the fate of the giants uncertain.

subject: Invisibility to Derro
fact: The Derro fail to notice the party because they are actively avoiding detection by Narrak; this reveals a hierarchy of fear within the cult, where subordinates prioritize appeasing their leader over battlefield awareness.
source_quote: I finally understand why that Derro, who should have seen us, has not noticed us. He’s trying to avoid being seen by Narrak.

subject: nature of death and sleep
fact: A philosophical thread introduced by Pelek/Derro, who questions whether death is a form of sleep. The party does not resolve it, but it lingers as an existential undercurrent, especially as Pelek is bound and half-dead.

subject: Nature of death and sleep
fact: Pelek muses on whether death is a form of sleep, sparking philosophical interest in Grygum. The thread remains open, as no definitive answer is provided, and the group must continue their mission. The question lingers as a thematic undercurrent, especially given Pelek’s ghostly nature and the Myconid’s zombie conversion process.

subject: Pelek’s identity and control
fact: Pelek is a ghost possessing a Derro body and fears losing control of the host. The group ties him up as a precaution after a past betrayal led to a member’s death. Pelek questions whether death is a form of sleep, and his true intentions remain ambiguous. The thread remains open: is Pelek a trustworthy ally, a hidden threat, or something beyond comprehension?

subject: Rump-a-dump
fact: The Myconid insists Rump-a-dump is an unhappy sprout from their circle who needs to be brought back, but the reason for their unhappiness and connection to the ape-like creatures remains unresolved.
source_quote: Rump-a-dump is a sprout from my circle who is unhappy. We need to go talk to Rump-a-dump, find out what’s going on, and bring them back.

subject: Rump-a-dump’s fate
fact: The Myconid insists that Rump-a-dump, a member of her circle, is unhappy and needs to be retrieved. She claims Rump-a-dump is connected to a prior group of ape-like creatures and that no one should be killed because the targets are like her. Zalthir postpones the matter, but the Myconid remains emotionally fixated. The thread remains unresolved, with Zalthir uncertain whether the Myconids are friends or foes, and whether Rump-a-dump is a victim, a traitor, or something else.

subject: Rump-a-dump’s fate
fact: The Myconid’s unresolved plea about Rump-a-dump creates a narrative thread about nonviolence, conversion of enemies, and whether the myconids are allies or threats. Zalthir dismisses it, but the question remains open.

subject: the curse spreading
fact: Narrak’s final scream — 'The curse spreads!' — introduces a looming threat beyond the immediate battle. The nature of the curse is undefined, but its inevitability is emphasized, leaving the party to wonder what comes next.

subject: The Curse Spreads
fact: A lingering, inevitable curse tied to Demogorgon is spreading through the ritual; despite attempts to disrupt it, the curse persists, suggesting the cult’s doom is not just planned but predestined.
source_quote: Narrak screams in rage - 'You cannot stop the inevitable... the curse spreads!'

subject: after the battle
fact: The events occur immediately after the ritual’s end, with no specific calendar date given; time is measured in the sequence of combat and aftermath.

subject: elapsed time
fact: An hour passes between two events in the session.
source_quote: An hour later

subject: end of the conflict
fact: The conflict ends with all enemies dead, the ritual disrupted, and the group now holding incriminating evidence.
source_quote: All enemies are now dead... We have survived, and now we have leverage.

subject: session date
fact: The session occurs on the 5th day of the 2nd Tenday of Taraskh 1493 DR.
source_quote: On the 5th day of the 2nd Tenday of Taraskh 1493

subject: session end
fact: The events concluded with all enemies dead, the ritual ended, and the party now in possession of critical evidence. This marks the end of the current session and the beginning of a new strategic phase.

subject: acquisition of evidence
fact: The group acquires evidence proving the king's alliance with assassins, the Derro's support for Demogorgon, and an egg useful to the Keepers of the Flame or Red Dragon.
source_quote: We have the evidence that the king has been working with assassins to kill Eldeth’s clan, an egg that would help the Keepers of the Flame or the Red Dragon, and proof of the Derro perfidity and support for Demogorgon.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz cast Magic Missile, with two bolts striking a weaker Derro northeast of Grygum and the third hitting a stronger one.
source_quote: I call upon the simplest, yet most reliable, of my spells: Magic Missile. Two bolts streak towards the weaker Derro northeast of Grygum, and the third unerringly finds its mark on a stronger one

subject: Daz
fact: Daz commanded the earthen hand to squeeze Narrak further.
source_quote: I command the earthen hand to squeeze him further

subject: Daz
fact: Daz examined the two-foot-tall statue that turned one of Hargaam’s giants mad.
source_quote: I examine the two-foot-tall statue that is the ritual that turned one of Hargaam’s giants mad

subject: Daz
fact: Daz found a 'bunch of texts,' including 'The Rituals of the Two-Headed Beast,' confirming Narrak's role as orchestrator.
source_quote: I find a 'bunch of texts,' including 'The Rituals of the Two-Headed Beast,' which Narrak was reading. This confirms his role as the orchestrator.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz laughed at the idea of installing democracy, noting the Duergar's innate invisibility prevents civil debate.
source_quote: The idea of 'installing democracy' is floated, but I laugh. The Duergar and their innate invisibility create a level of paranoia that prevents any kind of civil debate.

subject: Daz
fact: Narrak attacked Grygum while restrained by Daz's Maximilian's Earthen Grasp.
source_quote: Narrak, the foolish cultist of this twisted scene, attacks Grygum, although still restrained by my Maximilian's Earthen Grasp

subject: Daz
fact: Narrak's voice boomed, 'fools, your sacrifice is but a step toward glory!'
source_quote: Narrak's voice, strangely cutting out, booms, 'fools, your sacrifice is but a step toward glory!'

subject: Daz
fact: The weaker Derro crumpled, dead instantly.
source_quote: The weaker Derro crumples, dead instantly

subject: Death of Gru Manga
fact: Gru Manga, the Ettin, was blinded, grappled, and finally killed by Zalthir. His death marked the neutralization of the party’s primary physical threat during the ritual.

subject: death of Gru Manga
fact: Gru Manga, the hulking Ettin, is killed by Zalthir after being grappled and struck repeatedly.
source_quote: I deliver the final, decisive blow. Gru Manga falls to the ground.

subject: death of Narrak
fact: Narrak is killed by Thorin, his final words being a desperate plea that the ritual cannot be undone.
source_quote: Thorin makes the final, grim decision to kill Narrak, his last words a desperate plea: 'No, the ritual cannot be undone!'

subject: Death of Narrak
fact: Narrak, the cultist leader, was killed by Thorin after a final plea that 'the ritual cannot be undone.' His death ended the ritual and confirmed the party’s control over the situation.

subject: democracy proposal rejected
fact: The idea of 'installing democracy' is laughed off due to Duergar innate invisibility breeding paranoia.
source_quote: installing democracy

subject: disruption of the ritual
fact: The ritual involving the two-headed stone giant statue is disrupted after the death of Narrak and the clearing of the cavern.
source_quote: the true scope of this strange ritual, involving the two-headed stone giant statue, now presents itself.

subject: Dissipation of Silent Spell
fact: The 'silent spell' cast earlier in the encounter has now dissipated, revealing the true scope of the ritual and allowing the party to perceive the stone giant statue and its connection to the madness.

subject: evidence of king's conspiracy
fact: Evidence exists that the king has been working with assassins to kill Eldeth’s clan.
source_quote: the king has been working with assassins to kill Eldeth’s clan

subject: Gru Manga's death
fact: Gru Manga was neutralized after being blinded, grappled, and struck repeatedly; his death marked the first major threat eliminated in the battle.

subject: Grygum

fact: Daz declares that the Myconids have nothing to fear from the spores because their effect is limited to melee range and only affects the dead.
source_quote: They have the power to release spores. The dangerous spores are only hazardous in melee range. They can only turn creatures they have killed into Zombies. Until you are dead, the zombie process doesn’t work.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz explains that Zuggtmoy’s corruption requires consent or bodily exchange, not natural infection.
source_quote: Daz explains that, as this is a Demonic curse, the method of propagation is not natural but magical. And in most likelihood requires consent or some exchange of bodily fluids.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz felt the mindless infinite eternity, and then just as much as he felt it, he was awake.
source_quote: I can feel that mindless infinite eternity, and then just as much as I feel it, I am awake.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz heard her promise to 'bloom beyond the bounds of flesh and time,' but recognized it as a perversion and an infection that steals your very self.
source_quote: It promises to 'bloom beyond the bounds of flesh and time,' but that bloom is a perversion, an infection that steals your very self.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz heard the Dark Lady ask, 'Do you fear the rot... or do you understand its song?'
source_quote: “Do you fear the rot... or do you understand its song?”

subject: Daz
fact: Daz heard the Dark Lady say, 'I am the pulse... beneath the stone… The breath... within the spore… To walk my dream... is to touch the heart… Of all that grows... and all that withers…'
source_quote: “I am the pulse... beneath the stone… The breath... within the spore… To walk my dream... is to touch the heart… Of all that grows... and all that withers…”

subject: Daz
fact: Daz heard the Dark Lady say, 'We would bloom beyond the bounds of flesh and high. You could have lingered with me and found your heart entwined with me, forever. As part of the endless mycelium.'
source_quote: We would bloom beyond the bounds of flesh and high. You could have lingered with me and found your heart entwined with me, forever. As part of the endless mycelium.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz heard the Dark Lady say, 'Welcome... wanderers of flesh and bone…'
source_quote: “Welcome... wanderers of flesh and bone…”

subject: Daz
fact: Daz heard the Dark Lady say, 'You stand at the edge... between waking and dreaming… Where life... and decay... entwine in endless dance…'
source_quote: “You stand at the edge... between waking and dreaming… Where life... and decay... entwine in endless dance…”

subject: Daz
fact: Daz hears Voosbur’s telepathic voice offering a 'cosmic garden' and 'mind-expanding journey'.
source_quote: Hey, beautiful souls, you’ve been groovin’ through the dark for a while now, yeah? Dig this — there’s a far-out place, a hidden trip where the Lady herself spins the vibes. It’s like the ultimate underground rave, but in your mind, man.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz held onto Thorin and Grygum, worried that they would follow, but they didn’t.
source_quote: I hold onto Thorin and Grygum, worried that they will follow. But they don’t.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz mutters in embarrassment while covering his face as Rump-a-dump questions cannibalism.
source_quote: Daz has his hands in his face, embarrassed and muttering, 'Overbrighters. They understand nothing about the complex ecology of the Underdark.'

subject: Daz
fact: Daz noticed Grygum and Thorin wake up and not appear to be covered in rotting mycelium.
source_quote: Grygum and Thorin wake up. And they don’t appear to be covered in some kind of rotting mycelium, so that’s good.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz noticed her crown, a halo of glowing spores drifting lazily, casting an otherworldly glow across that twisted fungal throne.
source_quote: I notice her crown, a halo of glowing spores drifting lazily, casting an otherworldly glow across that twisted fungal throne.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz noticed her eyes shine like twin lanterns, radiant yet hollow, drawing you in with a pull that feels like a cold, hungry grasp on your mind.
source_quote: Her eyes shine like twin lanterns, radiant yet hollow, drawing you in with a pull that feels more like a cold, hungry grasp on your mind.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz noticed her face, delicate features framed by tendrils of glowing mycelium that pulse with a sickening inner light.
source_quote: Her face is… unsettling. Delicate features, but framed by tendrils of glowing mycelium that pulse with a sickening inner light.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz noticed her smile is slow and knowing, a curve that speaks of ancient secrets and fathomless power she shouldn't wield.
source_quote: Her smile is slow and knowing, a curve that speaks of ancient secrets and fathomless power she shouldn't wield.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz noticed her voice is a haunting melody—at once soothing and commanding, like a lullaby sung by a hungry cave bear after it's caught its prey.
source_quote: Her voice, when it reaches my mind, is a haunting melody—at once soothing and commanding, like a lullaby sung by a hungry cave bear after it's caught its prey.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz noticed spores fly out of Voosbur, glow, and then the dancers walk towards the moss on the edge of the cavern and disappear.
source_quote: Spores fly out of him, they glow, and then the dancers walk towards the moss on the edge of the cavern and disappear.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz noticed that when she moves, the very air bends around her, and the stench of damp earth and decay follows in her wake.
source_quote: When she moves, it's as if the very air bends around her, and the stench of damp earth and decay follows in her wake.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz noticed the spectral figure at the center, a flicker of grim certainty in their depths.
source_quote: My eyes fix on the spectral figure at the center, a flicker of grim certainty in their depths.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz refuses to take Voosbur’s hand and observes the ecstatic madness of demon clerics with disinterest.
source_quote: I have seen the ecstatic drug-fueled madness of the cleric of demons, and have no interest in participating.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz says the spores are not an infection but a 'gift' and a 'wild ride' from the Lady.
source_quote: She’s no infection. She’s the mama of the mushrooms, the queen of the dreamscape, and she’s got a gift — a ticket to ride through her cosmic garden.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz shrugs and refuses Voosbur’s hand, observing the ecstatic madness of demon cultists with detachment.
source_quote: I shrug. I have seen the ecstatic drug-fueled madness of the cleric of demons, and have no interest in participating.

subject: Daz’s revelation on demonic propagation
fact: Daz explains that Zuggtmoy’s corruption is not natural infection but magical possession, requiring consent or bodily exchange — distinguishing it from mundane disease and reinforcing its status as a divine affront.
source_quote: Daz explains that, as this is a Demonic curse, the method of propagation is not natural but magical. And in most likelihood requires consent or some exchange of bodily fluids.

subject: Dream Realm Incursion
fact: Thorin and Grygum were pulled into a series of shifting, hallucinatory caverns created by Zuggtmoy’s magic, each representing a stage of fungal corruption—from serene glow to festering rot. These realms are not illusions but semi-realized psychic extensions of the Demon Queen’s will.
source_quote: I open my eyes and realize I am in a different cavern... This ain't natural, not by a long shot.

subject: fear of rot or understanding its song
fact: Do you fear the rot... or do you understand its song?
source_quote: Do you fear the rot... or do you understand its song?

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum holds Voosbur’s hand and is transported into the fungal dreamscapes.
source_quote: Grygum mutters, 'This reminds me of that time. Well, I’ll be going around to make sure it isn’t a bad trip.' And he too is holding onto Voosbur’s hand.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum looks at the Myconids and at Thorin, still confused by their behavior.
source_quote: Grygum looks at the Myconids and looks at me, and is still confused.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum recalls that others ate the mushrooms after arriving and became changed, but he did not.
source_quote: The others... I think they ate the silly mushrooms after we arrived.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum says he did not eat the mushrooms and thus remains uncorrupted.
source_quote: I did not eat them. That is why I am not... like this.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum says the Myconids’ dances and speech are unnatural and forced, unlike true Myconid behavior.
source_quote: These are not our old dances. And the way they speak... about 'the Lady's dream,' it is confusing. Stool does not understand it either. It is not the way of myconids. We do not dance like this. This is... forced.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum says the Myconids’ transformation was sudden and unnatural.
source_quote: Then Voosbur's spores came, and the next thing we knew, we were *here*. It was... a sudden jump.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum takes Voosbur’s hand and becomes affected by the spores.
source_quote: Grygum mutters, 'This reminds me of that time. Well, I’ll be going around to make sure it isn’t a bad trip.' And he too is holding onto Voosbur’s hand.

subject: Grygum’s memory of the transition
fact: Grygum recalls the sudden, unexplained transition from Neverlight Grove to the corrupted cavern — a key indicator that Zuggtmoy’s influence operates through spatial and perceptual distortion, not mere physical movement.
source_quote: Then Voosbur's spores came, and the next thing we knew, we were *here*. It was... a sudden jump.

subject: Initiation into the Fungal Dreamscape
fact: Thorin and Grygum have been initiated into Zuggtmoy’s sentient fungal dreamscape via hand contact with the Myconid, resulting in their physical displacement and psychological absorption into a hallucinatory, pulsing cavern of glowing fungi.
