fact: The Lost Tomb of Khaem is a hidden ruin on the path to the Neverlight Grove, believed to contain a powerful weapon. The group plans to visit it before proceeding, hoping to arm themselves against the dangers ahead.
source_quote: Perhaps we could first go to the Lost Tomb of Khaem, secure whatever weapon it has, and then go?

subject: Neverlight Grove
fact: The Neverlight Grove is a dangerous location inhabited by a mighty demon, according to Zalthir.
source_quote: I explain that there is a very dangerous and mighty demon there, and that we might not want to go there at all.

subject: Neverlight Grove
fact: The Neverlight Grove is a mysterious, dangerous location in the Underdark rumored to be corrupted by demonic influence. It draws Sarith and others through compulsion, despite its lethal reputation.
source_quote: There is a very dangerous and mighty demon there, and that we might not want to go there at all.

subject: Neverlight Grove
fact: The Neverlight Grove is a mysterious, demon-haunted location in the Underdark, believed by Sarith and Thorin to be a destination of compulsion; it is associated with demonic plots and unwilling vows.

subject: Whorlstone Caverns
fact: The Whorlstone Caverns are a location previously visited by the party, where Sarith was mysteriously drawn to dancing Myconids. This experience now influences his compulsion toward the Neverlight Grove.
source_quote: The strange compulsion that drew him to the dancing Myconids in the Whorlstone Caverns draws him to the grove.

subject: Whorlstone Caverns
fact: The Whorlstone Caverns are where Sarith previously encountered dancing Myconids.
source_quote: The strange compulsion that drew him to the dancing Myconids in the Whorlstone Caverns draws him to the grove.

subject: bloodsucking giant mosquitoes
fact: Bloodsucking giant mosquitoes fall from the roof on the third day of travel.
source_quote: some bloodsucking giant mosquitoes fall from the roof.

subject: dead grey ghosts
fact: Dead grey ghosts litter the streets of Gracklstugh.
source_quote: The dead grey ghosts litter the street

subject: giant mosquito count
fact: Some bloodsucking giant mosquitoes fall from the roof on the third day.
source_quote: some bloodsucking giant mosquitoes fall from the roof

subject: Giant Mosquitoes
fact: Bloodsucking giant mosquitoes fall from the ceiling of the Underdark during the party’s journey; they are swiftly killed but represent the pervasive dangers of the environment.

subject: Themberchaud
fact: Themberchaud is a young red dragon, physically large but emotionally stunted and physically softened by pampering. He lacks the predatory grace, sharp claws, or battle-worn scales of a true dragon. His flight is clumsy, his landing ungainly, and his behavior childish. He is not a threat by nature, but his manipulation makes him unpredictable. He is a creature of power rendered harmless by his role.
source_quote: I need to show you my realm.

subject: Themberchaud
fact: Themberchaud is a young red dragon, physically oversized and poorly trained, whose scales are polished and claws painted; he does not hunt and behaves like a pampered pet, yet breathes fire with terrifying power when commanded.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz is a cautious member of the group who fears dragon flight and the consequences of being mistaken for the Ember Vanguard; he notices the Duergar’s panic and understands the weight of perception in their survival.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz is a cautious, observant member of the party who fears collateral damage from dragon-led chaos. He is relieved when the group avoids destructive decisions and relies on his own magical ability (Misty Step) to survive falls. He notices the dragon’s lack of control and the vulnerability of his companions.
source_quote: I do not want to have a dragon destroy a city while I am on its back.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz is a perceptive member of the group whose presence triggers panic among the Duergar, leading them to believe the group is the Ember Vanguard. He is not impressed by Themberchaud’s theatrics and notes the Duergar’s disdain for him.
source_quote: The Duergar are rolling their eyes. They don’t take him as seriously as he takes himself.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz observes that Themberchaud is a very large but not very old dragon.
source_quote: A young dragon would not have enough space for our gang, but this is a very large dragon. Not a very old dragon, a very large dragon.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz uses Misty Step to avoid falling off Themberchaud during a sharp turn.
source_quote: And then I am falling. Not for long, that’s what Misty Step is for.

subject: Eldeth
fact: Eldeth expresses surprise that Grygum can cast Mending.
source_quote: Eldeth looks at him, “Really?”

subject: Eldeth
fact: Eldeth is a pragmatic member of the group who understands the rarity of the mending spell among spellcasters due to naval warfare tactics; she is observant and skeptical of Grygum’s sudden proficiency.

subject: Eldeth
fact: Eldeth will demand to see what the party found, and sharing it will trigger violence.
source_quote: We have passes, but Eldeth will demand to see what we found. And if we share with her what we found, that will trigger violence.

subject: Errde
fact: Errde is a captain who will be warned about the party’s presence by the Duergar Stone Guard.
source_quote: I must warn Captain Errde at once!

subject: Gartokkar
fact: Gartokkar is a warning voice who has alerted the group that everyone in Gracklstugh is on edge and actively searching for the Ember Vanguard. His reports shape the group’s perception of their false identity.
source_quote: The Stone Guard is looking for the Ember Vanguard, the powerful mercenary group, and the Grey Ghosts are looking for the Ember Vanguard, and the Deep King is worried.

subject: Gartokkar
fact: Gartokkar is referenced as a source of warning about the state of Gracklstugh.
source_quote: Gartokkar has warned us that everyone is on edge.

subject: Gartokkar
fact: Gartokkar warned the party that everyone in Gracklstugh is on edge.
source_quote: Gartokkar has warned us that everyone is on edge.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum is a cleric who acts with ritual precision and symbolic intent. He deputizes the Duergar guard with a caltrop as a token of their mission, and later suggests scuttling the boat — showing a blend of faith and pragmatism.
source_quote: This is a symbol of our mission. Guard it and keep it secret.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum is a half-orc cleric of Bahamut who has escaped multiple prisons.
source_quote: Here I am, Gyrgum, half-orc cleric of Bahamut, and Gracklstugh is what makes an orc camp look pretty. ... I seem to keep having to escape from some prison, whether it’s the prisons on the overbrite, or the prisons of the Drow, or the prisons of the Duergar.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum is a half-orc cleric of Bahamut who repeatedly escapes imprisonment and believes he has a gift for it; he is deeply disturbed by the manipulation of Themberchaud and seeks to protect secrets that could destroy Gracklstugh.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum is a half-orc cleric of Bahamut, experienced in escapes and prison breaks, deeply aware of the manipulation of powerful beings. He is pragmatic, spiritually appalled by Themberchaud’s degradation, and attempts to navigate the dragon’s ego with flattery and subtle truth. He volunteers to take risks, including betting on his own survival.
source_quote: You’re not one of the peons who understands the little things. But we are as little as you get, and we can find the little things that are big for us.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum knows that spellcasters who can cast mending are rare because they are targeted first in naval combat.
source_quote: In naval combat, the first person you kill is the mender. Because until you kill him, you can’t sink the ship. So finding a spell caster who can cast it is rare.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum recalls escaping from prisons on the overbrite, the Drow, and the Duergar, and believes he has a gift for it.
source_quote: I seem to keep having to escape from some prison, whether it’s the prisons on the overbrite, or the prisons of the Drow, or the prisons of the Duergar. I have a gift for this. I suppose.

subject: Jimjar
fact: Jimjar bets an empty shell gem that the circle of joy will become a circle of unwilling vows.
source_quote: I'll bet you an empty shell gem that this circle of joy will reveal itself to be a circle of unwilling vows before you leave it.

subject: Jimjar
fact: Jimjar is a ghoul who makes morbid wagers and seems to intuit the group’s impending doom; he bets on Grygum’s survival and predicts their journey will become a circle of unwilling vows.

subject: Jimjar
fact: Jimjar is a ghoul with a morbid sense of humor, quick to make bets about survival in dangerous situations. He openly questions Grygum’s likelihood of surviving peril, treating life-and-death moments as entertainment.
source_quote: Anyone want to make a bet that Grygum is going to survive?

subject: Jimjar
fact: Jimjar is a reckless gambler who makes absurd bets with cryptic, prophetic phrasing. He recently wagered an empty shell gem that a 'circle of joy' will become a 'circle of unwilling vows,' unsettling the group.
source_quote: I'll bet you an empty shell gem that this circle of joy will reveal itself to be a circle of unwilling vows before you leave it.

subject: Jimjar
fact: Jimjar throws a rope to catch Grygum after he falls off Themberchaud.
source_quote: Jimjar throws a rope and catches the falling orc.

subject: Rump-a-dump
fact: Rump-a-dump insists the Neverlight Grove cannot be corrupted because their sovereign would not allow it.
source_quote: Zalthir, the circle cannot be corrupted. “Our sovereign would never let that happen.”

subject: Rump-a-dump
fact: Rump-a-dump is a childlike member of the group who believes in the inviolability of sacred circles and refuses to acknowledge danger. He speaks with naive certainty about his sovereign’s protection.
source_quote: Zalthir, the circle cannot be corrupted. Our sovereign would never let that happen.

subject: Sarith
fact: Sarith is a mysterious member of the group driven by compulsion; he is drawn to the Neverlight Grove by the same force that led him to the Myconids, suggesting he is under supernatural influence.

subject: Sarith
fact: Sarith is compelled to go to the Neverlight Grove by the same force that drew him to the Myconids in the Whorlstone Caverns.
source_quote: The strange compulsion that drew him to the dancing Myconids in the Whorlstone Caverns draws him to the grove.

subject: Sarith
fact: Sarith is driven by strange compulsions, previously drawn to Myconid dancing in the Whorlstone Caverns and now compelled to reach the Neverlight Grove. He is intuitive, not logical, and insists on leaving the boat despite the risk.
source_quote: The path to the Neverlight Grove goes past the Lost Tomb of Khaem. But we must leave the boat here.

subject: spellcaster rarity
fact: Spellcasters who can cast mending are rare due to naval combat tactics.
source_quote: spell casters who could cast mending were in high demand by the navies. And so spellcasters tended to avoid learning that spell. See, in naval combat, the first person you kill is the mender. Because until you kill him, you can’t sink the ship. So finding a spell caster who can cast it is rare.

subject: Stool
fact: Stool wants to go to the Neverlight Grove with the party.
source_quote: Rump-a-dump and Stool want to go to the Neverlight Grove.

subject: Themberchaud
fact: Themberchaud believes he is a powerful Wyrmsmith in charge of Gracklstugh, though he is in reality a glorified lighter for the Duergar.
source_quote: I am Themberchaud the Wyrmsmith, bringer of flame! ... He thinks he's in charge. Yet, I know the truth: he's merely a 'glorified lighter' for the Duergar forges.

subject: Themberchaud
fact: Themberchaud believes he is in charge of Gracklstugh, though he is merely a glorified lighter.
source_quote: It's clear that he "thinks he's in charge". Yet, I know the truth: he's merely a "glorified lighter" for the Duergar forges.

subject: Themberchaud
fact: Themberchaud breathes fire at a forge while declaring himself "Bringer of flame!".
source_quote: I am Themberchaud the Wyrmsmith, bringer of flame!"

subject: Themberchaud
fact: Themberchaud claims the party are his agents bound by his protection.
source_quote: we are his “agents, bound by my protection."

subject: Themberchaud
fact: Themberchaud declares he will provide express service to where the party must go next.
source_quote: he offers his "express service to where you must go next"

subject: Themberchaud
fact: Themberchaud is a dragon who believes himself to be the Wyrmsmith, a divine forger of flame. He loudly proclaims his identity, breathes fire at forges, and insists on dramatic flybys — all while being completely oblivious to the group’s strategic concerns.
source_quote: I am Themberchaud the Wyrmsmith, bringer of flame!

subject: Themberchaud
fact: Themberchaud is a young red dragon known as the Wyrmsmith of Gracklstugh.
source_quote: It's Themberchaud, the Wyrmsmith of Gracklstugh

subject: Themberchaud
fact: Themberchaud is a young red dragon, pampered and polished by the Duergar, serving as a glorified lighter for their forges; he believes himself to be a sovereign Wyrmsmith and is utterly unaware of how ridiculous and controlled he appears to others.

subject: Themberchaud
fact: Themberchaud is a young red dragon, pampered and polished, serving as a glorified lighter for the Duergar forges in Gracklstugh. He believes himself to be a powerful ruler but is deeply manipulated, unaware of his true role. His scales are meticulously kept shiny, his claws painted, and his demeanor childish and vain. He has a second chin and speaks with inflated authority, yet lacks strategic understanding. He thinks he is in charge of his realm, but is merely a tool.
source_quote: Climb aboard, unless you wish to question the will of your wormsmith.

subject: Themberchaud
fact: Themberchaud proclaims the cavern he flies through is "my town".
source_quote: proclaiming it "my town"

subject: Themberchaud
fact: Themberchaud shouts at the party to climb aboard or question the will of the Wyrmsmith.
source_quote: Climb aboard, unless you wish to question the will of your wormsmith"

subject: Themberchaud
fact: Themberchaud’s maturity has been adversely affected by the peculiar role he serves in Gracklstugh as a glorified lighter.
source_quote: Themberchaud’s maturity has been adversely affected by the peculiar role he serves in Gracklstugh as a glorified lighter. I wonder why the Duergar chose a Red Dragon? Surely magic would be cheaper and less dangerous.

subject: Themberchaud
fact: Themberchaud’s scales are shiny and his claws are painted, indicating he is pampered and deliberately kept from appearing fearsome.
source_quote: His scales are shiny. Someone has been carefully keeping them polished. And his claws are painted. They have none of the telltale signs of rending and destruction that they should have.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin agrees with Zalthir that they should have tied themselves to Themberchaud’s back.
source_quote: I agree with Zalthir that we really should have tied ourselves up rather than just sit on Themberchaud’s back.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin is a cynical but loyal member of the group who understands the absurdity of their situation; he supports deception to survive, quotes giant proverbs, and is drawn to dangerous choices despite knowing their risks.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin is a giant who believes in bold, chaotic action, often disregarding consequences. He recently shouted about a 'flyby to the docks' and invoked an old saying: 'To save the village, you must smash the village.' He has shown a pattern of ignoring advice and rolling the dice on dangerous decisions.
source_quote: Alright, one more flyby and to the docks!

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin is skeptical and reluctant to share information, preferring secrecy. He mutters dismissively about revealing everything, indicating a distrustful and guarded nature, but does not actively oppose the group’s decisions.
source_quote: We should just tell him everything. Nah.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin mutters the giant saying, "To save the village, you must smash the village."
source_quote: Thorin mutters an old giant saying, "To save the village, you must smash the village."

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir concludes that killing the Duergar Stone Guard is necessary to avoid mass bloodshed.
source_quote: In the interest of avoiding mass bloodshed, I think we must.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir is a pragmatic and observant member of the group who recognizes the deception surrounding Themberchaud and exploits the Duergar’s fear of the Ember Vanguard to avoid bloodshed; he carries the group’s most dangerous secrets and values moral restraint over violence.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir is a seasoned observer of powerful, egotistical figures, recognizing Themberchaud’s need for face-saving gestures. He intervenes with a strategic lie to redirect the dragon’s attention toward the docks, using the dragon’s own sense of superiority to manipulate him into action.
source_quote: There was an attack on the docks, so there might be new intelligence. Your agents didn’t miss it; they just haven’t been there recently.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir is a thoughtful, weary leader who weighs moral consequences and seeks to minimize bloodshed. He recognizes the group's false identity as the Ember Vanguard and uses it strategically. He is deeply aware of the secrets they carry and finds comfort in knowing they prevented mass destruction in Gracklstugh.
source_quote: The secrets we carried — of the Deep King’s plots, the corrupted dragon egg, and the lurking demonic plots — could have provoked mass death and destruction. And we took those secrets with us.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir notices Duergar panic upon seeing Daz, mistaking the party for the Ember Vanguard.
source_quote: They recognized us. Look at their panic. They weren’t afraid of Themberchaud but when they saw Daz, they suddenly freaked out. They think we are the Ember Vanguard.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir recalls that spellcasters who can cast Mending are rare because navies kill them first.
source_quote: spell casters who could cast mending were in high demand by the navies. And so spellcasters tended to avoid learning that spell. See, in naval combat, the first person you kill is the mender. Because until you kill him, you can’t sink the ship. So finding a spell caster who can cast it is rare.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir suggests exploiting the Duergar’s belief that the party is the Ember Vanguard.
source_quote: They think we are this all-powerful group; we take advantage of it.

subject: bet value
fact: Jimjar wagers an empty shell gem on the outcome of the circle's nature.
source_quote: I'll bet you an empty shell gem that this circle of joy will reveal itself to be a circle of unwilling vows before you leave it.

subject: Caltrop
fact: A caltrop is given by Grygum to the Duergar Stone Guard as a symbolic token of their mission; it serves as a ruse to buy time and avoid violence, representing the group’s deceptive strategy.

subject: caltrop
fact: A caltrop is used by Grygum as a symbolic token of the group’s mission. He gives it to the Duergar guard to bind him to secrecy, transforming a mundane object into a sacred relic of deception.
source_quote: This is a symbol of our mission. Guard it and keep it secret.

subject: caltrop
fact: Grygum gives a caltrop to the Duergar Stone Guard as a symbol of their mission.
source_quote: Grygum pulls out a caltrop, “This is a symbol of our mission. Guard it and keep it secret.”

subject: empty shell gem
fact: An empty shell gem is the wagered item in Jimjar’s bizarre bet about the Neverlight Grove. It represents his tendency toward cryptic gambling and foreshadows a future, possibly cursed, ritual.
source_quote: I'll bet you an empty shell gem that this circle of joy will reveal itself to be a circle of unwilling vows before you leave it.

subject: empty shell gem
fact: Jimjar bets an empty shell gem on the outcome of the party’s journey to the Neverlight Grove.
source_quote: I'll bet you an empty shell gem that this circle of joy will reveal itself to be a circle of unwilling vows before you leave it.

subject: Empty Shell Gem
fact: Jimjar wagers an empty shell gem that the party’s journey will become a circle of unwilling vows; the bet is accepted by Grygum, foreshadowing a binding magical consequence.

subject: Themberchaud’s painted claws
fact: Themberchaud’s claws are painted, a deliberate cosmetic choice that contradicts their intended function as weapons of destruction. They show no signs of battle, wear, or use — instead appearing decorative, like a toy’s. This detail symbolizes his complete domestication and the Duergar’s psychological control.
source_quote: his claws are painted. They have none of the telltale signs of rending and destruction that they should have.

subject: Themberchaud’s polished scales
fact: Themberchaud’s scales are meticulously polished to a high shine, an unnatural and obsessive grooming that renders him visually incongruous with a true dragon. This detail reflects his role as a status symbol rather than a warrior — a pet maintained for appearance, not power.
source_quote: his scales are shiny. Someone has been carefully keeping them polished.

subject: attack on the docks
fact: An unconfirmed attack on the docks of the Dark Lake District is the proposed lead for investigation. Zalthir suggests it as a plausible reason to go there, but its actual existence is uncertain — possibly fabricated to appease Themberchaud’s ego. The truth of the attack remains unresolved and critical to the mission.
source_quote: There was an attack on the docks, so there might be new intelligence.

subject: circle of unwilling vows
fact: Jimjar’s bet implies a hidden, possibly demonic ritual awaiting the party in the Neverlight Grove — one that will force them into binding, unwilling oaths. The nature of this thread is cryptic, but its implications are ominous.
source_quote: I'll bet you an empty shell gem that this circle of joy will reveal itself to be a circle of unwilling vows before you leave it.

subject: corrupted dragon egg
fact: The party carries a secret: a corrupted dragon egg, likely tied to the Deep King’s plots. Its existence could trigger catastrophic events if revealed, and its fate remains unresolved as they flee deeper into the Underdark.
source_quote: The secrets we carried — of the Deep King’s plots, the corrupted dragon egg, and the lurking demonic plots — could have provoked mass death and destruction.

subject: Corrupted Dragon Egg
fact: The party carries the secret of a corrupted dragon egg, a threat capable of mass destruction; they have chosen to conceal it from Gracklstugh, making this a moral burden with potential future consequences.

subject: Deep King’s plots
fact: The party carries the secret of the Deep King’s plots from Gracklstugh.
source_quote: The secrets we carried - of the Deep King’s plots, the corrupted dragon egg, and the lurking demonic plots - could have provoked mass death and destruction.

subject: demon egg
fact: The party carries the secret of a corrupted dragon egg from Gracklstugh.
source_quote: The secrets we carried - of the Deep King’s plots, the corrupted dragon egg, and the lurking demonic plots - could have provoked mass death and destruction.

subject: demonic plots
fact: The party carries the secret of lurking demonic plots from Gracklstugh.
source_quote: The secrets we carried - of the Deep King’s plots, the corrupted dragon egg, and the lurking demonic plots - could have provoked mass death and destruction.

subject: The Ember Vanguard
fact: The Ember Vanguard is a feared mercenary group that the Duergar and others believe to be real, though the party is merely impersonating them.
source_quote: They think we are the Ember Vanguard. ... I know you, you are the Ember Vanguard! I must warn Captain Errde at once!

subject: The Lost Tomb of Khaem
fact: The Lost Tomb of Khaem is a location the party plans to visit for a weapon, but its contents and dangers are unverified.
source_quote: Perhaps we could first go to the Lost Tomb of Khaem, secure whatever weapon it has, and then go?

subject: Themberchaud’s true role
fact: The party is aware that Themberchaud is not a sovereign but a glorified lighter for the Duergar, yet they must conceal this knowledge to survive. His delusions of power and the group’s need to manipulate him create a fragile, high-stakes tension. Uncovering his true function could destabilize the Duergar’s control — or trigger his wrath.
source_quote: My Bahamut-trained sensibilities are appalled at how they treat Themberchaud.

subject: Themberchaud’s True Role
fact: The party knows Themberchaud is a manipulated tool of the Duergar, not a sovereign Wyrmsmith; they have chosen not to reveal this truth, creating a moral tension between dragonkind’s dignity and their survival.

subject: Themberchaud’s true role
fact: Themberchaud is a Red Dragon forced into the role of a glorified lighter for the Duergar, though his true power and status are ignored.
source_quote: He's merely a 'glorified lighter' for the Duergar forges. My Bahamut-trained sensibilities are appalled at how they treat Themberchaud.

subject: The Neverlight Grove
fact: The Neverlight Grove is a dangerous location tied to demons and mushrooms, and its true nature is unknown to the party.
source_quote: Zalthir, the circle cannot be corrupted. 'Our sovereign would never let that happen.' ... I hope no one will take him up on his weird bet, but Grygum does.

subject: The Unwilling Vows
fact: Jimjar’s bet suggests the party’s journey to the Neverlight Grove will bind them to unwilling magical oaths; Grygum has accepted the wager, making this a looming, unresolved plot thread.

subject: 2nd day of the 2nd tenday of Myrkhul, 1495
fact: The date when the group entered the fungal forest and encountered the Shriekers. It marks a transition from the Faerzress cavern to a new biome and the first major non-undead environmental threat.
source_quote: 2nd day of the 2nd tenday of Myrkhul, 1495

subject: 2nd day of the 2nd tenday of Myrkhul, 1495
fact: The day the group entered the fungal forest, encountered shriekers, and tested the Faerzress crystals against them. A day of revelation and anticlimax.
source_quote: 2nd day of the 2nd tenday of Myrkhul, 1495

subject: 3rd day of the 2nd tenday of Myrkhul, 1495
fact: The date when the group collected more crystals and Jimjar made a bet with Grygum about their utility. This moment highlights the group’s growing reliance on the crystals and their emerging sense of strategy.
source_quote: 3rd day of the 2nd tenday of Myrkhul, 1495

subject: 3rd day of the 2nd tenday of Myrkhul, 1495
fact: The day the group discovered another crystal-rich cave and Jimjar initiated a bet about the crystals’ utility.
source_quote: 3rd day of the 2nd tenday of Myrkhul

subject: 5th day of the 2nd tenday of Myrkhul, 1495
fact: The date when the party reached the Lost Tomb of Khaem, encountered the trapped voice, fought the Spectres, and discovered the hidden passage. It marks the climax of their journey into the tomb’s depths and the first direct confrontation with its undead guardians.
source_quote: 5th day of the 2nd tenday of Myrkhul, 1495

subject: 5th day of the 2nd tenday of Myrkhul, 1495
fact: The day Zalthir’s narrative begins, marking a shift in perspective and potentially the start of internal group tension.
source_quote: 5th day of the 2nd tenday of Myrkhul

subject: elapsed time
fact: An hour passes between two events in the session.
source_quote: An hour later

subject: Session Date
fact: The events occur during a session of exploration in the Underdark, following a long descent and sustained vigilance.
source_quote: We descend a dusty staircase... We arrive at a large double door... The stairs finally give way to a shrine...

subject: session date
fact: The session occurs on the 7th day of the 1st tenday of Myrkhul, 1495 DR.
source_quote: On the 5th day of the 2nd Tenday of Taraskh 1493

subject: session time
fact: The events occur after a prolonged dungeon delve, with the party now at a critical juncture requiring rest, investigation, and decision-making before proceeding further into the Underdark.
source_quote: I'm gonna need a long rest here pretty soon... 'Is this, would this be a good time for us to take a… Long rest. By chance?' I inquire, hopefully.

subject: arrival at tomb entrance
fact: Sarith nods yes, this is the way. Of course, it does. Nothing in the Underdark is ever truly straightforward, yet here, a trapped voice leads us exactly where we intended to go, The Lost Tomb of Khaem.
source_quote: Sarith nods yes, this is the way. Of course, it does. Nothing in the Underdark is ever truly straightforward, yet here, a trapped voice leads us exactly where we intended to go, The Lost Tomb of Khaem.

subject: Baedora
fact: Baedora explained that demons attacked, the Drow fought back, and they ran to survive.
source_quote: “That it was demons that attacked. The Drow fought back. We ran. Figured we were more likely to stay alive away from Drow and Demons.”

subject: baedora's survival
fact: Baedora explains, 'That it was demons that attacked. The Drow fought back. We ran. Figured we were more likely to stay alive away from Drow and Demons.'
source_quote: Baedora explains, 'That it was demons that attacked. The Drow fought back. We ran. Figured we were more likely to stay alive away from Drow and Demons.'

subject: bet on crystal utility
fact: Jimjar shouts, 'Want to make a bet?' And so I turn to him, 'Wanna bet that these crystals will be useful?'
source_quote: Jimjar shouts, 'Want to make a bet?' And so I turn to him, 'Wanna bet that these crystals will be useful?'

subject: chill and moan
fact: A chill emanates from everywhere at once. Rime creeps across surfaces, and my breath plumes before me in the suddenly frigid air. A moan, pained and distant, rises with the wind.
source_quote: A chill emanates from everywhere at once. Rime creeps across surfaces, and my breath plumes before me in the suddenly frigid air. A moan, pained and distant, rises with the wind.

subject: Collection of Netherese treasure
fact: The group opens the sarcophagi and collects mummified remains, tattered burial garments, and Netherese artifacts worth great sums of gold and collector value, before proceeding deeper into the tomb.
source_quote: We open the sarcophagi. Each sarcophagus contains mummified remains, the tattered remnants of ancient burial garments, and treasure of Netherese origin. They are worth a great deal as gold, and perhaps even more to the right collector.

subject: crystal collection
fact: Before we leave the cave, we take as many crystals as we can.
source_quote: Before we leave the cave, we take as many crystals as we can.

subject: crystal collection
fact: We have collected so many strays that one more won’t harm us.
source_quote: We have collected so many strays that one more won’t harm us.

subject: Crystal Test Against Shriekers
fact: The group threw a Faerzress crystal at a shrieker, expecting a magical reaction, but the shrieking continued unaltered, revealing the creature’s biological nature and the crystals’ lack of offensive power.
source_quote: The crystal sailed through the air... and clattered against a broad fungal cap. And the shrieking... didn't change. It was a bit of an anticlimax, really. Just shrieking.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz and the group smashed the cavern and crystals to hide their tracks as if a monster had attacked.
source_quote: To hide our tracks, we smash the cavern and the crystals, as if some monster had attacked, not escaped slaves who took crystals that shone in the darkness.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz cast Magic Missile, striking two Spectres with three bolts.
source_quote: With a familiar incantation, I conjure the shimmering darts of pure force. Magic Missile. Two bolts streak through the darkness, finding their mark on one Spectre. Another bolt follows, striking a second Spectre.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz checked an altar and found nothing of arcane significance.
source_quote: Daz checks an altar, finding nothing of arcane significance, another dead end for now.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz decided to use magic missiles.
source_quote: Magic missiles it is,

subject: Daz
fact: Daz felt necrotic damage as one Spectre’s icy touch drained his life force.
source_quote: One Spectre lunges at me, its chilling form passing through my defenses. A jolt of cold, raw energy courses through me, necrotic damage, and I feel my very life force diminish.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz felt twice as much necrotic damage from a second Spectre's attack.
source_quote: Before I can fully process it, another Spectre attacks, a more potent drain this time, twice as much necrotic damage, and my strength wanes further.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz heard the same soft, feminine voice from before, pleading in his mind.
source_quote: "No, you must save me!" a soft, feminine voice cries out in my mind. It's the same voice from when we entered the tomb, trapped, pleading.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz inquired, "Is this, would this be a good time for us to take a… Long rest. By chance?"
source_quote: "Is this, would this be a good time for us to take a… Long rest. By chance?" I inquire, hopefully.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz invited Fuurm and Baedora to join the group.
source_quote: And so I invite them to join our group.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz knew that if they rested, the Spectres would return, and might pursue them.
source_quote: If we rest, we will find them here when we come back. And although they may just stay here, they may also pursue us.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz muttered, "I'm gonna need a long rest here pretty soon," a desperate plea for recovery.
source_quote: "I'm gonna need a long rest here pretty soon," I mutter, the words barely audible, a desperate plea for recovery.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz noticed fist-sized chunks of quartz crystals erupting from the wall, shedding dim ten-foot radiance.
source_quote: Fist-sized chunks of quartz crystals erupted from the wall, shedding a dim ten-foot radiance.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz noticed the air grow thick with the familiar, subtle hum of the Faerzress.
source_quote: We turned down yet another passageway, and the air grew thick with a familiar, subtle hum, the Faerzress.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz observed four Spectres hovering, incorporeal and menacing.
source_quote: Four Spectres now hover, incorporeal and menacing.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz observed the wall suffused with the arcane glowing magic of the Faerzress.
source_quote: Ahead, there was no longer the rough-hewn stone, but an area suffused with the arcane glowing magic of the Faerzress.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz opened the sarcophagi and found mummified remains, tattered burial garments, and Netherese treasure.
source_quote: We open the sarcophagi. Each sarcophagus contains mummified remains, the tattered remnants of ancient burial garments, and treasure of Netherese origin.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz realized the adventure was not about escape, but about learning and exploration.
source_quote: But now that we have been wandering through the world, I realize it’s an opportunity to learn and explore.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz recognized the Underdark not as a place to flee, but as a place to explore and learn.
source_quote: I never saw the Underdark for what it is, a place to explore and learn.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz remembered that many undead creatures return after being destroyed if the central evil force remains.
source_quote: I remember that many such creatures will return after being destroyed when the central evil force that created them remains.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz remembered that they are resistant to fire.
source_quote: Daz contemplates a Fireball, but then remembers that they are resistant to fire.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz saw two desperate humans in a corner and surmised they were escapees from the Drow.
source_quote: In a corner were two desperate humans. I stare at them and quickly surmise they are escapees from the Drow.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz suggested collecting crystals and looking around.
source_quote: “Let’s collect some of these crystals and look around.”

subject: Daz
fact: Daz understood this journey as an escape from a previous worldview, not to another place.
source_quote: And now I know this journey not as an escape to another place, but instead as an escape from a previous worldview.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz wanted to experience and explore the crystals, no longer seeing them as obstacles.
source_quote: Before, this would have been yet another obstacle, another exotic backdrop to our desperate flight to safety, but now I wanted to experience and explore.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz was hoping to see new things.
source_quote: I was hoping to see new things.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz wondered if Fuurm had skills as a rogue, fighter, wizard, or cleric.
source_quote: I look at him and wonder if he has any skills as a rogue, a fighter, a wizard, or a cleric, but he explains that he is just a farmer.

subject: daz's long rest plea
fact: 'I'm gonna need a long rest here pretty soon,' I mutter, the words barely audible, a desperate plea for recovery.
source_quote: 'I'm gonna need a long rest here pretty soon,' I mutter, the words barely audible, a desperate plea for recovery.

subject: daz's magic missile
fact: Magic Missile. Two bolts streak through the darkness, finding their mark on one Spectre. Another bolt follows, striking a second Spectre.
source_quote: Magic Missile. Two bolts streak through the darkness, finding their mark on one Spectre. Another bolt follows, striking a second Spectre.

subject: daz's necrotic damage
fact: A jolt of cold, raw energy courses through me, necrotic damage, and I feel my very life force diminish. Before I can fully process it, another Spectre attacks, a more potent drain this time, twice as much necrotic damage, and my strength wanes further.
source_quote: A jolt of cold, raw energy courses through me, necrotic damage, and I feel my very life force diminish. Before I can fully process it, another Spectre attacks, a more potent drain this time, twice as much necrotic damage, and my strength wanes further.

subject: Defeat of the four Spectres
fact: The four Spectres are defeated through combined efforts: Daz's Magic Missile strikes two, Zalthir punches and kills two, Grygum's turning attempt fails, and the group survives the necrotic drain from the undead touch.
source_quote: Magic Missile... two bolts... striking a second Spectre... Zalthir... kills one, then another... Grygum... tries to turn them, but the Spectres resist... One Spectre lunges at me... twice as much necrotic damage...

subject: discovery of hidden passage
fact: The northeast sarcophagus rests on hidden stone rollers. A possible secret, a hidden passage. This is it.
source_quote: The northeast sarcophagus rests on hidden stone rollers. A possible secret, a hidden passage. This is it.

subject: Discovery of the hidden passage
fact: The hidden passage is revealed when Thorin pushes the northeast sarcophagus on hidden rollers, while Zalthir envelops the area in magical darkness, allowing the group to access the true tomb.
source_quote: The northeast sarcophagus rests on hidden stone rollers... I call forth the shadows, plunging the area around the sarcophagus into a sphere of magical darkness... Thorin... pushes the heavy sarcophagus aside. The stone grinds, revealing... a hole. The true tomb, perhaps.

subject: drow origin
fact: My whole life, I was a Drow of Menzoberranzan. Trapped in the formalities of ritual and expectations, trying to avoid the predations of the Cult of Lolth and the machinations of the Noble Houses.
source_quote: My whole life, I was a Drow of Menzoberranzan. Trapped in the formalities of ritual and expectations, trying to avoid the predations of the Cult of Lolth and the machinations of the Noble Houses.

subject: Eldeth
fact: Eldeth hid our tracks for two days, during which all they could see were the dark passages.
source_quote: For two days, Eldeth has been hiding our tracks for two days, where all we could see when we could see was the dark passages.

subject: Eldeth
fact: Eldeth was worried that messing with the environment made it easier for the Drow to track them.
source_quote: Eldeth is worried; she’s reasonably convinced we have thrown the Drow off our tracks, but every time we mess with the environment, we make it easier for them.

subject: eldeth's track hiding
fact: For two days, Eldeth has been hiding our tracks for two days, where all we could see when we could see was the dark passages.
source_quote: For two days, Eldeth has been hiding our tracks for two days, where all we could see when we could see was the dark passages.

subject: escapee identification
fact: I stare at them and quickly surmise they are escapees from the Drow.
source_quote: I stare at them and quickly surmise they are escapees from the Drow.

subject: escapee origin
fact: He explains that his name is Fuurm Coppernose, or Copper to his friends, who had lost his sister and went looking for her in the Underdark.
source_quote: He explains that his name is Fuurm Coppernose, or Copper to his friends, who had lost his sister and went looking for her in the Underdark.

subject: escapee survival
fact: Baedora explains, 'That it was demons that attacked. The Drow fought back. We ran. Figured we were more likely to stay alive away from Drow and Demons.'
source_quote: Baedora explains, 'That it was demons that attacked. The Drow fought back. We ran. Figured we were more likely to stay alive away from Drow and Demons.'

subject: fargas' warning
fact: I remember Fargas Rumblefoot's warning about a 'secret room' or 'false tomb' here, adding another layer of treachery to this place.
source_quote: I remember Fargas Rumblefoot's warning about a 'secret room' or 'false tomb' here, adding another layer of treachery to this place.

subject: Feminine Voice
fact: Feminine voice spoke, 'In the sarcophagus! I can help you!'
source_quote: the soft, feminine voice from earlier, the one that first called to us, speaks again, "In the sarcophagus! I can help you!"

subject: furm's profession
fact: He explains that he is just a farmer.
source_quote: He explains that he is just a farmer.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum asked Jimjar to bet that the crystals would be useful.
source_quote: I turn to him, “Wanna bet that these crystals will be useful?”

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum concluded the fungi were not actively harmful, just loud alarms for bigger threats.
source_quote: Still, at least it meant the fungi weren't actively harmful themselves, just loud alarms for bigger, hungrier things.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum felt a cold, empty feeling of undeath as a Wraith rose from the sarcophagus.
source_quote: Then, a cold, empty feeling washes over me, a familiar touch of undeath. From the sarcophagus, a figure rises, ethereal and malicious. A Wraith.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum heard a sudden, piercing shriek that ripped through the air and vibrated through the rock — shriekers.
source_quote: Then, it hit. A sudden, piercing shriek that ripped through the heavy air and vibrated through the very rock beneath my feet. Not one, but many. Shriekers.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum noted recent damage but no tracks in the thick layer of dust.
source_quote: Grygum, thankfully, is more successful. He notes recent damage but no tracks in the thick layer of dust.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum noted that Stool was curled up contentedly against Thorin's back, reliving his idea to ride the dwarf.
source_quote: Stool, my new myconid friend, was curled up contentedly against Thorin's back, probably still reliving his 'good idea' to ride on the dwarf.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum noted the gilded sarcophagus gleamed against one wall, and a subtle shimmer of an invisible stone chest near its foot.
source_quote: A gilded sarcophagus gleams against one wall, clearly the focal point, and I notice the subtle shimmer of an invisible stone chest near its foot.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum noticed the air grow heavy with the subtle, earthy scent of damp loam and something indescribably sweeter.
source_quote: the air grew heavy with the subtle, earthy scent of the damp loam and something indescribably sweeter.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum noticed the northeast sarcophagus rested on hidden stone rollers.
source_quote: And then, Grygum points it out: the northeast sarcophagus rests on hidden stone rollers. A possible secret, a hidden passage.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum observed towering stalks and caps of fungi, a veritable forest of the subterranean, some glowing faintly with bioluminescent light.
source_quote: There were the towering stalks and caps of fungi, a veritable forest of the subterranean. Mushrooms of all kinds and of all types, stretching up into the unseen ceiling, some glowing faintly with a soft, bioluminescent light, others a muted, earthy brown.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum realized his mending skills were in high demand after the boat sank.
source_quote: The boat is sunk. My mending skills are in high demand.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum recalled old tales of floating undead creatures that rest in tombs.
source_quote: He then recalls old tales of “floating undead creatures that typically rest in tombs”.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum thought he might have to survive throwing a crystal at the shrieker.
source_quote: I even thought, "I was gonna have to survive throwing a crystal at the shrieker".

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum threw a crystal that clattered against a fungal cap, but the shrieking did not change.
source_quote: The crystal sailed through the air, a small, glowing arc, and clattered against a broad fungal cap. And the shrieking... didn't change.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum told Eldeth not to worry.
source_quote: I tell her not to worry.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum took the lead down the dusty staircase, carefully testing each step.
source_quote: We descend a dusty staircase. Grygum, with his keen perception, takes the lead, carefully testing each step.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum tried to turn the Spectres with his holy symbol, but they resisted.
source_quote: Grygum, in his devotion, tries to turn them, his holy symbol raised, but the Spectres resist, their wills too strong, or perhaps their existence too ancient to be swayed.

subject: grygum's memory

subject: Cult of Lolth
fact: The Cult of Lolth is a fanatical, spider-worshipping religious order that dominates Drow society with terror, sacrifice, and divine mandates. It is a primary force of oppression that Daz fled, and its influence is felt as a looming threat throughout the Underdark.
source_quote: Trapped in the formalities of ritual and expectations, trying to avoid the predations of the Cult of Lolth...

subject: Cult of Lolth
fact: The Cult of Lolth is a powerful, predatory religious order among the Drow, exerting control through fear and ritual violence. It is one of the forces Daz escaped.
source_quote: trying to avoid the predations of the Cult of Lolth

subject: Drow Noble Houses
fact: The Drow Noble Houses are powerful, scheming families in Menzoberranzan that enforce rigid social hierarchies and engage in constant political and magical warfare. They are a source of fear and oppression for Drow like Daz, who escaped their machinations.
source_quote: Trapped in the formalities of ritual and expectations, trying to avoid the predations of the Cult of Lolth and the machinations of the Noble Houses.

subject: Drow of Menzoberranzan
fact: The Drow of Menzoberranzan are a rigid, ritual-bound society dominated by noble houses and the Cult of Lolth, from which Daz and others have fled. They are hunters in the Underdark, tracking escapees and altering environments to reassert control.
source_quote: Trapped in the formalities of ritual and expectations, trying to avoid the predations of the Cult of Lolth and the machinations of the Noble Houses.

subject: Netherese Empire
fact: The Netherese Empire was a civilization of immensely powerful mages who built floating cities and defied gravity. Their hubris led to their catastrophic fall when a leader attempted to seize all magic. Their ruins, like the Lost Tomb of Khaem, are filled with relics, undead guardians, and cautionary tales of unchecked ambition.
source_quote: A civilization of immensely powerful magic users, whose cities defied gravity, only to fall catastrophically when one of their leaders tried to seize all magical power...

subject: Netheril Empire
fact: An ancient civilization of immensely powerful magic users whose cities defied gravity, ultimately collapsing when a leader sought to seize all magical power and tore reality.
source_quote: I know the lore of the Netheril Empire – a civilization of immensely powerful magic users, whose cities defied gravity, only to fall catastrophically when one of their leaders tried to seize all magical power, tearing the very fabric of reality.

subject: Chamber of Brysis
fact: A tomb chamber adorned with murals of Brysis of Khaem and her lost cities, housing a gilded sarcophagus, an invisible stone chest, and the source of spectral and wraithish undead; the air was thick with ancient stillness and undeath.
source_quote: The air grows heavier, thick with an ancient stillness. We enter a new chamber, and the faint light catches murals on the walls, depicting grand scenes, probably of the Netherese sorceress Brysis of Khaem and her lost cities.

subject: Drow outpost elevation

source_quote: Drow outpost was 100' in the sky

subject: Faerzress cave

source_quote: The air grew thick with a familiar, subtle hum, the Faerzress.

subject: Faerzress Cavern
fact: A cavern illuminated by the arcane glow of Faerzress crystals, where the air hums with latent magic. It was here that Daz and the group first encountered Fuurm and Baedora hiding in the dark. The cavern’s natural luminescence was so distinctive that the group later destroyed the crystals to disguise their passage as a monster attack.
source_quote: Ahead, there was no longer the rough-hewn stone, but an area suffused with the arcane glowing magic of the Faerzress... We turned down yet another passageway, and the air grew thick with a familiar, subtle hum, the Faerzress.

subject: Faerzress Crystal Cave
fact: A cavern filled with glowing quartz crystals that emit a dim, ten-foot radiance due to the Faerzress arcane energy. The group collected crystals here, then smashed the cavern to disguise their escape as a monster attack.
source_quote: An area suffused with the arcane glowing magic of the Faerzress. Fist-sized chunks of quartz crystals erupted from the wall... We smashed the cavern and the crystals, as if some monster had attacked.

subject: Faerzress crystal cave
fact: The Faerzress crystal cave contains fist-sized quartz crystals erupting from the walls, emitting a dim ten-foot radiance, and is where Eldeth hid the group's tracks for two days before they smashed the cavern to disguise their escape.
source_quote: Ahead, there was no longer the rough-hewn stone, but an area suffused with the arcane glowing magic of the Faerzress. Fist-sized chunks of quartz crystals erupted from the wall, shedding a dim ten-foot radiance... To hide our tracks, we smash the cavern and the crystals, as if some monster had attacked, not escaped slaves who took crystals that shone in the darkness.

subject: final chamber
fact: We enter a new chamber, and the faint light catches murals on the walls, depicting grand scenes, probably of the Netherese sorceress Brysis of Khaem and her lost cities. A gilded sarcophagus gleams against one wall, clearly the focal point, and I notice the subtle shimmer of an invisible stone chest near its foot.
source_quote: We enter a new chamber, and the faint light catches murals on the walls, depicting grand scenes, probably of the Netherese sorceress Brysis of Khaem and her lost cities. A gilded sarcophagus gleams against one wall, clearly the focal point, and I notice the subtle shimmer of an invisible stone chest near its foot.

subject: Fungal Forest
fact: A vast subterranean forest of towering fungi with bioluminescent caps and earthy brown stalks. The air is heavy with a sweet, damp loam scent. It is a natural habitat that emits no harmful spores but is infested with shriekers that act as alarm systems.
source_quote: The air grew heavy with the subtle, earthy scent of the damp loam and something indescribably sweeter... a veritable forest of the subterranean. Mushrooms of all kinds... glowing faintly with a soft, bioluminescent light.

subject: Fungal forest chamber
fact: The fungal forest chamber contains towering stalks and caps of fungi, some glowing faintly with bioluminescent light, others earthy brown, and is where the group encountered Shriekers whose noise did not react to thrown crystals.
source_quote: There were the towering stalks and caps of fungi, a veritable forest of the subterranean. Mushrooms of all kinds and of all types, stretching up into the unseen ceiling, some glowing faintly with a soft, bioluminescent light, others a muted, earthy brown... The crystal sailed through the air... and the shrieking... didn't change.

subject: Lost Tomb of Khaem
fact: The Lost Tomb of Khaem contains a stone diorama depicting Netherese noble Brysis of Khaem surrounded by her retinue, a sprawling mural of floating cities, a Netherese Calendar Stone, a shrine littered with dusty tapestries, four stone sarcophagi marked with robed human figures in repose, a hidden passage revealed by rolling the northeast sarcophagus, a chamber with a gilded sarcophagus, and an invisible stone chest near its foot.
source_quote: A stone diorama stands to the right, depicting a Netherese noble, Brysis of Khaem, surrounded by her retinue, flaunting wealth and power. To the left, a sprawling mural covers the wall, illustrating fantastic floating cities. ... On one landing, I note a Netherese Calendar Stone... The stairs finally give way to a shrine, its floor littered with shreds of dusty tapestries. ... Four stone sarcophagi. Markings of robed human figures in repose adorn their lids. ... The northeast sarcophagus rests on hidden stone rollers. ... A gilded sarcophagus gleams against one wall, clearly the focal point, and I notice the subtle shimmer of an invisible stone chest near its foot.

subject: Lost Tomb of Khaem
fact: The Lost Tomb of Khaem is an ancient, Netherese burial site containing a shrine, staircase, sarcophagi, hidden passages, and a gilded final chamber. It is guarded by undead, marked by murals of floating cities and a Netherese noblewoman, Brysis of Khaem. The tomb is saturated with lingering magic, cold, and the echoes of trapped souls, and it serves as the focal point of the party’s journey.
source_quote: We arrive at a large double door... Inside, a chill descends... A stone diorama stands to the right... A sprawling mural covers the wall... We descend a dusty staircase... a shrine, its floor littered with shreds of dusty tapestries.

subject: Netherese shrine

source_quote: Inside, a chill descends, and my eyes adjust to a faded grandeur. subject: Shriekers
