subject: Site of Negotiation
fact: The location where the narrator and Asha Vandree met is a place where illusions, oozes, and fungal corruption intersect; it is sufficiently remote and strange to allow for the concealment of Glabbagool and the plausibility of Ilvara’s influence.
source_quote: I came to you in my smaller form, and led you here.

subject: spore line
fact: The spore line is the boundary above which Zalthir hovers, separating him from the worst of the cloud.
source_quote: hovering in that particular way of someone who has made the tactically correct decision and is not happy about it. ... from somewhere above the spore line

subject: spore line elevation
fact: The spore line hung above the cavern floor, marking the boundary from which characters spoke while hovering — a tactical vantage point.
source_quote: from somewhere above the spore line

subject: The Bridge
fact: The bridge is a chokepoint where Jorlan has inscribed a Glyph of Warding — now a silent, deadly barrier controlling all movement across it.
source_quote: He moved to the crossing and started inscribing the Glyph of Warding into the stone itself.

subject: Twenty feet of maintained distance
fact: Twenty feet of maintained distance was the established safety buffer between infected and uninfected.
source_quote: Twenty feet of maintained distance. Separate food.

subject: Underdark equivalent of a table
fact: The party spread out tactical options on the Underdark equivalent of a table while crouched in the dark.
source_quote: Then the party spread out the options on the table, or whatever the Underdark equivalent of a table is when you're crouched in the dark...

subject: Underdark equivalent of a table
fact: The party spread out the options on the Underdark equivalent of a table when crouched in the dark with a drow informant and a borrowed crossbow.
source_quote: Then the party spread out the options on the table, or whatever the Underdark equivalent of a table is when you're crouched in the dark with a drow informant and a borrowed crossbow.

subject: Velkynvelve elevation
fact: Velkynvelve sits 100 feet above the cavern floor.
source_quote: Drow outpost was 100' in the sky

subject: Big Heart Fungus
fact: The Big Heart Fungus detonated a twenty-foot spore-thick poison cloud that hung in the cavern air like it had decided to stay — as if it belonged there, as if it had always belonged there, as if we were the interlopers in its home.
source_quote: The cloud didn't drift. That was the first thing I noticed. Normal smoke drifts. Normal gas disperses. This hung in the cavern air like it had decided to stay — twenty feet of spore-thick poison, sitting in the middle of the battlefield as if it belonged there, as if it had always belonged there, as if we were the interlopers in its home.

subject: Big Heart Fungus
fact: The Big Heart Fungus is a sentient, massive fungal organism that serves as the source of Ilvara’s corruption and the primary weapon of the Fungal Cult. It emits a persistent, non-dispersing spore cloud, infects creatures on contact, and regenerates slowly. It cannot be killed quickly or easily. It is not merely a hazard — it is an active, territorial entity that views intruders as invaders.
source_quote: The mushroom artifact from Neverlight Grove was the mechanism of corruption. The Big Heart Fungus was the primary weapon, would need sustained damage, would not die quickly or easily.

subject: Big Heart Fungus
fact: The Big Heart Fungus is still standing, anchoring the far end of the battlefield, and remains the reason Zalthir is hovering.
source_quote: The Big Heart Fungus. Still standing. Still anchoring the far end of the battlefield. Still the reason Zalthir was hovering above the fight instead of in it.

subject: Big Heart Fungus
fact: The Big Heart Fungus was the primary weapon, would need sustained damage, would not die quickly or easily.
source_quote: The Big Heart Fungus was the primary weapon, would need sustained damage, would not die quickly or easily.

subject: Big Heart Fungus
fact: The central anchor of the battlefield, still standing after multiple assaults; it is the root cause of the conflict, responsible for Zalthir’s aerial position and the need for decisive resource expenditure.
source_quote: The Big Heart Fungus. Still standing. Still anchoring the far end of the battlefield.

subject: chasme count
fact: Four chasme demons are present in the cavern above the prisoners' tower.
source_quote: four chasme and two vrock

subject: Dawnbringer blade
fact: The Dawnbringer blade delivered a critical strike to Jorlan after the glyph — its holy light cut cleanly, dealing 14 damage and exploiting his vulnerability from the earlier blast.
source_quote: Dawnbringer came down — crit, the blade's light cutting into him hard and clean, 14 damage landing exactly where it needed to.

subject: Fungal Creatures
fact: Fungal Creatures are mindless, infected beings transformed by the Big Heart Fungus. They are former allies of Ilvara, now reduced to biological extensions of the fungus. They lack individuality, act on instinct, and serve as both guards and vectors of corruption. They are not enemies of choice but consequences of exposure.
source_quote: All of those allies she seems to covet have turned into fungal creatures that are mindless.

subject: Fungal Creatures
fact: Fungal creatures are mindless, transformed followers of Ilvara; they are the result of a magical corruption that turns sentient beings into inert, spore-based entities, likely tied to Zuggtmoy's influence.
source_quote: all of those allies she seems to covet have turned into fungal creatures that are mindless.

subject: Fungal creatures
fact: Ilvara's allies had turned into mindless fungal creatures, a sign of her corruption.
source_quote: all of those allies she seems to covet have turned into fungal creatures that are mindless.

subject: Fungalized Velkynvelve Guards
fact: Four former Velkynvelve guards rose from the cavern floor with patient, purposeless movement — no longer choosing to act, but being directed. Their bodies had been repurposed through fungal colonization under Zuggtmoy’s influence, corrupted further by Ilvara’s will. Once drow with names, duties, and opinions, they are now weapons pointed at the party. Zalthir recognized their tragedy, reflecting on Valen — one of them who could have become this. Their existence embodies the fragility of identity under conquest and corruption.
source_quote: Those poor guards. They've been through quite a lot.

subject: Gelatinous Familiar
fact: A gelatinous familiar accompanies Asha Vandree — an unconventional companion suggesting her alignment with unnatural, fungal, or ooze-based entities.
source_quote: a gelatinous familiar was, on balance, the best available instrument for killing someone she needed dead.

subject: Glabbagool
fact: Glabbagool attempted to pass for a rock; his eyes drifted left and right with the unhurried curiosity of a creature that has never needed to pretend to be geological before.
source_quote: Glabbagool attempted to pass for a rock. The eyes gave him away. They drifted left. They drifted right. They did this with the unhurried curiosity of a creature that has never needed to pretend to be geological before and doesn't fully understand why it's being asked to start now.

subject: Glabbagool's eyes
fact: Glabbagool's eyes drifted left and right with unhurried curiosity, giving him away as not a rock.
source_quote: The eyes gave him away. They drifted left. They drifted right. They did this with the unhurried curiosity...

subject: Grey Ooze (Glabbagool)
fact: Glabbagool is a sentient grey ooze functioning as a bound familiar to the narrator; his unnatural eye movements and inability to maintain geological disguise reveal his non-rock nature and lack of experience with deception.
source_quote: The eyes gave him away. They drifted left. They drifted right. They did this with the unhurried curiosity of a creature that has never needed to pretend to be geological before and doesn't fully understand why it's being asked to start now.

subject: Heart Fungus
fact: The Heart Fungus is a sentient, non-scenic organism that detonated a twenty-foot cloud of spore-thick poison across the cavern floor. It did not disperse like normal gas — it hung deliberately, as if claiming the space as its own. It was observed since the party’s entry, and its activation confirmed prior notes: it is not scenery. It is an active, hostile entity that shifted the battlefield’s dynamics, turning the floor itself into an enemy. Its spore cloud poisoned Zalthir and forced tactical retreats, proving it to be a primary combatant rather than environmental hazard.
source_quote: that's not a metaphor. I took notes. It's what I do.

subject: Ilvara's fungal transformation
fact: Ilvara transformed into fungal matter and reappeared elsewhere, indicating a connection to the Big Heart Fungus.
source_quote: She came apart into the fungal matter beneath her feet — flowed through it like water pouring into a crack... and reappeared somewhere else...

subject: spore servant
fact: The spore servant is a former Velkynvelve guard repurposed by Zuggtmoy's influence.
source_quote: Former Velkynvelve guards. I recognized the posture of soldiers whose bodies had been repurposed, the fungal colonization of Zuggtmoy's influence made visible

subject: spore servant
fact: Twenty-one spore servants were caught in the glyph detonation — one was obliterated, others staggered and barely held together, their cohesion shattered by the blast.
source_quote: One servant came apart completely. Just gone. The others staggered; I watched one barely hold together, listing like a wall with one stone pulled from its base.

subject: spore servant count
fact: Four spore servants rose from the cavern floor with patient, purposeless movement — former Velkynvelve guards repurposed by Zuggtmoy's influence through Ilvara's corruption.
source_quote: Four shapes. Rising from the cavern floor with the patient, purposeless movement of things that are no longer choosing to move — they are simply directed. Former Velkynvelve guards.

subject: spore servant count
fact: One spore servant ceased to be a problem after the glyph detonated, while others staggered in a way suggesting they had not enjoyed the experience.
source_quote: One spore servant ceased to be a problem. The others staggered in a way that suggested they had not enjoyed the experience.

subject: Spore Servants
fact: Fungal reanimated drow warriors, corrupted by Zuggtmoy’s influence and controlled by Ilvara; they stagger after the Glyph and Fireball, one destroyed outright, others barely holding together, demonstrating vulnerability to area effects.
source_quote: One servant came apart completely. Just gone.

subject: The Big Heart Fungus
fact: The Big Heart Fungus is the primary weapon of corruption — a persistent, non-lethal entity that resists quick destruction and requires sustained damage.
source_quote: The Big Heart Fungus was the primary weapon, would need sustained damage, would not die quickly or easily.

subject: the fireball
fact: The fireball behaved as directed — it did not consume Zalthir and Thorin, and struck only Ilvara and the icon, demonstrating non-sentient obedience to arcane intent.
source_quote: It will go around — not because fire cares, fire doesn't care about anything, but because I told it the shape of what it cannot touch.

subject: Zuggtmoy icon
fact: The Zuggtmoy icon, representing a living seed of corruption, was targeted by Daz’s Fireball and rendered unstable — its presence on the battlefield was no longer passive but actively dangerous.
source_quote: A Zuggtmoy-aligned symbol of office left standing is not a symbol — it's a seed. You don't leave seeds.

subject: Asha
fact: Asha is referenced by Daz as the source of the stakes that prevent him from filing away the mission's importance.
source_quote: Asha was explicit enough about what's riding on this that I haven't been able to fully file it away

subject: Asha Vandree
fact: Asha Vandree is a drow who has seen through deception and constructed a coherent belief system around delusion, accepting a spore-maddened wizard with followers and a gelatinous familiar as the best available instrument to kill Ilvara. She remains uninfected through devotion and maintains a 20-foot distance from corrupted allies. Her hatred for Ilvara is genuine, not tactical, and she offers magical items — possibly contaminated — as payment.
source_quote: Ilvara, who was once a high priestess of Lolth, has become seduced by this abomination, this idea that Lolth wishes to be married. There is something foul and stinking about her, and then all of those allies she seems to covet have turned into fungal creatures that are mindless. We need to kill her. We need to butcher her! We need to send her to an unearthly grave! I fear that her disease will spread.

subject: Asha Vandree
fact: Asha Vandree is a drow who survived long enough to find spore-maddened lunatics willing to close lethal distance for her, using devotion as her shield and hatred as her weapon.
source_quote: I was going to kill her. That is what you… where you come in.

subject: Asha Vandree
fact: Asha Vandree is a drow who treats information as currency and deception as a professional skill; she has seen multiple iterations of the same con involving false divine possession by Lolth, and has chosen to accept the narrator as a deluded but potentially useful mage after rejecting his initial claim.
source_quote: Oh, dear goodness, have you two been infected by the spores, possessed by the crazed magic of Zuggtmoy? Convinced of the bride's power? Is this another trick of Ilvara's?

subject: Asha Vandree
fact: Asha Vandree is referenced by Jorlan as the authority who decides the fate of failed Drow, and whose hatred for Ilvara has been building in close quarters with a corrupted superior.
source_quote: I fear that her disease will spread.

subject: Asha Vandree
fact: Asha Vandree offered Ilvara’s magical items as additional payment, with the caveat that they might be contaminated, and filed that caveat.
source_quote: She offered Ilvara's magical items as additional payment, with the caveat that they might be contaminated. I noted that caveat. I filed it.

subject: Bahamut
fact: Bahamut is referenced as possibly watching, though notes are taken either way.
source_quote: Bahamut may or may not have been watching. I took notes either way.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz believes he is a deluded magic user with spores within him.
source_quote: Perhaps there are some spores within me, but I… it feels… I feel it.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz calculated the battlefield and chose to cast the Dust of Suleiman and a concentrated Fireball despite resource cost, targeting Ilvara and the Zuggtmoy icon simultaneously to maximize disruption.
source_quote: The priorities are clear: Ilvara, and the icon. In that order, or really in no particular order — they're the same problem wearing different faces.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz calculated the placement of Fireball to overlap Ilvara and the icon, using Sculpt Spells to avoid allies.
source_quote: Both targets, one sphere, and the geometry cooperates if I'm exact. ... I carve them out.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz executes a precisely sculpted Fireball at fourth level, simultaneously striking Ilvara and the Zuggtmoy icon while sparing Zalthir and Thorin; he calculates target priority with clinical precision and views tactical success as a matter of measurable change on the board.
source_quote: That worked better than I had any right to expect.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz is a wizard who attempted to pass as a divinely touched follower of Lolth but was exposed as a con artist. He pivoted to playing a deluded, spore-infected mage with genuine but misunderstood power, successfully convincing Asha Vandree that his madness is a viable asset. He retains the persona with steadiness, not eloquence, and has recruited followers and bound a gelatinous familiar, Glabbagool, as part of his performance.
source_quote: Perhaps my prayers have been answered through this… confused vessel… Perhaps there are some spores within me, but I… it feels… I feel it. And by the way, I've convinced others to join me.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz is referenced as having found purpose in precision and force, rejecting the notion that precision is the opposite of force.
source_quote: Precision is not the opposite of force. It is force, directed.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz is referenced by Grygum as the feared mage of the Ember Vanguard.
source_quote: I am the feared mage of the Ember Vanguard

subject: Daz
fact: Daz is referenced by Grygum as the one who cast the Fireball that overlapped with the Dust of Suleiman.
source_quote: Then Daz's shaped Fireball hit — Ilvara and the Zuggtmoy icon both, simultaneously

subject: Daz
fact: Daz is the feared mage of the Ember Vanguard, and finds purpose in reading the board and identifying highest-value targets.
source_quote: I have found purpose. I am the feared mage of the Ember Vanguard.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz noted that Ilvara half-saved the Fireball, which was professionally irritating but not unexpected.
source_quote: She half-saves, which is professionally irritating but not unexpected

subject: Daz
fact: Daz noted that Ilvara survived long in Menzoberranzan's social ecosystem by not being slow.
source_quote: she did not survive this long in Menzoberranzan's social ecosystem by being slow

subject: Daz
fact: Daz noted that the Fireball's damage to Ilvara and the icon was twelve each.
source_quote: Ilvara takes twelve. The icon takes twelve.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz noted that the Fireball's geometry cooperated because he was exact.
source_quote: the geometry cooperates if I'm exact

subject: Daz
fact: Daz noted that the Fireball's outcome changed the math of the fight in their favor.
source_quote: Twelve points is twelve points and the board looks different than it did thirty seconds ago, and that is the only metric that has ever mattered.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz noted that the Fireball's placement was the most useful thing he knows how to do.
source_quote: It is perhaps the most useful thing I know how to do.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz noted that the Fireball's success was a bet on precision overriding the need for coverage.
source_quote: But coverage is not what I need. I need placement.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz noted that the Fireball's success was not remarkable because it was the plan, and he noticed anyway.
source_quote: Plans working is not remarkable. But I notice.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz noted that the icon and Ilvara were still standing after the Fireball.
source_quote: The icon is still standing. Ilvara is still standing.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz noted that the stakes were not abstract — they were Asha and everything she told him.
source_quote: The stakes are not abstract. The stakes are Asha, and everything she told me

subject: Daz
fact: Daz said nothing about Zalthir and Thorin being unsinged, though he noted it.
source_quote: I note that Zalthir is unsinged. I note that Thorin is unsinged. I don't say anything about it.

subject: Glabbagool
fact: Glabbagool is a gelatinous ooze familiar bound to Daz, whose attempts to pass as a rock during negotiations failed due to untrained eye movements. Asha Vandree accepts him as part of the deluded-mage archetype — strange, uncategorizable, and fitting the profile of a mage with unusual, nontraditional power. He is not a combatant but a living symbol of the madness Daz projects.
source_quote: Glabbagool attempted to pass for a rock. The eyes gave him away. They drifted left. They drifted right. They did this with the unhurried curiosity of a creature that has never needed to pretend to be geological before.

subject: Glabbagool
fact: Glabbagool is a grey ooze creature attempting to pass as a rock during negotiations; his eyes betray him with unhurried, unnatural movement, indicating he has never before been asked to pretend to be geological and lacks the instinct for such deception.
source_quote: The eyes gave him away. They drifted left. They drifted right. They did this with the unhurried curiosity of a creature that has never needed to pretend to be geological before and doesn't fully understand why it's being asked to start now.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum called Jorlan an idiot and invited him toward the Glyph, betting on ego overriding tactical awareness.
source_quote: You call a man an idiot and invite him toward an explosive ward and you are making a bet on ego overriding tactical awareness

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum called out, 'Come get it, idiot,' and detonated the Glyph of Warding.
source_quote: Grygum called out. 'Come get it, idiot.'

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum devised and triggered the glyph trap, baiting Jorlan with taunts and expressing genuine surprise when it succeeded — his tactical gamble on ego over awareness paid off.
source_quote: Come get it, idiot." && "I didn't expect it to work.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum had a light crossbow, handed it over without drama, and was confirmed as not sloppy in maintenance.
source_quote: Grygum had a light crossbow. I asked him for it. Simple transaction, no drama — he handed it over and I checked the mechanism... He wasn't. That dwarf is okay.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum had the idea for the Glyph of Warding, or at least voiced it.
source_quote: The Glyph was Grygum's idea, or at least Grygum's mouth.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum is a dwarf who carries a light crossbow, understands the danger of the Neverlight Grove artifact, and refuses to touch it — his silence with Thorin a blood oath.
source_quote: Grygum had a light crossbow. I asked him for it. Simple transaction, no drama — he handed it over.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum laid the Glyph of Warding on the bridge as a bait trap, anticipating ego-driven aggression; he calls out to Jorlan with deliberate provocation and expresses genuine surprise when the trap succeeds.
source_quote: Come get it, idiot.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum noted that Jorlan came across the bridge like a man who had already decided the outcome.
source_quote: he came across that bridge like a man who had already decided the outcome

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum noted that Jorlan took the full force of the Glyph and now the Dawnbringer strike.
source_quote: He'd taken the full force of the Glyph and now this.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum noted that Jorlan was not having his best moment after the Glyph detonated.
source_quote: Jorlan himself was not having his best moment.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum noted that Jorlan's certainty was almost giant-brained, and that giants are usually right about the terrain.
source_quote: There's something almost giant-brained about that kind of certainty. Giants move like that. ... The problem is, giants are usually right about the terrain.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum noted that the Dust of Suleiman was committed because the creature had already demonstrated what it was willing to do.
source_quote: because the creature had already demonstrated what it was willing to do to us and I had no interest in finding out what it would do next if left unaddressed.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum noted that the Dust of Suleiman was not a small resource, and he made the decision anyway.
source_quote: This was not a small resource. I made the decision anyway

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum noted that the Glyph was placed by the group's execution, not just Grygum's idea.
source_quote: The placement was all of us.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum noted that the Glyph was placed like a welcome mat.
source_quote: We'd laid it on the bridge like a welcome mat

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum noted that the Glyph worked because they stopped expecting it to work.
source_quote: you stop expecting it, almost. You get tactical, you do the work, you lay the trap in exactly the right place — and then somewhere between placing it and watching it detonate, you forget to believe in yourself.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum noted that the Glyph's detonation caused a sphere of force and light that didn't care who was in the way.
source_quote: Force and light erupted outward in a sphere, the kind of detonation that doesn't care who's in the way.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum noted that the Glyph's detonation caused twenty-one damage to the cluster.
source_quote: Twenty-one damage blooming through the cluster all at once

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum noted that the battlefield fragmented faster than any of them had planned for.
source_quote: The battlefield had fragmented faster than any of us had planned for, allies pulled in three different directions by pressure we hadn't fully mapped before we walked in.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum noted that the battlefield had shifted in their favor after the combined spells.
source_quote: The battlefield had shifted in our favor

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum noted that the difference between soldiers and weapons is sometimes just time and circumstance, and he filed that thought away under 'things not to dwell on mid-combat.'
source_quote: I filed that thought away under *things not to dwell on mid-combat*.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum noted that the difference between soldiers and weapons is sometimes just time and circumstance.
source_quote: Soldiers. Now weapons. The difference between the two is sometimes just time and circumstance

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum noted that the fight was far from over, even after the combined spells.
source_quote: The fungus was still standing. The fight was far from over.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum noted that the spore servant that barely held together was listing like a wall with one stone pulled from its base.
source_quote: I watched one barely hold together, listing like a wall with one stone pulled from its base.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum noted that the spore servant that came apart completely was just gone.
source_quote: One servant came apart completely. Just gone.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum noted that the spore servants staggered in a way that suggested they had not enjoyed the experience.
source_quote: The others staggered in a way that suggested they had not enjoyed the experience.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum noted the conditions that made the Glyph work: bait the ego, trust the glyph, commit the resource, let Daz do what Daz does.
source_quote: I noted the specific combination of factors that had produced that outcome: bait the ego, trust the glyph, commit the resource, let Daz do what Daz does.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum observed that the spell worked better than expected, and values honest tactical assessment.
source_quote: *"That worked better than I had any right to expect."*

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum said, 'I didn't expect it to work,' after the Glyph detonated, with honesty.
source_quote: 'I didn't expect it to work.' That last part was honest.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum said, 'Kaboom,' and then, 'I didn't expect it to work,' with genuine surprise.
source_quote: Grygum said, 'Kaboom!' And then, with something like genuine surprise underneath it: 'I didn't expect it to work.'

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum said, 'That worked better than I had any right to expect,' after Daz's Fireball.
source_quote: Grygum's voice cuts through the settling heat: 'That worked better than I had any right to expect.'

subject: Ilvara
fact: Ilvara absorbed the combined effects of the Fireball and glyph detonation, taking punishment she hadn't budgeted for — her position was compromised, and she was left vulnerable.
source_quote: Ilvara absorbing punishment she hadn't budgeted for

subject: Ilvara
fact: Ilvara is a drow priestess of Ilvara who was grappled and constrained mid-combat, her movement fully controlled until she dissolved into fungal matter beneath her feet. She screamed at herself — a sign of her fury at having been hurt, and at the breaking of an illusion that her core self was inviolable. She is now out of reach, having put distance between herself and her attacker, and her scream lingers in the cavern as if left there deliberately.
source_quote: at herself.

subject: Ilvara
fact: Ilvara is a former high priestess of Lolth who has become corrupted by the Big Heart Fungus, believing Lolth wishes to be married. Her influence has turned allies into mindless fungal creatures. She is the target of Asha Vandree’s vendetta and the central threat of the operation. Her corruption is not merely magical but spiritual, and her transformation is irreversible without destruction.
source_quote: Ilvara, who was once a high priestess of Lolth, has become seduced by this abomination, this idea that Lolth wishes to be married. There is something foul and stinking about her… all of those allies she seems to covet have turned into fungal creatures that are mindless.

subject: Ilvara
fact: Ilvara is a former high priestess of Lolth who has become seduced by the delusion that Lolth wishes to be married; her followers have been transformed into mindless fungal creatures, and her corruption is spreading, inspiring deep, personal hatred in Asha Vandree.
source_quote: Ilvara, who was once a high priestess of Lolth, has become seduced by this abomination, this idea that Lolth wishes to be married. There is something foul and stinking about her, and then all of those allies she seems to covet have turned into fungal creatures that are mindless. We need to kill her. We need to butcher her! We need to send her to an unearthly grave! I fear that her disease will spread.

subject: Ilvara
fact: Ilvara is referenced by Daz as the authority who decides the fate of failed Drow.
source_quote: Ilvara might decide his fate should be precisely like Serith's

subject: Ilvara
fact: Ilvara is the orchestrator of the fungal corruption, having raised four former Velkynvelve guards as directed weapons under Zuggtmoy’s influence; she is targeted by Daz’s Fireball and absorbs significant damage but remains standing.
source_quote: Then Ilvara called them up.

subject: Ilvara
fact: Ilvara took twelve points of damage from the fireball, surviving due to her proficiency in Menzoberranzan's social ecosystem.
source_quote: She takes twelve. The icon takes twelve.

subject: Ilvara
fact: Ilvara's corruption made visible the fungal colonization of Zuggtmoy's influence through the repurposed Velkynvelve guards.
source_quote: Former Velkynvelve guards. I recognized the posture of soldiers whose bodies had been repurposed, the fungal colonization of Zuggtmoy's influence made visible through Ilvara's particular corruption.

subject: Ilvara
fact: Ilvara, who was once a high priestess of Lolth, has become seduced by this abomination, this idea that Lolth wishes to be married.
source_quote: Ilvara, who was once a high priestess of Lolth, has become seduced by this abomination, this idea that Lolth wishes to be married.

subject: Jorlan
fact: Jorlan committed to advancing across the bridge despite the glyph trap, demonstrating total confidence that proved fatal — he took full force of the detonation and was left reeling, unable to evade the follow-up strike.
source_quote: He came across that bridge like a man who had already decided the outcome.

subject: Jorlan
fact: Jorlan is a combatant who, in the midst of chaotic battlefield conditions, was drawn toward the Glyph of Warding on the bridge. He was distracted and angry enough that he failed to track the floor’s danger. An opponent calculated his trajectory in one second and baited him into the trap with the call, 'Come get it, idiot.' His movement was a predictable response to pressure, and his action was a catalyst for the next phase of the battlefield’s retaliation.
source_quote: Come get it, idiot.

subject: Jorlan
fact: Jorlan is a drow who charges recklessly into Grygum’s Glyph of Warding, trusting his own certainty over tactical awareness; he takes full damage from the explosion and is later struck by Thorin’s Dawnbringer, leaving him compromised and off-balance.
source_quote: Come get it, idiot.

subject: Jorlan
fact: Jorlan is an uninfected human who resists corruption through hatred, serves as a tactical anchor, and inscribes Glyphs of Warding into terrain to control movement.
source_quote: He moved to the crossing and started inscribing the Glyph of Warding into the stone itself.

subject: Jorlan
fact: Jorlan is referenced by Grygum as the one who committed to the trap on the bridge.
source_quote: Jorlan didn't hesitate, didn't slow — he came across that bridge like a man who had already decided the outcome

subject: Jorlan
fact: Jorlan is uninfected by the fungal corruption, sustained by hatred — which Asha Vandree identifies as its own kind of immunological theory. He is positioned on the bridge, inscribing a Glyph of Warding, and is perceived by Thorin as a predictable threat: a clear location to target. He is not part of the deception but a fixed variable in the tactical equation.
source_quote: Jorlan's side. He moved to the crossing and started inscribing the Glyph of Warding into the stone itself… Jorlan is not complicated. Jorlan is a threat with a location, which is the best kind of threat because it tells you exactly where to aim.

subject: Jorlan
fact: Jorlan remained uninfected through hatred, which is its own kind of immunological theory, and maintained twenty feet of maintained distance.
source_quote: Only she and Jorlan remained uninfected — Asha through devotion, Jorlan through hatred, which is its own kind of immunological theory. Twenty feet of maintained distance.

subject: Narrator
fact: The narrator believes precision is not the opposite of force — it is force, directed.
source_quote: Precision is not the opposite of force. It is force, directed.

subject: Narrator
fact: The narrator filed away the thought that the difference between soldiers and weapons is sometimes just time and circumstance, and chose not to dwell on it mid-combat.
source_quote: Soldiers. Now weapons. The difference between the two is sometimes just time and circumstance, and I filed that thought away under *things not to dwell on mid-combat*.

subject: Narrator
fact: The narrator finds the irony of being the feared mage of the Ember Vanguard almost invisible, even to themselves.
source_quote: The irony is almost invisible, even to me.

subject: Narrator
fact: The narrator prefers to file things away and not let stakes surface, but the stakes involving Asha keep surfacing.
source_quote: Asha was explicit enough about what's riding on this that I haven't been able to fully file it away the way I prefer to file things. It keeps surfacing.

subject: Narrator
fact: The narrator takes notes either way, whether Bahamut is watching or not.
source_quote: Bahamut may or may not have been watching. I took notes either way.

subject: The Feared Mage of the Ember Vanguard
fact: The mage is the architect of the sculpted fireball, directing precise destructive force with calculated intent.
source_quote: I am the feared mage of the Ember Vanguard.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin engaged Jorlan immediately after the glyph detonation, delivering a critical Dawnbringer strike and following up with a Sap to leave him disadvantaged — his aggression capitalized on the chaos.
source_quote: I was already closing on Jorlan. The explosion was still ringing through the cavern when Dawnbringer came down — crit, the blade's light cutting into him hard and clean, 14 damage landing exactly where it needed to.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin exploits the chaos following the Glyph’s detonation to close on Jorlan, landing a critical Dawnbringer strike and a Sap to impose disadvantage; he notes the fragility of the spore servants and remains focused on the larger threat.
source_quote: Kaboom! I didn't expect it to work.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin is a pragmatic tactician who borrows weapons, observes with cold precision, and files useful people and positions into a mental archive labeled *useful people*.
source_quote: I listened. I watched who spoke with certainty and who spoke with hedging.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin is referenced by Daz as the one who pressed the Sap after the Glyph detonated.
source_quote: I was already closing on Jorlan. ... I pressed the Sap after it

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin is unsinged after the fireball spell, as intended by the sculpted magic.
source_quote: I note that Thorin is unsinged.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin noted the conditions under which the Sap succeeded: using momentum wrong to do something right.
source_quote: using the momentum wrong to do something right — shoving him off-balance

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin noted the legendary action of the servant that landed a glancing blow for 5 damage.
source_quote: One of the servants wasn't finished with me. Legendary action, a swing that went so wide it almost circled back around to being impressive — natural 1, nothing — and then the follow-up connected for 5. Glancing. A reminder. Fair enough. I noted it.

subject: Valen
fact: Valen is referenced by Grygum as someone who could have been one of the repurposed guards.
source_quote: Valen, who had been one of them. Who could have been one of them, differently categorized.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir believed the fallen guards had been through quite a lot.
source_quote: Zalthir said, from his aerial vantage point, "Those poor guards. They've been through quite a lot."

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir felt frustration wearing a physical costume after being poisoned.
source_quote: The poisoned condition settling over a person looks different depending on who they are. On Zalthir it looked like frustration wearing a physical costume.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir filed Ilvara’s scream of self-anger as a true indicator of damage inflicted, noting it as a psychological turning point.
source_quote: *She's angry at herself,* I noted, and filed it away, and watched.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir is a dragonborn who took the full brunt of the Heart Fungus’s spore cloud. He did not collapse dramatically, but exhibited a subtle wrongness in movement — a falter that signaled the poisoned condition settling over him. He disengaged and ascended ten feet, making a tactically sound but emotionally resigned decision. He declared himself out of actions and bonus actions, and chose to observe in dry confusion, his voice carrying the weight of a plan unraveling faster than expected.
source_quote: I'm out of actions and bonus actions, so I guess I'll just kind of look on and be confused.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir is a spellcaster who bypasses distance through teleportation, strikes without warning, and turns authority into target in the space of a decision.
source_quote: One moment I was reading the geometry... and the next I was already there, adjacent, inside the radius where a priestess stops being an authority and becomes a target.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir is hovering above the battlefield, poisoned and frustrated, having disengaged after losing his tactical advantage over Ilvara; he is acutely aware of the repurposed guards and reflects silently on Valen's potential fate.
source_quote: Those poor guards. They've been through quite a lot.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir is referenced by Grygum as the authority who decides the fate of failed Drow.
source_quote: Zalthir might decide his fate should be precisely like Serith's

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir is unsinged after the fireball spell, as intended by the sculpted magic.
source_quote: I note that Zalthir is unsinged.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir said, 'Those poor guards. They've been through quite a lot,' from his aerial vantage point.
source_quote: Zalthir said, from his aerial vantage point, 'Those poor guards. They've been through quite a lot.'

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir teleported directly to Ilvara or grabbed her and moved her somewhere unpleasant, and filed teleportation as a weapon under *useful people*.
source_quote: Zalthir said he could teleport directly to Ilvara — or grab her and move her somewhere unpleasant. I stored that. Teleportation as a weapon. Thorin files that away in the part of his brain labeled *useful people.*

subject: Zuggtmoy
fact: Zuggtmoy is referenced as the source of the fungal colonization that repurposed the Velkynvelve guards.
source_quote: the fungal colonization of Zuggtmoy's influence made visible

subject: Big Heart Fungus
fact: The Big Heart Fungus was the primary weapon, would need sustained damage, would not die quickly or easily.
source_quote: The Big Heart Fungus was the primary weapon, would need sustained damage, would not die quickly or easily.

subject: Dancing Lights
fact: Dancing Lights were threaded down like a column of divine attention, absorbed into the speaker and blinking out.
source_quote: The Dancing Lights threading down like a column of divine attention, absorbed into the familiar, absorbed into me, blinking out.

subject: Dancing Lights
fact: The Dancing Lights were used by the narrator as an initial attempt to simulate divine presence; they were dismissed as a crude illusion by Asha, who recognized them as a common trick among charlatans.
source_quote: The Dancing Lights threading down like a column of divine attention, absorbed into the familiar, absorbed into me, blinking out.

subject: Dawnbringer
fact: Dawnbringer is the blade Thorin used to deliver a critical hit to Jorlan after the Glyph detonated.
source_quote: Dawnbringer came down — crit, the blade's light cutting into him hard and clean, 14 damage landing exactly where it needed to.

subject: Dust of Suleiman
fact: A rare and costly resource cast directly onto the Big Heart Fungus to neutralize its anchoring power; its use signals a commitment to decisive action despite the risk of resource depletion.
source_quote: I committed the Dust of Suleiman and cast it directly onto the fungus.

subject: Dust of Suleiman
fact: Dust of Suleiman is a magical substance available to the party, capable of disintegrating organic matter. It is intended as a weapon against Ilvara, with the plan to force her into its area of effect. Its use is calculated and economical, meant to let the battlefield do the killing. It is not yet deployed but is a critical component of the tactical plan.
source_quote: I looked at the cavern floor. At the Dust of Suleiman area. At the rough arithmetic of: priestess plus that zone equals someone else's problem.

subject: Dust of Suleiman
fact: Dust of Suleiman was among the tactical options laid out by the party for battlefield control.
source_quote: Glyph of Warding. Dust of Suleiman. Phantasmal Killer. Fireball.

subject: Dust of Suleiman
fact: The Dust of Suleiman is a non-replaceable resource committed to the Big Heart Fungus.
source_quote: This was not a small resource. I made the decision anyway

subject: Dust of Suleiman
fact: The Dust of Suleiman is a resource committed directly onto the Big Heart Fungus.
source_quote: I committed the Dust of Suleiman and cast it directly onto the fungus

subject: Dust of Suleiman
fact: The Dust of Suleiman was cast directly onto the Big Heart Fungus — a high-cost resource deployed despite risk, because the fungus had already demonstrated what it was willing to do.
source_quote: This was not a small resource. I made the decision anyway, because the creature had already demonstrated what it was willing to do to us.

subject: Dust of Suleiman
fact: The Dust of Suleiman was positioned on the cavern floor as a zone of lethal environmental hazard.
source_quote: I looked at the cavern floor. At the Dust of Suleiman area.

subject: Fireball
fact: Fireball was among the options spread out on the Underdark equivalent of a table as a potential 4th-level spell deployment.
source_quote: Glyph of Warding. Dust of Suleiman. Phantasmal Killer. Fireball.

subject: Fireball
fact: The Fireball was cast at fourth level and dealt twelve damage to both Ilvara and the icon.
source_quote: Ilvara takes twelve. The icon takes twelve.

subject: Fireball
fact: The Fireball was cast at fourth level with eight dice, sculpted to avoid Zalthir and Thorin.
source_quote: Fireball. Cast at fourth level. Eight dice. ... I carve them out. The fire will know the shape of them by the time it arrives and it will go around

subject: Fireball (Daz’s Sculpted)
fact: A fourth-level Fireball cast with Sculpt Spells to precisely target Ilvara and the Zuggtmoy icon while sparing allies; it deals 12 damage to each, altering the battlefield’s tactical calculus.
source_quote: Eight dice. I carve them out. The fire will know the shape of them...

subject: Glyph
fact: The Glyph was a trap laid on the bridge as a bait — its activation relied on Jorlan’s predictable ego-driven advance, turning his confidence into his downfall.
source_quote: We'd laid it on the bridge like a welcome mat, and then the whole job was just: don't stand on it yourself, and wait.

subject: Glyph of Warding
fact: A Glyph of Warding inscribed into bridge stone creates an invisible, persistent trap — activated by hostile movement, serving as a silent guardian of the chokepoint.
source_quote: He moved to the crossing and started inscribing the Glyph of Warding into the stone itself.

subject: Glyph of Warding
fact: A magically activated ward placed on the bridge by the party to exploit overconfidence; it detonates with force and light, dealing 21 damage in a sphere and destroying one spore servant while crippling Jorlan.
source_quote: The Glyph fired.

subject: Glyph of Warding
fact: The Glyph of Warding is a magical trap placed on the bridge with the explicit intent of exploiting chaotic battlefield conditions. It remains active and untriggered until Jorlan’s impulsive movement draws him into its range. It is not merely a spell — it is a tactical decision made in advance, a weapon of foresight. Its activation was inevitable once Jorlan was distracted. The glyph is a symbol of preparation, and its success proves that planning can outmaneuver raw power.
source_quote: We'd placed it with exactly this kind of chaos in mind

subject: Glyph of Warding
fact: The Glyph of Warding was inscribed into the stone of the bridge, with trigger: any hostile creature crossing, invisible once finished.
source_quote: Jorlan's side. He moved to the crossing and started inscribing the Glyph of Warding into the stone itself.

subject: Glyph of Warding
fact: The Glyph of Warding was placed on the bridge by Grygum's idea and the group's execution.
source_quote: The Glyph was Grygum's idea, or at least Grygum's mouth. The placement was all of us.

subject: Glyph of Warding (on the bridge)
fact: A Glyph of Warding has been inscribed into the stone of the bridge by Jorlan, triggered by any hostile creature crossing. It is invisible once active, patient, and designed to serve as a perimeter defense. It is a tactical tool meant to delay or eliminate threats approaching from Jorlan’s side, and is understood by Thorin as a fixed variable in the battlefield geometry.
source_quote: Jorlan... started inscribing the Glyph of Warding into the stone itself... The trigger: any hostile creature crossing. Invisible once finished. Patient in the way only traps can be patient.

subject: glyph of warding value
fact: The Glyph of Warding was a tactical gamble — a trap laid to exploit ego overriding caution — and it succeeded, dealing 21 damage and killing one servant.
source_quote: The tactic had been a gamble — you call a man an idiot and invite him toward an explosive ward and you are making a bet on ego overriding tactical awareness...

subject: Heart Fungus Spore Cloud
fact: The spore cloud is a physical manifestation of the Heart Fungus’s hostile will — a twenty-foot expanse of airborne poison that lingers, refuses to disperse, and selectively infects. It is not an accident of the environment; it is an intentional attack. It poisoned Zalthir, altered his movement, and forced a tactical retreat. The cloud is not a hazard — it is a weapon with memory, and its persistence marks the fungus as a sentient combatant.
source_quote: twenty feet of spore-thick poison, sitting in the middle of the battlefield as if it belonged there

subject: Ilvara's magical items
fact: Ilvara's magical items were offered as additional payment, with the caveat that they might be contaminated.
source_quote: She offered Ilvara's magical items as additional payment, with the caveat that they might be contaminated.

subject: Light Crossbow
fact: A light crossbow, borrowed from Grygum, is the chosen ranged weapon — reliable, non-magical, and ideal for precise, non-committal engagement.
source_quote: Grygum had a light crossbow. I asked him for it. Simple transaction, no drama — he handed it over and I checked the mechanism.

subject: Light Crossbow
fact: The light crossbow was borrowed from Grygum, checked for sloppiness by pulling the string, sighting down it, confirming the prior owner was not sloppy.
source_quote: I asked him for it. Simple transaction, no drama — he handed it over and I checked the mechanism the way you check anything borrowed before a fight: pull the string, sight down it, make sure the person who owned it before you wasn't sloppy.

subject: Mushroom Artifact from Neverlight Grove
fact: The Mushroom Artifact from Neverlight Grove is the original vector of corruption that enabled Ilvara’s transformation and the spread of the Big Heart Fungus. It is the catalyst, not the source, and remains a dangerous relic that must be contained or destroyed to halt the infection.
source_quote: The mushroom artifact from Neverlight Grove was the mechanism of corruption.

subject: Mushroom Artifact from Neverlight Grove
fact: The mushroom artifact from Neverlight Grove is the mechanism of corruption — a dangerous object that must not be touched, known to induce madness or transformation.
source_quote: The mushroom artifact from Neverlight Grove was the mechanism of corruption.

subject: Mushroom Artifact from Neverlight Grove
fact: The mushroom artifact from Neverlight Grove was the mechanism of corruption, the trigger for the fungal transformation of Ilvara’s allies.
source_quote: The mushroom artifact from Neverlight Grove was the mechanism of corruption.

subject: Phantasmal Killer
fact: Phantasmal Killer was among the options spread out on the Underdark equivalent of a table as a potential 4th-level spell deployment.
source_quote: Glyph of Warding. Dust of Suleiman. Phantasmal Killer. Fireball.

subject: Sap
fact: The Sap is a maneuver Thorin used to shove Jorlan off-balance after the Glyph detonated.
source_quote: I pressed the Sap after it, using the momentum wrong to do something right — shoving him off-balance, leaving him on the back foot

subject: silver candlestick value
fact: The silver candlesticks flanking the Lolth altar are worth 25 gp each.
source_quote: a pair of heavy silver candlesticks worth 25 gp each

subject: Spores
fact: Spores are the suspected vector of Ilvara’s corruption, transforming followers into mindless fungal entities; they are treated by Asha as a tangible, infectious agent rather than a metaphorical curse.
source_quote: have you two been infected by the spores… possessed by the crazed magic of Zuggtmoy?

subject: the fireball spell
fact: The fireball was shaped by intent to bypass specific targets and strike only designated ones, demonstrating mastery of spell sculpting.
source_quote: I carve them out. The fire will know the shape of them by the time it arrives and it will go around — not because fire cares, fire doesn't care about anything, but because I told it the shape of what it cannot touch.

subject: Zalthir's weapon
fact: Zalthir used a weapon that dealt sixteen damage on the first strike and fifteen on the second, totaling thirty-one.
source_quote: I drove the weapon in. Sixteen... The second strike... Fifteen more. Thirty-one total.

subject: Asha’s stakes
fact: The mission’s true stakes are tied to Asha — her words and warnings persistently surface in Daz’s calculations, making the Zuggtmoy icon more than a target — it’s a personal obligation.
source_quote: The stakes are not abstract. The stakes are Asha, and everything she told me...

subject: Asha's true loyalty
fact: Asha Vandree claims Lolth’s gratitude as sufficient — but her actions suggest deeper, unspoken motives, possibly independent of divine allegiance.
source_quote: I already feel the gratitude of Lolth. I have that.

subject: bait the ego, trust the glyph, commit the resource, let Daz do what Daz does
fact: The successful tactic combined psychological manipulation, precise timing, resource expenditure, and trusting a specialist’s instincts — this combination is now a documented pattern for future engagements.
source_quote: I noted the specific combination of factors that had produced that outcome: bait the ego, trust the glyph, commit the resource, let Daz do what Daz does.

subject: Big Heart Fungus
fact: The Big Heart Fungus remains standing and anchoring the far end of the battlefield — its continued existence is the root cause of the conflict and the reason Zalthir hovers above the fight.
source_quote: The fungus was still standing. Still anchoring the far end of the battlefield. Still the reason Zalthir was hovering above the fight instead of in it.

subject: contaminated magical items
fact: Ilvara's magical items may be contaminated — a potential trap or hidden threat that remains unverified and unaddressed.
source_quote: She offered Ilvara's magical items as additional payment, with the caveat that they might be contaminated.

subject: Ego vs. Tactical Awareness
fact: The success of the Glyph and Fireball depends on exploiting enemy overconfidence; this pattern is noted as a repeatable tactical lever, though its reliability remains uncertain.
source_quote: You call a man an idiot and invite him toward an explosive ward and you are making a bet on ego overriding tactical awareness...

subject: Ilvara's Corruption
fact: Ilvara’s descent into fungal worship and her transformation of allies into mindless spore-creatures represents a spreading contagion that threatens the balance of drow society; Asha Vandree believes it must be stopped before it infects more.
source_quote: I fear that her disease will spread.

subject: Ilvara's Corruption and the Spread of the Fungus
fact: The central unresolved thread is whether Ilvara’s corruption is reversible, and whether the Big Heart Fungus will continue to spread beyond the cavern. Asha fears the disease will spread, and the party must kill Ilvara before she can infect more of the Underdark. The fungal artifact and the spore cloud suggest this is not a localized event but an emerging plague.
source_quote: I fear that her disease will spread.

subject: Jorlan's position
fact: Jorlan is a known threat with a fixed location — his presence on the bridge is both tactical and psychological, a target waiting to be aimed at.
source_quote: Jorlan is not complicated. Jorlan is a threat with a location, which is the best kind of threat because it tells you exactly where to aim.

subject: Narrator's Delusion
fact: The narrator has constructed a coherent delusion of divine possession and fungal influence to survive Asha’s scrutiny; while false, it has been accepted as plausible because it aligns with known patterns of corruption in the region, making it a viable cover.
source_quote: Perhaps my prayers have been answered through this… confused vessel… Perhaps there are some spores within me, but I… it feels… I feel it.

subject: remaining targets
fact: Ilvara and the icon are still standing after the spell, indicating the fight is not over despite the tactical shift.
source_quote: Ilvara is still standing. But twelve points is twelve points and the board looks different than it did thirty seconds ago.

subject: Screams Left Behind
fact: Ilvara’s scream — not at her attacker, but at herself — was left echoing in the cavern like a physical artifact. This thread suggests that trauma, when profound enough, becomes part of the environment. The scream is not just sound; it is the sound of an illusion shattering. It lingers as a warning, a marker of vulnerability, and a testament to the psychological cost of combat. The party is now fighting not just bodies, but echoes of broken wills.
source_quote: at herself.

subject: The Battlefield as an Enemy
fact: The cavern floor — through the Heart Fungus and Ilvara’s fungalized reanimation — has become an active, sentient antagonist. The party planned for drow commanders and spellcasters, but not for the environment itself to retaliate. This thread suggests the setting is not passive; it remembers, adapts, and claims those who die within it. The fungal growths are not just hazards — they are the bones of the past, repurposed. The party is not invading a dungeon — they are trespassing in a living graveyard that fights back.
source_quote: as if we were the interlopers in its home.

subject: The Fate of Glabbagool
fact: Glabbagool’s nature remains ambiguous: is he a bound familiar, a sentient fungal offshoot, or an independent entity masquerading as a pet? His presence defies categorization, and his role in the mission is unspoken. He may be a liability, a weapon, or a harbinger — his true origin is a thread left deliberately unresolved.
source_quote: Glabbagool attempted to pass for a rock... He looked at me. Or at least, several of his eyes moved in my general direction.

subject: The Floor as Enemy
fact: The party realizes the battlefield itself — the cavern floor and its fungal growth — is an active, sentient threat, not just terrain; this shifts their tactical paradigm from fighting enemies to fighting the environment.
source_quote: You plan for the drow commander. You don't always plan for the floor itself to become an enemy.

subject: the goal all along
fact: The true objective — eyeing the prize — has never shifted, even as tactics, alliances, and weapons changed hands.
source_quote: *The goal the whole time*, I thought. *Eyeing the prize.*

subject: The Nature of Daz's Connection to Lolth
fact: Daz claims to feel Lolth’s gratitude — but whether he truly does, or is simply performing a delusion that has become real through belief, is unknown. His steadiness suggests internal conviction. Is he a fraud who became a prophet? Or a prophet who was mistaken for a fraud? This thread underlies the entire negotiation and may determine the party’s spiritual fate.
source_quote: I already feel the gratitude of Lolth. I have that... It's the kind of conviction this follower of Lolth shows.

subject: Things Not to Dwell On Mid-Combat
fact: The party recognizes the emotional weight of repurposed enemies and fallen allies as dangerous distractions; these thoughts are filed away as 'not to dwell on' to preserve combat effectiveness.
source_quote: I filed that thought away under *things not to dwell on mid-combat*.

subject: Valen
fact: Valen could have been one of the repurposed soldiers, and somewhere between then and now, he had lost the thread entirely.
source_quote: Then he reflected on Valen. Not out loud, really — it was more in the quality of the silence that followed. I felt the thought land in the room anyway. Valen, who had been one of them. Who could have been one of them, differently categorized. These bodies on the cavern floor had once been exactly what Valen was, and somewhere between then and now, they had lost the thread entirely.

subject: Valen’s Fate
fact: Valen’s potential transformation into one of the fungalized guards was silently reflected upon by Zalthir. The thought hung in the air — that Valen, once a living drow soldier, could have become what now rises from the floor. This thread connects identity, corruption, and the thin line between soldier and weapon. It is not spoken aloud, but its emotional weight lingers, suggesting a deeper narrative about loss, control, and what happens when people are repurposed by forces beyond their will.
source_quote: Valen, who had been one of them. Who could have been one of them, differently categorized.

subject: Valen’s Fate
fact: Zalthir silently reflects on Valen — who was once like the repurposed guards — and the thin line between identity and corruption; this unresolved emotional thread haunts the party’s understanding of the enemy’s humanity.
source_quote: Valen, who had been one of them. Who could have been one of them, differently categorized.

subject: 4th-level slot expenditure
fact: The plan hinges on the expenditure of one 4th-level spell slot, used to deploy the Dust of Suleiman against the Heart Fungus. This is the decisive tactical choice made before engagement.
source_quote: One 4th-level slot. I'd made my choice. The Dust of Suleiman on the fungus...

subject: elapsed time
fact: An hour passes between two events in the session.
source_quote: An hour later

subject: elapsed time before assault
fact: An hour passed before the assault began.
source_quote: I spent the hour before the assault

subject: Hour before the assault
fact: The critical preparation window immediately preceding the planned attack, during which Grygum finalized his spell strategy and Asha Vandree provided her decisive tactical correction. This hour is the pivot point between theoretical planning and actionable execution.
source_quote: I spent the hour before the assault doing the thing that was useful and quiet and required no discussion.

subject: session date
fact: The events described occurred during a single, continuous interaction in a subterranean chamber, likely during a critical mission phase. No external temporal markers are given, but the psychological and narrative weight suggests it is a pivotal moment in the campaign’s progression.
source_quote: I have noticed this before. I will notice it again.

subject: Session Date
fact: The events described occurred during a single, continuous session of roleplaying, with no temporal breaks. The narrative unfolds in real-time as the party navigates deception, paranoia, and strategy.
source_quote: I spent the hour before the assault doing the thing that was useful and quiet and required no discussion.

subject: session date
fact: The session occurs on the 5th day of the 2nd Tenday of Taraskh 1493 DR.
source_quote: On the 5th day of the 2nd Tenday of Taraskh 1493

subject: Session Date — The Battle of the Heart Fungus
fact: The events of the Battle of the Heart Fungus occurred during a single session of play, marked by intense tactical planning, emotional revelations, and irreversible character choices — a session that redefined the party’s understanding of morality, loyalty, and power in the Underdark.
source_quote: I took notes on the whole plan, the way I always do. Not on paper. In my head.

subject: Asha's belief vs knowledge distinction
fact: Asha says 'I believe' about the origin of the spore illness, undermining her authority by revealing uncertainty.
source_quote: I believe.

subject: Asha's contempt for the narrator
fact: Asha refuses to speak directly to the narrator, delivering critical intelligence only through Daz, signaling a loss of respect.
source_quote: My dear boy," she said, and then looked at me with contempt, and then turned to Daz. "Tell the Dragonborn that...

subject: Asha's emotional vulnerability
fact: Asha expresses genuine exasperation and unexpected warmth about Jorlan and Ilvara’s broken relationship, revealing human depth beneath her hostility.
source_quote: I agree!" she said, with a warmth she'd shown none of us since we'd met her. "Like, you would think that in the midst of the abyss with the demons, everyone could get over their relationship issues, but no, no, no, no, no...

subject: Asha’s Final Intelligence Delivery
fact: Asha delivers the true nature of the spore illness — it originates only from Ilvara’s spores — but undermines it with 'I believe,' revealing her uncertainty and transforming authoritative knowledge into fragile opinion.
source_quote: The particular spore illness only originates from Ilvara's spores and from her mushroom. I believe.

subject: Asha’s Revelation of Personal History
fact: Asha reveals she and Jorlan are the only two not captured by Ilvara’s spores — she because she clings to Lolth, he because he hates Ilvara — and discloses their romantic past, exposing vulnerability beneath her contempt.
source_quote: The only three people who are no longer captured by her spores are myself and Jorlan... I mean, they used to have an affair, it used to be this whole thing, and then she broke up with him...

subject: Asha's Test
fact: Asha Vandree conducted a verbal and psychological test on Daz and the party, using theological accusations and emotional pressure to assess their conviction, knowledge, and willingness to act. Her questions were designed to provoke panic or reveal ignorance. The party’s calm, strategic responses — particularly Daz’s use of doubt as sincerity — passed the test, convincing her they are viable agents for her agenda.
source_quote: Well put, well put. This was just a test.

subject: Asha Vandree
fact: Asha Vandree admitted she was not going to kill Ilvara herself and needed Daz to do it.
source_quote: I was not going to kill her. That is what you… where you come in.

subject: Asha Vandree
fact: Asha Vandree asked whether Daz and Glabbagool had been infected by the spores of Zuggtmoy.
source_quote: have you two been infected by the spores, possessed by the crazed magic of Zuggtmoy? convinced of the bride's power? Is this another trick of Ilvara's?

subject: Asha Vandree
fact: Asha Vandree expresses genuine exasperation and emotional vulnerability about being stuck between Jorlan and Ilvara’s past relationship.
source_quote: Do you have any idea how aggravating that is?

subject: Asha Vandree
fact: Asha Vandree identifies the spore servants as former drow who embraced Ilvara’s power and the ecstasy of the spores.
source_quote: They are the drow of our party whom have totally succumbed to Ilvara's power... who embraced the spores and the ecstasy that came through them.

subject: Asha Vandree
fact: Asha Vandree questioned whether Daz was a wizard who prays to Lolth.
source_quote: You're a wizard. A wizard… a wizard who prays to Lolth?

subject: Asha Vandree
fact: Asha Vandree realized Daz was testing her discernment as a follower of Lolth.
source_quote: you are trying to test me, to see if I was one of those fake followers of Lolth, who are willing to believe every charlatan magic user that is somehow being possessed by the power of Lolth.

subject: Asha Vandree
fact: Asha Vandree reluctantly engages with the party, showing visible effort to speak to them.
source_quote: I could hear the slight effort it cost her to engage with us at all.

subject: Asha Vandree
fact: Asha Vandree reveals that only she and Jorlan are no longer captured by Ilvara’s spores.
source_quote: The only three people who are no longer captured by her spores are myself and Jorlan.

subject: Asha Vandree
fact: Asha Vandree said she thought Daz had strong allies with tactical awareness and destructive magic.
source_quote: I thought you had strong allies, who had a tactical awareness and understanding how to use their magic for destructive purposes.

subject: Asha Vandree
fact: Asha Vandree shows unexpected warmth and agreement when the speaker comments on the complexity of relationships.
source_quote: I agree!" she said, with a warmth she'd shown none of us since we'd met her.

subject: Asha Vandree
fact: Asha Vandree told Daz not to touch her.
source_quote: Don't touch me.

subject: Battle of the Heart Fungus
fact: The Battle of the Heart Fungus is a coordinated assault in which the party uses terrain, psychological manipulation, and precise spellcasting to dismantle Ilvara’s power structure. The Heart Fungus is targeted with the Dust of Suleiman, Ilvara is grappled into Phantasmal Killer by Zalthir, the Glyph of Warding is triggered by Jorlan’s rage, and Thorin engages in melee while Daz and others provide area denial.
source_quote: The glyph went down on the bridge... One 4th-level slot. I'd made my choice. The Dust of Suleiman on the fungus, because Asha was right.

subject: capture status of drow
fact: Only Asha and Jorlan are no longer captured by Ilvara's spores — Asha due to devotion to Lolth, Jorlan due to hatred of Ilvara.
source_quote: The only three people who are no longer captured by her spores are myself and Jorlan... Me, because I have diligently kept the faith to Lolth... and Jorlan, because apparently he really hates Ilvara for something or other.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz claimed he was speaking through the body that had communed with Lolth.
source_quote: I am… you are not speaking to the wizard of this body. I… he… this body has communed with Lolth. And I… I am speaking through this body.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz is perceived by Asha as the owner of an ooze familiar, which elevates his status in her eyes.
source_quote: An ooze familiar," she said, looking at Daz now with something approaching respect.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz is the one who decides to trigger the glyph on Jorlan’s side, acknowledging Jorlan is not an ally despite his hatred of Ilvara.
source_quote: Okay," I said. "And then, I guess the trigger is — anyone approaching from the side that Jorlan is on.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz is the one who inscribes the Glyph of Warding on the bridge, knowing it will kill anyone crossing it — including Jorlan — without discrimination.
source_quote: I finished the inscription and straightened up. The bridge was now a threshold. Everything on the far side of it was already committed to a detonation it didn't know about yet.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz noticed the small wet sound of Glabbagool opening his eyes and tracking left and right.
source_quote: I heard — I am fairly certain I heard — the small wet sound of him opening his eyes, which then began tracking left and right with the particular energy of someone who absolutely cannot help himself.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz opens up with a Fireball shaped so precisely around his allies that it catches Ilvara and her precious mushroom icon in the center of it, 24 damage worth of fire finding her even through her save, and the icon smolders.
source_quote: Daz opens up with a Fireball shaped so precisely around his allies that it catches Ilvara and her precious mushroom icon in the center of it, 24 damage worth of fire finding her even through her save, and the icon smolders.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz refused to break posture when Glabbagool spoke, saying 'I'm taking care of this, it's fine.'
source_quote: Glabbagool, I'm taking care of this, it's fine.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz said he really believes he has been infected by spores and that he has convinced others to join him.
source_quote: I really do believe that I have. Perhaps there are some spores within me, but I… it feels… I feel it. And by the way, I've convinced others to join me.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz said the conviction he shows is the kind this follower of Lolth shows.
source_quote: It's the kind of conviction this follower of Lolth shows.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz smooths over the party’s caution about spores by framing it as tactical wisdom and seeking expert guidance, earning Asha’s brief approval.
source_quote: Our caution came from unfamiliarity with mushroom-related side effects, and that asking for expert guidance was tactically sound rather than ignorant.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz stated he already feels the gratitude of Lolth.
source_quote: I already feel the gratitude of Lolth. I have that.

subject: Daz's Fireball damage
fact: Daz's Fireball deals 24 damage to Ilvara.
source_quote: 24 damage worth of fire finding her

subject: Fireball detonates
fact: Daz's Fireball detonates with precise targeting, catching Ilvara and her mushroom icon in the center despite her saving throw.
source_quote: Daz opens up with a Fireball shaped so precisely around his allies that it catches Ilvara and her precious mushroom icon in the center of it, 24 damage worth of fire finding her even through her save.

subject: Fireball impact
fact: Daz's Fireball detonated with precise targeting, catching Ilvara and her mushroom icon in the center, dealing 24 fire damage and causing the icon to smolder.
source_quote: The mushroom is burning. Ilvara is bleeding. The math has changed.

subject: Fireball strike
fact: Daz opens up with a Fireball shaped so precisely around his allies that it catches Ilvara and her precious mushroom icon in the center of it, 24 damage worth of fire finding her even through her save, and the icon smolders.
source_quote: Daz opens up with a Fireball shaped so precisely around his allies that it catches Ilvara and her precious mushroom icon in the center of it, 24 damage worth of fire finding her even through her save, and the icon smolders.

subject: Glabbagool
fact: Glabbagool began to form the shape of an utterance during the negotiation.
source_quote: The ooze had, apparently, opinions about the negotiation. It began to form the shape of an utterance — which is not something you want from what is supposed to be an inanimate ooze familiar — and Daz caught it with the ease of someone who has managed Glabbagool before.

subject: Glyph Detonation
fact: Jorlan’s charge triggers the Glyph of Warding, dealing 21 damage, destroying one spore servant, weakening another, and destabilizing the Heart Fungus. This shifts the tactical balance of the battle.
source_quote: He comes straight onto the bridge, straight onto the glyph, and the detonation is immediate and total — 21 damage, one spore servant gone to nothing...

subject: Glyph detonation trigger
fact: Jorlan is deliberately provoked into stepping onto the Glyph of Warding, triggering its detonation and eliminating one spore servant while damaging the Heart Fungus.
source_quote: Come get it, idiot!" ... "Jorlan charges. He comes straight onto the bridge, straight onto the glyph, and the detonation is immediate and total...

subject: Glyph Inscription and Trigger Selection
fact: The narrator inscribes the glyph and chooses Jorlan’s side as the trigger zone, not because Jorlan is evil, but because he is not trusted. This decision reflects a pragmatic moral failure — the party kills based on alliance, not justice. The glyph becomes a monument to their compromise.
source_quote: Okay," I said. "And then, I guess the trigger is — anyone approaching from the side that Jorlan is on.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum carefully inscribed the Glyph of Warding into the stone of the bridge, anticipating its use against Jorlan.
source_quote: the Glyph of Warding that Grygum spent real patience setting into the stone of the bridge.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum explained he had Glyph of Warding, Dust of Suleiman, and Phantasmal Killer, but only one 4th-level spell slot.
source_quote: So these powerful spells I've been talking about… they're all 4th level, and I only have one fourth level slot. I can only cast one.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum is grinding the Heart Fungus down with something that sounds like the word *Suleiman* and delivers twenty force damage per turn like a promise.
source_quote: Grygum is grinding the Heart Fungus down with something that sounds like the word *Suleiman* and delivers twenty force damage per turn like a promise.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum laid out his three 4th-level spells as keys for one lock.
source_quote: Three keys. One lock. The planning was, in a sense, just a very elaborate way of deciding which door we most needed to open.

subject: Grygum's Heart Fungus damage
fact: Grygum delivers twenty force damage per turn to the Heart Fungus.
source_quote: delivers twenty force damage per turn

subject: Ilvara
fact: The mushroom icon smolders.
source_quote: the icon smolders.

subject: Introduction of Glabbagool as a Familiar
fact: The party fabricates a cover story that Glabbagool is Daz’s familiar to avoid suspicion. Asha’s shift from alarm to respect demonstrates how status and perception override reality in their world — an ooze is more acceptable if labeled as a familiar.
source_quote: An ooze familiar," she said, looking at Daz now with something approaching respect.

subject: Jorlan
fact: Jorlan is a former drow who has not been infected by Ilvara’s spores, but is not allied with the party.
source_quote: The only three people who are no longer captured by her spores are myself and Jorlan.

subject: Jorlan
fact: Jorlan is standing on the Glyph of Warding, unaware of its presence, and is lured onto it by Thorin’s provocation.
source_quote: Jorlan charges. He comes straight onto the bridge, straight onto the glyph...

subject: mushroom smoldering
fact: The mushroom is burning. Ilvara is bleeding. The math has changed.
source_quote: The mushroom is burning. Ilvara is bleeding. The math has changed.

subject: Phantasmal Killer duration
fact: Phantasmal Killer can last up to a minute.
source_quote: it can last up to a minute

subject: Precision Attack failed
fact: The Precision Attack fails when the attacker rolls a 2 against Jorlan's AC of 18.
source_quote: I know it the moment the blade leaves my hands at the wrong angle — too high, overcommitted, Jorlan's AC is 18 and I'm rolling a 2 and there's nothing in the world that fixes a 2. The Precision Attack doesn't find it.

subject: relationship history between Jorlan and Ilvara
fact: Jorlan and Ilvara had a romantic affair that ended with her breaking up with him, leaving him bitter and emotionally entangled.
source_quote: They used to have an affair, it used to be this whole thing, and then she broke up with him, and then he was bitter because she broke up with him.

subject: Spell Slot Dilemma
fact: Grygum possesses three 4th-level spells but only one spell slot, forcing a strategic decision: which spell to cast — Glyph of Warding, Dust of Suleiman, or Phantasmal Killer — and which to sacrifice. The choice will determine whether the team employs infrastructure destruction, psychological warfare, or environmental trapping.
source_quote: So these powerful spells I've been talking about… they're all 4th level, and I only have one fourth level slot. I can only cast one.

subject: spell slot limit
fact: The caster has only one 4th-level spell slot available.
source_quote: I only have one fourth level slot

subject: Spore Cloud Release
fact: The Heart Fungus unleashes a lethal cloud of spores that forces Zalthir to ascend ten feet to breathe, demonstrating its active hostility and tactical awareness.
source_quote: ...it unleashes a cloud of spores that hits Zalthir so hard he has to climb ten feet straight up just to breathe.

subject: spore infection risk
fact: Spores from Ilvara's fungal network can transform drow into mindless servants, as evidenced by Daz's condition.
source_quote: I mean, — look at him! He's already infected. I don't want to be infected.

subject: spore servant origin
fact: The spore servants are former drow who embraced Ilvara’s claims and succumbed to her spores.
source_quote: They are the drow of our party whom have totally succumbed to Ilvara's power... embraced the spores and the ecstasy that came through them.

subject: Tactical Reassessment of the Assassination Plan
fact: Grygum’s original plan to target Ilvara directly was overruled after Asha Vandree’s intervention, shifting focus to the Heart Fungus as the primary objective. This reorientation transforms the use of Dust of Suleiman from a direct attack into infrastructure demolition, and redefines the entire mission’s strategy.
source_quote: The Heart Fungus was the key. That was her point, and she wasn't wrong.

subject: The Battle of the Heart Fungus
