source_quote: I filed it under 'Zalthir: things that are not in the records but will be.'

subject: session date
fact: The events described occurred during a single, continuous narrative arc — likely a single session or multi-hour roleplay sequence — marked by thematic recursion, character breakthroughs, and meta-commentary on lore and system failure.
source_quote: Then: 'You are beginning to remember, I think, all those shadow monks that drove you nuts.'

subject: Session Date
fact: The events occurred during a single night of medical and metaphysical inquiry — the culmination of failed temple visits, failed examinations, and a final revelation.
source_quote: Twenty-three. My best of the evening, arriving too late to be medically useful and just in time to be philosophically concerning.

subject: session date
fact: The events occurred during the party’s arrival at Candlekeep, following their journey from the Underdark; the exact calendar date is unrecorded, but the temporal context is marked by the transition from subterranean chaos to institutional stillness.

subject: session date
fact: The session occurs on the 29th day of the 3rd Tenday of Taraskh 1493 DR.
source_quote: On the 5th day of the 2nd Tenday of Taraskh 1493

subject: session date
fact: The trial occurred during an unspecified but internally significant session in Candlekeep’s inner ward, marked not by calendar date but by the weight of accumulated tradition and the rupture of Zalthir’s unorthodox performance.
source_quote: Two hundred years old, half-elven, eighty years gone from the Garden of Shadow after refusing an order he never explained.

subject: six days
fact: Elin has been silent for six days, during which she has compulsively drawn the six-pointed star, establishing the duration of her perceptual crisis and the pattern of her non-verbal communication.
source_quote: My daughter Elin is 7 years old and has been silent for 6 days. She draws the same shape on every flat surface.

subject: The Day of Arrival at Candlekeep
fact: The day Zalthir and his party arrived at Candlekeep marks the convergence of the Underdark’s madness, the spy’s rebellion, and the institution’s refusal to resolve. It is the first day of delay — and perhaps, the beginning of something that cannot be contained.
source_quote: Centuries do that to a building.

subject: the moment Dawnbringer went quiet in Philemon's study
fact: Dawnbringer went quiet.
source_quote: Dawnbringer went quiet.

subject: the moment Daz told the truth in the Hall of Divination
fact: I told her the truth.
source_quote: I told her the truth.

subject: the moment Zalthir chose option C
fact: Zalthir chose option C.
source_quote: Zalthir chose option C.

subject: three years ago
fact: Tarvis Ulain died three years ago in Daggerford, and the monument to him was funded two years after his death, placing the current events approximately one year after the monument’s unveiling.
source_quote: The primary text told us this was Tarvis Ulain, paladin, dead three years... The whole thing was funded two years after the war...

subject: three years ago
fact: Tarvis Ulain died three years ago in Daggerford, marking the timeline of the monument’s creation and the beginning of the town’s quiet spiritual reckoning.
source_quote: Tarvis Ulain, paladin, dead three years.

subject: two years after the war
fact: The Metalworkers Guild funded the Tarvis Ulain monument two years after the war, indicating the delayed, institutional nature of post-conflict memorialization and ideological compromise.
source_quote: The whole thing was funded two years after the war by a Metalworkers Guild.

subject: Two Years Ago
fact: Two years ago, the drow woke up in a jail cell with no memories and a headache that never left. This is the temporal anchor for their loss of identity and the beginning of their current journey — a point before which their past is inaccessible, and after which they have been navigating a world they no longer recognize.
source_quote: before I woke up in a jail cell with no memories and a headache that apparently never left.

subject: two years post-war
fact: The Metalworkers Guild funded the monument two years after the war, situating its creation in the early recovery phase of Daggerford’s post-conflict society.
source_quote: The whole thing was funded two years after the war by a Metalworkers Guild.

subject: arrival at Candlekeep
fact: The party arrived at Candlekeep after traveling from the Underdark; their bag’s contents were discovered, triggering a formal review by the Gate Warden, assignments by the First Reader, and the beginning of a moral and institutional standoff over the spy’s fate.
source_quote: We gave them the books at the gate.

subject: bard performance event
fact: The bard performed 'The Kenku Could Not Fly' at the Burning Wizard Inn.
source_quote: She had a closing number she'd been doing all season. This one was called 'The Kenku Could Not Fly.'

subject: Blind Monk
fact: The blind monk asked Zalthir: 'Did you not practice your forms while traveling?'
source_quote: Did you not practice your forms while traveling?

subject: Blind Monk
fact: The blind monk said Zalthir skipped the third breath, didn't enter his ki in the hara, and let it bleed into his fingertips like a poison.
source_quote: You skip the third breath. You don't enter your ki in the hara. You let it bleed into your fingertips like a poison. It is technically wrong in every scroll.

subject: Blind Monk
fact: The blind monk said to Zalthir: 'Show me what else you haven't learned.'
source_quote: Show me what else you haven't learned.

subject: Blind Monk
fact: The blind monk said to Zalthir: 'You have learned nothing.' after Zalthir failed the Weightless Shadow.
source_quote: You have learned nothing.

subject: body-language contradiction
fact: Yvenne's body had been disagreeing with her words for the last five minutes — a practiced stillness that betrayed more than the public record allowed.
source_quote: I looked at her. At the way she was sitting. At the way she had been sitting for the last several minutes — the practiced stillness of someone who knows more than the public record allows her to say, maintaining the pose of a person who is simply informing rather than carefully navigating.

subject: Bookwyrm
fact: Bookwyrm noticed the bag containing Glabbagool and the miniaturized House T'sarran spy and found it unacceptable.
source_quote: She'd noticed the bag. Specifically, she'd noticed what was in the bag — because when we'd come through the gate, we'd had to open it to show the guards Glabbagool, and the miniaturized House T'sarran spy had been right there alongside him, which she apparently found unacceptable,

subject: Brick-Shattering Strike
fact: Zalthir’s 29-to-hit strike on a thrown brick resulted in its complete destruction — an unprecedented physical manifestation of shadow power that silenced skepticism and forced reevaluation of combat doctrine.
source_quote: The brick did not survive.

subject: Candlekeep's prisoner policy
fact: Candlekeep holds prisoners but does not keep them — they are delayed, not jailed, and eventually released with a warning.
source_quote: We hold prisoners. We do not keep them. If you give her to us, what you are giving us is a delay.

subject: Chant Degradation Pattern
fact: A specific, non-random degradation pattern in a liturgical chant has been observed in three individuals — the young scholar, Eldred, and the Field Ward Preacher — indicating a possible contagion, doctrinal corruption, or targeted cognitive assault.
source_quote: The same pattern. The same wrongness by a hair.

subject: dawnbringer restoration event
fact: Dawnbringer performed lesser restoration on Elin.
source_quote: Lesser restoration settled in.

subject: dawnbringer's entrance
fact: Dawnbringer made an entrance without invitation.
source_quote: Dawnbringer did not wait for a second invitation.

subject: Dawnbringer's healing enrollment
fact: Dawnbringer was formally enrolled in a two-stage healing process — light reclamation and mourning — initiated by Philemon after recognizing her sentient trauma from centuries of darkness and disuse.
source_quote: We're all gonna grow out of this. Hopefully, Dawnbringer grows a plus one.

subject: Dawnbringer's reconnection to light
fact: Dawnbringer is undergoing a two-stage process: first, reacquainting with daylight without combat, then grieving her past trauma — a ritual initiated by Philemon and accepted by the wielder.
source_quote: We will start with the first.

subject: Dawnbringer's silence in Philemon's study
fact: Dawnbringer went quiet. Not the silence of someone thinking. The other kind. The kind where the thing you'd been not-saying for a long time just gets asked out loud in a room with other people in it.
source_quote: Dawnbringer went quiet. Not the silence of someone thinking. The other kind. The kind where the thing you'd been not-saying for a long time just gets asked out loud in a room with other people in it.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz felt a recognition when reading the term 'Daz'issin' and its lit. meaning 'small shadow,' as if it resonated with his own name.
source_quote: I gotta tell you, the first line of this, where it says, *Daz'issin*, and lit., *small shadow*, made me feel like I was reading, like, millennial shorthand. And that I didn't understand it.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz noted the exits in the Burning Wizard Inn.
source_quote: I noted the exits. Front door, obvious. Side passage near the kitchen, partially obscured by a stack of barrels. Stairs to the upper rooms. The window behind the performer's corner, narrow but workable in an emergency.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz noticed his headache had been bothering him since arriving at Candlekeep.
source_quote: My head had been complaining since we arrived at Candlekeep.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz noticed the pressure in his own head.
source_quote: Daz mentioned the pressure in his own head — had been mentioning it, in various indirect ways, for a while now.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz noticed the ritual archive privileges of the fourth seat in Menzoberranzan and connected them to the concept of 'struck' as institutional erasure.
source_quote: She mentioned, almost as an aside, that the fourth seat holds ritual archive privileges in Menzoberranzan — that having archive privileges means having the legal apparatus to access and alter records.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz put his hand to his temple and kept it there.
source_quote: His hand went to his temple and stayed there.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz realized silence from Yvenne is an answer in the ledger — an acknowledgment of hidden truth.
source_quote: She said nothing. Which is, in the ledger, an answer.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz realized the headache was not from the sun but from the proximity to knowledge.
source_quote: The proximity — to the knowledge, or to whatever sat underneath the knowledge — was producing a friction I had been mis-attributing to the sun all day.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz realized the word 'blithering idiot' didn't fit him.
source_quote: I asked the second logical question. 'Am I the blithering idiot?'

subject: Daz
fact: Daz went quiet beside the narrator somewhere around the second hour of walking — not his usual quiet.
source_quote: Daz went quiet beside me somewhere around the second hour of walking. Not his usual quiet.

subject: daz's cataloging of the inn
fact: Daz catalogued the exits and history of the Burning Wizard Inn.
source_quote: The first thing I catalogued... I noted the exits.

subject: daz's examination of dwarven inscription
fact: Daz read the dwarven inscription twice to ensure he hadn't misread it.
source_quote: I read it twice because Dwarven is, you know, actually my language, or one of them, and I wanted to make sure I hadn't misread.

subject: daz's headache onset
fact: Daz had been experiencing pressure in his head for some time.
source_quote: Daz mentioned the pressure in his own head — had been mentioning it, in various indirect ways, for a while now.

subject: Daz's realization of possible maternal naming
fact: Daz realizes his name may have been given by his mother as a softening form — Daz'issin — intended to ensure his survival, and that this naming may be connected to a suppressed lineage.
source_quote: Well, isn't my name, Daz? Maybe it's my full name? I asked whether someone might call me Daz, and this was actually a name that, like, my mother used.

subject: Daz's silence
fact: Daz went quiet beside Zalthir, hand going to his temple — the first sign the madness from the Underdark had not stopped at the surface.
source_quote: Daz went quiet beside me somewhere around the second hour of walking. Not his usual quiet. His hand went to his temple and stayed there.

subject: Daz's truth disclosure
fact: Daz disclosed his full, unfiltered history — amnesia, imprisonment, escape from the Underdark — to Sister Yvenne, breaking drow cultural norms and triggering a rare moment of trust in Candlekeep’s knowledge exchange system.
source_quote: I just couldn't afford the usual approach. When you don't know what you're hiding, you can't protect it.

subject: Daz's truth-telling in the Hall of Divination
fact: Daz told Sister Yvenne the truth about his amnesia, his escape from the Underdark, and his unexplained headache, offering everything he knew in exchange for information.
source_quote: I have a headache, but I'll tell you the story. This is the short version. I don't have much memory before being locked up with a few people in a jail. Because some spider thing was, like, trying to keep us. And we've made an escape. We were in the Underdark. We've had many, many adventures, yada yada yada. Now I'm here in Candlekeep. My head hurts a little bit, and I don't know who I am, or my history, and I don't know why my head hurts.

subject: Eldred's pattern
fact: Eldred had the same pattern — the man who went insane. The Field Ward Preacher had it too.
source_quote: Eldred had it, earlier in the journey — the man who went insane. The Field Ward Preacher had it too.

subject: erasure of houses that used the name Daz'issin
fact: Most houses that used the name Daz'issin did not last, suggesting systemic suppression or destruction linked to the name's use.
source_quote: The houses that had used it, most of them, did not last.

subject: footnote removal
fact: A footnote referencing an appendix was removed mechanically — by razor, at least fifty years ago — from a two-hundred-year-old heraldry book, *Geography and Cities, Menzoberranzan, Pillars of Woe*.
source_quote: I found a footnote instead. 'I gotta tell you, the first line of this, where it says, *Daz'issin*, and lit., *small shadow*, made me feel like I was reading, like, millennial shorthand. And that I didn't understand it.' The footnote referenced an appendix. The appendix was missing. I looked at the cut. It was mechanical. A razor. Not age, not water damage, not the slow forgetting of paper that has been handled too many times. A razor, at least fifty years ago, someone had taken to this book and removed what the footnote pointed to.

subject: Glabbagool
fact: Glabbagool paused and asked Zalthir directly: 'Will I be more of a monk or less of a monk by watching her? Is this some kind of pre-monk training you've put me in?'
source_quote: Glabbagool paused, and asked me directly: "Zalthir? Will I be more of a monk or less of a monk by watching her? Is this some kind of pre-monk training you've put me in?"

subject: Glabbagool's Acceptance of the Spy as Curriculum
fact: Glabbagool, after being told by Zalthir that watching the spy was pre-monk training, drew himself up and declared: 'I will keep an eye on her!' — with six pseudo-eyes fixed on her simultaneously.
source_quote: Glabbagool took this with complete seriousness. The work counted; he had been told so. He drew himself up, or the ooze equivalent of it. "I will keep an eye on her!" Six pseudo-eyes fixed on the spy simultaneously.

subject: Glabbagool's prisoner training
fact: Glabbagool became a better monk by watching the spy — patience under provocation, stillness amid hostility, responding to aggression without being ruled by it.
source_quote: Will I be more of a monk or less of a monk by watching her? Is this some kind of pre-monk training you've put me in?

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum made a noise when he read that Tarvis Ulain had served Bahamut.
source_quote: Grygum made a sound when he got to the part confirming Tarvis had served Bahamut — not a word, just the noise a person makes when something clicks into place.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum noticed Daz's change and asked whether it connected to the spreading madness from the Underdark.
source_quote: Grygum noticed too, and asked whether it connected to the voices — the spreading madness we'd watched move through the Underdark like groundwater through stone.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum realized the madness from the Underdark was reaching the surface through Elin.
source_quote: Oh," I said, as something slid into place. "There's all the people — hearing voices?

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum received the love song about Stroud's chess game in the way he receives most things downgraded by translation: politely, and with the file already updated.
source_quote: Grygum received this in the way he receives most things downgraded by translation: politely, and with the file already updated.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum wrote down Elin’s words: 'The wells are not wells anymore.'
source_quote: I wrote it down. It is what I do.

subject: grygum's gold piece donation
fact: Grygum dropped a gold piece in for his pewter hand cast.
source_quote: Grygum dropped a gold piece in for his.

subject: grygum's observation of the kenku song
fact: Grygum noted that the Kenku song's principle mapped well onto Whistler.
source_quote: Grygum... observed drily that the song's principle — steal what was needed — mapped rather well onto Whistler.

subject: grygum's philosophical conclusion
fact: Grygum concluded there was a tenuous connection between Elin's condition and Daz's headache.
source_quote: There's some kind of tenuous connection there?

subject: Grygum's summary of the situation
fact: Grygum summarized the containment breach as: 'We've been caught.'
source_quote: We've been caught.

subject: Headache inquiry at Candlekeep
fact: The narrator attempts to ask about their persistent headache during a formal research session at Candlekeep, but is redirected toward the primary purpose of the inquiry.
source_quote: Can I see or read any of… do any of them… I'm… at this point, my headache… my headache's been bothering me.

subject: Healing work in Waterdeep
fact: The narrator and Dawnbringer performed healing work in Waterdeep by aiding orphans and the sick, allowing Dawnbringer to fulfill her purpose and visibly regain happiness.
source_quote: We'd done the healing work in Waterdeep on the road south, found orphans and the sick and let her do what she was built to do. She'd been visibly happy.

subject: Historical Erasure of Daz'issin Lineage
fact: The systematic removal of all records pertaining to Daz'issin — through book mutilation, archive strikes, and house annihilation — constitutes a large-scale, deliberate, and costly act of memory destruction targeting a single name and its bearers.
source_quote: That is not a small act. That is a very large, very expensive, very deliberate act.

subject: House Erasure Attempt
fact: One noble house attempted to wipe out a rival house but failed to eliminate a single survivor — a blithering child idiot. The house was subsequently destroyed by the wider community. The child’s fate remains officially unknown, and the survivor may be the drow.
source_quote: They had tried to wipe out another, and failed to account for one survivor. A child. A blithering child idiot, she said, and I noted the language was hers, not mine.

subject: information exchange start
fact: The information exchange between the drow and Sister Yvenne began with the disclosure of amnesia and imprisonment.
source_quote: I have a headache, but I'll tell you the story. This is the short version. I don't have much memory before being locked up...

subject: Khell-Vire's philosophy
fact: Khell-Vire said: 'I will not be there. This is your work, not mine.'
source_quote: I will not be there. This is your work, not mine.

subject: Lesser Restoration on Elin
fact: A Lesser Restoration spell cast by Dawnbringer cleared enough mental interference for Elin to speak one coherent sentence — 'The wells are not wells anymore.'
source_quote: And then she spoke. 'The wells are not wells anymore.'

subject: maerith's temple visits
fact: Maerith visited multiple temples seeking help for Elin.
source_quote: she'd been to the temples, plural, and the temples had no answer.

subject: Memory Restoration Trigger
fact: The drow’s headache and fragmented memories began to resolve upon hearing the word 'struck' and understanding its bureaucratic meaning. The recognition of linguistic nuance — not factual recall — triggered a cognitive shift, suggesting their identity and past are encoded in the language of Menzoberranzan’s power structures, not in their personal memory.
source_quote: Something in me landed on it before I could explain why.

subject: monument unveiling
fact: A bronze forearm monument to Tarvis Ulain was unveiled in Daggerford's market square, bearing a Stroudite inscription and a Gauntlet-approved record, creating theological tension between Bahamutian and Stroudite factions.
source_quote: There was a monument there — a bronze-cast forearm, severed at the elbow, mounted on a stone pillar... The secondary inscription... *The move is yours.*

subject: monument unveiling
fact: A bronze monument to Tarvis Ulain, depicting his severed forearm, was erected in Daggerford’s market square two years after his death, bearing layered inscriptions that reference both Bahamutian devotion and Stroudite symbolism.
source_quote: There was a monument there — a bronze-cast forearm, severed at the elbow, mounted on a stone pillar... The primary text told us this was Tarvis Ulain... Daz found the secondary inscription. Dwarven, on the base. *The move is yours.*

subject: Narrator
fact: The narrator noticed a young human scholar in the far corner reciting something under his breath — a rhythmic, almost liturgical chant.
source_quote: There was a young human scholar in the far corner — not a human scholar, a *young* human scholar, because those are meaningfully different things and I did not want to get the category wrong — who was reciting something under his breath. A chant of some kind. Rhythmic, almost liturgical.

subject: Narrator
fact: The narrator noticed the scholar's breathing was almost right but wrong by a hair in a way that required knowledge of the correct version to notice.
source_quote: His breathing was almost right. The pauses fell almost correctly. The pattern was almost the one it was supposed to be — and wrong by a hair in a way that took actual knowledge of the correct version to notice.

subject: Narrator
fact: The narrator realized the specific wrongness in the chant was not a beginner's error but a very particular kind of degradation.
source_quote: the specific wrongness of it — the way he syncopated his breath against the syllables, or tried to — was not a beginner's error. It was a very particular kind of degradation.

subject: Narrator
fact: The narrator wrote down the exact cadence, the placement of the false syncopation, and the point in the verse where the chant bent away from the original.
source_quote: I wrote it down. The exact cadence, the placement of the false syncopation, the point in the verse where the chant bent away from the original.

subject: Perceptual Distortion Diagnosis
fact: The party concluded that Elin’s condition is not a disease, infection, or magical effect, but a perceptual failure — the world is transmitting corrupted signals she cannot interpret, resulting in silence and symbolic repetition.
source_quote: It wasn't a disease in the conventional sense. It was more like the world had started speaking a language she couldn't process.

subject: pewter hand cast sales
fact: A village priest began selling miniature pewter reproductions of Tarvis Ulain's severed hand as donations to the Order of the Gauntlet, sparking irony and unease among the party due to their size and the monument's symbolism.
source_quote: He was carrying a tray of small pewter reproductions of Tarvis's hand cast, miniature things, charm-sized.

subject: priest's revelation about stroudite inscription
fact: The priest conceded the Stroudite inscription remained because it was a gift.
source_quote: It was a gift," he said finally. "And since it was a gift, we decided the inscription could remain.

subject: public record sealing
fact: There was one house she could not speak of in the room — not because she would not, but because the public record is sealed, and she is today the public record.
source_quote: Then she told me there was one house she could not speak of in the room. Not because she would not — because the public record is sealed, and she is today the public record.

subject: removal of appendix from Geography and Cities, Menzoberranzan, Pillars of Woe
fact: Someone used a razor at least fifty years ago to remove the appendix referenced by a footnote about Daz'issin, indicating deliberate erasure of information.
source_quote: A razor, at least fifty years ago, someone had taken to this book and removed what the footnote pointed to.

subject: revelation of identity
fact: The drow's identity as the 'blithering idiot' survivor of House destruction is implied but not confirmed.
source_quote: Am I the blithering idiot?

subject: Shadow Step + Strike Combination
fact: Zalthir’s synchronized use of shadow step and melee strike — though individually flawed — produced a result that resonated with ancient shadow monk principles, triggering Khell-Vire’s recognition and the award of a new technique.
source_quote: It is your combination of the shadow step and the hit that redeems your lack of skills in all other possible areas.

subject: shadow technique award
fact: Zalthir was awarded a specialized shadow technique after demonstrating an unorthodox, manually-ignored method that combined shadow step and strike — a breakthrough acknowledged by Khell-Vire as the most significant aspect of his combat identity.
source_quote: Zalthir chose option C.

subject: silence as answer
fact: She said nothing. Which is, in the ledger, an answer.
source_quote: I asked if they weren't successfully all gone? She said nothing. Which is, in the ledger, an answer.

subject: Silence of Yvenne
fact: Yvenne’s refusal to answer the question 'What if they weren't successfully all gone?' constitutes a deliberate, non-verbal affirmation in Menzoberranzan’s culture — where silence in the ledger is an answer — implying that at least one house or lineage tied to Daz'issin may still endure.
source_quote: She said nothing. Which is, in the ledger, an answer.

subject: Spy
fact: The spy announced that she was a prisoner and wished to be formally jailed by Candlekeep's guards.
source_quote: She turned to Kalan and announced that she was a prisoner and wished to be formally jailed by Candlekeep's guards.

subject: statue funding event
fact: The statue was funded by the Metalworkers Guild two years after the war.
source_quote: The statue had been funded by the Metalworkers Guild, two years post-war.

subject: Striking of the Fourth Seat
fact: The fourth seat in Menzoberranzan’s hierarchy holds ritual archive privileges, allowing legal access to and alteration of records; its being 'struck' was not political deletion but a sophisticated, infrastructural erasure requiring payment, influence, and obfuscation.
source_quote: Having archive privileges means having the legal apparatus to access and alter records. That a struck fourth seat was not merely a political erasure. It was the expensive kind.

subject: struck fourth seat in Menzoberranzan
fact: The fourth seat holds ritual archive privileges in Menzoberranzan, and when struck, it is not merely a political erasure but an expensive, infrastructure-dependent act requiring knowledge of the right people and payment that leaves no trace.
source_quote: The fourth seat holds ritual archive privileges in Menzoberranzan — that having archive privileges means having the legal apparatus to access and alter records. That a struck fourth seat was not merely a political erasure. It was the expensive kind. The kind that requires knowing the right people and paying the right price and having the infrastructure to make the payment look like it was never made.

subject: The Blind Monk's Final Judgment
fact: After Zalthir failed all three formal techniques, the blind monk sighed and walked away — declaring Zalthir had learned nothing.
source_quote: He tried stealth for the Eldritch Claw. His number landed somewhere that would have been insufficient even with generous interpretation. The monk sighed again and walked away.

subject: The Decision to Keep the Spy
fact: Candlekeep's Gate Warden Kalan Strongbranch offered only a delay — not imprisonment or execution — and declared that if the party needed something else, they would need to do it themselves.
source_quote: He laid out Candlekeep's position without apology: "... we will not deliver to House T'sarran, and we will not execute her. Eventually, we will release her at our gate with a warning. If you need something else, you will need to do it yourselves."

subject: The Decision to Keep the Spy
fact: The First Reader told the spy that the decision to keep or release her was not hers — it was the party's — as a guest and member of the adventuring party.
source_quote: The First Reader looked at her with something that might have been sympathy and explained that as a guest of Candlekeep — as a member, technically, of our adventuring party — the decision was ours, not hers.

subject: The Final Exchange Between Zalthir and the Blind Monk
fact: Zalthir asked whether he could punch the monk — and he did — and the sparring match that followed was evenly balanced.
source_quote: Zalthir asked whether he could punch the monk. ... He could. He did. The sparring match that followed was, by all observation, evenly balanced...

subject: The Final Note on the Spy
fact: The spy and Glabbagool became great friends — she screamed about the meditation, but they talked.
source_quote: He said they'd become great friends.

subject: the First Reader's reaction to the spy
fact: The First Reader looked at the spy with something that might have been sympathy and explained the decision was not hers.
source_quote: The First Reader looked at her with something that might have been sympathy and explained that as a guest of Candlekeep — as a member, technically, of our adventuring party — the decision was ours, not hers.

subject: The monk
fact: The monk stood there for a moment, something recalibrating behind his blindness.
source_quote: He stood there for a moment, something recalibrating behind his blindness

subject: the monk's final question
fact: The blind monk asked Zalthir: 'Show me what else you haven't learned.'
source_quote: Show me what else you haven't learned.

subject: the priest's declaration of faith
fact: The priest declared himself a pure Bahamutian.
source_quote: He himself was, he wanted us to know, *a pure Bahamutian*.

subject: The Question of the Bone King
fact: The note on Khell-Vire's desk reads: 'Zalthir, the Underdark, until the Bone King sings.' — a phrase neither Zalthir nor Khell-Vire could place.
source_quote: On Khell-Vire's desk, visible from where I was standing: *Zalthir, the Underdark, until the Bone King sings.* Zalthir stared at it. Khell-Vire stared at it. Neither of them could place it.

subject: The Question of the Broken Mirror
fact: Khell-Vire asked Zalthir: 'Does this phrase mean anything to you that you have lived through that resonates with the phrase?' — and Zalthir replied: 'Not particularly.'
source_quote: Perhaps if I asked it differently — does this phrase mean anything to you that you have lived through that resonates with the phrase?" "Not particularly."

subject: therapy session start
fact: The therapy session for Dawnbringer began with the first work: remembering daylight without needing to fight.
source_quote: The first work is light. The second work is mourning.

subject: the scholar's chant
fact: The young human scholar recited a chant under his breath — rhythmic, almost liturgical — and the pattern was wrong by a hair, in a way that took actual knowledge of the correct version to notice.
source_quote: There was a young human scholar in the far corner — not a human scholar, a *young* human scholar, because those are meaningfully different things and I did not want to get the category wrong — who was reciting something under his breath. A chant of some kind. Rhythmic, almost liturgical.

subject: The Shadow Monk Trial
fact: The blind monk tested Zalthir on three techniques: the Weightless Shadow, the Efficient Strike, the Eldritch Claw — and judged all three as failures.
source_quote: Then came the formal demonstration. Three techniques: the Weightless Shadow, the Efficient Strike, the Eldritch Claw. The monk had the rubric. Zalthir had to execute against it.

subject: the spy's demand
fact: The spy demanded to be formally jailed by Candlekeep, treating imprisonment as a right she had never before had to argue for.
source_quote: She announced that she was a prisoner and wished to be formally jailed by Candlekeep's guards.

subject: The Spy's Demand for Formal Imprisonment
fact: The spy turned to Kalan and announced: 'I am a prisoner and wish to be formally jailed by Candlekeep's guards.'
source_quote: The spy, for her part, was furious. She turned to Kalan and announced that she was a prisoner and wished to be formally jailed by Candlekeep's guards.

subject: the spy's fury
fact: The spy was furious when told she could not be formally jailed — she had opinions. Several of them.
source_quote: The spy was furious. She turned to Kalan and announced that she was a prisoner and wished to be formally jailed by Candlekeep's guards.

subject: the wall remembers
fact: The soot mark on the south wall sat where it always sat. The floor, scrubbed every season. The wall remembers.
source_quote: The soot mark on the south wall sat where it always sat. The floor, scrubbed every season. The wall remembers.

subject: Thorin's final question
fact: Thorin asked: 'Can he attack him while he's walking away? Blindside him, as it were?'
source_quote: Can he attack him while he's walking away? Blindside him, as it were?

subject: Thorin's observation on Glabbagool
fact: Thorin observed that Glabbagool seemed ambivalent about his role as prisoner watcher.
source_quote: Thorin observed that Glabbagool seemed ambivalent.

subject: Thorin's peace
fact: Thorin came back in with the settled look of a man who had had a thought that satisfied him. 'Life takes you in weird directions and weird places,' he said. 'You just gotta go with it.'
source_quote: Life takes you in weird directions and weird places," he said. "You just gotta go with it.

subject: travel to Menzoberranzan
fact: Menzoberranzan is approximately six weeks away via the Underdark.
source_quote: through the Underdark, through Waterdeep, into the libraries of Candlekeep

subject: travel to Sloobludop
fact: Sloobludop is approximately eight days away via the Darklake.
source_quote: the town of Sloopdopblop is just eight days away

subject: Yvenne
fact: Yvenne refused to answer whether Daz's name is connected to Daz'issin, leaving the question unresolved.
source_quote: She said nothing.

subject: Yvenne
fact: Yvenne's body stopped matching her words, revealing a careful navigation of information beyond the public record.
source_quote: Yvenne's body had been disagreeing with her words for the last five minutes.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir asked whether he could punch the monk.
source_quote: Zalthir asked whether he could punch the monk.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir came back down from the roof settled, with the expression of someone closing an internal argument, not opening an external one.
source_quote: Zalthir climbed to the roof to meditate. He came back down later, settled. The expression of someone closing an internal argument, not opening an external one.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir noticed Daz's unusual quiet and hand-to-temple gesture but did not say anything yet.
source_quote: I noticed. I didn't say anything yet.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir noticed the note on Khell-Vire's desk: 'Zalthir, the Underdark, until the Bone King sings.'
source_quote: On Khell-Vire's desk, visible from where I was standing: *Zalthir, the Underdark, until the Bone King sings.* Zalthir stared at it.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir responded flatly to Khell-Vire's question: 'Granted, given that constraint or specification, can you clarify?'
source_quote: Zalthir's response was immediate and flat: "Granted, given that constraint or specification, can you clarify?"

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir was annoyed by Khell-Vire's line of questioning, in the way he found shadow monk classes annoying.
source_quote: Zalthir, to his credit, didn't pretend to find it profound. He found it annoying, in the specific way that all those shadow monk classes he'd ignored had been annoying, which told its own story.

subject: Zalthir's failed demonstration
fact: Zalthir failed the Weightless Shadow, Efficient Strike, and Eldritch Claw by adhering to survival-based Underdark practice rather than formal monk form.
source_quote: The corridor was narrow. The form was irrelevant. Did you not practice your forms while traveling?

subject: Zalthir's final assessment
fact: Zalthir concluded: 'It was. Patience under provocation. Maintaining stillness when the environment is actively hostile. Responding to aggression without being ruled by it.'
source_quote: It was. Patience under provocation. Maintaining stillness when the environment is actively hostile. Responding to aggression without being ruled by it.

subject: Zalthir's final strike
fact: Zalthir performed a final, precise strike through the shadows themselves — landing with unambiguous power — which prompted Khell-Vire to recognize his transformation and offer him a specialized technique.
source_quote: His strike landed at a number that left no ambiguity.

subject: Zalthir's meditation
fact: Zalthir climbed to the roof to meditate. He came back down later, settled. The expression of someone closing an internal argument, not opening an external one.
source_quote: Zalthir climbed to the roof to meditate. He came back down later, settled. The expression of someone closing an internal argument, not opening an external one.

subject: Zalthir's Realization About the Blind Monk's Question
fact: Zalthir realized that Khell-Vire wasn't asking what he knew — he was asking what he had become through what he'd lived.
source_quote: I found this genuinely interesting. Not the answer — there wasn't one — but the structure of the question. Khell-Vire wasn't asking what Zalthir knew. He was asking what Zalthir had *become* through what he'd lived.

subject: Zalthir's realization about the chant
fact: Zalthir knows the chant — he knows what the scholar was doing wrong, and the specific wrongness of it — the way he syncopated his breath against the syllables — was not a beginner's error.
source_quote: I know that chant. I know it well enough to know what he was doing wrong, and the specific wrongness of it — the way he syncopated his breath against the syllables, or tried to — was not a beginner's error.

subject: Zalthir's reflection on shadow monk pedagogy
fact: Zalthir said: 'I've played this game before, my friends,' referencing five centuries of shadow monk tradition.
source_quote: I've played this game before, my friends

subject: Zalthir's response to the monk
fact: Zalthir asked whether he could punch the monk — and did.
source_quote: Zalthir asked whether he could punch the monk.

subject: Zalthir's roll
fact: Zalthir rolled a 30 to hit the monk as he walked away.
source_quote: I mean, I rolled a 30 to hit. Does that get me anything?

subject: Zalthir's shadow punch through the shadows
fact: Zalthir recalled something from the Underdark — a moment where he'd found a way to punch *through* the shadows themselves, precise as a surgical cut. He proposed showing that. He warned the blind monk, then executed it. His strike landed at a number that left no ambiguity.
source_quote: Zalthir recalled something from the Underdark — a moment where he'd found a way to punch *through* the shadows themselves, precise as a surgical cut.

subject: Zalthir's trial of the broken mirror
fact: Zalthir skipped the third breath, bled ki into fingertips, and arrived three seconds faster than the Grandmaster, despite technically violating every scroll.
source_quote: You skip the third breath. You don't enter your ki in the hara. You let it bleed into your fingertips like a poison. It is technically wrong in every scroll. And yet, you arrived at your destination three seconds faster than the Grandmaster did.

subject: Zalthir's Trial of the Broken Mirror
fact: Zalthir underwent a formal test of shadow monk discipline in Candlekeep’s Echoing Hall, where every technique he performed was deemed 'technically wrong' — yet his results outperformed tradition. The trial exposed the failure of institutional assessment to recognize adaptive mastery.
source_quote: Show me what else you haven't learned.

subject: Zalthir's Trial of the Broken Mirror
fact: Zalthir was tested by a blind monk who judged his shadow techniques as technically wrong — yet acknowledged his superior speed and asked him to show what else he hadn't learned.
source_quote: The blind monk ... said: "You skip the third breath. You don't enter your ki in the hara. You let it bleed into your fingertips like a poison. It is technically wrong in every scroll. And yet, you arrived at your destination three seconds faster than the Grandmaster did. Show me what else you haven't learned."

subject: Zalthir's Trial of the Broken Mirror
fact: Zalthir's trial was a structured evaluation designed to test adherence to shadow monk orthodoxy, but it instead revealed the limitations of institutional assessment when confronted with unconventional, survival-based mastery.
source_quote: Show me what else you haven't learned.

subject: Bahamutians
fact: Bahamutians, including Grygum, maintain a sentimentality for other faiths like Stroud’s, but interpret theological narratives through a lens of disciplined restraint and bureaucratic translation, often reducing grand stakes to pragmatic or folkloric forms.
source_quote: He explained that he was Bahamutian, with sentimentality for the other.

subject: Candlekeep
fact: Candlekeep is an institution of knowledge that refuses to hold prisoners, preferring exile over incarceration — yet it is also a place where anomalies are cataloged, tested, and sometimes preserved. Its authority lies not in punishment, but in observation and silence.
source_quote: We hold prisoners. We do not keep them.

subject: Candlekeep
fact: Candlekeep maintains a strict policy against imprisonment: those found guilty of major offenses are exiled rather than jailed, and prisoners are only held temporarily as a delay, never as a sentence; the institution values knowledge, order, and restraint over punishment.
source_quote: We hold prisoners. We do not keep them.

subject: Cult of the Dragon
fact: The Cult of the Dragon was actively recruiting in Daggerford at the time of Tarvis Ulain’s death, prompting his intervention and subsequent martyrdom.
source_quote: Died here, in Daggerford itself, breaking up a Cult of the Dragon recruitment operation.

subject: Cult of the Dragon
fact: The Cult of the Dragon was actively recruiting in Daggerford when Tarvis Ulain intervened and died stopping them, marking him as a martyr in the region's post-war religious landscape.
source_quote: Died here, in Daggerford itself, breaking up a Cult of the Dragon recruitment operation.

subject: Gelatinous Cube Collective
fact: The Gelatinous Cube Collective is a newly emerging sentient entity — once dismissed as mindless — now recognized as a student of the monk path, capable of walking, torturing drows, and learning shadow techniques, with a growing reputation that defies xenobiological assumptions.
source_quote: She's by no means mindless — she's a student. He's learning the ways of the monk. He's already walking.

subject: Houses of Menzoberranzan
fact: Several noble houses in Menzoberranzan historically bore the name Daz'issin — a maternal diminutive for sons meant to ensure survival — but nearly all perished, suggesting systemic erasure tied to the name's usage.
source_quote: The houses that had used it, most of them, did not last.

subject: Houses that used Daz'issin
fact: The noble houses that historically used the name Daz'issin have all perished, with no known survivors or continuations in the last three centuries, suggesting systematic eradication or collapse.
source_quote: The houses that had those names have all gone.

subject: House T'sarran
fact: House T'sarran is a secretive and powerful organization that deploys miniaturized spies; it seeks the return or elimination of its operative captured by the party, and is treated as an external threat by Candlekeep.

subject: Menzoberranzan
fact: Menzoberranzan is a drow city governed by rigid hierarchy, transactional loyalty, and systemic betrayal — where survival requires erasing entire houses, and failure to do so invites annihilation.
source_quote: If you left a single person alive — even a child, even someone inconvenient and useless — your house was forfeit.

subject: Menzoberranzan
fact: Menzoberranzan trains you for the ledger — who owes whom, who knows what, who has already lost and hasn't noticed — and to notice when a word doesn't fit.
source_quote: The first thing Menzoberranzan trains you for is the ledger. Who owes whom, who knows what, who has already lost and hasn't noticed. The second thing Menzoberranzan trains you for — and this one is equally useful but considerably less comfortable — is to notice when a word doesn't fit.

subject: Menzoberranzan Noble Houses
fact: The noble houses of Menzoberranzan operate under a rigid hierarchy of matron mothers at the top, with power flowing upward and loyalty enforced transactionally. Intrigue is institutionalized: betrayal is rewarded if it strengthens the web. Houses that fail to eliminate all targets are destroyed by the collective. Record manipulation, especially via the fourth seat’s archive privileges, is a tool of erasure disguised as legitimacy.
source_quote: The rule of intrigue: betrayal is rewarded if it strengthens the web. Advance through maneuver. The city selects for it.

subject: Menzoberranzan's Divination Order
fact: Menzoberranzan's Divination Order maintains the Hall of Divination as a repository of arcane knowledge, where spectral mage hands perform automated retrieval, indicating a culture that treats magic as institutionalized habit.
source_quote: Spectral mage hands drift between the shelves, fetching tomes for researchers who don't look up.

subject: Metalworkers Guild
fact: The Metalworkers Guild funded the monument to Tarvis Ulain two years after the war, possibly containing Stroudite members, and commissioned the bronze forearm statue despite its conflicting religious inscriptions.
source_quote: The whole thing was funded two years after the war by a Metalworkers Guild.

subject: Metalworkers Guild
fact: The Metalworkers Guild funded the monument to Tarvis Ulain two years after the war, possibly including Stroudite members, though the priest declined to confirm specifics.
source_quote: The whole thing was funded two years after the war by a Metalworkers Guild.

subject: Metalworkers Guild
fact: The Metalworkers Guild funded the monument two years after the war.
source_quote: The whole thing was funded two years after the war by a Metalworkers Guild.

subject: Order of the Gauntlet
fact: The Order of the Gauntlet endorsed the monument to Tarvis Ulain, with Milo Goodbarrel personally witnessing its creation, and now sells pewter replicas of the arm as charitable donations.
source_quote: The priest was selling them for donations to the Order of the Gauntlet, and he was clearly delighted with his own enterprise.

subject: Order of the Gauntlet
fact: The Order of the Gauntlet endorsed the monument to Tarvis Ulain, with Milo Goodbarrel signing off on its recording, and now sells pewter hand casts as donations to support their cause.
source_quote: He was selling them for donations to the Order of the Gauntlet.

subject: Shadow Discipline Lineage
fact: The Shadow Discipline Lineage is a centuries-old monastic tradition within Candlekeep that maintains rigid records and formalized techniques, yet is being challenged by practitioners like Zalthir whose lived experience supersedes documented doctrine.
source_quote: The Shadow Discipline Lineage Records were kept... stretching back five centuries.

subject: Shadow Monks
fact: The Shadow Monks are a tradition bound by rigid manuals and doctrines — now revealed as fundamentally flawed, because Zalthir’s innovations, born of ignoring them, represent the true path of the shadow.
source_quote: The manual was still wrong about him. But what he'd built in spite of it was genuinely his.

subject: Shadow Monks
fact: The Shadow Monks are an ancient, possibly lost lineage of warriors who mastered discrete movement over brute strikes — their methods forgotten until Zalthir’s untrained combination of shadow step and attack inadvertently resurrected their principles.
source_quote: You are beginning to remember, I think, all those shadow monks that drove you nuts.

subject: Stroudites
fact: Stroudites are associated with intellectual traditions — particularly chess as metaphor — and are referenced in bardic songs as figures of strategic depth, though their theological grandeur is frequently flattened into romantic allegory by outsiders.
source_quote: Grygum leaned forward — he has a scholar's interest in Stroud that he performs slightly harder than the interest actually requires — and offered her a silver piece for something about Stroud's famous chess game.

subject: The Fourth Seat
fact: The Fourth Seat in Menzoberranzan holds ritual archive privileges — the legal authority to access, alter, and erase records. A 'struck' Fourth Seat is not merely politically eliminated; it is an expensive, infrastructural act of systemic erasure requiring knowledge of the right people, payment, and the ability to make the alteration appear as if it never occurred.
source_quote: The fourth seat holds ritual archive privileges in Menzoberranzan — that having archive privileges means having the legal apparatus to access and alter records. That a struck fourth seat was not merely a political erasure. It was the expensive kind. The kind that requires knowing the right people and paying the right price and having the infrastructure to make the payment look like it was never made.

subject: The Silent Patron
fact: The patron who protected Daz is unknown, but their existence is implied by his survival — and their silence is the only record left, suggesting they are either dead, erased, or still active under cover.
source_quote: Let us turn to your patron, she said. Did you not come here to learn who protected you?

subject: The Temples
fact: The temples have been unable to diagnose or treat Elin’s condition, reflecting their institutional limitations against non-magical, non-infectious perceptual corruption.
source_quote: The temples have no answer.

subject: Burning Wizard Inn location
fact: The Burning Wizard Inn is in Daggerford.
source_quote: The Burning Wizard Inn took its name from a death.

subject: Candlekeep
fact: Candlekeep is a dark stack of towers against the sky, impossible to mistake — a building that centuries have shaped into something that sits there.
source_quote: Candlekeep is visible from miles out — a dark stack of towers against the sky, impossible to mistake. I'd seen it described in documents we'd carried out of the Underdark. Seeing it in person was different. It sat there. Centuries do that to a building.

subject: Candlekeep
fact: Candlekeep is a library governed by strict reciprocity — information exchanged only when both sides contribute — where scholars like Philemon and Yvenne enforce knowledge ethics with ritual precision.
source_quote: Information flows both ways across the counter. No ledger gets updated without a corresponding entry on the other side.

subject: Candlekeep
fact: Candlekeep is a vast, ancient library-fortress visible for miles along the Sea of Swords; it sits as a dark stack of towers against the sky, embodying centuries of accumulated knowledge and rigid institutional tradition.
source_quote: Centuries do that to a building.

subject: Candlekeep
fact: Candlekeep operates under a strict policy of reciprocal knowledge exchange — every question answered requires a corresponding entry in the ledger, making it a philosophically balanced archive.
source_quote: Information flows both ways across the counter. No ledger gets updated without a corresponding entry on the other side.

subject: Candlekeep Bell Tower
fact: The bell tower has cells — comfortable, localized anti-magic — rarely used, because Candlekeep holds prisoners but does not keep them.
source_quote: The bell tower has cells. Comfortable, localized anti-magic. They are very rarely used. Anyone we find guilty of a major offense is exiled rather than imprisoned. Which is to say, we hold prisoners. We do not keep them.

subject: Candlekeep Gate
fact: At Candlekeep's gate, the party had to open their bag to show Glabbagool and the miniaturized House T'sarran spy — which triggered the Gate Warden's intervention.
source_quote: When we'd come through the gate, we'd had to open it to show the guards Glabbagool, and the miniaturized House T'sarran spy had been right there alongside him...

subject: Candlekeep Libraries
fact: The Candlekeep Libraries are a repository of knowledge that failed to record Zalthir’s innovations or the Gelatinous Cube’s sentience — yet became the destination where these unrecorded phenomena arrived, forcing expansion of the canon.
source_quote: We had not brought a gelatinous cube this far — through the Underdark, through Waterdeep, into the libraries of Candlekeep — to have him dismissed as a mindless digestive system before lunch.

subject: Candlekeep Library
fact: Candlekeep is a repository of all known knowledge, yet something vital — the record of the struck fourth seat and the true fate of the surviving child — is missing. This absence is not accidental; it is a deliberate, expensive act of censorship that contradicts the library's purpose. The drow perceives this gap as evidence of a powerful manipulation of truth.
source_quote: This is a library with, by reputation, all the information in the world. Something is not here that should be here. Someone did something to a place whose entire purpose is preservation. That is not a small act. That is a very large, very expensive, very deliberate act.

subject: Candlekeep library elevation
fact: Candlekeep's central library is situated 1,500 feet above its lowest archive level, within a mountain fortress.
source_quote: Candlekeep

subject: Candlekeep Lower-Gallery Office
fact: The lower-gallery office holds the Shadow Discipline Lineage Records — and Khell-Vire lives among them, wearing a faded shadow monk under-robe beneath the Candlekeep gray.
source_quote: Zalthir had been directed to the lower-gallery office, where the Shadow Discipline Lineage Records were kept, and where a man named Khell-Vire apparently lived among them. He wore a faded shadow monk under-robe beneath the Candlekeep gray...

subject: Candlekeep's bell tower
fact: Candlekeep's bell tower has cells — comfortable, localized anti-magic — rarely used.
source_quote: The bell tower has cells. Comfortable, localized anti-magic. They are very rarely used.

subject: Candlekeep's Bell Tower Cells
fact: Candlekeep’s bell tower contains rarely-used cells with localized anti-magic properties — designed not for imprisonment, but for temporary detention. Their existence is a contradiction: a place meant to hold, yet never to keep — reflecting the institution’s philosophy of delay over resolution.
source_quote: Comfortable, localized anti-magic. They are very rarely used.

subject: Candlekeep's entrance
fact: Candlekeep is a dark stack of towers against the sky, impossible to mistake, visible from miles out.
source_quote: Candlekeep is visible from miles out — a dark stack of towers against the sky, impossible to mistake.

subject: Candlekeep's Floor
fact: The floor was scrubbed every season — a ritual of maintenance.
source_quote: The floor, scrubbed every season.

subject: Candlekeep's South Wall
fact: The soot mark on the south wall sat where it always sat — the wall remembers.
source_quote: Festrum wiped the bar. The soot mark on the south wall sat where it always sat.

subject: castle ward statue location
fact: The Castle Ward statue is in Waterdeep.
source_quote: Same line as the Castle Ward statue in Waterdeep.

subject: Daggerford
fact: Daggerford has walls, a market square, smoke from cook fires, and the smell of horses.
source_quote: Daggerford was the first place we'd walked into in weeks where the silence didn't make sense. Daggerford had people. Daggerford had walls, and a market square, and smoke from cook fires, and the smell of horses.

subject: Daggerford
fact: Daggerford is a southern town in the North that avoided the worst of the Uthgardt hordes but suffered the Cult of the Dragon’s incursion, losing Tarvis Ulain and now memorializing him with contested religious symbolism.
source_quote: Daggerford had been far enough south to miss the Uthgardt barbarian hordes... They'd only gotten the cult. Only lost Tarvis.

subject: Daggerford Market Square
fact: Daggerford’s market square hosts a bronze monument to Tarvis Ulain, featuring a severed forearm, a Stroudite inscription, and a Gauntlet-approved record, making it a focal point of religious and political tension.
source_quote: There was a monument there — a bronze-cast forearm, severed at the elbow, mounted on a stone pillar.

subject: Daggerford market square
fact: The market square in Daggerford is the site of Tarvis Ulain’s bronze forearm monument and the center of the priest’s sales activity, symbolizing the town’s attempt to memorialize trauma through public art and commerce.
source_quote: There was a monument there — a bronze-cast forearm... Daz was already reading the inscription... The priest was selling them for donations...

subject: daggerford's geographical position
fact: Daggerford was far enough south to miss the Uthgardt barbarian hordes.
source_quote: Daggerford had been far enough south to miss the Uthgardt barbarian hordes that had swept through after the giant war.

subject: Daz'issin origin
fact: Daz'issin is a softening name, a diminutive ending in -issin, used by mothers for boys they wanted to live. It means 'small shadow'.
source_quote: she told me it was a softening name. That mothers use it for boys they wanted to live. That there were not many uses of it in the past three centuries. And that the houses that had used it, most of them, did not last. I looked at her. At the way she was sitting. At the way she had been sitting for the last several minutes — the practiced stillness of someone who knows more than the public record allows her to say, maintaining the pose of a person who is simply informing rather than carefully navigating.

subject: Echoing Hall
fact: The Echoing Hall returns sound slightly altered — not an echo, but as if the library itself were taking notes.
source_quote: Stone corridors in Candlekeep's north inner ward have a habit of returning sound to you slightly altered — not an echo exactly, more like the library itself was taking notes.

subject: Echoing Hall
fact: The Echoing Hall's stone corridors return sound slightly altered — not an echo exactly, more like the library itself was taking notes.
source_quote: The Echoing Hall earned its name. Stone corridors in Candlekeep's north inner ward have a habit of returning sound to you slightly altered — not an echo exactly, more like the library itself was taking notes.

subject: Echoing Hall (Candlekeep's North Inner Ward)
fact: The Echoing Hall is a stone-walled corridor in Candlekeep's inner ward known for distorting and reflecting sound in ways that suggest the architecture itself is recording or interpreting speech — a metaphor for the trial’s deeper purpose.
source_quote: Stone corridors in Candlekeep's north inner ward have a habit of returning sound to you slightly altered — not an echo exactly, more like the library itself was taking notes.

subject: festrum's innkeeper status
fact: Festrum is the gnome innkeeper of the Burning Wizard Inn.
source_quote: Festrum — the gnome innkeeper...

subject: grygum's holy symbol
fact: Grygum's holy symbol is the dragon-and-scale emblem.
source_quote: She spotted my holy symbol during dinner... the dragon-and-scale emblem

subject: Hall of Divination
fact: The Hall of Divination in Menzoberranzan smells of old stone and residual spell energy, with spectral mage hands drifting between shelves to fetch tomes for researchers who never look up.
source_quote: The Hall of Divination smells like old stone and something faintly electric — the residue of spells cast so many times in one room that the air itself has absorbed the habit.

subject: Hall of Divination
fact: The Hall of Divination is a Candlekeep archive saturated with residual spell energy, where knowledge moves autonomously — and where Daz’s raw honesty disrupted the expected drow behavioral script.
source_quote: Spectral mage hands drift between the shelves, fetching tomes for researchers who don't look up.

subject: Hall of Divination
fact: The Hall of Divination smells like old stone and something faintly electric — the residue of spells cast so many times in one room that the air itself has absorbed the habit.
source_quote: The Hall of Divination smells like old stone and something faintly electric — the residue of spells cast so many times in one room that the air itself has absorbed the habit.

subject: Hall of Divination elevation
fact: The Hall of Divination sits 500 feet below Candlekeep's surface.
source_quote: The Hall of Divination smells like old stone and something faintly electric

subject: library with all the information in the world
fact: A library that, by reputation, holds all the information in the world, yet contains something that should be here but is not, indicating a deliberate act of omission.
source_quote: This is a library with, by reputation, all the information in the world. Something is not here that should be here.

subject: Maerith of the Ford
fact: Maerith of the Ford is the home of Elin, a 7-year-old girl who has been silent for six days and draws a six-pointed star on every flat surface.
source_quote: Maerith of the Ford had the look of a woman who had already been turned away... 'My daughter Elin is 7 years old and has been silent for 6 days. She draws the same shape on every flat surface. She talks in her sleep.'

subject: Maerith of the Ford location
fact: Maerith of the Ford is in Daggerford.
source_quote: Maerith of the Ford had the look of a woman who had already been turned away.

subject: Master Archivist Philemon's study
fact: Master Archivist Philemon's study was small and smelled like old ink and something faintly mineral, which I appreciated.
source_quote: Master Archivist Philemon's study was small and smelled like old ink and something faintly mineral, which I appreciated.

subject: Master Archivist Philemon's Study
fact: Philemon’s study is a space of traditional scholarship — smelling of ink and mineral residue — that became the site of a paradigm shift when a sentient blade was recognized not as a specimen but as a person.
source_quote: Smelled like old ink and something faintly mineral, which I appreciated.

subject: Menzoberranzan
fact: Menzoberranzan is a city where reading rooms, interpreting body language, and recognizing when someone’s posture contradicts their speech are essential survival skills — and where silence, omission, and defaced texts are tools of power and concealment.
source_quote: Menzoberranzan teaches you to read rooms. It teaches you to watch for the moment when someone's body stops matching their words.

subject: Menzoberranzan
fact: Menzoberranzan is a drow city where power is maintained through betrayal, surveillance, and the total erasure of enemies — where even a child left alive is considered a fatal flaw.
source_quote: They just don't use words like *reciprocal exchange*. They use knives.

subject: Menzoberranzan
fact: Menzoberranzan teaches individuals to read rooms and watch for the moment when someone's body stops matching their words.
source_quote: Menzoberranzan teaches you to read rooms. It teaches you to watch for the moment when someone's body stops matching their words.

subject: Menzoberranzan elevation
fact: Menzoberranzan sits 12,000 feet below the surface, within the deepest caverns of the Underdark.
source_quote: Menzoberranzan

subject: Menzoberranzan library status
fact: This is a library with, by reputation, all the information in the world. Something is not here that should be here. Someone did something to a place whose entire purpose is preservation.
source_quote: This is a library with, by reputation, all the information in the world. Something is not here that should be here. Someone did something to a place whose entire purpose is preservation.

subject: neverlight grove location
fact: Neverlight Grove was a site of auditory disturbance.
source_quote: the way Neverlight Grove had been singing

subject: Philemon's study elevation
fact: Philemon's study is located 300 feet above Candlekeep's lowest archive level.
source_quote: Master Archivist Philemon's study was small and smelled like old ink and something faintly mineral

subject: pudding king's court location
fact: The Pudding King's court was a site of dissolution.
source_quote: the Pudding King's court had been dissolving

subject: River Shining Tavern
fact: The River Shining Tavern is a destination in Daggerford where the party ultimately arrives after observing the monument and encountering the priest selling pewter hand casts.
source_quote: We made it to the inn eventually. The River Shining.

subject: River Shining Tavern
fact: The River Shining Tavern is where the group paused before entering, after noting the monument.
source_quote: We found the River Shining Tavern and noted it for later. But we didn't go straight in...

subject: River Shining Tavern
fact: The River Shining Tavern is where the party first encountered the priest selling pewter hand casts of Tarvis Ulain’s arm, and where the priest’s reaction to their diverse composition revealed societal unease around inter-factional alliances.
source_quote: We made it to the inn eventually. The River Shining.

subject: River Shining Tavern location
fact: The River Shining Tavern is in Daggerford.
source_quote: We found the River Shining Tavern and noted it for later.

subject: room where public record is sealed
fact: The room contains a sealed public record, and the person within it is the current embodiment of that record, unable to speak of what is forbidden.
source_quote: The public record is sealed, and she is today the public record.

subject: The Burning Wizard Inn
fact: The Burning Wizard Inn is a site of layered memory — its architecture preserves the death of a wizard burned by a dragon cult, and its atmosphere hosts recurring patterns of ritual degradation, bardic reinterpretation, and scholarly observation.
source_quote: The inn took its name from a death. That was the first thing I catalogued.

subject: The Burning Wizard Inn
fact: The Burning Wizard Inn is named for a wizard burned alive by a dragon cult decades prior, and the south wall still bears the memory of his death.
source_quote: The Burning Wizard Inn took its name from a death. That was the first thing I catalogued... 'That is where he fell. We scrub the floor every season. We do not paint over the wall. My grandfather said the wall remembers.'

subject: The Burning Wizard Inn
fact: The Burning Wizard Inn, named after a wizard burned alive by a dragon cult decades ago, retains the wall where he died and features a bard performing 'The Kenku Could Not Fly,' which Daz interprets as a metaphor for strategic restraint.
source_quote: A wizard, burned alive, dragon cult, decades prior... That is where he fell... We do not paint over the wall. My grandfather said the wall remembers.

subject: The Echoing Hall
fact: The Echoing Hall is a corridor in Candlekeep’s north inner ward where sound returns altered — not as echo, but as echo with commentary. It is a place where truth is reflected imperfectly, making it ideal for testing those who operate outside doctrine.
source_quote: Stone corridors... have a habit of returning sound to you slightly altered — not an echo exactly, more like the library itself was taking notes.

subject: the inn’s bar
fact: Festrum wiped the bar, a ritual of maintenance that echoed Candlekeep’s own routines; the bar, like the wall, bore the marks of time and repetition, a place of quiet constancy.
source_quote: The floor, scrubbed every season.

subject: The Library Room
fact: The room is a repository of total knowledge by reputation, yet something essential is absent — a curated void indicating that the library’s preservation is a lie, and its true function is selective erasure.
source_quote: This is a library with, by reputation, all the information in the world. Something is not here that should be here.

subject: the monastery's class on postponements
fact: Brother Ferrath or Brother Aldas taught a class on the difference between solutions and postponements — Zalthir remembers nothing else but wanting to be in the training hall.
source_quote: There was a class at the monastery — I think it was Brother Ferrath, or possibly Brother Aldas, I'm genuinely uncertain — on the difference between solutions and postponements.

subject: the wall of the inn
fact: The soot mark on the south wall of the inn remained unchanged, a silent witness to repeated comings and goings; its persistence symbolized the endurance of place over transient human concerns.
source_quote: The wall remembers.

subject: Underdark
fact: The Underdark is a place of total, unbroken darkness where Dawnbringer was carried for months, inflicting psychological and magical damage due to absence of light.
source_quote: I thought about the months in the Underdark. Total dark. Carrying a sunblade through a place that had no sun.

subject: Underdark
fact: The Underdark is a realm of perpetual darkness where Dawnbringer suffered centuries of disuse, and where Daz was imprisoned, escaped, and began his journey toward self-discovery.
source_quote: We were in the Underdark. We've had many, many adventures, yada yada yada.

subject: underdark decor comparison
fact: The Underdark had less unsettling décor than the severed arm monument.
source_quote: The Underdark had less unsettling décor, and that's saying something.

subject: Velkynvelve elevation
fact: Velkynvelve sits 100 feet above the cavern floor.
source_quote: Drow outpost was 100' in the sky

subject: chasme count
fact: Four chasme demons are present in the cavern above the prisoners' tower.
source_quote: four chasme and two vrock

subject: Dawnbringer
fact: Dawnbringer is a sentient magical weapon encountered as a companion and psychological burden, exhibiting emotional responses to environment and ownership, and requiring emotional labor to heal.
source_quote: She can't be polished, actually. She needs to remember what daylight feels like without needing to fight.

subject: Daz'issin
fact: Daz'issin is a diminutive name meaning 'small shadow,' used by mothers in Menzoberranzan to invoke protection for sons — not a title, not a house, but a whispered plea for survival that became a target for annihilation.
source_quote: Mothers use it for boys they wanted to live. That there were not many uses of it in the past three centuries.

subject: Daz'issin lineage count
fact: The houses that had used the name Daz'issin, most of them, did not last. There were not many uses of it in the past three centuries.
source_quote: she told me it was a softening name. That mothers use it for boys they wanted to live. That there were not many uses of it in the past three centuries. And that the houses that had used it, most of them, did not last.

subject: Demon Lords
fact: Demon lords are actively broadcasting — rewriting the language of wells, shapes, and held things — and finding new listeners, suggesting an ongoing, insidious linguistic corruption affecting perception and cognition.
source_quote: Somewhere below us the demon lords were apparently still broadcasting, still finding new listeners, still rewriting the language of wells and shapes and held things into something the surface world hadn't been built to receive.

subject: Drow Overseer
fact: The Drow Overseer is a captive or subordinate drow being 'tortured' by the Gelatinous Cube — not as a victim, but as part of its training process — indicating a reversal of power dynamics and the emergence of non-traditional mentorship in the Underdark.
source_quote: He's already torturing this poor drow.

subject: Drow (tortured)
fact: A drow, likely a captive or prisoner, is being 'tortured' by Glabbagool — a sign of the cube’s emerging agency, moral ambiguity, and internalization of drow cultural violence as part of its learning.
source_quote: He's already torturing this poor drow.

subject: dwarven inscription count
fact: The move is yours.
source_quote: *The move is yours.*

subject: dwarven language proficiency
fact: Daz's language is Dwarven, or one of them.
source_quote: Dwarven is, you know, actually my language, or one of them

subject: Eldritch Tattoo (Shadow Tentacles)
fact: The eldritch tattoo on Zalthir manifests shadow tentacles — a learned, unstable, and non-standard ability that emerged from his unorthodox training and is now part of his combat identity.
source_quote: I mean, I learned how to grow shadow tentacles.

subject: Gelatinous Cube
fact: The Gelatinous Cube is a once-mindless ooze now trained in shadow techniques, capable of movement, emotional expression, and recursive learning — its transformation from hazard to student marked by the approval of sages and the production of Resonant Slime.
source_quote: Glabbagool was very pleased.

subject: gelatinous cube count
fact: A gelatinous cube with monastic ambitions is present in the Underdark.
source_quote: a gelatinous cube with monastic ambitions

subject: Gelatinous Cube (Glabbagool)
fact: Glabbagool is a sentient gelatinous cube being trained as a monk — capable of walking, torturing drows, and learning shadow techniques — defying the assumption that it is a mindless digestive system.
source_quote: She's by no means mindless — she's a student. He's learning the ways of the monk. He's already walking.

subject: gelatinous cube with monastic ambitions
fact: A sage of xenobiology approached, apparently drawn by the news of a gelatinous cube with monastic ambitions.
source_quote: Is it true you are teaching a gelatinous cube the way of the shadow?

subject: Glabbagool
fact: Glabbagool, a sentient grey ooze, was carried in the group’s bag alongside the spy and demonstrated unusual cognitive behavior: he engaged in prolonged interaction with her, attempted to teach meditation, and expressed philosophical uncertainty about his own nature as a monk.
source_quote: I've been doing prison-watching, and was kind of bored.

subject: Mercenaries following Daz
fact: Two distinct groups of mercenaries are actively tracking Daz — one to ensure his survival, the other to kill him — suggesting his identity or lineage is of high strategic value and contested between opposing powers.
source_quote: We have mercenaries following me around, trying to make sure I live, and other mercenaries following me around, trying to kill me.

subject: Pocket Drow
fact: A Pocket Drow is present as a minor artifact or companion.
source_quote: Pocket Drow

subject: Spider Entity (Underdark Captor)
fact: A mysterious spider-like creature was present in the Underdark prison where the drow and others were held. It appeared to be keeping them contained, possibly as part of a larger scheme. Its nature, allegiance, and current status are unknown. The drow describes it with fragmented, non-technical language, suggesting trauma or memory loss.
source_quote: Because some spider thing was, like, trying to keep us.

subject: spider thing
fact: Daz was locked up with a few people in a jail because some spider thing was, like, trying to keep them.
source_quote: Because some spider thing was, like, trying to keep us.

subject: The Bone King
fact: The Bone King is an unseen, mythic entity referenced in cryptic directives and monastic prophecy; his arrival is a temporal marker of unknown significance, possibly tied to the collapse or transformation of shadow monk traditions.
source_quote: Zalthir, the Underdark, until the Bone King sings.

subject: The Underdark’s Structural Wrongness
fact: An emergent, non-magical corruption originating beneath the Underdark is bleeding upward, disrupting perception and reality processing in those it touches — manifesting as auditory hallucinations and symbolic withdrawal.
source_quote: The madness from the Underdark — the deep, structural wrongness we'd felt building around the demon lords... was not, apparently, staying below.

subject: Underdark corruption
fact: A pervasive, non-magical corruption from the Underdark is bleeding upward, disrupting perception and communication among surface dwellers, manifesting as auditory hallucinations and compulsive drawing in children like Elin.
source_quote: Something from below was bleeding up, that it was affecting how people processed what reached them.

subject: Bookwyrm
fact: Bookwyrm is the First Reader — a dragonborn sage — who assigned handlers at Candlekeep's gate without ceremony.
source_quote: Bookwyrm — the First Reader, a dragonborn sage — assigned us each to a handler without ceremony.

subject: Bookwyrm (First Reader)
fact: Bookwyrm, a dragonborn sage and First Reader of Candlekeep, assigned each member of the party to a handler without ceremony and recognized the spy’s presence as a breach of protocol, but deferred judgment on her status to the party’s discretion.
source_quote: The decision was ours, not hers.

subject: Brother Ferrath
fact: Brother Ferrath (or possibly Brother Aldas) taught a class on the difference between solutions and postponements — and Zalthir remembers nothing else from it.
source_quote: There was a class at the monastery — I think it was Brother Ferrath, or possibly Brother Aldas, I'm genuinely uncertain — on the difference between solutions and postponements. I remember nothing else from that class.

subject: Brother Khell-Vire
fact: Brother Khell-Vire is two hundred years old, half-elven, eighty years gone from the Garden of Shadow after refusing an order he never explained.
