fact: When asked where she was during the murder, Bookwyrm paused before saying 'I had nothing to do with it.' This was not an alibi — it was a denial of complicity. The pause suggests she knows more than she admits. She may have been present, or she may have authorized access to the Keeper. Her role is ambiguous — protector, conspirator, or victim of a larger scheme.

subject: Bookwyrm's Pause
fact: When Thorin asked 'Where were you?', Bookwyrm paused — just long enough to weigh something. That pause is the most significant moment in the interrogation so far, and the narrator chose not to write down what it meant — but took notes anyway.
source_quote: I did not write down what I thought her expression meant... But I took notes.

subject: brain-based communication
fact: There is a theoretical possibility of communicating with the corpse using only the brain, bypassing the missing heart, but prior attempts have failed.
source_quote: We don't need the heart — we just need the brain to be able to talk to him, you know.

subject: Brother Heslin or Brother Arrath
fact: It is unclear whether Brother Heslin or Brother Arrath ran the theory sessions on repurposed threat.
source_quote: I wasn't sure the monks at the Garden Shadow would have approved of the metaphor, but Brother Heslin — or possibly Brother Arrath, I was never certain which of them ran the theory sessions on repurposed threat — had said something along those lines once.

subject: Daz's suspicion of Bookwyrm
fact: Daz notes that Bookwyrm volunteered information about Kalan's resignation at a strategic moment.
source_quote: She delivered it like a gift. Information, freely offered, before anyone had thought to ask.

subject: door left ajar on third floor
fact: The door to the third floor apartment was left conspicuously ajar, suggesting deliberate access or a distraction.
source_quote: a large apartment at the third with its door left conspicuously ajar. I noted the apartment. Noted that the door was open. Filed it for later.

subject: fixed points
fact: Grygum references 'fixed points' as a possible theological framework for the investigation.
source_quote: It could be one of those fixed points

subject: Fourth school of thought
fact: A fourth school of thought has been proposed — that the universe contains fixed points of cosmic constraint, around which mortal actions must revolve, with freedom existing only between them, and the architecture of belief subtly shaping evidence to enforce invariance.
source_quote: What if there are certain fixed points around which our actions must revolve? And the closer we come to one of those fixed points, the more constrained we are, but between them, perhaps we have a great deal of freedom of action.

subject: Gate Warden removed before questioning
fact: The Gate Warden was removed from his position before being questioned about what he found during his inspection.
source_quote: The Gate Warden again at eleven, alone, for a full inspection — careful, deliberate, left to make his report to the Council.

subject: Glabbagool's ontological status
fact: The nature of an ooze’s consciousness, its capacity for discipline, and the meaning of its desire for freedom remain unexplored, creating a metaphysical mystery.
source_quote: I didn't know what *out* meant for an ooze. Neither did he. But the want was there.

subject: Grygumite School
fact: The Grygumite School is a newly declared school of thought that captured the council's interest.
source_quote: I am the head of the Grygumite School." A beat. "Founder, in fact.

subject: Grygum school of thought
fact: The Grygum school of thought is filed under things that started as offhand remarks.
source_quote: The Grygum school of thought. Filed under: things that started as offhand remarks.

subject: heart removal to prevent resurrection
fact: The removal of Janussi's heart was deliberate to prevent resurrection rituals from working.
source_quote: Grygum named the precaution out loud, and once he said it I couldn't believe I hadn't thought of it first: you can't bring someone back from death by ritual if their vital organs aren't present.

subject: identity of the killer
fact: The killer was likely someone familiar with the chamber’s protocols, able to enter without raising suspicion, and knew to preserve the scene. The absence of forced entry, the timing of the smoke and candles, and the deliberate removal of the notes suggest an insider — possibly someone who had access to the study and knew Janussi’s work.
source_quote: Nobody smokes in a sealed room and leaves smoke that lingers for hours unless the room has been sealed for hours.

subject: identity of the murderer
fact: The identity of the murderer remains unknown, with no consensus among the Council, and the party’s arrival has introduced unverified external variables into the investigation.
source_quote: First, we must find the murderer!

subject: inventory of unfulfilled prophecies
fact: The fate of Candlekeep's prophecy archive when the inventory runs out remains unknown, posing a foundational theological and existential question.
source_quote: Nobody knew what happened when the inventory ran out.

subject: Kalan's Eyes Were Not
fact: Kalan Strongbranch’s bow was correct, but his eyes were not — a silent, potent indicator of hidden intent. This observation marks him as the primary subject of the narrator’s next move, and the thread of his loyalty or guilt remains unspoken.
source_quote: He was the first person I planned to question.

subject: legitimacy of Grygum’s authority
fact: Grygum’s claim to found the Grygumite School is unverified, and its sudden introduction into the Council’s crisis may be a deliberate distraction or an authentic intellectual incursion.
source_quote: I am the head of the Grygumite School." A beat. "Founder, in fact.

subject: Missing Heart
fact: Janussi’s heart was removed post-mortem to prevent resurrection — the motive suggests the killer intended to ensure permanent death, raising the question of who had the knowledge and means to perform such an act — and why.
source_quote: They wanted Janussi to stay dead in every sense that mattered.

subject: motive for murder
fact: The murder appears to have been motivated by the theft of Janussi’s most recent research — specifically the notes on The Golden Ass, written in midnight blue ink. The victim’s chest was hollowed out, suggesting the object removed was not jewelry but something tied to his research — possibly a magical artifact or component.
source_quote: Whatever he took, it wasn't jewelry... That felt deliberate in the way that things feel deliberate when you stop trying to find an innocent explanation for them.

subject: nature of the stolen object
fact: The object removed from Janussi’s chest was not jewelry — it was likely a magical artifact or component tied to his research on The Golden Ass. The hollow in his chest and the missing notes together suggest the killer sought a physical manifestation of the magic he was studying — perhaps a soul-bound glyph, a spell core, or a living inscription.
source_quote: There was a hollow in his chest where something used to be... Whatever he took, it wasn't jewelry.

subject: new philosophy of the universe
fact: Grygum claims to have found a new philosophy of the universe.
source_quote: And I have found a new philosophy of the universe.

subject: Poirot and Colombo
fact: Thorin and Grygum claim to be students of the great Masters Poirot and Colombo.
source_quote: Thorin said we were students of the great Masters Poirot and Colombo

subject: prophecy inventory
fact: Candlekeep recites unfulfilled prophecies from Alaundo's inventory.
source_quote: What remained was the unfulfilled inventory.

subject: protocol failure
fact: Tadric’s admission that his role was crowd control, not surveillance, reveals a critical failure in crime scene protocol. No one was monitoring what individuals did once inside — allowing the killer to remove the notes and the object without detection.
source_quote: Tadric admitted his job had been crowd control, not surveillance — watching who came in and out, not watching what they did once they were inside.

subject: repurposed threat
fact: Brother Heslin or Brother Arrath taught a theory about repurposing dangerous entities into knowledge repositories.
source_quote: Brother Heslin — or possibly Brother Arrath, I was never certain which of them ran the theory sessions on repurposed threat — had said something along those lines once.

subject: resurrection prevention
fact: The heart was removed not as a trophy but as a deliberate act to ensure Janussi could not be resurrected, implying the killer intended permanent death.
source_quote: They wanted Janussi to stay dead in every sense that mattered.

subject: strong-weak hypothesis
fact: Vareth names the proposed theological theory the 'strong-weak hypothesis'.
source_quote: He names this the strong-weak hypothesis with the satisfaction of a man who has just filed something correctly.

subject: The Ajar Door
fact: The third-floor apartment door was left open — unexamined and unexplained — potentially connected to the murder, the missing book, or the cat’s behavior; it remains the next critical location to investigate.
source_quote: That was where I needed to be.

subject: The cat on the stairs
fact: The cat had been observed tracking the party without moving, and its nature as a potential power or familiar remained unproven and unresolved.
source_quote: Nobody had been able to conclusively prove the cat was some kind of power that lived here, and nobody had been able to conclusively prove that it was not.

subject: The Cat's Nature
fact: The cat’s behavior and the conflicting interpretations of it by the party suggest a hidden supernatural truth; its persistence, indifference, and the theological debate surrounding it imply it is more than it appears — or that someone wants others to believe it is.
source_quote: That's kind of how cats always are, I think," I said, because it is.

subject: the dragon scale building’s origin
fact: The Drakonoikos is built from dragon scales and bones — not mere decoration, but structural material. Who killed the dragon? Why were its remains used? Is this connected to Dawnbringer? To the Astronomicon’s celestial records? To the death of the Avowed? The building is a physical artifact of a hidden history that may hold the key to the murder.

subject: The Garden Shadow's curriculum
fact: The Garden Shadow never specified in their curriculum the conditions under which the party trained.
source_quote: After months of training under conditions the Garden Shadow had never specified in their curriculum, a few flights was nothing.

subject: The Gate Warden's Discovery
fact: The Gate Warden exited the crime scene after his inspection with a demeanor of discovery, yet was removed before reporting; his findings remain unknown, making him the most critical unspoken witness.
source_quote: Tadric noted that Kalan looked more determined coming out than going in.

subject: The Gate Warden’s Secret
fact: The Gate Warden performed the 'Speak with Dead' ritual and left the scene determined — he knows something no one else does, and his removal from the investigation before debriefing suggests suppression or fear.
source_quote: He looked more determined after he walked out.

subject: The Grygum School of Thought
fact: A new theological framework — the Grygum school — has emerged as an accidental proposition, positing fixed cosmic points that constrain agency while allowing freedom between them; it is now being treated as the central question of Candlekeep’s age, with Vareth actively researching it.
source_quote: The Grygum school of thought. Filed under: things that started as offhand remarks.

subject: The Grygum school of thought
fact: The Grygum school of thought was proposed as an offhand remark and is now being treated as the question of the age.
source_quote: I just proposed a school of theological thought by accident, and an aging scholar with forty-one years in this corner of the library is now treating it as the question of the age.

subject: The identity and purpose of the Drakonoikos
fact: The Drakonoikos is mentioned but not explained — its nature, function, or significance in Candlekeep remains an unresolved mystery.
source_quote: Then the Drakonoikos.

subject: The Identity of the Heart Seller
fact: The prophecy 'the heart is sold' remains unexplained, creating a second layer of mystery beyond the Keeper’s death — suggesting that a betrayal or sacrifice of institutional integrity is imminent or already underway.
source_quote: *On the longest night of winter's deepest cold, the keeper falls, the heart is sold.*

subject: The Missing Book
fact: 'The Golden Ass' is gone — the book Janussi was annotating with fresh ink — and its absence implies the research contained within was dangerous, heretical, or valuable enough to be stolen.
source_quote: Whatever Janussi had been working on most recently... was gone. That felt deliberate.

subject: the missing resignation record
fact: Bookwyrm revealed that Janussi requested Kalan’s resignation the morning of his death, but no written record of it was produced. The timing suggests it may have been destroyed or never documented — a deliberate act. The absence of this record is a critical gap in the investigation and may point to internal corruption or a cover-up.

subject: the nature of negligence
fact: Janussi accused Kalan of negligence, but the type of negligence was never specified. Was it failure to monitor the Dragon Breath Chamber? Allow unauthorized access? Neglect the Avowed? Or something more esoteric — like ignoring celestial signs recorded in the Astronomicon? The ambiguity is intentional and conceals a deeper institutional failure.

subject: The Nature of the Emerald Door
fact: The emerald door is a restricted passage used for clandestine access, implying that the First Reader operates outside standard institutional channels; its existence and use raise questions about hidden power structures within Candlekeep’s scholarly hierarchy.
source_quote: through the emerald door, before the avowed awake!

subject: The Need to Enter
fact: The party has not yet entered the third-floor apartment; its open door, proximity to the crime scene, and lack of documentation make it the next logical point of inquiry — the place where answers may be hidden.
source_quote: I hadn't been inside yet. That was where I needed to be.

subject: The Ooze’s Awakening
fact: Glabbagool’s desire to be released from the bag of holding signals a nascent sentience and existential yearning — potentially mirroring the Grygum school’s idea of constrained freedom — and may foreshadow his role in a larger theological or metaphysical revelation.
source_quote: He wanted out. I didn't know what *out* meant for an ooze. Neither did he. But the want was there.

subject: The Open Door
fact: The open door of the third-floor apartment is an unexplained anomaly in a highly controlled environment; its purpose and contents are unknown, but its existence implies a deliberate act or hidden evidence.
source_quote: A door left ajar on the third floor landing.

subject: The open door on the third floor
fact: The door to the apartment on the third floor landing had been left conspicuously ajar, and its significance had not yet been explained.
source_quote: A door left ajar on the third floor landing.

subject: the party’s philosophical framing
fact: Grygum and Thorin framed their investigation through pop culture (Poirot, Colombo) and philosophical claims — suggesting they are not just solving a crime, but testing a worldview. The murder may be a symptom of a deeper philosophical rupture in Candlekeep’s doctrine — perhaps between knowledge-as-control and knowledge-as-reverence. The party’s methods may be the solution, not just the means.

subject: the strong-weak hypothesis
fact: The theological framework of 'strong-weak' positions toward fixed points, derived from Stroud and Bahamut, was accidentally proposed as a school of thought and now stands as an unresolved doctrinal structure.
source_quote: I feel like I handled that competently," I say, to no one in particular. The Grygum school of thought. Filed under: things that started as offhand remarks.

subject: The Unfulfilled Prophecy Inventory
fact: Candlekeep maintains an inventory of unfulfilled prophecies from Alaundo; the recitation of 'the keeper falls' immediately after the Keeper’s death suggests that prophecies are not mere predictions but active, self-fulfilling mechanisms within the universe’s architecture.
source_quote: What remained was the unfulfilled inventory. Nobody knew what happened when the inventory ran out.

subject: The Unobserved Gap
fact: Tadric admitted he was not observing, only controlling; the Gate Warden’s movements inside the chamber during his inspection were unrecorded; this gap in observation is the most significant vulnerability in the timeline.
source_quote: He had not been watching closely enough to track what he'd done in there.

subject: The Unspoken Protection
fact: The Council had been protecting something — access, knowledge, or perhaps a person — without realizing it. The request for full library access exposed this, and the murder became secondary to the revelation of institutional concealment.
source_quote: We had not realized we were protecting.

subject: tobacco smoke lingering
fact: Lingering tobacco smoke in the sealed Keeper's Chambers indicated the murder occurred hours before discovery.
source_quote: The windows were shut. Nobody had been smoking recently. The smoke was old. ... Nobody smokes in a sealed room and leaves smoke that lingers for hours unless the room has been sealed for hours.

subject: Why the First Reader chose Daz and Grygum
fact: The First Reader bypassed institutional channels to summon Daz and Grygum specifically — the reason for this trust remains unexplained and must be answered.
source_quote: The question of why she thought that was, I noted, a question I would need answered.

subject: 2–3 a.m.
fact: Sylvira Savikas was seen glowing in candlelight at 2–3 a.m. — a time when the tower should have been silent, and her presence with a lantern defied her natural abilities.
source_quote: I swear I could see... around 2 or 3 in the morning...

subject: afternoon nap
fact: Janussi was awakened from his afternoon nap approximately thirty minutes before his death. This establishes the critical timeline for the attack.
source_quote: some thirty minutes later by our Sylvira Savikas, this is in the morning

subject: dawn discovery
fact: The body of Janussi was found at dawn, after he had been killed and his heart removed.
source_quote: The Great Reader A'lai Aivenmore had knocked it over in shock when he found the body at dawn.

subject: Deadwinter Day
fact: Deadwinter Day is the scheduled event before which Janussi was clearing business — a date of administrative importance that may have been a source of pressure or conflict among the Great Readers.
source_quote: clearing business before Deadwinter Day

subject: Deadwinter Day
fact: Janussi’s final meetings were scheduled to clear business before Deadwinter Day — a ceremonial deadline that may have triggered the murder, as the victim sought to expose or protect something before the holiday.
source_quote: clearing business before Deadwinter Day.

subject: elapsed time
fact: An hour passes between two events in the session.
source_quote: An hour later

subject: elapsed time
fact: Queenie was awakened thirty minutes later by Sylvira Savikas.
source_quote: some thirty minutes later by our Sylvira Savikas

subject: elapsed time
fact: The murder occurred in the narrow window between dinner and the moment his heart was carved out.
source_quote: within the evening — Janussi had eaten dinner with his face intact and his teeth whole. Whatever happened, happened in the narrow window between that meal and his death

subject: evening arrival
fact: Queenie observed guests arriving in order after supper — Fheminor first, Daral later — placing the events in the evening, shortly before the discovery of the body.
source_quote: She woke from her afternoon nap around eight, after supper, and watched the evening's guests arrive in order — first Fheminor... and later Daral...

subject: evening of Daral's departure
fact: Daral departed with *The Golden Ass* during the evening, after supper, when Queenie observed him running downstairs.
source_quote: after supper

subject: midnight
fact: The thud occurred at midnight — the time when the caretaker was awake but the Master was not to be disturbed — making it the last known moment Janussi was alive.
source_quote: I thought I heard a thud upstairs... I never slept before eleven...

subject: morning of Sylvira's attack
fact: Sylvira Savikas attacked Janussi’s armchamber approximately thirty minutes before Queenie was awakened — occurring in the morning.
source_quote: some thirty minutes later by our Sylvira Savikas, this is in the morning

subject: nighttime observation of imposter
fact: The shapeshifter wearing Sylvira’s form was observed prowling the nighttime cycle — after Queenie’s afternoon nap and before her final departure.
source_quote: she'd prowled the nighttime cycle and seen *the torn demon lady* coming down the steps

subject: rivalry revealed
fact: Daral Yashenti is the rival who called the sellswords and has been at Janussi's throat for years.
source_quote: That'll be Daral Yashenti. Those two have been at each other's throats for years.

subject: session date
fact: The events described occur during a single investigative session, beginning with the discovery of Janussi’s body and culminating in the planning to interview Hollypocket, the housekeeper. No calendar date is given, but the temporal flow is continuous and urgent.

subject: session date
fact: The events occur during the evening between dinner and the discovery of the body at dawn.
source_quote: Somewhere between dinner and the moment his heart was carved out

subject: session date
fact: The session occurs on the 5th day of the 2nd Tenday of Taraskh 1493 DR.
source_quote: On the 5th day of the 2nd Tenday of Taraskh 1493

subject: The Evening of Grygum’s Death
fact: The timeline of Grygum’s death can be reconstructed: dinner, assault (broken nose), reading the poisoned book (poisoning onset), heart removal (postmortem), and the killer’s departure. The sequence spans hours, not minutes.
source_quote: Somewhere between dinner and the moment his heart was carved out...

subject: attack on Janussi
fact: Janussi was violently awakened from his afternoon nap by Sylvira Savikas, who blasted the armchamber with a lance of unerring force light. This occurred approximately thirty minutes before his death and initiated the chain of events leading to his murder.
source_quote: She had settled into Janussi's armchair for a nap, she said, 'only to be rudely awakened some thirty minutes later by our Sylvira Savikas, this is in the morning, blasting the armchamber with a lance of unerring force light.'

subject: book access
fact: Unauthorized access to *The Golden Ass* — likely via the key to the Hightower Library — caused deletion of its contents and induced a state of stillness in those who opened it.
source_quote: they just sit there and don't tickle!

subject: book disappearance
fact: *The Golden Ass* was removed from the desk after Janussi annotated it — the only object missing from the room, despite evidence of its prior presence.
source_quote: The comedy book had walked out of the room.

subject: Daral's drunken confrontation
fact: Daral Yashenti drunkenly confronted Janussi at 10:30 PM, shouting insults and fleeing afterward.
source_quote: Daral came back at half past ten, drunk as a skunk, pounding on the door... another loud argument, then the slam and the great reader running back down the stairs.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz noticed blotches of midnight blue across the cuff.
source_quote: And blotches of midnight blue across the cuff.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz noticed the chip in Janussi's front tooth was recent and jagged.
source_quote: And a chip in one of his front teeth, the edge jagged. Recent.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz noticed the clotted blood under the nose and smeared bloodstains on the right sleeve of the tunic.
source_quote: Clotted blood under the nose. Smeared bloodstains on the right sleeve of the tunic — the *right* sleeve, the working hand.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz noticed the killer had rolled Janussi onto his back after death.
source_quote: And then someone had come in, after, and rolled him onto his back to take the heart.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz noticed the three circular impacts and holes in the armchair were from darts of pure force.
source_quote: Three circular impacts, horsehair stuffing scattered, two holes punched clean through the chair back.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz observed the empty pouches and sapphires in the safe and concluded someone was trying to build a sapphire spell.
source_quote: a little bit of this, a little bit of that... some sapphire spell.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz realized Janussi had fallen face-first, chipping his tooth on the stone.
source_quote: He had fallen forward. Face-first. Chipped the tooth on the way down.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz realized the black stain on the finger and lip was not ink.
source_quote: No. Not ink. That was the entire point of the long look — not that the finger was stained, but that the stain was *wrong*.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz stopped paying attention to the weeping Hollypocket and became lost in his own thoughts.
source_quote: Daz, I noticed, was paying the weeping woman no attention whatsoever, off somewhere in his own ledger.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz suddenly started listening when Hollypocket mentioned the lantern.
source_quote: Hmm," said Daz, suddenly listening after all.

subject: Daz talks to the cat
fact: Daz used a Stonespeaker crystal to communicate with the five-year-old housecat in Janussi's chamber.
source_quote: I think I can talk to the cat... It's part of what the stone speaker crystal grants me.

subject: death sequence
fact: Janussi was struck, returned to his desk, wrote jokes, then spell notes, was poisoned (masked by smoke), and died — his heart removed and valuables taken after death.
source_quote: Someone had struck him, broken his nose, waited or returned, killed him, rolled him over, taken his heart and one sapphire and a locket from his neck — and left the gold.

subject: deletion from Hightower Library book
fact: Content was deleted from a book in the Hightower Library that no one should have accessed. This was made possible by unauthorized entry using Janussi’s key, likely by the shapeshifter or Daral, who then used 'The Golden Ass' to induce stillness during the act.
source_quote: Someone snuck in. That might explain why that stuff got deleted off that book that no one should have touched.

subject: deletion of library content
fact: Certain passages in a restricted book were erased — an act that could only be performed by someone with access to the Hightower Library’s secure systems. The theft of Janussi’s key and the locket strongly suggests the deletion was intentional and tied to the murder.

subject: desecration of Janussi
fact: Janussi's body was meticulously desecrated after death — heart removed, ribcage shattered, nose broken prior to death, and black substance applied to finger and lip — suggesting a ritualistic or magical act performed with deliberate timing and calm intent.
source_quote: He had been desecrating a corpse at his leisure, with nowhere to be.

subject: evening guest arrival sequence
fact: First Fheminor arrived, and later Daral.
source_quote: first Fheminor, ... and later Daral

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum noticed the bruising around the broken nose was dark and settled, indicating it occurred before death.
source_quote: The bruising around the broken nose held color, dark and settled, the way bruising only sits when blood was still moving when it formed.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum noticed the impression of a chain on Janussi's neck and two broken lead links.
source_quote: The impression of a chain on the back and sides, and beneath it two broken lead links.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum noticed the safe was open with undamaged lock, indicating no forced entry.
source_quote: The safe. A box of metal as wide as a man's reach, sunk into the tower wall, its door standing open.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum noticed the statue of the Great Reader A'lai Aivenmore had fallen and concluded it was knocked over in shock.
source_quote: The statue had simply fallen... The Great Reader A'lai Aivenmore had knocked it over in shock when he found the body at dawn.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum observed the silver pedestal, ebony pipe, and cherry tobacco on the desk.
source_quote: A silver pedestal by the desk, an ebony pipe finely carved, cherry tobacco.

subject: Grygum's murder
fact: Grygum was assaulted before death — his nose broken, likely in a struggle — then poisoned by reading a magically tainted book, and finally had his heart removed after death. The killer entered without forcing the safe, suggesting knowledge of the combination or access.
source_quote: Somewhere between dinner and the moment his heart was carved out, someone had struck this man in the face hard enough to break the bone.

subject: Hollypocket
fact: Hollypocket heard Sylvira Savikas screaming at Janussi and thought they might have come to blows.
source_quote: Raging, screaming that Janussi was a traitor, the two of them sounding for a moment as though they had come to blows, before she stormed out and nearly took the door off its hinges.

subject: Hollypocket
fact: Hollypocket noticed Sylvira Savikas was carrying a lantern despite being a tiefling who can see in the dark.
source_quote: But what was really odd was not that Sylvira was there in the middle of the night — I've seen her in the middle of the night before — but that she was carrying a lantern. She's a tiefling, and she can see in the dark without any light at all.

subject: Hollypocket
fact: Hollypocket saw Sylvira Savikas’s face glowing red in the candlelight at 2 or 3 in the morning.
source_quote: I swear I could see that devil woman's — Sylvira Savikas's — face glowing red in the candlelight.

subject: Janussi's Final Day
fact: On the day of his death, Janussi held a series of explosive one-on-one meetings with Great Readers, culminating in Daral’s second violent confrontation and a mysterious thud heard at midnight, after which he was never seen alive again.
source_quote: I'd never seen him run away so fast.

subject: Janussi's final morning meetings
fact: Janussi spent his last morning in one-on-one meetings with the Great Readers, each ending in explosive shouting matches — at least half of them, according to Hollypocket — indicating escalating hostility among colleagues.
source_quote: Janussi had spent his last morning in a series of one-on-one meetings with the Great Readers, clearing business before Deadwinter Day.

subject: Janussi's murder
fact: Janussi was killed under suspicious circumstances, with his locket and the Hightower Library key he held both missing. The deletion of content from a restricted book suggests a deliberate attempt to erase evidence, implicating someone with access to the library’s security system.

subject: Kalan's thunderous face
fact: Kalan Strongbranch had a face like thunder when encountered by Hollypocket at dawn.
source_quote: I was bringing the keeper his morning tea when I passed Kalan Strongbranch on the steps. He had a face like thunder...

subject: Midnight Thud
fact: A heavy thud was heard from Janussi’s chamber around 2–3 a.m., coinciding with Sylvira Savikas’s unexplained presence and the disappearance of the locket and the comedy book; it likely marked the moment of death or the removal of evidence.
source_quote: I thought I heard a thud upstairs.

subject: midnight thud
fact: A thud was heard upstairs around midnight, after which Janussi was no longer alive — the caretaker had assumed he was alive until that sound, as she never slept before eleven in case the Master needed something.
source_quote: I thought I heard a thud upstairs... I never slept before eleven... that was how she knew he had been alive until the thud.

subject: midnight thud
fact: A thud was heard upstairs around midnight, after which Janussi was no longer alive.
source_quote: I heard a thud upstairs... around 2 or 3 in the morning.

subject: murder sequence
fact: Janussi was assaulted, breaking his nose, then returned to his desk to write, ingested a black poison while reading, fell face-first, chipping his tooth, and was later rolled over and had his heart removed by a deliberate, unhurried killer.
source_quote: A man at his books, wetting his finger to turn a poisoned page. The black climbing through him while he read on, suspecting nothing. A fall, forward, hard — a broken nose, a chipped tooth on the stone. And then the patient hands arriving after, in no hurry at all, rolling the body and opening the chest to make certain he stayed gone.

subject: murder sequence
fact: The murder occurred in a precise, non-rushed sequence: Janussi was first assaulted (broken nose, bruising formed while alive), returned to his desk, and continued writing in blue ink on *The Discoveries*. While reading a poisoned spellbook, he ingested a black substance that slowly poisoned him. He fell face-first, chipping his tooth. After death, his killer rolled him onto his back, removed his heart, and took one sapphire and a locket from his neck — leaving behind a vast treasury. The killer had no need to force entry and possessed intimate knowledge of the safe’s combination.
source_quote: He had been dead before his chest was opened. Whoever did this had not been in a rush. He had not been trying to kill. He had been desecrating a corpse at his leisure.

subject: Narrator
fact: The narrator noticed the phrase 'hypnotic block' was doing work the describer didn't understand.
source_quote: Something in the phrasing snagged. I have spent my life learning to notice when a description is doing work the describer doesn't understand.

subject: poison ingestion
fact: Janussi ingested the black substance by wetting his fingertip to turn pages, indicating the poison was embedded in the parchment and designed to be absorbed through touch and ingestion.
source_quote: Finger to a page, finger to the lip — turning pages, wetting the fingertip the way readers do without thinking, a hundred times an hour, never once considering that the page might be the thing reading *them*.

subject: poison smoke cover
fact: Tobacco smoke was used to mask the smell of poison in Janussi's chamber.
source_quote: The one thing that tobacco smoke would do is hide the smell of poison.

subject: Queenie
fact: Queenie noticed Daral running downstairs with a hypnotic block.
source_quote: when I later saw him run downstairs with a hypnotic block.

subject: Queenie
fact: Queenie recalled being rudely awakened by Sylvira Savikas blasting the armchamber with a lance of force.
source_quote: she said, "only to be rudely awakened some thirty minutes later by our Sylvira Savikas, this is in the morning, blasting the armchamber with a lance of unerring force light."

subject: safe breach
fact: The safe was opened without force, and only one sapphire and one parchment were taken — the rest of a king’s ransom left untouched — indicating the thief sought a specific component, not wealth.
source_quote: Whoever did this came in, took one sapphire, and walked past a king's ransom.

subject: sequence of death
fact: The sequence was: nose broken, then writing, then fall, then heart removed.
source_quote: A man at his books, wetting his finger to turn a poisoned page. A fall, forward, hard — a broken nose, a chipped tooth on the stone. And then the patient hands arriving after, in no hurry at all, rolling the body and opening the chest

subject: sequence of discovery
fact: The statue was knocked over when A'lai Aivenmore discovered the body at dawn.
source_quote: The Great Reader A'lai Aivenmore had knocked it over in shock when he found the body at dawn

subject: sequence of last writing
fact: Janussi's last writing was in blue ink on The Discoveries, after writing on The Golden Ass.
source_quote: The blue ink on The Discoveries had been laid down after the blue ink on another book. The Golden Ass.

subject: shapeshifter impersonation
fact: A figure wearing Sylvira Savikas’s shape but lacking her scent was seen descending the steps after her attack. This indicates a shapeshifter was active, impersonating her to mislead observers and conceal true intentions.
source_quote: But she didn't smell like the demon lady, though.

subject: statue fall
fact: The statue of the Great Reader A'lai Aivenmore fell when the scholar discovered the body, proving it was an accident, not sabotage.
source_quote: The Great Reader A'lai Aivenmore had knocked it over in shock when he found the body at dawn.

subject: Sylvira's traitor accusation
fact: Sylvira Savikas accused Janussi of being a traitor and nearly came to blows with him.
source_quote: Sylvira Savikas... screaming that Janussi was a traitor, the two of them sounding for a moment as though they had come to blows.

subject: Teles's hypocrite accusation
fact: Teles Ahvoste shouted 'hypocrite' at Janussi during their meeting at the ninth bell.
source_quote: I did hear Teles shout, *hypocrite*, at poor Janussi before he stormed out.

subject: the argument with Kalan Strongbranch
fact: Kalan Strongbranch passed Hollypocket on the steps with a face like thunder, nearly knocking the tea tray out of her hands.
source_quote: I passed Kalan Strongbranch on the steps. He had a face like thunder, nearly knocked the tray out of my hands

subject: the argument with Teles Ahvoste
fact: Teles Ahvoste shouted 'hypocrite' at Janussi during their meeting around the ninth bell, ending in a shouting match.
source_quote: I did hear Teles shout, *hypocrite*, at poor Janussi before he stormed out

subject: the cipher hypothesis
fact: The cipher hypothesis arose from the annotated comedy book — jokes and spell notes in the same hand, suggesting the book itself was a key to a replacement cipher.
source_quote: There's something written in the book that wasn't part of the original book — or maybe he's using the book and the notes to do some sort of cipher. Some sort of replacement cipher, and there's, like, some sort of code that the book ends up being the key to.

subject: the confrontation with Daral at half past ten
fact: Daral Yashenti returned drunk at half past ten, pounded on Janussi’s door until let in, argued loudly, then fled down the stairs in terror — the fastest Janussi had ever seen him run.
source_quote: Daral came back at half past ten, drunk as a skunk, pounding on the door until Janussi let him in... another loud argument, then the slam and the great reader running back down the stairs... I'd never seen him run away so fast

subject: the discovery of the missing book
fact: The comedy book — *The Golden Ass* — was confirmed missing from the room, its absence the only physical change, and its annotations the only evidence of its presence.
source_quote: the comedy book had walked out of the room... you do not annotate a thing you do not hold... And now it was gone, and it was the only thing gone

subject: the final hypothesis
fact: The final hypothesis combined poison, cipher, and rivalry — the book was a cipher key, the smoke concealed poison, the locket was stolen to implicate a rival, and Daral and Sylvira were the prime suspects.
source_quote: The poison and the cipher could both be true. The missing book carried both. We had read the room down to what it was willing to give. The rest of it lived somewhere else, and we'd have to go find it.

subject: theft of 'The Golden Ass'
fact: The book 'The Golden Ass' was removed from the scene by Daral. It is not a magical device but a mundane object capable of inducing stillness and disinterest — effectively a 'hypnotic block.' Its removal coincides with the deletion of content from a restricted book in the Hightower Library.
source_quote: The Golden Ass, the missing volume, walking out of the room under Daral's arm.

subject: the gift delivery
fact: A gift was delivered to Janussi — a Dead Winter gift inscribed by a rival — written in a resentful, cramped hand, and left in the wastebasket.
source_quote: A gift tag surfaced from the wastebasket... 'To Janussi, read it and weep, you old snob, a proper Dead Winter gift, your loving rival.'

subject: the midnight thud
fact: At midnight, Hollypocket heard a thud from above — the last sound she associated with Janussi being alive — and later recalled seeing Sylvira Savikas’s glowing red face in candlelight, carrying a lantern she had no use for.
source_quote: I heard a thud upstairs... I swear I could see that devil woman's — Sylvira Savikas's — face glowing red in the candlelight... she was carrying a lantern. She's a tiefling, and she can see in the dark without any light at all

subject: the poison hypothesis
fact: The poison hypothesis emerged from the absence of the book, the black residue, the smoke, and the locket — all pointing to a murder masked by environmental concealment.
source_quote: The black on the pages of a book that was no longer in the room. The smoke that hid the smell of it... The one thing that tobacco smoke would do is hide the smell of poison... you don't fill a room with smoke to kill a man — you fill a room with smoke to keep him from smelling what's already there

subject: third dart impact
fact: Three darts of pure force struck the chair.
source_quote: Three circular impacts, horsehair stuffing scattered, two holes punched clean through the chair back

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin declined Hollypocket’s herbal tea.
source_quote: No thank you, I'm good.

subject: tobacco use
fact: Cherry tobacco was lit in the ebony pipe to mask the smell of poison, suggesting the killer or someone present was attempting to conceal the nature of the death.
source_quote: Tobacco smoke would hide the smell of poison. Of course it would.

subject: travel to Sloobludop
fact: Sloobludop is approximately eight days away via the Darklake.
source_quote: the town of Sloopdopblop is just eight days away

subject: wake-up time
fact: Queenie woke from her afternoon nap around eight, after supper.
source_quote: She woke from her afternoon nap around eight, after supper

subject: writing sequence
fact: Janussi first wrote jokes in blue ink in *The Golden Ass*, then shifted to recording spell research in *The Discoveries*, with the joke annotations having dried ink before the spell notes were added.
source_quote: Jokes first. The ink on those had dried. Then he'd flopped over into the spell research.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir accepted Hollypocket’s herbal tea with more enthusiasm than the situation required.
source_quote: Yes, I love… Absolutely!

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir noticed the blue ink on *The Discoveries* was fresher than the blue ink on *The Golden Ass*.
source_quote: The blue ink on *The Discoveries* had been laid down after the blue ink on another book. *The Golden Ass.*

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir noticed the locket or necklace was missing from Janussi’s neck.
source_quote: Something had hung there, and someone had torn it off him. A locket, a necklace — gone, snapped at the chain.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir realized the black substance on Janussi’s finger and lip was not ink.
source_quote: With ink?

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir suggested Glabbagool might have ingested the black substance and could help identify it.
source_quote: Wouldn't Glabbagool have ingested, like, all sorts of different kinds of materials and poisons and goo in the Underdark?

subject: Candlekeep Librarians
fact: The Candlekeep Librarians, as keepers of arcane texts, were likely targets of the attack — Janussi was actively writing in the books at time of death, suggesting the assailant sought to silence or intercept knowledge contained in his notes.
source_quote: Wasn't the blue ink — the ink they used in the books? It was.

subject: Candlekeep Scholars
fact: The scholars of Candlekeep maintain grudges like dragons hoard gold — silently, meticulously, over years — and resolve conflicts through scholarly discourse that often masks violent intent.
source_quote: In the Underdark everyone runs six angles at once and at least there it's honest about being a knife fight. Up here they smile and they file the grievance and they wait.

subject: Candlekeep Scholars
fact: The scholars of Candlekeep maintain grudges with obsessive, almost draconian patience, treating intellectual rivalries as sacred vendettas. Thorin despises this culture as dishonest and corrosive, contrasting it with the transparent violence of the Underdark.

subject: Clerics of Bahamut
fact: The clerics of Bahamut operate on tighter margins than their theatrics suggest — a remark made by Queenie’s observer to explain Grygum’s inability to afford a potion. This reflects a cultural observation about their order’s austerity.
source_quote: clerics of Bahamut, it turns out, run on a tighter margin than their theatrics suggest.

subject: Curator of the Infernal Fortress
fact: The Curator of the Infernal Fortress is Sylvira Savikas’s official job function — a scholar who studies devils — not a pejorative label, clarifying that 'devil woman' was a misinterpretation of her role.
source_quote: Sylvira is the Curator of the Infernal Fortress. A woman who studies devils. Not an epithet. A job function.

subject: Hightower Library
fact: The Hightower Library is a restricted archive with two physical keys — one held by Janussi, the other by Kalan — and its contents were altered by unauthorized access.
source_quote: that stuff got deleted off that book that no one should have touched

subject: Stonespeaker Crystal Users
fact: Users of the Stonespeaker crystal have the ability to communicate with beasts. The narrator is one such user, and the crystal — once a curiosity — is now a witness to events and a tool of investigation.
source_quote: the stone speaker crystal grants me.

subject: The Garden Shadow
fact: The Garden Shadow (or possibly Brother Tharusk) held the belief that a room reveals its truth most clearly through what is missing rather than what remains.
source_quote: Count what should be present before you count what is.

subject: The Keeper’s Order
fact: Grygum was a member of a secretive order that preserved arcane knowledge, evidenced by his library, spell pouches, and the sacred statue of the candle-holding elder. His death suggests an internal or targeted breach.
source_quote: I have catalogued a great many sacred spaces in my time, and there is a particular grief in an empty setting where something belonged.

subject: The Order of the Great Reader A'lai Aivenmore
fact: Janussi was a member of this scholarly order, evidenced by the toppled marble statue of A'lai Aivenmore in the chamber — a symbol of the order. The statue's fall was accidental, caused by shock upon discovering the body at dawn, confirming Janussi’s identity as a devoted scholar of the order’s traditions.
source_quote: The Great Reader A'lai Aivenmore had knocked it over in shock when he found the body at dawn.

subject: armchair
fact: Queenie settled into Janussi's armchair for a nap, only to be rudely awakened thirty minutes later by Sylvira Savikas blasting the armchamber with a lance of unerring force light.
source_quote: She had settled into Janussi's armchair for a nap, she said, "only to be rudely awakened some thirty minutes later by our Sylvira Savikas, this is in the morning, blasting the armchamber with a lance of unerring force light."

subject: armchamber
fact: The armchamber was blasted with a lance of unerring force light by Sylvira Savikas.
source_quote: blasting the armchamber with a lance of unerring force light.

subject: candle height
fact: The candle on the statue is present but no height is stated.
source_quote: shake the candle

subject: Candlekeep
fact: Candlekeep is a revered archive of knowledge, but its scholarly culture is deeply poisoned by long-held grudges and hidden rivalries. Thorin sees it as a place where violence is masked as intellect — making it more dangerous than the Underdark.

subject: Candlekeep
fact: Candlekeep’s culture — not the library, but the scholars — is defined by grudges filed like scrolls, polished over years, and deployed as weapons.
source_quote: I despise this whole place a little — not Candlekeep, Candlekeep's fine, the books are fine — but the *culture* of it, the scholars who keep grudges the way a dragon keeps gold, sitting on them for years, polishing them

subject: corridor
fact: Queenie retreated to the corridor after Daral's shouting.
source_quote: she retreated to the corridor — "when I later saw him run downstairs with a hypnotic block."

subject: corridor
fact: The corridor is where Queenie retreated after Daral’s noisy departure — a place of temporary refuge.
source_quote: she retreated to the corridor

subject: Corridor
fact: The location where Queenie retreated after Daral began shouting. She later observed him running downstairs with the book — 'hypnotic block' — from this vantage point.
source_quote: she retreated to the corridor — 'when I later saw him run downstairs with a hypnotic block.'

subject: downstairs
fact: Downstairs is the location Daral fled to with *The Golden Ass*, observed by Queenie as he ran with the 'hypnotic block'.
source_quote: run downstairs with a hypnotic block

subject: Grygum’s Study
fact: The study contained a locked safe with untouched riches, scattered spell components, a toppled statue, a damaged armchair with dart holes, an ebony pipe with cherry tobacco, and a silver pedestal. The room was staged to appear like a robbery but revealed a precise, non-greedy target.
source_quote: Still inside the safe were four sealed pouches, each with its sapphire — and beside them a figurine of a raven, a potion of supreme healing...

subject: Hightower Library
fact: A restricted repository where a book was altered or had content deleted. Access requires two keys — one held by Janussi, the other by Kalan. The theft of 'The Golden Ass' is linked to unauthorized access here.
source_quote: Someone snuck in. That might explain why that stuff got deleted off that book that no one should have touched.

subject: Hightower Library
fact: The Hightower Library has two keys — one held by Janussi, missing from his neck, and one held by the gate warden Kalan.
source_quote: Janussi held one of the two keys of the Hightower Library... the other key is heralded by the gate warden, Kalan

subject: Hightower Library
fact: The Hightower Library holds forbidden or restricted texts; only those with the two keys — one held by Janussi, one by Kalan — may access its deepest archives, making the missing locket a potential key to forbidden knowledge.
source_quote: Janussi held one of the two keys of the Hightower Library.

subject: Hightower Library
fact: The Hightower Library is a restricted archive whose contents were altered — access requires one of two keys, held by Janussi and Kalan.
source_quote: that stuff got deleted off that book that no one should have touched

subject: Hightower Library
fact: The Hightower Library is a restricted section of Candlekeep with dual-key security. Access requires both keys — one held by Janussi (now missing), the other by Kalan. Unauthorized access likely led to the deletion of content and the murder.

subject: Hightower Library
fact: The Hightower Library is the location whose contents were deleted from a book no one should have touched, likely due to unauthorized access with one of the two keys.
source_quote: That might explain why that stuff got deleted off that book that no one should have touched. Someone snuck in.

subject: Hollypocket's apartment
fact: Hollypocket, the housekeeper, resides in a modest, warm apartment below the Keeper's tower.
source_quote: Hollypocket's apartment sat below the Keeper's tower — modest, but with room to breathe, and warm...

subject: Janussi's apartment
fact: Janussi's apartment, located below the Keeper's tower, is the site of the caretaker’s observations — where tea was offered, arguments were overheard, and the final moments of Janussi’s life were quietly witnessed.
source_quote: Hollypocket's apartment sat below the Keeper's tower — modest, but with room to breathe...

subject: Janussi's Armchair
fact: The location where Janussi was napping when attacked. Queenie observed the entire event from this spot. It is the epicenter of the initial violence and the origin of the timeline.
source_quote: She had settled into Janussi's armchair for a nap...

subject: Janussi's armchamber
fact: Janussi's armchamber is the site of Sylvira’s force attack and the location where Queenie napped after being disturbed.
source_quote: blasting the armchamber with a lance of unerring force light

subject: Janussi's Chamber
fact: Janussi’s chamber was filled with tobacco smoke, contained the comedy book and locket before death, and was the site of the midnight thud — now a crime scene where the absence of objects reveals more than their presence.
source_quote: A room tells you most by what it is missing.

subject: Janussi's desk
fact: Janussi's desk was the central locus of activity — holding *The Discoveries*, *The Golden Ass*, blue ink, and the gift tag — and the only place where physical evidence of his final hours remained.
source_quote: The desk again. We came back to it.

subject: Keeper's Chamber
fact: The Keeper's Chamber contained a silver pedestal, an ebony pipe with cherry tobacco, and an open safe with scattered empty pouches, loose sapphires, and scraps of parchment naming spells.
source_quote: A silver pedestal by the desk, an ebony pipe finely carved, cherry tobacco... Empty pouches scattered in front of it, sapphires loose and dazzling, scraps of parchment naming spells.

subject: Keeper's Chamber
fact: The chamber showed no signs of forced entry, and the safe was opened cleanly — indicating the killer had access or knowledge of the combination.
source_quote: Open, but undamaged. No forced entry. The killer had the combination, or had no need of one.

subject: Keeper's Chamber
fact: The safe still held four sealed pouches with sapphires, a figurine of a raven, a potion of supreme healing, a potion of water breathing, five diamonds, a heap of platinum and gold — all untouched.
source_quote: Still inside the safe were four sealed pouches, each with its sapphire — and beside them a figurine of a raven, a potion of supreme healing, another of water breathing, five diamonds each worth a fortune, a heap of platinum and gold, a small treasury left untouched.

subject: Keeper's Chamber, Candlekeep
fact: The Keeper's Chamber was the site of Janussi’s murder and desecration — bloodless spray, scattered tooth fragment, smeared ink and black substance on clothing, and signs of a struggle or interruption during writing — all pointing to an attack occurring during or shortly after evening activities.
source_quote: Janussi had been taking notes when this happened. Writing hand, fresh stains.

subject: Keeper's Chamber, Candlekeep
fact: The chamber contained evidence of a targeted, non-greedy theft: an open safe with four sealed sapphire pouches, a raven figurine, healing and water-breathing potions, diamonds, platinum, and gold — all untouched except for one missing sapphire and one missing parchment. A silver pedestal, ebony pipe, and cherry tobacco were present, suggesting the killer used smoke to mask poison. A chair bore three puncture wounds from force darts aimed at the seat, not the victim. The statue of A'lai Aivenmore lay toppled — a sign of shock, not sabotage.
source_quote: Someone is trying to build a sapphire spell... and left the gold.

subject: Keeper's Desk
fact: The desk held *The Discoveries*, *The Golden Ass*, blue ink, and evidence of multiple ink colors, with the latest writing in blue on *The Discoveries*.
source_quote: In the middle of the desk sat a spellbook. *The Discoveries.* Beside it, blue ink, fresh enough that it had a sequence to it.

subject: Keeper's tower
fact: The Keeper's tower is the central location of the investigation, housing Janussi's apartment below, the bell tower, and the quarters of the Great Readers — a place where scholarly tension, midnight movements, and violent confrontation converge.
source_quote: The bell tower rang... I thought I heard a thud upstairs...

subject: key to Hightower Library
fact: Janussi held one of the two keys to the Hightower Library; the other is held by the gate warden Kalan.
source_quote: Janussi held one of the two keys of the Hightower Library. The other key is heralded by the gate warden, Kalan.

subject: murder chamber
fact: The murder chamber is where Janussi was killed. The air in the hall outside is described as 'better — not good, but better,' indicating the lingering tension and horror of the crime scene.

subject: Queenie's tower
fact: Queenie's tower is her domain — the place where all observations were made and where she finally dismissed the investigators.
source_quote: please give yourself a proper licking before returning to my tower

subject: safe contents count
fact: Four sealed pouches, one figurine, two potions, five diamonds, and a heap of platinum and gold remained in the safe.
source_quote: four sealed pouches, each with its sapphire — and beside them a figurine of a raven, a potion of supreme healing, another of water breathing, five diamonds each worth a fortune, a heap of platinum and gold

subject: safe dimensions
fact: The safe is as wide as a man's reach.
source_quote: a box of metal as wide as a man's reach

subject: statue height
fact: The marble statue of A'lai Aivenmore is three feet tall.
source_quote: Three feet of marble

subject: steps
fact: The steps are where the shapeshifter wearing Sylvira’s form was observed descending — the last known location of the imposter.
source_quote: coming down the steps

subject: Sylvira's glowing face
fact: Sylvira Savikas's face glowed red in candlelight at 2–3 AM, though she is a tiefling who needs no light.
source_quote: I swear I could see that devil woman's — Sylvira Savikas's — face glowing red in the candlelight.

subject: the Garden Shadow
fact: The Garden Shadow had a saying about absence — that a room tells you most by what it is missing — possibly echoed by Brother Tharusk, the tall one who always smelled of incense.
source_quote: The Garden Shadow had a saying about that — or possibly Brother Tharusk did, the tall one who always smelled of incense

subject: the murder chamber
fact: The murder chamber was filled with tobacco smoke — a habit Janussi kept to mask his failing lungs — and now served as the site where the smell of poison was hidden.
source_quote: A man who fills his own room with smoke as a habit... The one thing that tobacco smoke would do is hide the smell of poison... you fill a room with smoke to keep him from smelling what's already there

subject: Velkynvelve elevation
fact: Velkynvelve sits 100 feet above the cavern floor.
source_quote: Drow outpost was 100' in the sky

subject: wastebasket
fact: The wastebasket contained the gift tag, indicating the rival’s note was discarded after delivery — possibly by Janussi or the killer.
source_quote: A gift tag surfaced from the wastebasket as we were leaving — almost behind the desk, in a cramped, sour hand.

subject: chasme count
fact: Four chasme demons are present in the cavern above the prisoners' tower.
source_quote: four chasme and two vrock

subject: drow count
fact: No drow are mentioned.

subject: Glabbagool
fact: Glabbagool, an ooze from the Underdark, was given the black substance from Janussi’s lip and finger, but could not identify it — confirming its unnatural and dangerous nature.
source_quote: We gave him the substance. He gave it his best. It wasn't enough — a thin first effort, then a second pass with help, and still nothing he could name.

subject: Glabbagool (Ooze)
fact: Glabbagool, an ooze familiar with Underdark toxins, was presented with the black substance. He made two attempts to identify it — first a thin effort, then a second with help — and failed. His inability to classify the poison confirms its origin is not natural, not of the Underdark, and likely designed to evade detection by even the most experienced absorbers of poisons.
source_quote: When even a creature that has eaten the Underdark can't place a poison, you've learned the poison is worth being afraid of.

subject: ooze count
fact: Glabbagool, an ooze, was tested for poison identification.
source_quote: Glabbagool

subject: shapeshifter
fact: A shapeshifter wearing Sylvira Savikas's form but lacking her scent was observed by Queenie — an imposter mimicking her appearance.
source_quote: But she didn't smell like the demon lady, though.

subject: statue
fact: A statue of marble, three feet tall, had fallen over — not awakened by magic, but knocked down accidentally by the discoverer of the body.
source_quote: The statue had simply fallen, it turned out.

subject: the cat
fact: A cat, whose involvement is described as a 'long story,' provided information to the party during their interrogation of Fembris. Its role remains cryptic but confirmed as a source of unexpected insight.

subject: The Poisoned Book
fact: A book enchanted with a slow-acting poison that seeped into ink, causing death through ingestion via licking fingers. It was not a creature, but a weaponized object designed to kill through ritualistic reading.
source_quote: the black climbing through him while he read on, suspecting nothing.

subject: the torn demon lady
fact: A figure resembling Sylvira Savikas — referred to by Queenie as 'the torn demon lady' — was seen descending the steps. But she did not smell like Sylvira, indicating a shapeshifter impersonation. The term 'torn' may refer to a physical or magical distortion.
source_quote: coming down the steps — Sylvira's shape — 'But she didn't smell like the demon lady, though.'

subject: Tobacco Smoke
fact: The tobacco smoke in Janussi’s chamber was not a habit, but a deliberate concealment mechanism — used to mask the scent of poison, making it functionally a weapon of deception.
source_quote: You don't fill a room with smoke to kill a man — you fill a room with smoke to keep him from smelling what's already there.

subject: unknown assailant
fact: The assailant exhibited extreme precision and calm, disabling Janussi before death (broken nose, chipped tooth) and then performing post-mortem desecration (heart removal, black substance application) — indicating familiarity with arcane practices and a desire to prevent resurrection or extract hidden knowledge.
source_quote: The blows had been precise. Too precise, too close together, for a man fighting back.

subject: A'lai Aivenmore
fact: A'lai Aivenmore discovered Janussi’s body at dawn and knocked over the statue in shock.
source_quote: The Great Reader A'lai Aivenmore had knocked it over in shock when he found the body at dawn.

subject: Daral
fact: Daral carried The Golden Ass under his arm and ran downstairs with a hypnotic block.
source_quote: when I later saw him run downstairs with a hypnotic block.

subject: Daral
fact: Daral is a man with a stinky breath whom Queenie observed running downstairs with a hypnotic block — later revealed to be the missing book, *The Golden Ass*.
source_quote: when I later saw him run downstairs with a hypnotic block

subject: Daral
fact: Daral is associated with a book — 'The Golden Ass' — that he carried away from the scene. This book, not a device, induces stillness and uninterest. He shouted excessively, prompting Queenie to retreat. He left the scene while the victim was still alive.
source_quote: when I later saw him run downstairs with a hypnotic block.

subject: Daral
fact: Daral is the stinky breath one, the second guest to arrive in the evening.
source_quote: first Fheminor, *the short-legged one*, and later Daral, *the stinky breath one*.

subject: Daral Yashenti
fact: Daral Yashenti had been at Janussi's throat for years, drank excessively, shouted at Janussi twice in one day, called him 'nothing but a glorified book peddler,' and fled the second argument in terror.
source_quote: Daral Yashenti... those two have been at each other's throats for years... he drinks way too much... 'You're not fit to be the candle keep's keeper'... 'nothing but a glorified book peddler'... he ran away so fast

subject: Daral Yashenti
fact: Daral Yashenti is a long-standing rival of Janussi, having harbored a bitter, years-long grudge. He publicly displayed disdain for the sell-swords, making him the prime suspect in their eyes. His hostility and access to the library’s secrets position him as a central antagonist.

subject: Daral Yashenti
fact: Daral Yashenti was Janussi’s long-standing rival, known for drinking heavily, engaging in explosive arguments with him twice in one day, and fleeing after the second confrontation; he is the one who called in the sellswords and is now the prime suspect.
source_quote: He's the one who called you sellswords.

subject: Daral Yashenti
fact: Daral Yashenti, nursing a hangover, verbally attacked Janussi twice — calling him unfit to be candle keeper and a 'glorified book peddler' — and later returned drunk at half past ten, leading to a loud argument followed by Janussi fleeing down the stairs.
source_quote: You're not fit to be the candle keep's keeper... nothing but a glorified book peddler... I'd never seen him run away so fast.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz believed the black substance was likely poisonous.
source_quote: I thought it the likeliest answer.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz believes a corpse does not lie and that everything it knows is written on it.
source_quote: There is a particular comfort in a corpse. It does not lie. It does not run a counter-play. Everything it knows is written on it, and all I have to do is read.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz believes he can talk to the cat using the Stonespeaker crystal.
source_quote: I think I can talk to the cat," I said.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz carries the Stonespeaker crystal as a useful tool for communicating with beasts.
source_quote: Talking to beasts, yeah. It's part of what the stone speaker crystal grants me.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz conducted the forensic investigation of Grygum’s body and room, identifying patterns of poisoning, trauma, and missing components. He recognized the significance of the sapphire pouches and the implication of a targeted spell requiring a single sapphire.
source_quote: a little bit of this, a little bit of that

subject: Daz
fact: Daz has a sharp instinct for connecting disparate clues — he immediately recognized the significance of the locket and the Hightower Library keys, and was the first to link the deletion of content to a possible intrusion using one of the keys.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz is a detached investigator who ignored emotional testimony until a critical forensic detail — the lantern — was mentioned, suggesting he is methodical, possibly biased toward physical evidence, and may have prior knowledge of Sylvira's habits.
source_quote: Daz, I noticed, was paying the weeping woman no attention whatsoever... Hmm," said Daz, suddenly listening after all.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz is a stone speaker with access to a Stonespeaker crystal; he is methodical, detached, and the only one capable of communicating with the housecat — making him critical to reconstructing the timeline of the murder.
source_quote: I think I can talk to the cat.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz performed a forensic reading of the body, noting the tempo of the killer, the sequence of injuries, and the nature of the black substance.
source_quote: I logged that. *The first thing to read is the tempo of the killer.* This one had time.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz performed the initial forensic analysis of Janussi’s body, identifying the precise sequence of death, the unnatural timing of the heart removal, and the significance of the black stain. He noted the tempo of the killer — calm, unhurried, desecrating rather than killing — and correctly deduced the poison was not ink. He later connected the sapphire and parchment to a targeted spell.
source_quote: The first thing to read is the tempo of the killer. This one had time.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz recognized the significance of the lantern carried by Sylvira Savikas — a tiefling who needs no light — and was the first to link it to the candlelight as a cover for poison.
source_quote: That explains the candle.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz, the Stonespeaker, used his crystal to prepare to interrogate the housecat — the only living witness in the chamber — and was the first to notice the significance of Sylvira’s lantern.
source_quote: Daz... 'I think I can talk to the cat.'... 'Talking to beasts, yeah. It's part of what the stone speaker crystal grants me.'... Daz was paying the weeping woman no attention whatsoever... 'That explains the candle.'

subject: Fembris
fact: Fembris is a reluctant but persistent source of information, offering key details about Daral Yashenti’s rivalry with Janussi, the missing locket, and the two Hightower Library keys — one held by Janussi, the other by Kalan the gate warden. He speaks in hesitant, meandering phrases but consistently reveals critical plot points.

subject: Fembris
fact: Fembris supplied that Janussi held one of the two keys to the Hightower Library.
source_quote: Fembris, *by golly*, supplied the column I was missing: Janussi held one of the two keys to the Hightower Library.

subject: Fembris
fact: Fembris supplies the missing piece: Janussi held one of the two keys to the Hightower Library. His contribution enables the narrator to connect the book’s deletion to unauthorized access.
source_quote: Janussi held one of the two keys to the Hightower Library.

subject: Fembris
fact: Fembris, the assistant, identified Daral Yashenti as Janussi’s long-time rival and revealed that Janussi held one of the two keys to the Hightower Library.
source_quote: Fembris... 'Oh, that'll be Daral Yashenti. Those two have been at each other's throats for years.'... 'Janussi held one of the two keys of the Hightower Library.'

subject: Fheminor
fact: Fheminor is referred to by Queenie as 'the short-legged one.' He was among the first evening guests to arrive, noted for his gait. His relevance is observational, not causal.
source_quote: first Fheminor, *the short-legged one*,

subject: Fheminor
fact: Fheminor is the short-legged one, the first guest to arrive in the evening.
source_quote: first Fheminor, *the short-legged one*, and later Daral, *the stinky breath one*.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum approaches problems pragmatically, focusing on tangible evidence and systemic gaps. He prioritizes identifying what is missing from the Hightower Library over political rivalries, and is already planning to interrogate the housekeeper to establish a baseline of normalcy.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum does not like Daral Yashenti.
source_quote: Hmm, well, I already don't like him.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum established the timeline of the assault using bruising patterns, confirming the broken nose occurred before death and identifying the chain marks from a removed locket.
source_quote: My focus narrowed and held, and the picture came clear and certain: this happened before he died. Not the fall. Earlier.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum established the timeline of the assault using trauma analysis — confirming the broken nose and bruising occurred before death. He identified the locket chain’s wear pattern and deduced the killer had prior access to Janussi. He ruled out forced entry and understood the significance of the untouched treasure — framing the crime as ritualistic, not criminal.
source_quote: You don't bruise after you're dead.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum felt a quiet grief at the image of a clerk dying mid-sentence in his own library.
source_quote: I noted that and felt something I didn't examine too closely — a clerk dying mid-sentence in his own library.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum finds most things funnier than the narrator does.
source_quote: Most things, he does.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum found the idea of buying another adventure as a product placement humorous and insisted the mystery required purchasing the referenced book.
source_quote: Oh, the mystery, you have to go buy the other adventure.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum found the idea of buying the other adventure funnier than the narrator did.
source_quote: He found this funnier than I did.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum insisted on interviewing the housekeeper to determine what was missing — grounding the investigation in physical absence rather than political motive.
source_quote: One thing we need is somebody who knows what should be here, so they can tell us if anything's missing... go find, say, the housekeeper, and ask her, what is missing or out of place

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum intends to ask the housekeeper what is missing or out of place.
source_quote: go find, say, the housekeeper, and ask her, what is missing or out of place.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum is cost-conscious, tracks expenses on his account, and is relieved when others absorb costs. He is pragmatic, noticing the locket’s absence and prompting the narrator to ask Queenie about it. He holds the key to the Hightower Library’s other lock.
source_quote: Daz, why don't you ask the cat anyway? It's gonna be a weird description from a cat, but…

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum is relieved that someone else has taken an expense off his account.
source_quote: Well, that saves me money on potions," said Grygum, relieved — someone else had just taken an expense off his account.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum is the investigator who focuses on tangible absence — he insists on interviewing the housekeeper to determine what is missing, grounding the investigation in physical evidence rather than speculation.
source_quote: Let me go over that one more time... go find, say, the housekeeper, and ask her, what is missing or out of place.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum recalled that bruising cannot form on a corpse because there is no living tissue to swell.
source_quote: Bruising doesn't form on a corpse; there's no living tissue to swell.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum wants to find the housekeeper to determine what is missing from the room.
source_quote: One thing we need is somebody who knows what should be here, so they can tell us if anything's missing.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum was found dead in his study, his nose broken, tooth chipped, tongue and lip blackened with ink poisoning, and his heart removed postmortem. He had been reading a poisoned book, smudging his fingers and licking the ink, indicating he was a meticulous reader to the end.
source_quote: He had been reading a book, smudging his fingers on the ink, and licking the smudges off his lip.

subject: Hollypocket
fact: Hollypocket believes Janussi always wore the locket and never took it off.
source_quote: the locket — Janussi carried it always, all the time, never took it off. He carried it all.

subject: Hollypocket
fact: Hollypocket is afraid of Sylvira Savikas.
source_quote: That devil woman! She gives me the heebie-jeebies!

subject: Hollypocket
fact: Hollypocket is the elderly gnome caretaker of Janussi's apartment, who offered tea and seats to the investigators, and provided key testimony about the victim's final days and the tensions among the scholars.
source_quote: I do hate gossip, but if it's necessary for the investigation…

subject: Hollypocket
fact: Hollypocket is the housekeeper who will be questioned next to determine what items are missing or out of place in the library. She is the party’s next critical source for establishing objective baseline knowledge — the only truth they can stand on.

subject: Hollypocket
fact: Hollypocket, the housekeeper, observed Janussi’s daily routines, noted the timing and nature of his final confrontations, and was the only witness to the midnight thud and Sylvira’s nocturnal lantern-lit passage.
source_quote: I swear I could see that devil woman's — Sylvira Savikas's — face glowing red in the candlelight.

subject: Hollypocket
fact: Hollypocket, the housekeeper, witnessed all major confrontations with Janussi, heard the midnight thud, and saw Sylvira Savikas glowing red in candlelight carrying a lantern she had no use for.
source_quote: Hollypocket... brought the keeper his morning tea... heard Teles shout 'hypocrite'... overheard Daral calling him 'glorified book peddler'... heard the midnight thud... saw Sylvira Savikas’s face glowing red... carrying a lantern... she can see in the dark without any light at all

subject: investigators count
fact: Six individuals are actively investigating: Daz, Grygum, Thorin, Zalthir, Tadric, and Milo.
source_quote: Grygum, Thorin, Zalthir, Daz, Tadric, and Milo

subject: Janussi
fact: Janussi carried a locket always, never took it off, and kept his chamber thick with tobacco smoke to medicate his failing lungs, living inside a haze on purpose.
source_quote: Janussi held one of the two keys of the Hightower Library, carried it always, never took it off, kept his chamber thick with it, medicated his failing lungs with the smell of it, lived inside a haze on purpose

subject: Janussi
fact: Janussi had a broken nose and bruising that formed before death, indicating an assault occurred between dinner and his murder.
source_quote: The bruising around the broken nose held its color, dark and settled, the way bruising only sits when blood was still moving when it formed.

subject: Janussi
fact: Janussi is a man in an on-and-off-again relationship with Sylvira Savikas, who carried a locket at all times and held one of the two keys to the Hightower Library.
source_quote: He carried it all the time. He never took it off.

subject: Janussi
fact: Janussi is in an on-and-off-again relationship with Sylvira Savikas and owned an armchair where Queenie napped.
source_quote: Sylvira the tiefling, and Janussi, an on-and-off-again relationship. A lover's quarrel, then, opened with a flung working of force.

subject: Janussi
fact: Janussi was a Keeper of the Tome who was writing in blue ink on *The Discoveries* at the time of his death, with blackened fingertip and lower lip, and a chipped front tooth from a forward fall.
source_quote: Janussi had been taking notes when this happened. Writing hand, fresh stains. A man interrupted at work.

subject: Janussi
fact: Janussi was a scholar who held one of the two keys to the Hightower Library and wore a locket that is now missing. His death and the disappearance of both the locket and his key indicate he was targeted, and his rival Daral Yashenti is the most likely perpetrator.

subject: Janussi
fact: Janussi was a scholar who kept private jokes in a comedy book, annotated with blue ink, and later used the same book for spell research; he wore a locket always, kept his chamber thick with tobacco smoke, and was found dead under mysterious circumstances.
source_quote: He was noting down jokes, and then flopped over to spell research.

subject: Janussi
