fact: Janussi was an on-again, off-again lover of Sylvira Savikas, carried a locket at all times, and held one of the two keys to the Hightower Library. He was killed after being awakened from a nap by Sylvira’s force light attack. His body was found with the locket missing.
source_quote: She had settled into Janussi's armchair for a nap, she said, 'only to be rudely awakened some thirty minutes later by our Sylvira Savikas, this is in the morning, blasting the armchamber with a lance of unerring force light.'

subject: Janussi
fact: Janussi was struck in the face, returned to his desk, wrote notes in blue ink, and was then killed. His nose was broken, his heart removed, and one sapphire and a locket taken from his neck. The gold was left behind.
source_quote: He'd been struck in the face, returned here, and written. Then he'd died.

subject: Janussi
fact: Janussi’s tongue and left forefinger were blackened with a substance darker than ink, and the same smudge was on his lower lip, indicating ingestion and deliberate contact with a poison.
source_quote: The tip of his left forefinger was blackened. Not blue. Darker than blue. And the same dark smudge sat dead-center on his lower lip.

subject: Janussi, Keeper of the Tome
fact: Janussi was murdered after being assaulted — his nose broken, tooth chipped, and heart torn out posthumously. He died while reading a poisoned spellbook, smudging his finger on blackened ink and wetting it with his lip. His left forefinger, lower lip, and tongue were stained with an unidentified black substance. A locket was torn from his neck. He was writing in blue ink moments before death, documenting unfamiliar spells in *The Discoveries*. The black substance was not ink, not poison he recognized, and defied identification even by an Underdark ooze.
source_quote: Body is dead. The stain was wrong. Darker than anything in his inkwell.

subject: Janussi, Keeper of the Tome
fact: Janussi, Keeper of the Tome, was killed after eating dinner with his face intact and teeth whole; his heart was torn out, ribcage smashed, nose broken, tongue and fingertip blackened, and a chip found in his front tooth — all indicating he was alive during initial trauma and later desecrated post-mortem.
source_quote: He had been dead before his chest was opened.

subject: Kalan
fact: Kalan is the gate warden and holds the second key to the Hightower Library. His possession of the key makes him a potential suspect or player in the theft of the book and the deletion of its contents.
source_quote: The other key, I learned, rested with Kalan, the gate warden.

subject: Kalan
fact: Kalan is the gate warden who holds the other key to the Hightower Library.
source_quote: The other key, I learned, rested with Kalan, the gate warden.

subject: Kalan
fact: Kalan is the gate warden who holds the second key to the Hightower Library. His possession of the key makes him a critical figure in the mystery, as the missing key from Janussi’s neck suggests a breach that may have involved him or someone who stole from him.

subject: Kalan Strongbranch
fact: Kalan Strongbranch is the gate warden who holds the second key to the Hightower Library; he was seen with a face like thunder on the morning of the murder, suggesting tension with Janussi.
source_quote: He had a face like thunder, nearly knocked the tray out of my hands.

subject: Kalan Strongbranch
fact: Kalan Strongbranch was seen by the apartment caretaker on the steps with a face like thunder, nearly knocking over the morning tea tray shortly before Janussi's death.
source_quote: He had a face like thunder, nearly knocked the tray out of my hands.

subject: Kalan Strongbranch
fact: Kalan Strongbranch, the gate warden, holds the second key to the Hightower Library and was seen with a face like thunder the morning of the murder.
source_quote: the other key is heralded by the gate warden, Kalan... He had a face like thunder, nearly knocked the tray out of my hands

subject: keeper's assistants count
fact: Grygum, Thorin, Zalthir, Daz, Tadric, and Milo are present as investigators.
source_quote: Grygum, Thorin, Zalthir, Daz, Tadric, and Milo

subject: Narrator
fact: The narrator despises the culture of Candlekeep, especially its scholars who harbor long-standing grudges.
source_quote: I despise this whole place a little — not Candlekeep, Candlekeep's fine, the books are fine — but the *culture* of it, the scholars who keep grudges the way a dragon keeps gold, sitting on them for years, polishing them.

subject: Narrator
fact: The narrator does not respond to Daz’s approval of Thorin’s thinking.
source_quote: I said nothing to that.

subject: Narrator
fact: The narrator recognizes rage that has had time to set as a vector that points somewhere.
source_quote: I've learned to read that. Rage that's had time to set is a vector. It points somewhere.

subject: Queenie
fact: Queenie assessed two-leggers: "I try to hold my breath whenever a two-legger passes. It's clear that you hardly ever lick yourselves at all. I've met cleaner dogs in my time."
source_quote: "How would I know? I try to hold my breath whenever a two-legger passes. It's clear that you hardly ever lick yourselves at all. I've met cleaner dogs in my time."

subject: Queenie
fact: Queenie believes good ticklers are the only good reason for disturbing her beauty sleep.
source_quote: Any good ticklers are the only good… and good ticklers are… tickles are only the good reason for disturbing my beauty sleep.

subject: Queenie
fact: Queenie believes the hypnotic block makes people sit there and not tickle.
source_quote: Every time they open that block," Queenie said, "they just sit there and don't tickle!

subject: Queenie
fact: Queenie believes the narrator should lick themselves properly before returning.
source_quote: please give yourself a proper licking before returning to my tower.

subject: Queenie
fact: Queenie categorizes people by gait and smell, not titles or politics.
source_quote: There is a precision to how cats categorize people that I find I respect. No titles. No politics. Just the relevant data: gait, smell.

subject: Queenie
fact: Queenie does not know what the locket was.
source_quote: I don't know what it was.

subject: Queenie
fact: Queenie ended the interaction by saying, "You may now leave, and please give yourself a proper licking before returning to my tower."
source_quote: "You may now leave," she said, "and please give yourself a proper licking before returning to my tower."

subject: Queenie
fact: Queenie finds two-leggers unclean and avoids them by holding her breath.
source_quote: I try to hold my breath whenever a two-legger passes. It's clear that you hardly ever lick yourselves at all.

subject: Queenie
fact: Queenie is a five-year-old sleet-grey cat who is entirely uninterested in being disturbed and announced, 'I did not order any more ticklers!'
source_quote: The cat introduced herself, after a fashion. Queenie — five years old, sleet-grey, and entirely uninterested in being disturbed. "I did not order any more ticklers!" she announced, stretching.

subject: Queenie
fact: Queenie is a five-year-old, sleet-grey cat who is entirely uninterested in being disturbed, and has settled into Janussi's armchair for a nap after being rudely awakened by Sylvira Savikas.
source_quote: I did not order any more ticklers!

subject: Queenie
fact: Queenie is a five-year-old, sleet-grey housecat who refuses to be disturbed, observes human behavior with precision, and communicates through cryptic declarations about tickles, beauty sleep, and the habits of two-leggers. She is a witness to key events and has settled into Janussi's armchair for naps. She claims to have seen Sylvira Savikas blast the armchamber with force light, Daral carry away a book that induces stillness, and a figure wearing Sylvira's shape but not her scent.
source_quote: I did not order any more ticklers! Any good ticklers are the only good… and good ticklers are… tickles are only the good reason for disturbing my beauty sleep.

subject: Queenie
fact: Queenie is done being generous after too many questions and too little tickling.
source_quote: There have been too little Tickles and too many questions.

subject: Queenie
fact: Queenie is entirely uninterested in being disturbed.
source_quote: Queenie — five years old, sleet-grey, and entirely uninterested in being disturbed.

subject: Queenie
fact: Queenie knows the locket was always on Janussi and never taken off.
source_quote: The locket itself is intimate. He carried it all the time. He never took it off.

subject: Queenie
fact: Queenie noticed the torn demon lady did not smell like Sylvira.
source_quote: But she didn't smell like the demon lady, though.

subject: Queenie
fact: Queenie said, "Every time they open that block," they just sit there and don't tickle! — revealing The Golden Ass as a book that immobilizes.
source_quote: "Every time they open that block," Queenie said, "they just sit there and don't tickle!"

subject: Queenie age
fact: Queenie is five years old.
source_quote: Queenie — five years old

subject: Sylvira
fact: Sylvira appeared as a torn demon lady descending the steps, but did not smell like the demon lady.
source_quote: She'd prowled the nighttime cycle and seen *the torn demon lady* coming down the steps — Sylvira's shape — "But she didn't smell like the demon lady, though."

subject: Sylvira Savikas
fact: Sylvira Savikas is a tiefling who blasted the armchamber with a lance of unerring force light, triggering a lover's quarrel with Janussi.
source_quote: Sylvira the tiefling, and Janussi, an on-and-off-again relationship. A lover's quarrel, then, opened with a flung working of force.

subject: Sylvira Savikas
fact: Sylvira Savikas is a tiefling with a volatile relationship to Janussi. She attacked him with force light during a lover’s quarrel. A figure wearing her shape but not her scent was seen later — suggesting she was impersonated or replaced by a shapeshifter.
source_quote: But she didn't smell like the demon lady, though.

subject: Sylvira Savikas
fact: Sylvira Savikas, Curator of the Infernal Fortress and a tiefling, had a violent confrontation with Janussi in the morning and was seen at night carrying a lantern she had no need for — suggesting she used it to obscure her natural darkvision while moving through the tower.
source_quote: She was carrying a lantern. She's a tiefling, and she can see in the dark without any light at all.

subject: Sylvira Savikas
fact: Sylvira Savikas, a tiefling Curator of the Infernal Fortress, screamed at Janussi calling him a traitor, was seen glowing red in candlelight at 2–3 a.m. carrying a lantern she had no use for, and had incurred his wrath that morning.
source_quote: Sylvira Savikas... gave me the heebie-jeebies... screamed that Janussi was a traitor... glowing red in the candlelight... carrying a lantern... she can see in the dark without any light at all

subject: Sylvira Savikas
fact: Sylvira Savikas, the Curator of the Infernal Fortress and a tiefling, was seen raging at Janussi, accusing him of being a traitor, and later seen carrying a lantern at 2–3 a.m. despite having darkvision — a contradiction that suggests the light was used to conceal her identity or actions.
source_quote: I swear I could see that devil woman's — Sylvira Savikas's — face glowing red in the candlelight... She was carrying a lantern. She's a tiefling, and she can see in the dark without any light at all.

subject: Tadric
fact: Tadric guarded the scene and reacted with suspicion when asked to shake the candle of the toppled statue, implying he knew something about its significance or had been involved in its placement.
source_quote: Tadric, who'd been hovering and guarding the scene, gave him a look.

subject: Tadric
fact: Tadric was the scene guardian, visibly unnerved by Thorin’s warnings about the statue. His reaction confirmed the statue’s appearance was unsettling enough to trigger fear — even though it was harmless — suggesting the figure’s design may have been intentionally intimidating, possibly linked to the order’s rituals.
source_quote: Are you sure this — is it true about candles?

subject: Teles Ahvoste
fact: Teles Ahvoste had a heated argument with Janussi during which he shouted 'hypocrite' before storming out, indicating deep personal animosity.
source_quote: I did hear Teles shout, *hypocrite*, at poor Janussi before he stormed out.

subject: Teles Ahvoste
fact: Teles Ahvoste shouted 'hypocrite' at Janussi during their meeting, ending in a shouting match.
source_quote: I did hear Teles shout, *hypocrite*, at poor Janussi before he stormed out

subject: Teles Ahvoste
fact: Teles Ahvoste shouted *hypocrite* at Janussi during a meeting around the ninth bell, after which she stormed out, despite claiming she wasn't listening.
source_quote: I did hear Teles shout, *hypocrite*, at poor Janussi before he stormed out.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin believes the gift tag supports his theory about a rival giving Janussi a bitter gift.
source_quote: Okay, so that supports my theory. Some sort of rival gave him a gift, but it was sort of like a bitter thing.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin connected the gift tag to the rivalry theory and identified the black residue as inconsistent with the blue ink, reinforcing the poison hypothesis.
source_quote: Okay, so that supports my theory. Some sort of rival gave him a gift, but it was sort of like a bitter thing... Black. Definitively not the blue ink

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin contributed observational details — noting the chipped tooth’s location, questioning the statue’s potential animation, and pointing out the force darts missed the victim. His skepticism about magical hazards revealed his experience with cursed objects, and his comment on eye-for-detail humorously underscored the team’s forensic intensity.
source_quote: I don't want it to wake up and attack us. I've had bad experiences.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin is a reserved investigator who declines tea, speaks minimally, and ends conversations with blunt phrases like 'Nothing more,' which unintentionally trigger new revelations.
source_quote: Nothing more," Thorin said... "No thank you, I'm good.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin is deeply suspicious of Candlekeep's scholarly culture, which he sees as hypocritical and grudge-obsessed, contrasting it with the honest violence of the Underdark. He recognizes Daral Yashenti as a calculated enemy with a long-standing grudge against Janussi, and views this as a vector of danger.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin is methodical, notices when descriptions are doing unacknowledged work, and presses witnesses with precise questions. He connects the dots between force bolts, the missing book, and the shapeshifter. He confirms the timeline: the victim was alive when Daral left. He identifies the shapeshifter situation and links it to the candle.
source_quote: That explains the candle.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin is the theorist who connects the dots between the missing book, the cipher, the poison, and the rival’s motives — he believes the comedy book is the key to a replacement cipher and is the driving force behind the investigation’s direction.
source_quote: There's something written in the book that wasn't part of the original book — or maybe he's using the book and the notes to do some sort of cipher.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin muttered that he had the second-worst eye for detail in the room.
source_quote: Thorin muttered something about having the second-worst eye for detail in the room.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin noted that the victim was still alive when Daral left, and the timeline held.
source_quote: "But the victim was still alive when Daral left," Thorin noted, and the timeline held. Yes. Daral exited with the book, and the dead man was not yet dead.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin observed and verbalized key physical evidence: the darts missed the body, the chain links were broken, and the tooth chip was recent — helping establish sequence and intent.
source_quote: those darts never miss their mark, and the man bore no such marks.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin questioned the candle on the statue out of fear of magical awakening, revealing his past trauma and causing Tadric to panic.
source_quote: Are you sure this — is it true about candles?

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin theorized that a rival had given Janussi a bitter gift, evidenced by the gift tag written in a cramped, resentful hand, and that the black residue on Janussi's mouth was unrelated to blue ink.
source_quote: Okay, so that supports my theory. Some sort of rival gave him a gift, but it was sort of like a bitter thing.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin was suspicious that the candle on the statue might be magical and could wake the statue.
source_quote: I don't want it to wake up and attack us... When there's magic with the statue, who knows what's going on with the candle.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin wonders if the missing comedy book might be part of a cipher or replacement code.
source_quote: Am I reaching too deep here?

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir assisted in the investigation with instinctual deductions, questioning the nature of injuries and magical possibilities, and noted the inconsistency of a robbery that left behind immense wealth.
source_quote: In other words, score what they left them.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir focused on the ink, parchment, and magical context — isolating the final writing in *The Discoveries*, recognizing the use of tobacco to mask poison, and identifying the locket’s symbolic value. He proposed the black substance might be poison and connected Glabbagool’s failure to its extraplanar nature. He questioned the chair darts and the statue’s fall, pushing the team toward psychological and ritualistic motives.
source_quote: Wasn't the blue ink — the ink they used in the books? It was. Janussi had been taking notes when this happened.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir identified the sequence of ink usage, confirming that Janussi’s final act was writing in *The Discoveries*, and noted the literary homage in the notes.
source_quote: The blue ink on *The Discoveries* had been laid down after the blue ink on another book. *The Golden Ass.* 'So that's the last thing he was writing?' Confirmation.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir is a thoughtful investigator who listens closely, asks clarifying questions, and recognizes implications — such as the significance of the lantern — and accepts tea with unusual enthusiasm, possibly to disarm or gain rapport.
source_quote: That explains the candle," said Zalthir... "Yes, I love… Absolutely!

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir is rarely surprised, keeps a private tally of rare moments of astonishment, and is fascinated by the idea of talking to cats. He makes intuitive leaps that sometimes misfire but arrive at correct conclusions — such as equating a book with a TV. He is engaged in the investigation and prompts Queenie for details, especially about the candle and the shapeshifter.
source_quote: Oh, it's a TV!

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir is the empathetic interlocutor who draws out witnesses through compassion and permission — he helps Hollypocket feel safe enough to reveal the glowing face and the lantern, crucial clues others might have missed.
source_quote: I mustn't, but for the investigation.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir respected Janussi’s practice of carefully cataloging unfamiliar spells.
source_quote: Musings on unfamiliar spells. Notes on how they might be cast — a wizard cataloguing things he'd seen others do and never managed himself. The sort of thing a careful man writes when he is trying to understand something larger than he is. I have a passing respect for that.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir said, "Oh, it's a TV!" — not quite the deduction but arrived at the same destination.
source_quote: "Oh, it's a TV!" said Zalthir, which was not quite the deduction but arrived at the same destination.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir was the one who noted the significance of Sylvira’s lantern and the connection between the candlelight and the poison’s concealment.
source_quote: That explains the candle.

subject: armchair
fact: The armchair had three circular impacts and two holes punched clean through the back, consistent with darts of pure force, but no matching wounds on the body.
source_quote: Three circular impacts, horsehair stuffing scattered, two holes punched clean through the chair back. Darts of pure force.

subject: blackened fingertip
fact: The blackened fingertip and lip were not from ink, but from a substance that mimicked ink but was darker, more dangerous, and likely sentient — a reading poison.
source_quote: That was the entire point of the long look — not that the finger was stained, but that the stain was *wrong*.

subject: black residue
fact: Black residue was found on Janussi’s fingers and mouth, definitively not blue ink, and likely from poison or another substance deliberately concealed.
source_quote: Black. Definitively not the blue ink — Grygum had already settled that, checked it twice and certain.

subject: Black Residue
fact: Black residue was found on Janussi’s mouth and pages — not from the blue ink — and may be a byproduct of poison, a ritual substance, or the result of a spell cast at the moment of death.
source_quote: The black on the pages of a book that was no longer in the room.

subject: black substance
fact: A mysterious black substance, darker than ink, was found on Janussi’s left forefinger, lower lip, and tongue — confirmed not to be ink or any known material, and resistant to identification even by Glabbagool, an ooze that has consumed the Underdark’s poisons and gloop.
source_quote: The skill wasn't in identifying the substance. It was in knowing, with certainty, what it was not.

subject: black substance
fact: The black substance on Janussi’s finger, lip, and tongue was not ink, not poison that Glabbagool recognized, and was deliberately used to contaminate the reader — implying it was sentient or magical.
source_quote: The skill wasn't in identifying the substance. It was in knowing, with certainty, what it was *not*.

subject: Black Substance (on finger, lip, tongue)
fact: A dark, non-ink, non-standard poison stained Janussi’s left forefinger, lower lip, and tongue. It was not identifiable by Glabbagool — an ooze that has consumed the Underdark’s poisons — indicating its origin is arcane, extraplanar, or uniquely engineered. It was absorbed through skin contact and ingestion while reading a poisoned page, suggesting the spellbook itself was the vector.
source_quote: That was the entire point of the long look — not that the finger was stained, but that the stain was *wrong*.

subject: blue ink
fact: Blue ink on *The Discoveries* was fresher than on *The Golden Ass*, indicating Janussi was actively researching unfamiliar spells at the time of death.
source_quote: There was more than one color on those pages, and I wanted the newest one isolated before anything else.

subject: Blue Ink
fact: Blue ink was used by Janussi to write jokes and spell notes in the comedy book; it was distinct from the black residue found on his mouth, indicating multiple substances were involved in his final hours.
source_quote: The blue ink captures both notes on obscure spells and jokes?

subject: cherry tobacco value
fact: Cherry tobacco is present but has no stated value.
source_quote: cherry tobacco

subject: chip in front tooth
fact: A fresh, jagged chip in Janussi’s front tooth was found on the floor beside his body, indicating he fell face-first before death — a trauma unrelated to the post-mortem desecration but critical to establishing the timeline of events.
source_quote: He had fallen forward. Face-first. Chipped the tooth on the way down.

subject: chipped tooth
fact: The chipped front tooth was jagged and recent, caused by Janussi falling face-first onto stone after being poisoned, not by violence.
source_quote: He had fallen forward. Face-first. Chipped the tooth on the way down.

subject: comedy book cipher
fact: The comedy book, *The Golden Ass*, may be a cipher key — something written in it was not part of the original text.
source_quote: There's something written in the book that wasn't part of the original book — or maybe he's using the book and the notes to do some sort of cipher.

subject: ebony pipe value
fact: The ebony pipe is finely carved but has no stated value.
source_quote: an ebony pipe finely carved

subject: Force Darts (in armchair)
fact: Three puncture wounds in the armchair, with horsehair stuffing scattered and two holes punched through the back, indicate the use of magical force darts. The darts missed Janussi entirely — suggesting the attacker was enraged, but not at him. The darts were aimed at the chair, possibly in frustration, as a failed attempt to trigger a trap, or as a signal to another party.
source_quote: Somebody had been furious. But not at the keeper — those darts never miss their mark, and the man bore no such marks.

subject: gift tag
fact: A gift tag in a cramped, resentful hand was found in the wastebasket, addressed to Janussi: 'To Janussi, read it and weep, you old snob, a proper Dead Winter gift, your loving rival.'
source_quote: *To Janussi, read it and weep, you old snob, a proper Dead Winter gift, your loving rival.*

subject: gift tag to Janussi
fact: A gift tag addressed to Janussi reads: 'To Janussi, read it and weep, you old snob, a proper Dead Winter gift, your loving rival.'
source_quote: To Janussi, read it and weep, you old snob, a proper Dead Winter gift, your loving rival.

subject: Great Reader A'lai Aivenmore
fact: A three-foot marble statue of the Great Reader A'lai Aivenmore, holding a candle aloft, had been knocked over — not by magic, but by shock when the body was discovered.
source_quote: The statue had simply fallen... A scholar discovers a murdered keeper with his heart cut out and reaches blindly for the wall and the wall is a statue.

subject: Hightower Library key (Janussi's)
fact: One of two keys to the Hightower Library, previously worn by Janussi, is now missing. Its disappearance, alongside the locket, indicates a targeted theft and possible unauthorized access to restricted materials.

subject: Hightower Library key (Kalan's)
fact: The second key to the Hightower Library is held by Kalan, the gate warden. Its existence creates a binary access system — if one key is stolen, the other may be used to bypass security, or it may be the only remaining legitimate means of entry.

subject: Hightower Library Keys
fact: Two keys exist: one held by Janussi, the other by Kalan, the gate warden. Access to the library’s restricted materials requires both. Janussi’s key was used to access the book that was later deleted, suggesting internal betrayal.
source_quote: Janussi held one of the two keys to the Hightower Library. The other key, I learned, rested with Kalan, the gate warden.

subject: ink color count

subject: The Broken Lead Chain Links

subject: The Candle Statue
fact: A three-foot marble statue of a hooded bearded elder holding a candle aloft, toppled near the tea table. When shaken, it may have concealed something — Tadric’s reaction suggests it was not merely decorative.

subject: the comedy book
fact: The comedy book — *The Golden Ass* — was annotated with jokes and obscure spell notes in the same hand and fresh ink, then vanished from the room, leaving only its absence as proof it had been there.
source_quote: *The Golden Ass* was a comedy... writing down jokes he found funny... blue ink captures both notes on obscure spells and jokes?... the same hand, the same fresh ink... the comedy book had walked out of the room... you do not annotate a thing you do not hold

subject: The Dart-Struck Armchair
fact: An armchair with three circular punctures and horsehair stuffing scattered, two holes punched clean through the back. The darts were not aimed at Grygum — their target was the chair, indicating rage or ritual intent unrelated to the victim.
source_quote: darts of pure force... somebody had aimed three bolts of force at a chair.

subject: The Discoveries
fact: *The Discoveries* was a spellbook containing fresh blue ink annotations of obscure spells and their potential castings, the final written work under Janussi’s hand.
source_quote: The spell research was the final thing under his hand.

subject: *The Discoveries*
fact: *The Discoveries* was the last book Janussi was writing in, with fresh blue ink noting unfamiliar spells and their potential casting methods.
source_quote: The blue ink on *The Discoveries* had been laid down after the blue ink on another book. *The Golden Ass.* 'So that's the last thing he was writing?' Confirmation.

subject: The Discoveries (spellbook)
fact: This spellbook, open on the desk, contained the last writings of Janussi — blue ink notes on unfamiliar spells he observed but could not cast. The ink was fresher than that in *The Golden Ass*, confirming this was his final act before death. The content revealed a scholar actively expanding his knowledge, not preparing for defense or escape.
source_quote: The blue ink on *The Discoveries* had been laid down after the blue ink on another book. *The Golden Ass.*

subject: The Ebony Pipe
fact: An intricately carved ebony pipe filled with cherry tobacco, likely used to mask the scent of poison in the room, indicating premeditation and knowledge of the method of murder.
source_quote: tobacco smoke would hide the smell of poison. Of course it would.

subject: the gift tag
fact: The gift tag read: 'To Janussi, read it and weep, you old snob, a proper Dead Winter gift, your loving rival.' Written in a cramped, sour hand, by someone who resented the act of writing it.
source_quote: 'To Janussi, read it and weep, you old snob, a proper Dead Winter gift, your loving rival.'... cramped, sour hand... script of someone who resented the act of writing it

subject: The Golden Ass
fact: *The Golden Ass* was a comedic text annotated by Janussi with jokes he found funny, written in the same blue ink as his spell notes, but with dried ink on the joke passages.
source_quote: Janussi had been writing down jokes he found funny — the man had a sense of humor he'd evidently kept private.

subject: The Golden Ass
fact: A physical book, dull and unremarkable, capable of rendering a person motionless and uninterested — referred to by Queenie as a 'hypnotic block.' It was carried away by Daral and is linked to the deletion of content from the restricted Hightower Library book.
source_quote: Every time they open that block," Queenie said, "they just sit there and don't tickle!

subject: The Golden Ass
fact: The Golden Ass is a book, dull enough to hold a person motionless and uninterested in scratching a cat, taken by Daral.
source_quote: "The Golden Ass", the missing volume, walking out of the room under Daral's arm.

subject: The Golden Ass
fact: The Golden Ass is a dull, mundane book that can hold a person motionless and uninterested in scratching — the missing volume taken by Daral, and the object that, when opened, prevented tickling.
source_quote: Every time they open that block, they just sit there and don't tickle!

subject: the lantern
fact: Sylvira Savikas was seen carrying a lantern at 2–3 a.m. despite being a tiefling with innate darkvision — the light was unnecessary for her vision, suggesting it was used to illuminate something else, or to mask her presence.
source_quote: She was carrying a lantern. She's a tiefling, and she can see in the dark without any light at all.

subject: the locket
fact: The locket was missing from Janussi’s neck — he carried it always, never took it off, and it was the only thing gone from the room.
source_quote: The locket was missing. Off Janussi's neck. And that knocked something loose in his memory... Janussi carried it always, never took it off

subject: The Missing Sapphire
fact: One sapphire was missing from the safe’s five pouches, and one parchment naming a sapphire-dependent spell was gone — suggesting the killer sought to complete a single, specific spell requiring that component.
source_quote: one sapphire was missing. One parchment. 'Somebody is trying to build a sapphire spell,' he said, 'a spell that requires a sapphire.'

subject: The Silver Pedestal
fact: A polished silver pedestal by the desk, possibly used to display a sacred or magical item now missing — its presence suggests ritual significance in Grygum’s practice.
source_quote: A silver pedestal by the desk, an ebony pipe finely carved, cherry tobacco.

subject: tobacco smoke
fact: Janussi habitually filled his chamber with tobacco smoke to medicate his failing lungs, and this smoke was used to mask the smell of poison administered to him.
source_quote: You don't fill a room with smoke to kill a man — you fill a room with smoke to keep him from smelling what's already there.

subject: Cipher in the Book
fact: The comedy book may contain a cipher — using jokes as a key to decode hidden arcane knowledge — and its removal implies the killer sought to erase or claim that knowledge.
source_quote: There's something written in the book that wasn't part of the original book — or maybe he's using the book and the notes to do some sort of cipher.

subject: cipher in the book
fact: There is speculation that the missing book contains a cipher — specifically a replacement cipher — designed to conceal information. The book may have been used to encode or decode sensitive material, and its absence is critical to solving the mystery.

subject: Daral's double confrontation
fact: Daral Yashenti confronted Janussi twice in one day — once verbally during a meeting, and again in a drunken argument at the door — followed by Janussi fleeing from him for the first time ever, making him a prime suspect.
source_quote: I'd never seen him run away so fast.

subject: Daral's motive
fact: Daral’s theft of *The Golden Ass* may have been for suppression — the book’s effect suggests it contains dangerous or forbidden knowledge.
source_quote: Every time they open that block, they just sit there and don't tickle!

subject: Daz's indifference
fact: Daz paid no attention to the grieving caretaker while she wept, only suddenly listening when the lantern detail was revealed — indicating his focus is on evidence, not emotion, and possibly hiding prior knowledge.
source_quote: Daz, I noticed, was paying the weeping woman no attention whatsoever... Hmm," said Daz, suddenly listening after all.

subject: hypnotic block
fact: The phrase 'hypnotic block' was a misdescription by Queenie for *The Golden Ass* — a clue that the witness didn't understand the true nature of the object.
source_quote: when I later saw him run downstairs with a hypnotic block

subject: identity of the rival
fact: The gift tag suggests a bitter rival gave Janussi a poisoned gift, but the rival's identity and motive remain unknown.
source_quote: Some sort of rival gave him a gift, but it was sort of like a bitter thing.

subject: intent of the gift
fact: The 'Dead Winter gift' was likely a trap or poison delivery mechanism, but its intended function and the rival’s full plan remain unknown.
source_quote: a proper Dead Winter gift, your loving rival.

subject: missing book
fact: A book that was once in the room is now gone. It is suspected to have contained encrypted or altered content — possibly a cipher or replacement code — and may be the key to understanding what was deleted from the library records.

subject: missing book
fact: The disappearance of *The Golden Ass* is the central absence — the only item removed from the room despite clear evidence of its prior presence and annotation.
source_quote: A room tells you most by what it is missing.

subject: Missing Comedy Book
fact: The comedy book containing Janussi’s private annotations — jokes in blue ink, spell notes, and possibly a cipher — vanished from the room, and its absence suggests it was the key to a hidden message or the motive for murder.
source_quote: The comedy book had walked out of the room.

subject: Missing Locket
fact: Janussi’s locket — always worn, never removed — was taken from his neck after death, and since he held one of two keys to the Hightower Library, its removal implies the locket contained or was the key itself.
source_quote: Janussi held one of the two keys of the Hightower Library.

subject: missing locket
fact: The locket’s contents or purpose are unknown — its removal or replication may be tied to the book’s deletion or the shapeshifter’s presence.
source_quote: He carried it all the time. He never took it off.

subject: origin of the black substance
fact: The black substance on Janussi’s body resists identification even by Glabbagool — implying it is either an unknown poison, a magical residue, or a substance native to a realm beyond the Underdark — and its presence on the lip and finger suggests it was ingested or applied as part of a ritual or curse.
source_quote: When even a creature that has eaten the Underdark can't place a poison, you've learned the poison is worth being afraid of.

subject: Poison and Smoke
fact: The tobacco smoke in Janussi’s chamber was used not to medicate, but to mask the smell of poison — suggesting the murder was deliberate, concealed, and involved a substance that left no visible trace.
source_quote: The one thing that tobacco smoke would do is hide the smell of poison.

subject: poison source
fact: The black residue indicates poison was used, but its origin, delivery method, and the identity of the poisoner are unresolved.
source_quote: The one thing that tobacco smoke would do is hide the smell of poison.

subject: purpose of the finger-to-lip gesture
fact: The pattern of black substance on finger and lip mirrors the habitual gesture of a reader wetting their fingertip to turn pages — implying the victim was reading or writing when attacked, and the assailant may have used this gesture to apply the poison as part of a cursed text or sentient ink.
source_quote: Turning pages, wetting the fingertip the way readers do without thinking, a hundred times an hour, never once considering that the page might be the thing reading them.

subject: shapeshifter identity
fact: The imposter wearing Sylvira's form remains unidentified — the scent mismatch suggests a deliberate deception, possibly linked to the book's deletion or the locket's theft.
source_quote: But she didn't smell like the demon lady, though.

subject: Sylvira's attack
fact: Sylvira’s lance of force may have been a distraction or a cover for someone else accessing the book or locket — the timing and motive remain unclear.

subject: Sylvira Savikas’s midnight lantern
fact: Sylvira Savikas carried a lantern she did not need, suggesting she was hiding her presence — but her motive remains unclear.
source_quote: But what was really odd was not that Sylvira was there in the middle of the night — I've seen her in the middle of the night before — but that she was carrying a lantern. She's a tiefling, and she can see in the dark without any light at all.

subject: Sylvira's midnight presence
fact: Sylvira Savikas was seen glowing red in candlelight at 2–3 a.m. — an impossible sighting given her darkvision — raising the question of why she was in the tower, why she carried a lantern, and whether she was the last person to see Janussi alive.
source_quote: I swear I could see that devil woman's face glowing red in the candlelight... She was carrying a lantern.

subject: the candle’s significance
fact: Zalthir connects the candle to the shapeshifter, suggesting it may be a magical tool, a focus, or a decoy. Its exact role in the deception is unconfirmed, but its mention by Zalthir implies it was present during the impersonation.
source_quote: That explains the candle.

subject: The Candle Statue’s Secret
fact: The toppled statue of the candle-holding elder may conceal something — its shaking was met with suspicion. It may hold the key to the killer’s identity, the spell’s origin, or the locket’s destination.

subject: the cat's final dismissal

source_quote: You may now leave

subject: The Cat’s Testimony

source_quote: The animal had been in the chamber; the dead don't volunteer alibis, but a five-year-old housecat with opinions might.

subject: The Dart Attack on the Chair
fact: Three force darts struck the armchair — not the man. The reason remains unknown: was it a ritual, a warning, or an attempt to destroy something hidden in the chair?
source_quote: Why would you loose three darts of force at a chair?

subject: the deletion’s purpose
fact: Why was content deleted from the Hightower Library book? Was it to erase evidence of the keys’ use, the shapeshifter’s identity, or the book’s true nature? The connection to 'The Golden Ass' suggests the deletion was enabled by the book’s stillness-inducing property.
source_quote: That might explain why that stuff got deleted off that book that no one should have touched.

subject: The Identity of the Gift-Giver
fact: The gift tag found in the wastebasket — addressed to Janussi in a 'cramped, sour hand' — was signed by a 'loving rival,' suggesting the giver was someone who knew him intimately and resented him — possibly Daral or Sylvira.
source_quote: *To Janussi, read it and weep, you old snob, a proper Dead Winter gift, your loving rival.*

subject: The Identity of the Killer
fact: The killer had access to the safe, knew of the sapphire spell, carried no greed, and used ritualistic methods — likely someone from within the Keeper’s Order, or an acolyte seeking forbidden knowledge.
source_quote: This was a man who needed exactly one thing.

subject: The Identity of the Killer
fact: The killer had no need to force entry, knew the safe’s combination, moved with deliberate calm, and targeted only what would silence Janussi and empower a specific ritual. The broken nose occurred before death — suggesting a prior confrontation. The locket and sapphire were personal and magical targets. The black poison defied identification, indicating the killer has access to obscure, likely forbidden, arcane knowledge — possibly from within Candlekeep’s restricted archives.
source_quote: Who had been certain enough to want him silent on both sides of death.

subject: The identity of the killer
fact: The person who broke Janussi’s nose and took his heart and one sapphire remains unidentified.
source_quote: who had been certain enough to want him silent on both sides of death.

subject: the licking observation

subject: The locket
fact: The locket or necklace taken from Janussi’s neck is unidentifiable and its significance is unknown.

subject: The locket

subject: The missing comedy book
fact: The missing comedy book may contain a cipher or hidden code, but its contents and purpose remain unknown.

subject: The Missing Locket
fact: The locket or necklace torn from Grygum’s neck is unaccounted for — its contents, symbolism, or magical properties may be the true target of the murder, not the sapphire.
source_quote: Whatever it was, he'd carried it a long time.

subject: The missing sapphire and parchment
fact: The specific spell requiring the missing sapphire and parchment is unknown.
source_quote: one sapphire was missing. One parchment. "somebody is trying to build a sapphire spell"

subject: The Missing Sapphire Spell
fact: One sapphire and one parchment were taken from the safe — both required for a single, high-level spell. The remaining four sapphires and other valuables were untouched. The killer’s goal was not theft, but acquisition of a specific magical component. The parchment likely contained the incantation for a sapphire-dependent spell — possibly one that binds, silences, or resurrects the dead — aligning with the heart’s removal and the black poison’s purpose.
source_quote: Someone is trying to build a sapphire spell... and left the gold.

subject: the nature of the thud
fact: The thud heard at midnight may not have been accidental — the caretaker's realization that the sound was distinct, and the timing after Sylvira’s sighting, suggests it may have been a physical attack.
source_quote: The three of us closer to her did what we could to settle her... I wrote it down slowly. That one mattered.

subject: The Rivalry Between Janussi and Daral
fact: The rivalry between Janussi and Daral Yashenti was not mere professional jealousy — it was a decades-long, deeply personal feud that culminated in Daral’s drunken second confrontation and flight, making him the most emotionally volatile suspect.
source_quote: Those two have been at each other's throats for years.

subject: The second key to the Hightower Library
fact: The second key to the Hightower Library is held by the gate warden Kalan, but its connection to the murder is unconfirmed.
source_quote: that the other key is heralded by the gate warden, Kalan.

subject: the shapeshifter’s identity
fact: A figure wearing Sylvira Savikas’s form but lacking her scent is active. The true identity of this shapeshifter remains unknown. The candle mentioned by Zalthir may be a clue to their method or origin.

subject: the two-leggers’ hygiene
fact: Queenie’s final assessment — that two-leggers rarely lick themselves — is an insult that doubles as a narrative clue. It may imply the killer is not human, or that hygiene is a marker of identity in this world.
source_quote: It's clear that you hardly ever lick yourselves at all. I've met cleaner dogs in my time.

subject: timing of the nose fracture
fact: The broken nose occurred before death, as bruising requires living tissue — placing the initial assault within the narrow window between Janussi’s last meal and his death, and suggesting the attacker was present during a private moment.
source_quote: Bruising doesn't form on a corpse; there's no living tissue to swell.

subject: writer of the blue ink
fact: It is confirmed that Janussi wrote both the jokes and spell notes in blue ink, but the abrupt transition between registers and the timing of his death remain unexplained.

subject: Before Nine in the Morning

source_quote: I also want to understand where Bookwyrm was before nine in the morning.

subject: Day I Was Sleeping
fact: The day the player missed the silent communication lesson is one among many days they were sleeping — a recurring pattern that symbolizes avoidance, distraction, or disengagement from deeper truths. Glabbagool’s mastery contrasts sharply with this neglect.
source_quote: There are, by now, a great many days I was sleeping. 'Was I ever there?'

subject: day of the murder

subject: December 31st, 1999

subject: eight o'clock
fact: Eight o’clock is a critical temporal anchor — marking Grygum’s meeting with Janussi and the initial inspection on the day of the murder.

subject: elapsed time
fact: An hour passes between two events in the session.
source_quote: An hour later

subject: Midnight of Death
fact: The victim died at midnight — a precise temporal anchor that became the critical clue linking the poison’s delayed effect to the timing of the murder.
source_quote: He died at roughly midnight.

subject: midnight of the murder
fact: The murder occurred precisely at midnight, matching the delayed effect of midnight tears poison, and is the temporal anchor for all forensic reconstruction.
source_quote: The creature that ingests this poison suffers no effect until the stroke of midnight. He died at roughly midnight.

subject: night of the murder
fact: The murder occurred on the night of the event, with Janussi consuming the poison during the day and dying precisely at midnight; the impersonation of Sylvira Savikas occurred that same night; Kalan’s last verified sighting of Janussi was at the eight o’clock meeting, and his body was discovered shortly after midnight.
source_quote: Kalan said: 'The morning of the murder: the inspection just after eight, the cordon, the posted watcher.'

subject: poisoning time
fact: The poison was transferred by licking a finger and turning pages, implicating the book.
source_quote: the poison carried on a book, transferred by a man licking his finger and turning the pages

subject: quarter-past-ten
fact: Quarter-past-ten is the time Grygum claims to have met Sylvira Savikas — later revealed to be a deception.
source_quote: The quarter-past-ten visit to Sylvira Savikas...

subject: quarter-past-ten visit to Sylvira Savikas
fact: Kalan claimed to have visited Sylvira Savikas at quarter-past-ten on the night of the murder, but this alibi was compromised by the revelation that Sylvira had been impersonated; this time stamp is now a critical point of investigation, as the real Sylvira may have been elsewhere, or the impersonator was active during this window.
source_quote: Kalan said: 'The quarter-past-ten visit to Sylvira Savikas over some cosmological question.'

subject: session date
fact: The events described occurred during the investigation phase following the Candlekeep Murders, after the dispersal of the Council of the Great Readers and before the final episode of the investigators' work.
source_quote: we're down to the last episode, and we're saving it.

subject: session date
fact: The session occurs on the 11th hour of the day, Janussi the philistine’s meeting.

subject: session date
