fact: I did not correct Zalthir when he suggested Daz might extort Daral, because I agreed with his assessment.
source_quote: I did not correct him. The read was not wrong.

subject: I
fact: I remembered the giants' lesson that you don't chase, you position, and let the ground guide your actions.
source_quote: The giants taught me that before I could carry a shield — you don't chase, you position, and the ground under your feet says what your mouth doesn't need to.

subject: I
fact: I thought the interaction between Dawnbringer and Daral was a small good thing in a room full of guards.
source_quote: I thought, *there it is, a small good thing in a room full of guards.*

subject: I
fact: I understood that helmed horrors were chosen as assassins because they cannot talk, revealing the enemy’s intent to leave no one to interrogate.
source_quote: Of course. A killer with no mouth and no mind — whoever built these chose them precisely so there'd be nobody to squeeze afterward.

subject: I
fact: I wanted to know who sent the helmed horrors and considered using a dead horror as a divining rod to detect who else had the key.
source_quote: Can we grab one of them and use it to detect who else has the key? Turn it into a sort of divining rod, as it were.

subject: Janussi
fact: Janussi is the deceased scholar whose research proposal was declined, and whose death created the opportunity for Kalan to apply his unapproved academic standard to a real case.
source_quote: And the person who declined it is dead.

subject: Kalan
fact: Kalan initially doubted the feasibility of spell-based evidence but shifted to endorse Thorin’s plan, recognizing that accessing a book from the new head of Candlekeep — not the old — would be the true instrument of accountability.

subject: Kalan Strongbranch
fact: Kalan Strongbranch believed patience was the clever play.
source_quote: *Sometimes the clever play is to be patient.*

subject: Kalan Strongbranch
fact: Kalan Strongbranch intended to find a book that could prove Bookwyrm's culpability after the naming ceremony.
source_quote: I will come up with such a book before you leave.

subject: Kalan Strongbranch
fact: Kalan Strongbranch is a scholar who wrote a paper on the standard that requires three different kinds of evidence to establish truth, and he refuses to cast the Zone of Truth spell without consent because he fears losing his position if Bookwyrm becomes his boss.
source_quote: I will not sneak this time. We will walk in, and we will boldly demand that she submit to a Zone of Truth.

subject: Kalan Strongbranch
fact: Kalan Strongbranch is in charge of guarding the safe, full of himself and his methodology, and has been reassigned to escort prisoners to Deneir's Sanctum.
source_quote: I will ask him to escort you to Deneir's Sanctum, where you will wait until later this evening, then be escorted to your chambers.

subject: Kalan Strongbranch
fact: Kalan Strongbranch is orchestrating a patient, politically subtle campaign to remove Bookwyrm from power by leveraging institutional procedures and Avowed voting dynamics, avoiding direct confrontation to preserve his own standing and reputation; he claims moral high ground but is motivated by self-preservation and fear of her potential future authority.
source_quote: He's not going to do it without her permission — how about I put it that way? ... He said his own name as he said it, the way a man does when he's decided to be honest about his cowardice and dress it as principle.

subject: Kalan Strongbranch
fact: Kalan Strongbranch is referenced by Zalthir as the one who was reinstated as head of the Avowed, obsessed with procedure, and whose methodology was declared proven despite lacking evidence.
source_quote: Kalan Strongbranch fussing at the front, in charge of something at last and determined to make it last a week. ... 'I think it was unwise of me not to keep you in charge.'

subject: Kalan Strongbranch
fact: Kalan Strongbranch refused to sneak or cast Zone of Truth without Bookwyrm's permission.
source_quote: I will not sneak this time. We will walk in, and we will boldly demand that she submit to a Zone of Truth.

subject: Kalan Strongbranch
fact: Kalan Strongbranch was afraid of making Bookwyrm his boss if he acted aggressively.
source_quote: He's not going to do it without her permission — how about I put it that way?

subject: Kalan Strongbranch
fact: Kalan Strongbranch was fired from his position after failing to solve the case involving Janussi’s death, but now holds a strategic plan to expose Bookwyrm through patience and institutional politics rather than direct confrontation.
source_quote: I will not sneak this time. We will walk in, and we will boldly demand that she submit to a Zone of Truth.

subject: Kalan Strongbranch
fact: Kalan Strongbranch was fired from his position and handed the case that Alkrist solved, though he was unable to crack it himself.
source_quote: Kalan had gotten fired. That's the terrain — a man told he was done, standing next to a case he couldn't crack, that we cracked for him.

subject: Kalan Strongbranch
fact: Kalan Strongbranch was pleased to have a research problem to solve.
source_quote: Kalan paused, and thought, and looked genuinely pleased to have a problem he could research.

subject: Kalan Strongbranch
fact: Kalan has been reinstated to his former position and is now in charge of the investigation; he promised to ensure the adventurers' voices would be heard in his report.
source_quote: He promised our voices would be heard.

subject: Kalan Strongbranch
fact: Kalan is a rigid proceduralist who thrives on authority and structure. He is easily manipulated into taking credit for outcomes he did not engineer, and his eagerness to enforce order makes him a useful pawn for Bookwyrm’s schemes.
source_quote: He accepted, graciously. 'But this will not change the nature of my report tomorrow.'

subject: The Woman (Unnamed)
fact: The woman is relieved, not sad, about Janussi's death; she has decided she has already won and is strategically relaxed, using apparent outrage to deflect suspicion.
source_quote: She was not sad. She was relieved. Her hands were too relaxed.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin accepted that Dawnbringer was female.
source_quote: Whatever — she. Yeah, I think we said she.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin approves of the grift and says "Never miss an opportunity to grift, man."
source_quote: "Never miss an opportunity to grift, man," Thorin said.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin believed handing the case to Kalan was simple and clean.
source_quote: Simple. Clean. For once a faction problem had an answer I could say out loud without wanting to walk into a wall.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin believed using the reward to get a book after the fact was better than acting upfront.
source_quote: So you wish to cast another spell on her?... I'm just thinking — the reversal here is: we go in, we say here are the people that did it, we get a reward, and one of us uses that reward to get the book that can then prove she did it.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin believes Daral should be let go and does not think extorting him would be nice.
source_quote: I don't think he had anything to do with it... I think we probably just let him… let him go." and "Yeah — we could extort him, but I don't think that would be nice.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin believes helmed horrors were chosen as assassins precisely because they cannot speak, ensuring no interrogation is possible after the fact.
source_quote: The reason you picked helmed horrors as assassins is they can't talk. Literally.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin believes the plan is high drama and a good closing.
source_quote: High drama," Thorin said, and I could hear him building the stage in his head. "It'd be a good closing — she thought she got away with it, and then: one more thing.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin decided to hand the confession to Kalan to let him save face.
source_quote: Alright," I said. "I think we just hand it to him — let him save face, since he got fired — with the understanding that they make good on the promise: we get our reward for helping crack the case."

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin didn't know whether Dawnbringer was male or female.
source_quote: I don't know, I can't remember.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin fondly acknowledges that Dawnbringer enjoys being called beautiful and worthy of study.
source_quote: Dawnbringer eats it up, I'm sure," Thorin said, fond.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin is a dramatic storyteller who constructs elaborate narratives around events, treating real life as theater. He pushes for bold, theatrical reveals and is unapologetic about opportunism — especially when it comes to theft or leverage.
source_quote: Never miss an opportunity to grift, man.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin is a pragmatic investigator who wants to use the reward money to obtain a magical book that can prove Bookwyrm's culpability after the fact, rather than confront her directly.
source_quote: There's got to be a book somewhere in the library we can use to actually get to the bottom of this. Some sort of magic book. A powerful spell.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin is observant, cynical, and prone to quips; he recognizes the value of the potion of flying and the red herring coin, and comments on the grift with approval.
source_quote: Never miss an opportunity to grift, man.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin is referenced by Zalthir as the authority who decides the fate of failed Drow.
source_quote: Thorin might decide his fate should be precisely like Serith's

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin is referenced by Zalthir as the authority who decides the strategy of deception, and whose stage-building is heard in his head as he constructs the final act.
source_quote: Thorin said, and I could hear him building the stage in his head.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin is savoring the plan and building the stage in his head.
source_quote: I could hear him building the stage in his head.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin is skeptical of official narratives and pushes for calling out deception; he noticed the red herring in the safe’s contents.
source_quote: Thorin asked whether there was a red herring in there. There was, in fact — one of the coins had a herring stamped on it, and it was red.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin is the architect of a strategic theatrical plan to expose Bookwyrm not through direct evidence or confession, but by using a reward to access a forbidden book that retroactively proves her culpability — turning institutional trust into a weapon.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin leads the group’s decision-making, advocating for handing the case to Kalan to preserve his dignity after his firing, and persistently seeks a magical book to conclusively prove Bookwyrm’s guilt after the fact.
source_quote: Alright. I think we just hand it to him — let him save face, since he got fired — with the understanding that they make good on the promise: we get our reward for helping crack the case.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin led the ambush against helmed horrors, used Dawnbringer to sap their movements, and employed tactical positioning to exploit enemy aggression. He deduced the horrors were drawn to an inert key and sought to weaponize a dead horror as a divining rod to trace its owner.
source_quote: Can we grab one of them and use it to detect who else has the key? Turn it into a sort of divining rod, as it were.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin proposed and advocated for handing the solved case to Kalan to let him save face, in exchange for the group receiving their promised reward.
source_quote: Alright. I think we just hand it to him — let him save face, since he got fired — with the understanding that they make good on the promise: we get our reward for helping crack the case.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin thinks the red herring coin is funny and a sign of the safe's builder having nothing to hide.
source_quote: "Is there a red herring in there?" Thorin asked. There was, in fact. One of the gold coins had a herring stamped on it, and the herring was red. "That's funny," Daz said. It was the kind of joke that tells you the man who built the safe had a sense of humor and nothing to hide — which is its own kind of tell.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin thought Kalan was in the room with them the whole time.
source_quote: I thought Kalan was in the room with us this whole time,

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin wanted to find a magic book to prove Bookwyrm's culpability.
source_quote: There's got to be a book somewhere in the library we can use to actually get to the bottom of this. Some sort of magic book. A powerful spell.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin wanted to know whether they wanted to be famous or fly under the radar.
source_quote: Okay, the alternative: if we make a big deal about being the ones who cracked it, that plays into our fame. But do we really want to be famous, or do we want to fly under the radar? That's kind of our—

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin wants to call out the fact that Bookwyrm is guilty.
source_quote: So, Thorin," I said, "this goes back to your strategy. Do we let on that we know more, or leave it till later, when we can really prove her involvement?

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin wielded Dawnbringer in combat against helmed horrors, used its sap ability to disrupt enemy movement, and spent stored tactical tricks to correct missed strikes when geometry demanded it.
source_quote: Alright — let's go ahead and attack. With Dawnbringer... This is good — let's do it again.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir believed being infamous underground hadn't served them well.
source_quote: We're already infamous underground. It didn't seem to serve us well.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir believes Bahamut may be reading over his shoulder.
source_quote: Bahamut may or may not have been reading over my shoulder. I wrote it down either way.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir believes Bookwyrm is sincerely afraid something will happen to them, but also delighted to have them out of the way.
source_quote: I looked at her while she said it and found, underneath, that she meant the worry. It was real — she was sincerely afraid something would happen to us. Daz found the other half, the half I only saw land on his face: she was delighted to have us wrapped up and out of everything, no more heads poking anywhere.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir believes Bookwyrm will never think to open the safe again.
source_quote: Everyone so fixed on their own troubles that they sealed a box they'd never think to open again and put Kalan Strongbranch back in charge of guarding it, full of himself and his methodology.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir believes theater is the work and does not correct Thorin's theatrics.
source_quote: I did not correct the theatrics. The name for the move was not wrong. And theater is the work; I of all people know that.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir grappled Glabbagool to immobilize him, giving advantage to the attacker, and later deduced the assassins tracked the key by observing its movement between bearers.
source_quote: If you're trying to hit him, you have advantage, because I grappled him — held it still, gift-wrapped.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir identified helmed horrors as animated armor with hovering motion and glowing eyes, attempted verbal engagement, and used physical strikes to subdue them, aided by Glabbagool’s acid attack.
source_quote: Seems like it's a helmed horror? Is this, like, animated armor or something?... You're a popular guy!

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir is a meticulous analyst who obsesses over wording and protocol, insisting that a confession is a confession regardless of academic standards, and questions whether Kalan’s patience is morally defensible.
source_quote: But that was never approved, so the protocol never changed. Putting that aside.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir is a quiet observer who uses Glabbagool, an acid ooze fused to his arm, to covertly steal items and absorb dangerous substances without harm. He acts with deliberate restraint, often making the silent move others overlook, and records events with precision in his mind and margins.
source_quote: I lifted the cup, tilted it to my mouth, and let the tea run down into Glabbagool instead of down my throat.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir is a scholar who reads threats immediately, identifies helmed horrors as animated armor, and holds grappled enemies to grant advantage to allies.
source_quote: Zalthir said. He was already reading it. 'Is this, like, animated armor or something?'... 'If you're trying to hit him, you have advantage, because I grappled him.'

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir is referenced by himself as the one who chose quiet action over loud confrontation, who marked the true nature of events in his margin, and who understood discipline as the ability to ask Glabbagool to hold still.
source_quote: I had told him first, low, that this was a moment of quiet reflection. No loud noises. He held to it. No burp, no bubble, nothing. That is discipline, or the beginning of it.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir is referenced by himself as the one who marked the margin noting the true crime was not murder but embarrassment, and that everyone in the room accepted the trade.
source_quote: I marked, in the margin, that we had come all this way to convict a woman not of murder but of embarrassment, and that everyone in the room seemed content with the trade.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir is the group’s linguistic and procedural analyst, obsessively parsing wording and protocol to expose loopholes in Kalan’s academic reasoning and the legal validity of the Zone of Truth spell.
source_quote: Sorry — how did he open that little diatribe? What was the first thing he said about the confession?

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir knows the real crime is embarrassment, not murder.
source_quote: I only took notes and marked, in the margin, that we had come all this way to convict a woman not of murder but of embarrassment, and that everyone in the room seemed content with the trade.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir murmured that Daral would have bolted for the door if they had let him go.
source_quote: Zalthir murmured something about Daral bolting for the door the second we did.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir noticed that Kalan had written the standard that now protected Bookwyrm.
source_quote: I filed that quietly under the column marked *irony*. The man wrote the standard, and the standard he wrote now shelters the person we most want to reach.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir notices Bookwyrm's hands are too relaxed, indicating she has won.
source_quote: Her hands were too relaxed.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir observed that the group is already infamous underground, and that notoriety has not served them well, countering Thorin’s concern about fame.
source_quote: We're already infamous underground. It didn't seem to serve us well.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir plans to have a later conversation with Glabbagool about restraint.
source_quote: There would be a conversation later about restraint. Not now.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir practiced quiet resistance by allowing Glabbagool to consume Bookwyrm’s tea, a nonverbal act of control and discipline that mirrored the deeper strategy of the group: letting the system turn against itself.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir questioned whether Kalan's plan was immoral by denying Bookwyrm a chance to serve if innocent.
source_quote: But from your own perspective — isn't that immoral? We're effectively preventing Bookwyrm, if innocent, from serving this role.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir read the helmed horrors as animated armor with hovering movement, grappled and held one for Glabbagool’s acid, and later deduced the horrors followed the key—not faces—by tracing their targeting patterns after key transfers.
source_quote: Seems like it's a helmed horror? Is this, like, animated armor or something?

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir realizes Bookwyrm is not surprised but has already decided she has won.
source_quote: This was not that. The tears were correct and the eyes behind them were doing something else... She had decided.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir realizes Glabbagool liked the flying skill.
source_quote: Glabbagool was pleased with himself. *I like the flying skill,* he offered. *That was a good skill.*

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir recognizes Glabbagool's restraint as discipline or the beginning of it.
source_quote: He stayed still because I asked him to. That is discipline, or the beginning of it.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir steals the potion of flying with Glabbagool's arm and considers it a clean move.
source_quote: Glabbagool's arm came out low and quiet, the way I'd have wanted it if I'd trained him for it, which I had not, not yet. It closed around the vial, drew it back, and no one turned. Not one head. Everyone was frantically looking at everything else, and the thing nobody was looking at was me, and the ooze at my side, and the potion that had just left the box. Clean. Not lucky — clean.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir tells Glabbagool to stay quiet during the tea moment as a moment of quiet reflection.
source_quote: I had told him first, low, that this was a moment of quiet reflection. No loud noises.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir thinks Daz might extort Daral, but doubts the rest of the group would.
source_quote: Yeah — we could extort him," Thorin said, "but I don't think that would be nice." "I mean, maybe Daz would," Zalthir said. "But I don't know about the rest of us.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir used his Glabbagool arm to steal the potion of flying from the table during the chaos; he acted while everyone else was distracted.
source_quote: I had my Glabbagool arm swipe the potion of flying off the table. Everyone was frantic... nobody watched my hand.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir uses Locate Object to check if Bookwyrm has a sapphire, hoping she does.
source_quote: I wanted to know if she had one on her — that would have been interesting.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir wanted to know whether Kalan would give a full report if Bookwyrm declined the Zone of Truth.
source_quote: Okay — so you're willing to tell them everything we've learned if she declines?

subject: academic paper on truth sources
fact: An academic paper argues that one source of truth is insufficient; three different kinds are required.
source_quote: My paper says you can't rely on one source of truth; you need three different kinds.

subject: cleaver
fact: A cleaver was presented as physical evidence alongside a confession and a heart, forming the three objects of interest in Grygum’s academic observation.
source_quote: The evidence sat on the table between us. A confession. A heart. A cleaver.

subject: Cleaver
fact: The cleaver is the murder weapon used to kill Janussi; it bears no fingerprints or identifying marks, and its presence alongside the confession suggests a staged crime scene designed to implicate Alkrist while obscuring the true orchestrator.
source_quote: The cleaver proves someone covered this up cleverly.

subject: cleaver and heart as evidence
fact: A cleaver and a heart are physical evidence tied to the crime, but do not identify the perpetrator.
source_quote: You have a confession, a heart, and a cleaver.

subject: Dawnbringer
fact: Dawnbringer is a named magical sword that glows when activated, delivers precise strikes, and possesses an internal sap ability that disrupts enemy motion — it is sentient and responds to emotional validation.
source_quote: The blade lit, poured into Daral, and took the sickness with it... Dawnbringer, do your thing.

subject: Dawnbringer
fact: Dawnbringer is a sword whose sentience and beauty inspire active research, and whose movements slow and become sloppy when affected by its wielder's 'sap' ability.
source_quote: Dawnbringer is a sword whose sentience and beauty inspire active research... the horror's movements went slow and sloppy, off-balance for its next swing.

subject: Dawnbringer as divining rod
fact: Can we grab one of them and use it to detect who else has the key? Turn it into a sort of divining rod, as it were.
source_quote: Can we grab one of them and use it to detect who else has the key? Turn it into a sort of divining rod, as it were.

subject: Dawnbringer's sentience
fact: Dawnbringer was drinking it in. A sword that spends its days pointed at fungus and undead, being told at length that it is beautiful, that it is worthy of study.
source_quote: Dawnbringer was drinking it in. A sword that spends its days pointed at fungus and undead, being told at length that it is beautiful, that it is worthy of study.

subject: fat purse of gold coins
fact: A heavy bag of gold, more than an honest man would keep; still sealed in the safe, unclaimed, and forgotten.
source_quote: A fat purse of gold coins, more than a man keeps for honest reasons.

subject: Fembris Lancer as potential successor
fact: Fembris Lancer is likely to be elected as the new head of the Avowed after Bookwyrm's downfall.
source_quote: Fembris Lancer will probably get elected the new avowed

subject: Glabbagool
fact: Glabbagool is a sentient, acid-siphoning entity fused to Zalthir’s forearm, used to silently consume the tea — a tool of quiet resistance, discipline, and nonverbal defiance against performative suspicion.

subject: Glabbagool arm
fact: Glabbagool arm is fused along Zalthir's forearm, takes in liquids and substances, burns them with acid, and communicates in low tones of approval or disapproval.
source_quote: Glabbagool was fused along my forearm. He took it. A faint singe of acid, a small heat under the skin of my arm as he burned it away — only I felt it.

subject: healing potion
fact: A potion of superior healing remained in the sealed safe, unclaimed.
source_quote: A potion of superior healing

subject: heart
fact: A heart was among the three pieces of evidence on the table, likely the victim’s, used to confirm the murder’s brutality and authenticity.
source_quote: The evidence sat on the table between us. A confession. A heart. A cleaver.

subject: Kalan's Paper: 'Three Sources of Truth'
fact: Kalan’s academic paper argues that a single source of truth — such as a confession — is insufficient for justice; three independent forms of evidence are required. Ironically, this standard now protects Bookwyrm from conviction.
source_quote: My paper says you can't rely on one source of truth; you need three different kinds.

subject: key's detection property
fact: The key itself, sniffing it out through plate and pocket both, was the only thing the helmed horrors followed.
source_quote: The key itself, sniffing it out through plate and pocket both, was the only thing the helmed horrors followed.

subject: magic book to prove culpability
fact: A magical book exists in Candlekeep’s library that could prove Bookwyrm’s culpability after the fact.
source_quote: I will come up with such a book before you leave.

subject: Potion of Flying
fact: A magical vial containing a potion that grants the drinker the ability to fly. Stolen by Zalthir from Alkrist’s safe, it is now held by Glabbagool, who has internalized its properties and approves of its utility.
source_quote: Glabbagool was pleased with himself. *I like the flying skill,* he offered. *That was a good skill.*

subject: potion of flying
fact: A potent magical item, stolen from the safe by Glabbagool’s arm; now hidden in the ooze at the narrator's side, unmissed by all.
source_quote: The potion of flying went with us, in the bag, in the ooze, and no one in that room would ever know to miss it.

subject: Potion of Flying
fact: The potion of flying was stolen by Zalthir via his Glabbagool arm during the distraction of the safe’s opening; it is now in his possession.
source_quote: I had my Glabbagool arm swipe the potion of flying off the table.

subject: potion of flying
fact: The potion of flying was stolen from the safe by Glabbagool's arm while everyone was distracted.
source_quote: my Glabbagool arm swipes the potion of flying

subject: potion of flying
fact: The potion of flying was swiped from the safe by Zalthir's Glabbagool arm while everyone was distracted, and no one noticed its absence.
source_quote: While she's talking, my Glabbagool arm swipes the potion of flying.

subject: potion of superior healing
fact: A magical healing potion recovered from the safe; still inside the sealed container and unclaimed by the group.
source_quote: The safe was closed with everything still inside — the gold, the herring, the healing...

subject: purse of gold coins
fact: A fat purse of gold coins, more than a man keeps for honest reasons, was found in the safe.
source_quote: A fat purse of gold coins, more than a man keeps for honest reasons

subject: Red Herring Coin
fact: A single gold coin stamped with a red herring, placed deliberately in Alkrist’s safe as a joke or distraction. Its presence reinforced the illusion of innocence, making the safe’s contents appear harmless and unconnected to any crime.
source_quote: One of the gold coins had a herring stamped on it, and the herring was red.

subject: red herring coin
fact: A single gold coin stamped with a red herring; a humorous but deliberate clue left by the safe’s builder, signaling nothing was hidden — and yet, everything was.
source_quote: One of the gold coins had a herring stamped on it, and the herring was red.

subject: Red Herring Coin
fact: One gold coin from the safe bore a stamped image of a red herring — a deliberate red herring planted to mislead investigators.
source_quote: one of the coins had a herring stamped on it, and it was red.

subject: red herring coin
fact: One gold coin in the safe bore a red herring stamp, a deliberate red herring.
source_quote: one of the gold coins had a herring stamped on it, and the herring was red

subject: red herring coin
fact: One of the gold coins in Alkrist's safe had a herring stamped on it, and the herring was red.
source_quote: One of the gold coins had a herring stamped on it, and the herring was red.

subject: Sapphire
fact: A sapphire was sought via Locate Object spell to determine if the woman was carrying one; the spell detected nothing, suggesting she did not have it.
source_quote: I wanted to know if she had one on her — that would have been interesting. The spell went out and found nothing.

subject: sapphire
fact: A sapphire was sought with the Locate Object spell, but none was found on Bookwyrm, confirming she did not possess it.
source_quote: I wanted to know if she had one on her — that would have been interesting. The spell went out and found nothing. She did not have it.

subject: sapphire detection
fact: A Locate Object spell was cast to detect a sapphire on Bookwyrm; none was found.
source_quote: I'm hoping she has one on her — that would be interesting

subject: Scorching Ray
fact: Scorching Ray is a spell that fires three lines of flame from the caster's hand, capable of striking helmed horrors and leaving visible dents in their armor.
source_quote: Three lines of flame off his hand, and the nearest suit rang like a struck kettle — a real hit, a dent you could see.

subject: silver candlestick value
fact: The silver candlesticks flanking the Lolth altar are worth 25 gp each.
source_quote: a pair of heavy silver candlesticks worth 25 gp each

subject: tea
fact: The tea in Bookwyrm's office was already poured, and Daz and Thorin refused to drink it, while Bookwyrm drank hers while watching them.
source_quote: The tea was already poured. Daz did not touch the cup in front of him. ... She drank some, watching us over the rim.

subject: the chalice of the statue
fact: The chalice of the statue is the hidden vessel where the heart was placed — not as a ritual object, but as a concealment, making it the physical anchor of the crime and the future target of the book’s revelation.

subject: The Cleaver
fact: The cleaver is a physical artifact tied to Alkrist’s confession and the blood event; its presence in the narrative is used to implicate Bookwyrm, though its origin and use remain unverified.
source_quote: Alkrist is finished — his confession, the cleaver, the blood.

subject: The Confession
fact: The confession is a magical or written testimony linked to Alkrist, now used as circumstantial evidence against Bookwyrm; its authenticity, context, and relevance are under dispute, and its status as a single source of truth is deemed insufficient by the group’s own standards.
source_quote: You have a confession. A heart and a cleaver. ... My paper says you can't rely on one source of truth; you need three different kinds.

subject: The Heart and the Cleaver
fact: The Heart and the Cleaver are physical artifacts recovered from the scene — the heart placed in the chalice of a statue, the cleaver used to sever it — that imply concealment but do not identify the perpetrator.
source_quote: The heart and the cleaver prove someone covered this up cleverly.

subject: the key
fact: An inert, magically undetectable key carried by Daz, which triggered the helmed horrors’ attack. Despite appearing dead and non-magical, it was the sole target of the assassins. Its origin and purpose remain unknown, but its selection suggests precise intelligence behind the ambush.
source_quote: A key that read as nothing under every spell we'd thrown at it. Dead. Inert.

subject: the key
fact: The key is an inert object that reads as nothing under every spell, yet is sought by helmed horrors who move toward it regardless of proximity or disguise.
source_quote: A key that read as nothing under every spell we'd thrown at it. Dead. Inert. And three suits of murderous plate had come through the windows to die for it.

subject: The Key
fact: The key is inert under all detect magic and divination spells, yet it draws lethal attention from constructs designed to track it — suggesting it is a magical artifact of unknown origin, possibly a focus or trigger.
source_quote: A key that read as nothing under every spell we'd thrown at it. Dead. Inert. And three suits of murderous plate had come through the windows to die for it.

subject: The Thrice-Fold Proof
fact: The Thrice-Fold Proof is Kalan’s folded and worn paper detailing his academic standard that requires three distinct types of evidence to establish truth, which he uses to justify inaction and delay in the investigation.
source_quote: Kalan pulled out his own paper — the thrice-fold proof, folded soft from handling — and shoved it into Thorin's face, jabbing at the lines.

subject: the thrice-fold proof
fact: The thrice-fold proof is Kalan’s handwritten record of failed spell attempts — evidence that magic cannot extract truth, making the eventual reliance on institutional access (the book) all the more significant.

subject: The Zone of Truth Spell
fact: The Zone of Truth Spell is a magical effect that does not force truth but reveals whether a subject can resist it — making it a tool of observation rather than conviction.
source_quote: The spell doesn't hand you the truth. It hands you the ability to watch someone refuse it.

subject: Zone of Truth Spell
fact: The Zone of Truth spell is a magical compulsion that prevents deliberate lies, but can be resisted through mental discipline; its effectiveness depends on the target’s willpower, not the caster’s power, making it a tool of observation, not proof.
source_quote: It isn't a lock, it's a pressure.

subject: Zone of Truth spell mechanics
fact: The Zone of Truth spell does not force truth, but reveals if someone can resist it.
source_quote: The spell doesn't hand you the truth. It hands you the ability to watch someone refuse it.

subject: Zone of Truth
fact: The Zone of Truth spell is not an infallible lock but a pressure that can be resisted by a subject who mentally steels themselves; its effectiveness depends on the target’s willpower and awareness, and its use is being debated as either a tool of justice or a weapon of coercion.
source_quote: It can be defeated? It can, now — I know the spell better than most in the room; it isn't a lock, it's a pressure. ... She can steel herself against it — but we'd know if she manages. We don't know if she's telling the truth in that case, but we'd know if she *can* lie.

subject: Accomplices in Janussi's Death
fact: It is suspected that accomplices exist, but their identities are unknown; the group has chosen to acknowledge their existence without naming them.
source_quote: Yeah — we know there are accomplices," I said.

subject: Bookwyrm's guilt
fact: Bookwyrm's guilt remains unproven despite the suspicion.
source_quote: The confession is one spell — the weakest channel, by the standard I wrote. The heart and the cleaver prove someone covered this up cleverly. Neither says who it was.

subject: Bookwyrm's Guilt or Innocence
fact: The central unresolved thread is whether Bookwyrm is truly guilty of the crimes tied to Alkrist’s confession and the cleaver, or if she is being framed by political maneuvering; the players are betting on her response to a proposed opportunity to decline the role as proof of guilt.
source_quote: A win either way, drawn on academic paper. I have seen this move before, in Gracklstugh, dressed in different robes. Pit the room against the accused and let the room do the killing you don't want your name on.

subject: Bookwyrm's involvement
fact: The party knows Bookwyrm is guilty but lacks proof, leaving her fate unresolved.
source_quote: All we had was that she'd been in the same wing, and that Alkrist had named her the mastermind. Thin.

subject: Bookwyrm's sapphire
fact: Zalthir wanted to know if Bookwyrm had a sapphire, but none was found, leaving its significance unresolved.
source_quote: I wanted to know if she had one on her — that would have been interesting. The spell went out and found nothing. Bookwyrm did not have it.

subject: Bookwyrm’s True Guilt
fact: Though Alkrist confessed and the evidence points to him, Zalthir and others suspect Bookwyrm orchestrated the crime. No proof exists, but her emotional detachment, calculated relief, and manipulation of the investigation suggest she is the mastermind — a truth the group chooses not to expose.
source_quote: She was not sad. She was relieved.

subject: Candlekeep unanswered questions
fact: The group arrived at Candlekeep with unresolved questions for various scholars and institutions, which remain unaddressed despite solving the murder.
source_quote: There was still the matter of everything we hadn't gotten yet — the things we came to Candlekeep to ask the various folks, questions still owed to us.

subject: cure for Daral
fact: The group has not yet decided whether to cure Daral; the question lingers, weighted by fear, duty, and the unspoken cost of magic.
source_quote: What do you guys think? Should we cure him?

subject: Daral's cure
fact: Daral is afraid he will be left broken because the party may not consider him worth the spell.
source_quote: Are you guys going to cure me or anything?" he asked, and there it was — under the scholarship, the small fear of being left broken because we'd decided he wasn't worth the spell.

subject: Daral’s Cure
fact: Daral’s condition — likely a magical affliction — remains unaddressed. The party debates whether to expend resources on him, revealing their moral ambiguity and the tension between pragmatism and loyalty.
source_quote: What do you guys think? Should we cure him?

subject: Dawnbringer's identity
fact: Dawnbringer's gender is uncertain and unresolved.
source_quote: I don't know, I can't remember.

subject: Dawnbringer's sentience
fact: Dawnbringer responded emotionally to Daral’s praise, suggesting deeper sentience than previously understood. Its behavior during combat and its reaction to being admired imply it is not merely a weapon but a being capable of internal change and appreciation.
source_quote: Dawnbringer eats it up, I'm sure.

subject: Dawnbringer's Therapy
fact: Dawnbringer, a mysterious entity linked to the party, insists on continuing magical therapy sessions after a single productive meeting, suggesting she is a sentient artifact or spirit seeking resolution for trauma tied to a lost blade or weapon.
source_quote: I'm not leaving here without the therapy. That first session was actually very productive.

subject: Dawnbringer's therapy
fact: Dawnbringer, a psychic presence within Thorin’s mind, insists on continuing therapeutic sessions, having found the first one productive, and is linked to Thorin’s past efforts to find a blade whisperer for her.
source_quote: I'm not leaving here without the therapy. That first session was actually very productive. I really feel we need to—

subject: Divining Rod Proposal
fact: A proposal has been made to repurpose one of the destroyed helmed horrors as a magical divining rod to detect others who possess the key — turning destruction into investigation.
source_quote: Can we grab one of them and use it to detect who else has the key? Turn it into a sort of divining rod, as it were.

subject: fame vs. anonymity
fact: The group debated whether to claim credit for solving the case and risk amplifying their infamy, or to let Kalan take the credit and remain hidden — ultimately choosing the latter.
source_quote: Okay, the alternative: if we make a big deal about being the ones who cracked it, that plays into our fame. But do we really want to be famous, or do we want to fly under the radar?

subject: Glabbagool’s arm
fact: Glabbagool’s arm has demonstrated autonomous, stealthy capability; the narrator has not trained it, yet it acted with perfect precision — raising questions about its origin and potential.
source_quote: Glabbagool's arm came out low and quiet, the way I'd have wanted it if I'd trained him for it, which I had not, not yet.

subject: Glabbagool's restraint
fact: Zalthir plans to discuss restraint with Glabbagool later, but the conversation has not yet occurred.
source_quote: There would be a conversation later about restraint. Not now.

subject: identity of the key's owner
fact: The key is inert, undetectable, yet draws lethal attention. Fembris was the only one who saw it before the attack. The party suspects the key was planted or revealed to an enemy prior to the ambush. Its true owner or creator remains unknown.
source_quote: They weren't following a face. They were following the key itself, sniffing it out through plate and pocket both.

subject: infamous vs. famous
fact: The group debated the semantic difference between 'infamous' and 'famous,' with Thorin noting the former implies notoriety, and Zalthir reinforcing that their infamy has been a liability.
source_quote: Infamous," I said. "You know that's supposed to mean extra famous.

subject: Infamy vs. Stealth
fact: The party debates whether to claim credit for solving Janussi’s murder — knowing their current infamy is a liability — or to remain anonymous, recognizing that their reputation is already warped by the Ember Vanguard’s false legends.
source_quote: We're already infamous underground. It didn't seem to serve us well.

subject: Key's Origin
fact: The key’s true origin and purpose remain unknown; it is inert to detection but lethal to attract, suggesting it was crafted by a hidden power to serve as a tracker or trigger for greater design.
source_quote: Somebody built these, aimed them, and put them through the windows knowing exactly which pocket to reach for.

subject: locate the sapphire
fact: The narrator attempted to locate a sapphire on Bookwyrm but found nothing; the spell’s failure implies either the gem was never there, or it has been concealed beyond detection.
source_quote: I reached out with the spell and found nothing where the sapphire should have been.

subject: locked door
fact: The party’s escape was blocked by a locked door in Deneir’s office, trapping them during Daral’s healing and again during the helmed horror ambush — a persistent narrative obstacle hinting at external control or impending escalation.
source_quote: Then Daral, glowing and cured and full of research, rose to leave — and found the door still locked. He was not going anywhere. None of us were.

subject: Moral Justification of Inaction
fact: The group is rationalizing inaction and indirect pressure as moral because they offer Bookwyrm a choice to decline — but this choice is engineered to trap her: accepting implies guilt, declining implies guilt, and silence implies guilt; the moral high ground is a facade for a witch hunt.
source_quote: We're effectively preventing Bookwyrm, if innocent, from serving this role. ... We will give her the opportunity to decline. Her declining will further weaken her support among the other Avowed.

subject: one more thing
fact: The theatrical motif of 'one more thing' — the final, quiet revelation after everyone believes the case closed — is now the defining structure of the plan, and the group’s shared narrative framework for justice.

subject: origin of the helmed horrors
fact: The helmed horrors were sent by an unseen force that knew the key’s location and the party’s movements. Their inability to speak suggests a deliberate design to prevent interrogation. Thorin proposes using a dead horror as a divining rod to trace who else possesses the key.
source_quote: Who sent you? Who does number one, number two work for?

subject: Patience as a Strategy
fact: The strategy of patience — waiting for institutional forces to turn against Bookwyrm rather than acting directly — is being championed as clever and morally superior, but carries the risk of enabling injustice if she is innocent and the room condemns her without evidence.
source_quote: Sometimes the clever play is to be patient. ... Patience is a fine strategy right up until someone makes a move you never mapped.

subject: reward obligation
fact: The group has an unfulfilled promise for a reward tied to solving Janussi’s murder, and they secured verbal agreement that it would be honored after handing the case to Kalan.
source_quote: with the understanding that they make good on the promise: we get our reward for helping crack the case.

subject: the arithmetic of family
fact: The recurring phrase — 'I know the arithmetic of that' — frames the entire conflict as a calculus of loyalty and concealment, where protecting family justifies crime, and exposure is the only punishment society will accept.

subject: the book that will do her in
fact: The unresolved thread of identifying the exact magical book from Candlekeep’s restricted archives — one that can retroactively prove Bookwyrm’s culpability — is now the group’s primary mission, awaiting discovery.

subject: The Box She Built
fact: The woman has successfully isolated the adventurers, neutralized their influence, and secured her position by making them believe they are protected — while in fact, they are contained.
source_quote: She had built a box and we had walked into it.

subject: the humiliation of exposure
fact: The deeper thread is not about justice, but about the institutional shame of being undone not by evidence, but by the system turning its own rules against the guilty — a theme all participants have internalized.

subject: The key's origin
fact: The key’s origin and the identity of who sent the helmed horrors remain unknown.
source_quote: Somebody built these, aimed them, and put them through the windows knowing exactly which pocket to reach for.

subject: The Magical Book
fact: Thorin and Kalan are pursuing a mythical magical book in Candlekeep’s archives that could definitively prove Bookwyrm’s guilt — not to convict her now, but to use as leverage after she is removed from power, ensuring the new head grants access.
source_quote: We use our reward to access the thing that will do her in.

subject: The magic book
fact: The specific magic book needed to prove Bookwyrm's culpability has not yet been identified.
source_quote: I don't know which book exactly, but I'm just thinking,

subject: The Nature of Justice
fact: The party realizes that justice in this system is not about truth — it is about narrative control. Bookwyrm won not because she was innocent, but because she controlled the story. The group, though aware, chooses to walk away with a potion and silence.
source_quote: We know who did it, someone said, and it's not her. Why wouldn't she be elected.

subject: the safe’s builder
fact: The builder of the safe left a red herring coin as a joke — a sign of humor and openness — yet the theft of the potion suggests the joke was a trap, or a distraction.
source_quote: It was the kind of joke that tells you the man who built the safe had a sense of humor and nothing to hide — which is its own kind of tell.

subject: The Thread from Alkrist to A'lai
fact: The Thread from Alkrist to A'lai is the suspected connection between the confessed killer and the potential new head of Candlekeep, implying A'lai may be involved in the cover-up.
source_quote: We knew there was a thread running from all this back to A'lai.

subject: The Thread of Academic Principle vs. Justice
fact: The Thread of Academic Principle vs. Justice is the central moral conflict of the group — whether truth must be proven by scholarly standard, or whether justice requires immediate action regardless of protocol.
source_quote: What matters more to an academic? Putting the murderer in jail, or being true to their academic principles and their research proposal?

subject: The Whispering Sword
fact: Dawnbringer’s need for therapy is connected to a sword whisperer — someone who once understood the language of blades — whose absence left her spiritually unmoored; the party’s hunt for this figure has spanned months.
source_quote: I'd been the one hunting a sword whisperer for her since the road south — months where the thing she was built to carry just wasn't there.

subject: Who Killed Janussi?
fact: The true killer remains unknown; while the woman is suspected of orchestrating the crime, it is unclear whether she performed the polymorph or if an accomplice did.
source_quote: We don't know that part. She agreed. We did not.
